abhipharaṇatā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun in -tā from abhipharaṇa. In the sentence it is one of a series of synonyms of pīti, in the nominative singular, describing joy pervading the mind.
abhipharaṇatā.example_1: pītīti yā pañcakāmaguṇapaṭisaññuttā pīti pāmujjaṃ āmodanā pamodanā hāso pahāso vitti tuṭṭhi odagyaṃ attamanatā abhipharaṇatā cittassa.

jagu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa list of synonyms for 'man' as a being. Probably a dialectal or defective variant; not found in the main dictionaries as a separate word.
jagu.example_1: Maccoti satto naro mānavo poso puggalo jīvo jāgu [jātu (syā.), jagu (ka.)] jantu indagu [hindagū (sī. syā.)] manujo.
jagu.translation_1: “Mortal” (macco) means a being, a person, a human, a creature, an individual, a living being, one who passes from death to birth, a creature, one who proceeds by faculties, or a person.

heti.meaning_2: here; in this place; in this matter; on this occasion
heti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ha (emphatic particle) + iti; alternative to atha antena jahati; variant reading in the text (syā.).
heti.example_1: Atha antena jahati [atho antena heti (syā.), asahantena dahati (ka.)], sarīraṃ sapariggahaṃ;
heti.translation_1: At the end, one abandons the body along with one's belongings.

gatadiso.meaning_2: who has reached the goal; who has attained the final destination; one whose direction is fulfilled
gatadiso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound of gata (gone, reached) and disa (direction, quarter), used as an epithet of an arahant in a stock description; nominative singular in the text. Spelling varies gatadiso / gatadisa; cf. gataddha and gatakoṭi in the same list.
gatadiso.example_1: so vutthavāso ciṇṇacaraṇo gataddho gatadiso gatakoṭiko pālitabrahmacariyo uttamadiṭṭhippatto bhāvitamaggo, pahīnakileso paṭividdhākuppo sacchikatanirodho.
gatadiso.example_2: so vuṭṭhavāso ciṇṇacaraṇo gataddho gatadiso gatakoṭiko pālitabrahmacariyo uttamadiṭṭhippatto bhāvitamaggo pahīnakileso paṭividdhākuppo sacchikatanirodho, dukkhaṃ tassa pariññātaṃ, samudayo pahīno, maggo bhāvito, nirodho sacchikato, abhiññeyyaṃ abhiññātaṃ, pariññeyyaṃ pariññātaṃ, pahātabbaṃ pahīnaṃ, bhāvetabbaṃ bhāvitaṃ, sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ.

visinitvā.meaning_2: having dispelled; having removed; having settled (free from clinging)
visinitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of a causative-type verb visineti (vi + sineti), sometimes written visīneti; here glossed 'having dispelled', standing free of entanglement. Indeclinable form, so stem and pattern are left blank.
visinitvā.example_1: neva saṃsibbati na ussineti, visinitvā ṭhito.
visinitvā.example_2: Neva saṃsibbati [neva sineti (sī.), neva visīneti (syā.)] na ussineti, visinitvā ṭhito.
visinitvā.translation_2: They do not knit together, nor do they rise up; they stand having dispelled.

vichanno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle with the prefix vi-, used in a string of synonyms for 'covered, concealed' (channo vichanno ucchanno...). Nom sg in -o agreeing with satto.
vichanno.example_1: sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārehi channo vichanno ucchanno āvuto nivuto ovuto pihito paṭicchanno paṭikujjitoti—
vichanno.example_2: Sabbakilesehi sabbaduccaritehi sabbadarathehi sabbapariḷāhehi sabbasantāpehi sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārehi channo vichanno ucchanno āvuto nivuto ovuto [ophuto (syā.)] pihito paṭicchanno paṭikujjitoti – satto guhāyaṃ bahunābhichanno.
vichanno.translation_2: Covered by all defilements, by all misconduct, by all torments, by all fevers, by all burning sensations, by all unwholesome volitional formations; covered over and over, obstructed, blocked, hampered, enclosed, veiled, placed upside down — this is ‘a being attached in the cave, covered by many things.’

ucchanno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used in a list of terms meaning covered or concealed. One of a series of synonyms in the Niddesa prose.
ucchanno.example_1: sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārehi channo vichanno ucchanno āvuto nivuto ovuto pihito paṭicchanno paṭikujjitoti—
ucchanno.example_2: Sabbakilesehi sabbaduccaritehi sabbadarathehi sabbapariḷāhehi sabbasantāpehi sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārehi channo vichanno ucchanno āvuto nivuto ovuto [ophuto (syā.)] pihito paṭicchanno paṭikujjitoti – satto guhāyaṃ bahunābhichanno.
ucchanno.translation_2: Covered by all defilements, by all misconduct, by all torments, by all fevers, by all burning sensations, by all unwholesome volitional formations; covered over and over, obstructed, blocked, hampered, enclosed, veiled, placed upside down — this is ‘a being attached in the cave, covered by many things.’

sampamuyhanti.meaning_2: is completely confused; is utterly bewildered
sampamuyhanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd plural present in the text: saṃ + pa + muyhanti. The prefix saṃ- is assimilated to sam- before p.
sampamuyhanti.example_1: yebhuyyena devamanussā pañcasu kāmaguṇesu muyhanti sammuyhanti sampamuyhanti, mūḷhā sammūḷhā sampamūḷhā avijjāya andhīkatā āvutā nivutā ovutā pihitā paṭicchannā paṭikujjitā, taṃ kāraṇā mohanā vuccanti pañca kāmaguṇā.
sampamuyhanti.example_2: pamūḷhāti yebhuyyena devamanussā pañcasu kāmaguṇesu muyhanti sammuyhanti sampamuyhanti mūḷhā sammūḷhā sampamūḷhā avijjāya andhīkatā āvutā nivutā ovutā pihitā paṭicchannā paṭikujjitāti—

duccajjā.meaning_2: hard to give up; difficult to abandon; hard to relinquish
duccajjā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural nominative in -ā agreeing with kāmā. Formed with du- (difficult) + the gerundive cajja from √caj; listed among synonyms of duppahāya.
duccajjā.example_1: kāmā hi loke duppahāyā duccajjā duppariccajjā dunnimmadayā dunniveṭhayā dubbiniveṭhayā duttarā duppatarā dussamatikkamā dubbinivattāti—
duccajjā.example_2: Kāmā hi loke duppahāyā duccajjā duppariccajjā dunnimmadayā dunniveṭhayā dubbiniveṭhayā duttarā duppatarā dussamatikkamā dubbinivattāti – kāmā hi loke na hi suppahāyā.
duccajjā.translation_2: Sensual pleasures in the world are not easily abandoned, not easily left behind, not easily forsaken, not easily made pride-less, not easily disentangled, not easily released, not easily crossed over, not easily specifically crossed, not easily traversed, not easily returned from — thus, ‘for sensual pleasures in the world are truly not easily abandoned.’

duppariccajjā.meaning_2: hard to give up; hard to forsake; hard to abandon
duppariccajjā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of duppariccajja; used in the Niddesa list of epithets for kāma. Nominative singular feminine in the text.
duppariccajjā.example_1: kāmā hi loke duppahāyā duccajjā duppariccajjā dunnimmadayā dunniveṭhayā dubbiniveṭhayā duttarā duppatarā dussamatikkamā dubbinivattāti—
duppariccajjā.example_2: Kāmā hi loke duppahāyā duccajjā duppariccajjā dunnimmadayā dunniveṭhayā dubbiniveṭhayā duttarā duppatarā dussamatikkamā dubbinivattāti – kāmā hi loke na hi suppahāyā.
duppariccajjā.translation_2: Sensual pleasures in the world are not easily abandoned, not easily left behind, not easily forsaken, not easily made pride-less, not easily disentangled, not easily released, not easily crossed over, not easily specifically crossed, not easily traversed, not easily returned from — thus, ‘for sensual pleasures in the world are truly not easily abandoned.’

dunniveṭhayā.meaning_2: hard to unravel; difficult to disentangle; difficult to resolve
dunniveṭhayā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of dunniveṭha listed with dubbiniveṭhaya in the Niddesa; describes kāmā and manosampadā. Plural in -ā used distributively in the text.
dunniveṭhayā.example_1: kāmā hi loke duppahāyā duccajjā duppariccajjā dunnimmadayā dunniveṭhayā dubbiniveṭhayā duttarā duppatarā dussamatikkamā dubbinivattāti—
dunniveṭhayā.example_2: manosampadā duppamuñcā dummocayā duppamocayā dunniveṭhayā dubbiniveṭhayā, duttarā duppatarā dussamatikkamā dubbinivattā.

dubbiniveṭhayā.meaning_2: difficult to unravel; hard to resolve; hard to get rid of
dubbiniveṭhayā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form is the plural (agreeing with kāmā) or a noun utilised in a list of adjectives; the prefix du- takes the form dub- before b-.
dubbiniveṭhayā.example_1: kāmā hi loke duppahāyā duccajjā duppariccajjā dunnimmadayā dunniveṭhayā dubbiniveṭhayā duttarā duppatarā dussamatikkamā dubbinivattāti—
dubbiniveṭhayā.example_2: manosampadā duppamuñcā dummocayā duppamocayā dunniveṭhayā dubbiniveṭhayā, duttarā duppatarā dussamatikkamā dubbinivattā.

pucchañchikatā.meaning_2: desire to ask; readiness to question; inquisitiveness
pucchañchikatā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A taṇhā synonym in the Niddesa list of defilements, paired with sādhukamyatā. Possibly pucchā + chika + tā or pucchaṃ + chika + tā ("desiring to ask").
pucchañchikatā.example_1: yo rāgo sārāgo anunayo anurodho nandī nandirāgo, cittassa sārāgo icchā mucchā ajjhosānaṃ gedho paligedho saṅgo paṅko, ejā māyā janikā sañjananī sibbinī jālinī saritā visattikā, suttaṃ visaṭā āyūhinī dutiyā paṇidhi bhavanetti, vanaṃ vanatho sandhavo sneho apekkhā paṭibandhu, āsā āsīsanā āsīsitattaṃ, rūpāsā saddāsā gandhāsā rasāsā phoṭṭhabbāsā, lābhāsā dhanāsā puttāsā jīvitāsā, jappā pajappā abhijappā jappanā jappitattaṃ loluppaṃ loluppāyanā loluppāyitattaṃ pucchañchikatā sādhukamyatā, adhammarāgo visamalobho nikanti nikāmanā patthanā pihanā sampatthanā, kāmataṇhā bhavataṇhā vibhavataṇhā, rūpataṇhā arūpataṇhā nirodhataṇhā, rūpataṇhā saddataṇhā gandhataṇhā rasataṇhā phoṭṭhabbataṇhā dhammataṇhā, ogho yogo gantho upādānaṃ āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ chadanaṃ bandhanaṃ, upakkileso anusayo pariyuṭṭhānaṃ latā vevicchaṃ, dukkhamūlaṃ dukkhanidānaṃ dukkhappabhavo mārapāso mārabaḷisaṃ māravisayo, taṇhānadī taṇhājālaṃ taṇhāgaddulaṃ taṇhāsamuddo abhijjhā lobho akusalamūlaṃ.

vibaddhā.meaning_2: bound fast; attached; enmeshed; tied up
vibaddhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used adjectivally in the Niddesa passage; nominative singular masculine agreeing with the craving-bound person, alongside ābaddha, lagga, laggita, palibaddha. Some analyses take it as a synonym of baddha with intensive vi-. Feminine nominative singular form in -ā.
vibaddhā.example_1: manosampadāya baddhā, vibaddhā ābaddhā laggā laggitā palibaddhāti—
vibaddhā.example_2: Bhavasātabaddhā, sukhāya vedanāya sātabaddhā, iṭṭhasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ baddhā, yobbaññe baddhā, ārogye baddhā, jīvite baddhā, lābhe baddhā, yase baddhā, pasaṃsāyaṃ baddhā, sukhe baddhā, manāpikesu rūpesu baddhā, saddesu … gandhesu … rasesu … manāpikesu phoṭṭhabbesu baddhā, cakkhusampadāya baddhā, sotaghānajivhākāyamanosampadāya baddhā, vibaddhā ābaddhā laggā laggitā palibaddhāti – icchānidānā bhavasātabaddhā.
vibaddhā.translation_2: “Bound by the pleasure of existence” means bound to pleasant feeling, bound to the desirable object, bound to youthfulness, bound to health, bound to life, bound to gain, bound to fame, bound to praise, bound to pleasure, bound to pleasing forms, bound to pleasing sounds … smells … tastes … pleasing tangibles, bound to the accomplishment of the eye, bound to the accomplishment of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; bound, attached, clinging, stuck, fastened—these are those with craving as their origin, bound by the pleasure of existence.

palibaddhāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is palibaddhā ti, i.e. the past participle palibaddhā (nominative singular feminine) followed by the quotation particle ti; the entry is for palibaddha. Used in a string of near-synonyms for 'bound' (baddhā, vibaddhā, ābaddhā, laggā, laggitā).
palibaddhāti.example_1: manosampadāya baddhā, vibaddhā ābaddhā laggā laggitā palibaddhāti—
palibaddhāti.example_2: Bhavasātabaddhā, sukhāya vedanāya sātabaddhā, iṭṭhasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ baddhā, yobbaññe baddhā, ārogye baddhā, jīvite baddhā, lābhe baddhā, yase baddhā, pasaṃsāyaṃ baddhā, sukhe baddhā, manāpikesu rūpesu baddhā, saddesu … gandhesu … rasesu … manāpikesu phoṭṭhabbesu baddhā, cakkhusampadāya baddhā, sotaghānajivhākāyamanosampadāya baddhā, vibaddhā ābaddhā laggā laggitā palibaddhāti – icchānidānā bhavasātabaddhā.
palibaddhāti.translation_2: “Bound by the pleasure of existence” means bound to pleasant feeling, bound to the desirable object, bound to youthfulness, bound to health, bound to life, bound to gain, bound to fame, bound to praise, bound to pleasure, bound to pleasing forms, bound to pleasing sounds … smells … tastes … pleasing tangibles, bound to the accomplishment of the eye, bound to the accomplishment of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; bound, attached, clinging, stuck, fastened—these are those with craving as their origin, bound by the pleasure of existence.

dubbinivattā.meaning_2: difficult to turn back; hard to reverse; hard to dispel
dubbinivattā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes mano-sampadā and sense pleasures that are hard to give up. Plural nominative agreeing with sampadā, written dubbinivattā.
dubbinivattā.example_1: manosampadā duppamuñcā dummocayā duppamocayā dunniveṭhayā dubbiniveṭhayā, duttarā duppatarā dussamatikkamā dubbinivattā.
dubbinivattā.example_2: manosampadāya dummocayā duruddharā, dussamuddharā dubbuṭṭhāpayā dussamuṭṭhāpayā dunniveṭhayā dubbiniveṭhayā duttarā duppatarā dussamatikkamā dubbinivattā.

paridāyavacanametaṃ.meaning_2: this is the word 'paridāyana'; this statement is a comprehensive term
paridāyavacanametaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (syā.) for pariyādiyanavacanametaṃ; a sandhi of paridāyavacanaṃ (nt) and etaṃ (pron). Refers to 'yaṃ kiñci' as an all-embracing term.
paridāyavacanametaṃ.example_1: Yaṃ kiñcīti sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ asesaṃ nissesaṃ pariyādiyanavacanametaṃ [paridāyavacanametaṃ (syā.)]– yaṃ kiñcīti.
paridāyavacanametaṃ.translation_1: “Whatever” is an exhaustive and summary term for all, by all means, in every respect, completely—this is what “whatever” means.

dhīkatapāpāti.meaning_2: whose evil has been exposed; whose wickedness is laid bare
dhīkatapāpāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading dhikkhatapāpa; the Niddesa glosses dhīkatapāpā as dhīrā. Vocative plural used as an address in the text, written with -ti from iti.
dhīkatapāpāti.example_1: dhīrāti dhīrā, dhitimāti dhīrā, dhitisampannāti dhīrā, dhīkatapāpāti dhīrā.

paphandanti.meaning_2: quivers; writhes; struggles convulsively; thrashes about
paphandanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Pa + √phand, intensive/frequentative in sense; occurs in a string of near-synonyms (phandanti, paphandanti, samphandanti, vipphandanti, vedhanti...). 3rd plural present in the text.
paphandanti.example_1: vipariṇatepi phandanti paphandanti samphandanti vipphandanti vedhanti pavedhanti sampavedhanti.
paphandanti.example_2: yathā macchā appodake parittodake udakapariyādāne kākehi vā kulalehi vā balākāhi vā paripātiyamānā ukkhipiyamānā khajjamānā phandanti paphandanti samphandanti vipphandanti vedhanti pavedhanti sampavedhanti;

tirayitvā.meaning_2: having investigated; having examined; having discerned
tirayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of tīrayitvā in the Niddesa passage. The form in the text is listed as a variant (ka.); tirayitvā = tīrayitvā with shortening of the vowel before the conjunct. Absolutive in a list of parallel absolutives.
tirayitvā.example_1: Etaṃ ādīnavaṃ disvā passitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā [tirayitvā (ka.)] vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā mamattesūti – etampi disvā.
tirayitvā.translation_1: Seeing this danger, having perceived it, calculated it, investigated it, made it distinct, and made it clear, [one should live] unselfish regarding what is appropriated—this is “seeing this too.”

anibbattayamāno.meaning_2: not producing; not generating; not bringing forth
anibbattayamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle in the accusative singular, in a list of synonyms with ajanayamāna and asañjanayamāna.
anibbattayamāno.example_1: bhavesu āsattiṃ akubbamāno, chandaṃ pemaṃ rāgaṃ khantiṃ akubbamāno ajanayamāno asañjanayamāno anibbattayamāno anabhinibbattayamānoti—
anibbattayamāno.example_2: evaṃ attagarahitaṃ kammaṃ akubbamāno ajanayamāno asañjanayamāno anibbattayamāno anabhinibbattayamānoti—

yadanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Unidentified form; possibly not a genuine finite verb (perhaps a sandhi or textual corruption). PEU lists only yadagga, which does not fit. No root assigned.

pakāsayitvā.meaning_2: having made clear; having announced; having declared
pakāsayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of pakāsayati (causative of pakāsati). In the text: avaṇṇaṃ pakāsayitvā, 'having announced the faults'. The form is built on the causative base with -itvā.
pakāsayitvā.example_1: yaṃ te titthiyā sundariparibbājikaṃ hantvā samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ avaṇṇaṃ pakāsayitvā “evaṃ etaṃ lābhaṃ yasasakkāraṃ sammānaṃ paccāharissāmā”ti te evaṃdiṭṭhikā evaṅkhantikā evaṃrucikā evaṃladdhikā evaṃajjhāsayā evaṃadhippāyā, te nāsakkhiṃsu sakaṃ diṭṭhiṃ sakaṃ khantiṃ sakaṃ ruciṃ sakaṃ laddhiṃ sakaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ sakaṃ adhippāyaṃ atikkamituṃ;
pakāsayitvā.example_2: Yaṃ te titthiyā sundariparibbājikaṃ hantvā samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ avaṇṇaṃ pakāsayitvā ‘‘ evaṃ etaṃ lābhaṃ yasasakkāraṃ sammānaṃ paccāharissāmā ’’ ti te evaṃdiṭṭhikā evaṃkhantikā evaṃrucikā evaṃladdhikā evaṃajjhāsayā evaṃadhippāyā, te nāsakkhiṃsu sakaṃ diṭṭhiṃ sakaṃ khantiṃ sakaṃ ruciṃ sakaṃ laddhiṃ sakaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ sakaṃ adhippāyaṃ atikkamituṃ;
pakāsayitvā.translation_2: Because those sectarians, having killed the wandering nun Sundarī and announced the faults of the Sakyan-son ascetics, thinking “In this way we shall reap such gain, honor, respect, and regard,” were possessed of such a view, such patience, such preference, such a theory, such an inclination, [and] such an intention, they were unable to go beyond their own view, their own patience, their own preference, their own theory, their own inclination, [and] their own intention.

accantasanti.meaning_2: complete peace; utter tranquillity; total calm (a name for Nibbāna)
accantasanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound of accanta (extreme; absolute) and santi (peace). Used in Niddesa as one of three kinds of peace (with tadaṅgasanti and sammutisanti) and glossed as amataṃ nibbānaṃ; nominative singular in the text.

tadaṅgasanti.meaning_2: peace by that factor; cessation through that aspect; tranquillity by the corresponding factor
tadaṅgasanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound with santi (peace, cessation). In the text it is nominative singular, one of three kinds of peace: accantasanti, tadaṅgasanti, sammutisanti.

bilaggāho.meaning_2: taking in portions; grasping piece by piece; partial grasp
bilaggāho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] One of a list of terms for grasping (odhiggāho, varaggāho, koṭṭhāsaggāho, etc.) in Niddesa prose. Nominative singular in the text.
bilaggāho.example_1: samuggahītanti nivesanesu odhiggāho bilaggāho varaggāho koṭṭhāsaggāho uccayaggāho samuccayaggāho.
bilaggāho.example_2: samuggahītanti odhiggāho bilaggāho varaggāho koṭṭhāsaggāho uccayaggāho samuccayaggāho, “idaṃ saccaṃ tacchaṃ tathaṃ bhūtaṃ yāthāvaṃ aviparītan”ti gahitaṃ parāmaṭṭhaṃ abhiniviṭṭhaṃ ajjhositaṃ adhimuttaṃ natthi na santi na saṃvijjati nupalabbhati, pahīnaṃ samucchinnaṃ vūpasantaṃ paṭipassaddhaṃ abhabbuppattikaṃ ñāṇagginā daḍḍhanti—

vicchindiyamāno.meaning_2: being cut off; being severed; being excluded; being abandoned
vicchindiyamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive present participle, masculine nominative singular, describing one who is being cut off (from teacher, teaching, etc.). The PEU suggests 'should be given up', but the passive sense fits these sentences better.
vicchindiyamāno.example_1: evaṃ vicchindiyamāno satthāraṃ nirassati, dhammakkhānaṃ nirassati, gaṇaṃ nirassati, diṭṭhiṃ nirassati, paṭipadaṃ nirassati, maggaṃ nirassati.
vicchindiyamāno.example_2: evaṃ vicchindiyamāno satthārā cavati, dhammakkhānā cavati, gaṇā cavati, diṭṭhiyā cavati, paṭipadāya cavati, maggato cavati.

pettivisayikoti.meaning_2: one belonging to the realm of the departed; a being in the ghost realm; a dweller in the world of the petas
pettivisayikoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text joined with -ti (-iti) and quoted as a designation of beings; nominative singular. The word is a bahubbīhi-type adjective used as a noun. First member is petti (from peta) + visaya.
pettivisayikoti.example_1: nerayikoti vā tiracchānayonikoti vā pettivisayikoti vā manussoti vā devoti vā rūpīti vā arūpīti vā saññīti vā asaññīti vā nevasaññīnāsaññīti vā, so hetu natthi paccayo natthi kāraṇaṃ natthi yena vadeyyuṃ katheyyuṃ bhaṇeyyuṃ dīpeyyuṃ vohareyyunti—
pettivisayikoti.example_2: nerayikoti vā tiracchānayonikoti vā pettivisayikoti vā manussoti vā devoti vā rūpīti vā arūpīti vā saññīti vā asaññīti vā nevasaññīnāsaññīti vā.

cāpasakuṇaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (ka.) of cāṭakasakuṇa; accusative singular in the text.
cāpasakuṇaṃ.example_1: Te kālato vuṭṭhahitvā abhimaṅgalagatāni rūpāni passanti – cāṭakasakuṇaṃ [vātasakuṇaṃ (syā.), cāpasakuṇaṃ (ka.)] passanti, phussaveḷuvalaṭṭhiṃ passanti, gabbhinitthiṃ passanti, kumārakaṃ khandhe āropetvā gacchantaṃ passanti, puṇṇaghaṭaṃ passanti, rohitamacchaṃ passanti, ājaññaṃ passanti, ājaññarathaṃ passanti, usabhaṃ passanti, gokapilaṃ passanti.
cāpasakuṇaṃ.translation_1: They arise very early and see forms that have gone towards the auspicious: they see a sparrow, they see a young bamboo sprout, they see a pregnant woman, they see a child being carried on the shoulders, they see a full pot, they see a red fish, they see a thoroughbred, they see a chariot of thoroughbreds, they see an ox, they see a tawny cow.

poṭayitvā.meaning_2: having struck; having shaken; having smashed; having broken
poṭayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading phoṭayitvā in some texts and the Burmese edition. Absolutive of the causative poṭeti (√puṭ 'wrap, envelop' with the causative sign); here used of breaking or smashing the bonds (ganthe).
poṭayitvā.example_1: Atha vā ganthe gadhite ganthite bandhe vibandhe ābandhe lagge laggite palibuddhe bandhane poṭayitvā –[phoṭayitvā (syā.)] visajja.
poṭayitvā.translation_1: Or, having smashed the knots, ties, bonds, particular bonds, multiple bonds, the attached, the tied, the held, and the bonds of craving, conceit, and view—having released.
poṭayitvā.example_2: Atha vā ganthe gadhite ganthite bandhe vibandhe ābandhe lagge laggite palibuddhe bandhane poṭayitvā visajjāti – ādānaganthaṃ gathitaṃ visajja.
poṭayitvā.translation_2: Or, having smashed the knots, ties, bonds, particular bonds, multiple bonds, the attached, the tied, the held, and the bonds of craving, conceit, and view—having released—thus: 'having cut the knotted bonds of holding'.

visajjaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the phrase sajjaṃ visajjaṃ (paired with sajja), describing a vehicle left loose and released. Could also be analysed as a contraction of visajjetvā, but here it agrees with sajjaṃ.
visajjaṃ.example_1: yathā yānaṃ vā vayhaṃ vā rathaṃ vā sakaṭaṃ vā sandamānikaṃ vā sajjaṃ visajjaṃ karonti vikopenti—
visajjaṃ.example_2: yathā vayhaṃ vā rathaṃ vā sakaṭaṃ vā sandamānikaṃ vā sajjaṃ visajjaṃ karonti vikopenti;

saṃvaccharikopi.meaning_2: even one who is a year old; even at one year of age
saṃvaccharikopi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the word is part of a long list of ages (addhamāsikopi ... vīsativassikopi) describing when a being dies. The final -pi is the emphatic particle.
saṃvaccharikopi.example_2: Kalalakālepi cavati marati antaradhāyati vippalujjati, abbudakālepi cavati marati antaradhāyati vippalujjati, pesikālepi cavati marati antaradhāyati vippalujjati, ghanakālepi cavati marati antaradhāyati vippalujjati, pasākhakālepi cavati marati antaradhāyati vippalujjati, jātamattopi cavati marati antaradhāyati vippalujjati, sūtigharepi [pasūtighare (syā.), sūtikaghare (ka.)] cavati marati antaradhāyati vippalujjati, addhamāsikopi cavati marati antaradhāyati vippalujjati, māsikopi cavati marati antaradhāyati vippalujjati, dvemāsikopi … pe … temāsikopi … catumāsikopi … pañcamāsikopi cavati marati antaradhāyati vippalujjati, chamāsikopi … sattamāsikopi … aṭṭhamāsikopi … navamāsikopi … dasamāsikopi … saṃvaccharikopi cavati marati antaradhāyati vippalujjati, dvevassikopi … tivassikopi … catuvassikopi … pañcavassikopi … chavassikopi … sattavassikopi … aṭṭhavassikopi … navavassikopi … dasavassikopi … vīsativassikopi … tiṃsavassikopi … cattārīsavassikopi … paññāsavassikopi … saṭṭhivassikopi … sattativassikopi … asītivassikopi … navutivassikopi cavati marati antaradhāyati vippalujjatīti – oraṃ vassasatāpi miyyati.
saṃvaccharikopi.translation_2: In the stage of the embryo, he moves on, dies, disappears, breaks up; in the stage of the vesicle... in the stage of the flesh-piece... in the stage of the plump mass... in the stage of the limbs... even just born... in the birth-house... half-monthly... monthly... two-monthly... three-monthly... four-monthly... five-monthly... six-monthly... seven-monthly... eight-monthly... nine-monthly... ten-monthly... yearly... two-yearly... three-yearly... four-yearly... five-yearly... six-yearly... seven-yearly... eight-yearly... nine-yearly... ten-yearly... twenty-yearly... thirty-yearly... forty-yearly... fifty-yearly... sixty-yearly... seventy-yearly... eighty-yearly... ninety-yearly, he moves on, dies, disappears, breaks up—this is the meaning of ‘he dies even within a hundred years.’

santamevidanti.meaning_2: this is the highest peace (indeed); 'this is the highest peace'
santamevidanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of santaṃ eva idaṃ iti. No sentences were supplied, so the analysis is provisional; the quotation particle -ti is part of the written form. The Niddesa's discussion of 'santamevidanti' is likely an exegetical gloss on etaṃ santam etaṃ paṇītaṃ.

jahīyati.meaning_2: is abandoned; is given up; is left; perishes; disappears
jahīyati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive of jahati (√hā + ya); listed in the text as a synonym of pahīyati, vijahīyati, antaradhāyati and vippalujjati ('is abandoned, perishes'). 3rd singular passive in -īyati.
jahīyati.example_2: rūpagataṃ vedanāgataṃ saññāgataṃ saṅkhāragataṃ viññāṇagataṃ pahīyati jahīyati vijahīyati antaradhāyati vippalujjati, nāmaṃyevāvasissati.

vijahīyati.meaning_2: is abandoned; is given up; is left behind; disappears
vijahīyati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive verb listed among synonyms for pahīyati (is abandoned; vanishes). 3rd singular, passive in form; sometimes printed as vihīyati in some editions.
vijahīyati.example_2: rūpagataṃ vedanāgataṃ saññāgataṃ saṅkhāragataṃ viññāṇagataṃ pahīyati jahīyati vijahīyati antaradhāyati vippalujjati, nāmaṃyevāvasissati.

dīpayituṃ.meaning_2: to explain; to illustrate; to make clear; to point out
dīpayituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of dīpayati, causative of √dīp (shine, explain). In the text it occurs in a list of synonyms of 'to speak' (akkhātuṃ kathetuṃ bhaṇituṃ dīpayituṃ voharituṃ). The causative base dīpaya + -tuṃ gives dīpayituṃ with i-svaraṇa (cf. dīpetuṃ).
dīpayituṃ.example_2: Akkhātuṃ kathetuṃ bhaṇituṃ dīpayituṃ voharitunti – nāmaṃ evāvasissati akkheyyaṃ.
dīpayituṃ.translation_2: For the purpose of proclaiming, speaking, saying, describing, or using — this is “only the name remains, what is proclaimable.”

yāpiṃsu.meaning_2: causes to go; makes continue; leads; conducts (life); sustains; keeps going
yāpiṃsu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd plural in the text (yāpiṃsu, also written yapiṃsu), from the causative yāpeti. The PEU entry suggests a causative in -ṇe/-ṇāpe; some editions read yāpesuṃ. Meaning here: they lived, carried on, kept going.
yāpiṃsu.example_1: munayo taṇhāpariggahaṃ pariccajitvā diṭṭhipariggahaṃ paṭinissajjitvā cajitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantiṃ karitvā anabhāvaṃ gametvā acariṃsu vihariṃsu iriyiṃsu vattiṃsu pāliṃsu yapiṃsu yāpiṃsu.

sampamussati.meaning_2: is forgotten; is lost; is destroyed; perishes
sampamussati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Third person singular in a series mussati / sammussati / pamussati / sampamussati; saṃ- and pa- are intensive/perfectivising prefixes of the same √mus 1.
sampamussati.example_1: tampi mussati sammussati pamussati sampamussati paribāhiro hotīti—
sampamussati.example_2: Tampi mussati sammussati pamussati sampamussati paribāhiro hotīti – evampi mussate vāpi sāsanaṃ.
sampamussati.translation_2: Even that perishes, is forgotten, is lost, and he becomes an outsider; thus, the teaching also perishes.

paridayhantīti.meaning_2: is burned; is scorched; is tormented (by)
paridayhantīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it occurs as paridayhantīti = paridayhanti + iti, present 3rd plural of paridayhati, with the quotative iti. The form is passive or intransitive in sense: 'they are burned/scorched by many fevers'. The root √dah with the prefix pari and the -ya passive sign becomes dayha.
paridayhantīti.example_1: puthu kilese janentīti puthujjanā, puthu avihatasakkāyadiṭṭhikāti puthujjanā, puthu satthārānaṃ mukhullokikāti puthujjanā, puthu sabbagatīhi avuṭṭhitāti puthujjanā, puthu nānābhisaṅkhāre abhisaṅkharontīti puthujjanā, puthu nānāoghehi vuyhantīti puthujjanā, puthu nānāsantāpehi santapantīti puthujjanā, puthu nānāpariḷāhehi paridayhantīti puthujjanā, puthu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu rattā giddhā gadhitā mucchitā ajjhosannā laggā laggitā palibuddhāti puthujjanā, puthu pañcahi nīvaraṇehi āvutā nivutā ovutā pihitā paṭicchannā paṭikujjitāti puthujjanā.
paridayhantīti.example_2: Puthu kilese janentīti puthujjanā, puthu avihatasakkāyadiṭṭhikāti puthujjanā, puthu satthārānaṃ mukhullokikāti puthujjanā, puthu sabbagatīhi avuṭṭhitāti puthujjanā, puthu nānābhisaṅkhāre [nānābhisaṅkhārehi (syā.)] abhisaṅkharontīti puthujjanā, puthu nānāoghehi vuyhantīti puthujjanā, puthu nānāsantāpehi santapantīti puthujjanā, puthu nānāpariḷāhehi paridayhantīti puthujjanā, puthu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu rattā giddhā gadhitā mucchitā ajjhosannā [ajjhopannā (sī. syā.)] laggā laggitā palibuddhāti puthujjanā, puthu pañcahi nīvaraṇehi āvutā nivutā ovutā pihitā paṭicchannā paṭikujjitāti puthujjanā.
paridayhantīti.translation_2: They are run-of-the-mill people because they generate many defilements; they are run-of-the-mill people because they have many undestroyed self-identity views; they are run-of-the-mill people because they look to many teachers; they are run-of-the-mill people because they have not risen from many destinations; they are run-of-the-mill people because they formulate many various volitional formations; they are run-of-the-mill people because they are carried away by many various floods; they are run-of-the-mill people because they are burned by many various torments; they are run-of-the-mill people because they are scorched by many various fevers; they are run-of-the-mill people because they are lusted, greedy, grasped, infatuated, utterly committed to, attached, tied, and connected in many five-fold sensual pleasures; they are run-of-the-mill people because they are covered, enveloped, wrapped, hidden, concealed, and bent down by many five-fold hindrances.

sandhisamalasaṅkaṭire.meaning_2: hole or gap at the junction of a wall; junction, level ground and threshold
sandhisamalasaṅkaṭire.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text (sandhisamalasaṅkaṭire). The compound describes an uneven place where a cat might wait for mice; sandhi = junction, samala = level ground, saṅkaṭīra = threshold or doorway.
sandhisamalasaṅkaṭire.example_1: yathā ulūko rukkhasākhāyaṃ mūsikaṃ magayamāno jhāyati pajjhāyati nijjhāyati apajjhāyati, yathā kotthu nadītīre macche magayamāno jhāyati pajjhāyati nijjhāyati apajjhāyati, yathā biḷāro sandhisamalasaṅkaṭire mūsikaṃ magayamāno jhāyati pajjhāyati nijjhāyati apajjhāyati, yathā gadrabho vahacchinno sandhisamalasaṅkaṭire jhāyati pajjhāyati nijjhāyati apajjhāyati;

upalakkhayitvā.meaning_2: having noticed; having observed; having made a mental note
upalakkhayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā; in the text it follows other participles such as sutvā and upadhāretvā. The form is upalakkhayitvā, from the causative base upalakkhaya; the root is √lakkh.
upalakkhayitvā.example_1: sutvānahaṃ vīramakāmakāminti sutvā suṇitvā uggahetvā upadhāretvā upalakkhayitvā.
upalakkhayitvā.example_2: sutvāna nāgassa apanamissanti itoti tuyhaṃ vacanaṃ byappathaṃ desanaṃ anusāsanaṃ anusiṭṭhaṃ sutvā suṇitvā uggahetvā upadhārayitvā upalakkhayitvā ito apanamissanti vajissanti pakkamissanti disāvidisaṃ gamissantīti—

saṃgāhati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for 'pagāhati' in the Niddesa passage; cp. √gāh 'dive, plunge'. Third person singular present.
saṃgāhati.translation_1: This is his great bond; he engages in false speech.

kissati.meaning_2: is exhausted; becomes emaciated; is worn out; is tormented (by hardship)
kissati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive-like meaning; appears in stock Niddesa phrase kissati parikissati parikilissati, describing one who is wretched and worn down. 3rd singular present in the text.
kissati.example_1: kapaṇo viya mando viya momūho viya kissati parikissati parikilissati.

vesuṅgaṃ.meaning_2: Vesuṅga; name of a distant port or land reached by sea traders
vesuṅgaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Listed among far-off trading destinations in the Niddesa's description of the merchant's sea journey. Accusative singular after gacchati.
vesuṅgaṃ.example_1: atha vā kāmataṇhāya abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto bhoge pariyesanto nāvāya mahāsamuddaṃ pakkhandati, sītassa purakkhato uṇhassa purakkhato ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassehi pīḷiyamāno khuppipāsāya miyyamāno tigumbaṃ gacchati, takkolaṃ gacchati, takkasīlaṃ gacchati, kālamukhaṃ gacchati, purapūraṃ gacchati, vesuṅgaṃ gacchati, verāpathaṃ gacchati, javaṃ gacchati, tāmaliṃ gacchati, vaṅgaṃ gacchati, eḷabandhanaṃ gacchati, suvaṇṇakūṭaṃ gacchati, suvaṇṇabhūmiṃ gacchati, tambapāṇiṃ gacchati, suppārakaṃ gacchati, bhārukacchaṃ gacchati, suraṭṭhaṃ gacchati, bhaṅgalokaṃ gacchati, bhaṅgaṇaṃ gacchati, paramabhaṅgaṇaṃ gacchati, yonaṃ gacchati, paramayonaṃ gacchati, vinakaṃ gacchati, mūlapadaṃ gacchati, marukantāraṃ gacchati, jaṇṇupathaṃ gacchati, ajapathaṃ gacchati, meṇḍapathaṃ gacchati, saṅkupathaṃ gacchati, chattapathaṃ gacchati, vaṃsapathaṃ gacchati, sakuṇapathaṃ gacchati, mūsikapathaṃ gacchati, daripathaṃ gacchati, vettācāraṃ gacchati.
vesuṅgaṃ.example_2: sītassa purakkhato uṇhassa purakkhato ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassehi pīḷiyamāno khuppipāsāya miyyamāno tigumbaṃ gacchati, takkolaṃ gacchati, takkasīlaṃ gacchati, kāḷamukhaṃ gacchati, purapūraṃ gacchati, vesuṅgaṃ gacchati, verāpathaṃ gacchati, javaṃ gacchati, tāmaliṃ gacchati, vaṅkaṃ gacchati, eḷabandhanaṃ gacchati, suvaṇṇakūṭaṃ gacchati, suvaṇṇabhūmiṃ gacchati, tambapaṇṇiṃ gacchati, suppārakaṃ gacchati, bhārukacchaṃ gacchati, suraṭṭhaṃ gacchati, bhaṅgalokaṃ gacchati, bhaṅgaṇaṃ gacchati, paramabhaṅgaṇaṃ gacchati, yonaṃ gacchati, paramayonaṃ gacchati, vinakaṃ gacchati, mūlapadaṃ gacchati, marukantāraṃ gacchati, jaṇṇupathaṃ gacchati, ajapathaṃ gacchati, meṇḍapathaṃ gacchati, saṅkupathaṃ gacchati, chattapathaṃ gacchati, vaṃsapathaṃ gacchati, sakuṇapathaṃ gacchati, mūsikapathaṃ gacchati, daripathaṃ gacchati, vettācāraṃ gacchati;

daḷahaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears to be a compound (daḷha + a) rather than a simple word, but the exact formation is uncertain; possibly a variant of daḷha. Accusative singular here, agreeing with ekaccariyaṃ.
daḷahaṃ.example_1: Dvīhi kāraṇehi ekaccariyaṃ daḷahaṃ kareyya – pabbajjāsaṅkhātena vā gaṇāvavassaggaṭṭhena vā.
daḷahaṃ.translation_1: He should keep the solitary life firm for two reasons—by way of renunciation, or by way of avoiding the companionship of a group.

samādāno.meaning_2: taking up firmly; firm commitment; undertaking; adopting
samādāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa passage daḷhaṃ samādāno assa, samādāno is likely a nominative singular of samādāna used predicatively with assa (not part of a compound). If taken as a bahubbīhi compound modifying the subject, it could be a masculine nominative samādāno; but here it is best explained as an nt nominative in -o (compare the PEU lemma samādāna).
samādāno.example_1: ekacariyaṃ daḷhaṃ kareyya, thiraṃ kareyya, daḷhaṃ samādāno assa, avaṭṭhitasamādāno assa kusalesu dhammesūti—
samādāno.example_2: Evaṃ gaṇāvavassaggaṭṭhena ekaccariyaṃ daḷhaṃ kareyyāti – ekaccariyaṃ daḷhaṃ kareyya, thiraṃ kareyya, daḷhaṃ samādāno assa, avaṭṭhitasamādāno assa kusalesu dhammesūti – ekaccariyaṃ daḷhaṃ kayirā.
samādāno.translation_2: He should keep the solitary life firm by way of avoiding the companionship of a group in this way—thus: he should keep the solitary life firm, keep it stable, should have firm commitment, should have fixed commitment in wholesome things—thus: “He should keep the solitary life firm.”

yāpayatoti.meaning_2: causes to go; keeps going; maintains; sustains; lives
yāpayatoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of √yā. In the text it is part of a string of synonyms for walking, living, moving about: iriyato vattayato pālayato yapayato yāpayato. The -ti is the quotation marker ti, so the headword is the verb form yāpayati. Related causative forms are yāpeti and yapayati.
yāpayatoti.example_1: kathaṃ satassa caratoti kathaṃ satassa sampajānassa carato viharato iriyato vattayato pālayato yapayato yāpayatoti—
yāpayatoti.example_2: evaṃ satassa caratoti evaṃ satassa sampajānassa carato viharato iriyato vattayato pālayato yapayato yāpayatoti—

āveṭhiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun in -iyā from āveṭheti (entangle, wrap). In these Niddesa passages it is the counterpart of nibbeṭhiyā (unravelling); nominative singular, but read as nominative plural āveṭhiyā te akatā if the parallel nibbeṭhiyā te dukkaṭā is taken the same way; possibly plural here.
āveṭhiyā.example_1: “attho te dunnīto, byañjanaṃ te duropitaṃ, atthabyañjanaṃ te dunnītaṃ duropitaṃ, niggaho te akato, paṭikammaṃ te dukkaṭaṃ, viseso te akato, paṭiviseso te dukkaṭo, āveṭhiyā te akatā, nibbeṭhiyā te dukkaṭā, chedo te akato, maṇḍalaṃ te dukkaṭaṃ visamakathaṃ dukkathitaṃ dubbhaṇitaṃ dullapitaṃ duruttaṃ dubbhāsitan”ti apaharanti.
āveṭhiyā.example_2: “attho te dunnīto, byañjanaṃ te duropitaṃ, atthabyañjanaṃ te dunnītaṃ duropitaṃ, niggaho te akato, paṭikammaṃ te dukkaṭaṃ, viseso te akato, paṭiviseso te dukkaṭo, āveṭhiyā te akatā, nibbeṭhiyā te dukkaṭā, chedo te akato, maṇḍalaṃ te dukkaṭaṃ visamakathaṃ dukkathitaṃ dubbhaṇitaṃ dullapitaṃ duruttaṃ dubbhāsitan”ti, apaharantīti—

nibbeṭhiyā.meaning_2: unravelling; disentangling; unravelling (of a disputed point)
nibbeṭhiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative plural nibbeṭhiyā in the text, paired with āveṭhiyā ('entrapment'). Denominal from nibbeṭheti; the -ya suffix makes a neuter abstract noun.
nibbeṭhiyā.example_1: “attho te dunnīto, byañjanaṃ te duropitaṃ, atthabyañjanaṃ te dunnītaṃ duropitaṃ, niggaho te akato, paṭikammaṃ te dukkaṭaṃ, viseso te akato, paṭiviseso te dukkaṭo, āveṭhiyā te akatā, nibbeṭhiyā te dukkaṭā, chedo te akato, maṇḍalaṃ te dukkaṭaṃ visamakathaṃ dukkathitaṃ dubbhaṇitaṃ dullapitaṃ duruttaṃ dubbhāsitan”ti apaharanti.
nibbeṭhiyā.example_2: “attho te dunnīto, byañjanaṃ te duropitaṃ, atthabyañjanaṃ te dunnītaṃ duropitaṃ, niggaho te akato, paṭikammaṃ te dukkaṭaṃ, viseso te akato, paṭiviseso te dukkaṭo, āveṭhiyā te akatā, nibbeṭhiyā te dukkaṭā, chedo te akato, maṇḍalaṃ te dukkaṭaṃ visamakathaṃ dukkathitaṃ dubbhaṇitaṃ dullapitaṃ duruttaṃ dubbhāsitan”ti, apaharantīti—

virandhamesī.meaning_2: seeking faults; looking for flaws; searching for openings
virandhamesī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound adjective describing someone who seeks faults; nominative singular in the text. Probably vi + randha (fault, flaw) + esī (seeking), not a verb form.
virandhamesī.example_2: Randhamesīti virandhamesī aparaddhamesī khalitamesī gaḷitamesī vivaramesīti – nindāya so kuppati randhamesī.
virandhamesī.translation_2: “Seeking faults” means he is seeking fissures, seeking transgressions, seeking stumbles, seeking downfalls, or seeking openings—this is the meaning of “He becomes angry at the blame, seeking faults.”

maddayitvā.meaning_2: having crushed; having trampled; having pressed down
maddayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive formed with -tvā from the causative stem maddaya-, used with abhibhavitvā, ajjhottharitvā, pariyādiyitvā in an escalating list of oppressive actions; glossed by the Pṭ as crushing or trampling down.
maddayitvā.example_1: atha vā maṃ vādena vādaṃ abhibhavitvā ajjhottharitvā pariyādiyitvā maddayitvā carati viharati iriyati vattati pāleti yapeti yāpetīti.

thambhayitvā.meaning_2: having stiffened; having made firm; having strengthened
thambhayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of the causative thambhayati (from √thambh, 'be stiff'), in a string of absolutives describing making one's doctrine firm and evident; PEU splits it as thambha + ṇaya + tvā.
thambhayitvā.example_1: khattiyaparisāya vā brāhmaṇaparisāya vā gahapatiparisāya vā samaṇaparisāya vā majjhe attano vādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā anuvādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā thambhayitvā brūhayitvā dīpayitvā jotayitvā voharitvā pariggaṇhitvāti—
thambhayitvā.example_2: Khattiyaparisāya vā brāhmaṇaparisāya vā gahapatiparisāya vā samaṇaparisāya vā majjhe attano vādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā anuvādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā thambhayitvā brūhayitvā dīpayitvā jotayitvā voharitvā pariggaṇhitvāti – akkhāya vādaṃ parisāya majjhe.
thambhayitvā.translation_2: In the midst of an assembly of khattiyas, an assembly of brahmins, an assembly of householders, or an assembly of ascetics, having declared and announced his own doctrine, having declared and announced his secondary doctrine, having stiffened, having expanded, having made evident, having illuminated, having expressed, and having held forth—this is the meaning of “Having declared his doctrine in the midst of the assembly.”

brūhayitvā.meaning_2: having increased; having expanded; having magnified; having furthered
brūhayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is one of a series of absolutives (thambhayitvā, dīpayitvā, jotayitvā) describing how a doctrine is set forth and expanded. Causative absolutive from √brūh (increase); variant of brūhetvā.
brūhayitvā.example_1: khattiyaparisāya vā brāhmaṇaparisāya vā gahapatiparisāya vā samaṇaparisāya vā majjhe attano vādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā anuvādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā thambhayitvā brūhayitvā dīpayitvā jotayitvā voharitvā pariggaṇhitvāti—
brūhayitvā.example_2: Khattiyaparisāya vā brāhmaṇaparisāya vā gahapatiparisāya vā samaṇaparisāya vā majjhe attano vādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā anuvādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā thambhayitvā brūhayitvā dīpayitvā jotayitvā voharitvā pariggaṇhitvāti – akkhāya vādaṃ parisāya majjhe.
brūhayitvā.translation_2: In the midst of an assembly of khattiyas, an assembly of brahmins, an assembly of householders, or an assembly of ascetics, having declared and announced his own doctrine, having declared and announced his secondary doctrine, having stiffened, having expanded, having made evident, having illuminated, having expressed, and having held forth—this is the meaning of “Having declared his doctrine in the midst of the assembly.”

dīpayitvā.meaning_2: having made clear; having demonstrated; having explained; having illuminated
dīpayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of the causative dīpayati, in a list of synonymous absolutives (thambhayitvā, brūhayitvā, jotayitvā, etc.).
dīpayitvā.example_1: khattiyaparisāya vā brāhmaṇaparisāya vā gahapatiparisāya vā samaṇaparisāya vā majjhe attano vādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā anuvādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā thambhayitvā brūhayitvā dīpayitvā jotayitvā voharitvā pariggaṇhitvāti—
dīpayitvā.example_2: Khattiyaparisāya vā brāhmaṇaparisāya vā gahapatiparisāya vā samaṇaparisāya vā majjhe attano vādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā anuvādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā thambhayitvā brūhayitvā dīpayitvā jotayitvā voharitvā pariggaṇhitvāti – akkhāya vādaṃ parisāya majjhe.
dīpayitvā.translation_2: In the midst of an assembly of khattiyas, an assembly of brahmins, an assembly of householders, or an assembly of ascetics, having declared and announced his own doctrine, having declared and announced his secondary doctrine, having stiffened, having expanded, having made evident, having illuminated, having expressed, and having held forth—this is the meaning of “Having declared his doctrine in the midst of the assembly.”

jotayitvā.meaning_2: having caused to shine; having illuminated; having made clear
jotayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -itvā from the causative joteti (to illuminate, make clear). In the sentence it belongs to a series of absolutives describing the declaration of a doctrine.
jotayitvā.example_1: khattiyaparisāya vā brāhmaṇaparisāya vā gahapatiparisāya vā samaṇaparisāya vā majjhe attano vādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā anuvādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā thambhayitvā brūhayitvā dīpayitvā jotayitvā voharitvā pariggaṇhitvāti—
jotayitvā.example_2: Khattiyaparisāya vā brāhmaṇaparisāya vā gahapatiparisāya vā samaṇaparisāya vā majjhe attano vādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā anuvādaṃ akkhāya ācikkhitvā thambhayitvā brūhayitvā dīpayitvā jotayitvā voharitvā pariggaṇhitvāti – akkhāya vādaṃ parisāya majjhe.
jotayitvā.translation_2: In the midst of an assembly of khattiyas, an assembly of brahmins, an assembly of householders, or an assembly of ascetics, having declared and announced his own doctrine, having declared and announced his secondary doctrine, having stiffened, having expanded, having made evident, having illuminated, having expressed, and having held forth—this is the meaning of “Having declared his doctrine in the midst of the assembly.”

paṭipurisaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, in a list of synonyms for an opponent. The Pali English Ultimate gives 'the man who is the opposite desire'.
paṭipurisaṃ.example_1: so gajjanto uggajjanto abhigajjanto eti upeti upagacchati paṭisūraṃ paṭipurisaṃ paṭisattuṃ paṭimallaṃ icchanto sādiyanto patthayanto pihayanto abhijappantoti—
paṭipurisaṃ.example_2: tesu arahantesu khīṇāsavesu kiṃ labhetho paṭisūraṃ paṭipurisaṃ paṭisattuṃ paṭimallanti—

paṭipuriso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text nominative singular, in a list of epithets for an opponent (paṭisūro paṭipuriso paṭisattu paṭimallo). The PEU gives the sense as 'a man who is the opposite desire'.
paṭipuriso.example_1: yeneva so diṭṭhigatiko tena palehi, tena vaja, tena gaccha, tena atikkama, so tuyhaṃ paṭisūro paṭipuriso paṭisattu paṭimalloti—
paṭipuriso.example_2: Yeneva so diṭṭhigatiko tena palehi, tena vaja, tena gaccha, tena atikkama, so tuyhaṃ paṭisūro paṭipuriso paṭisattu paṭimalloti – yeneva so tena palehi sūra.
paṭipuriso.translation_2: Where that one holding a view is, go there, proceed there, go there, advance there; that is your counter-hero, counter-man, counter-enemy, and counter-wrestler—this is the meaning of “Where he is, go there, hero.”

āveṭhiyāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa passage it occurs in the instrumental singular āveṭhiyāya, paired with nibbeṭhiyāya as a rhetorical 'turning around' and 'unravelling'. The related PEU entry gives āveṭhiya as ā + veṭha + ṇya.
āveṭhiyāya.example_1: te tvaṃ diṭṭhigatike vadassu vādena vādaṃ, niggahena niggahaṃ, paṭikammena paṭikammaṃ, visesena visesaṃ, paṭivisesena paṭivisesaṃ, āveṭhiyāya āveṭhiyaṃ, nibbeṭhiyāya nibbeṭhiyaṃ, chedena chedaṃ, maṇḍalena maṇḍalaṃ, te tuyhaṃ paṭisūrā paṭipurisā paṭisattū paṭimallāti—
āveṭhiyāya.example_2: Te tvaṃ diṭṭhigatike vadassu vādena vādaṃ, niggahena niggahaṃ, paṭikammena paṭikammaṃ, visesena visesaṃ, paṭivisesena paṭivisesaṃ, āveṭhiyāya āveṭhiyaṃ, nibbeṭhiyāya nibbeṭhiyaṃ, chedena chedaṃ, maṇḍalena maṇḍalaṃ, te tuyhaṃ paṭisūrā paṭipurisā paṭisattū paṭimallāti – te tvaṃ vadassū na hi tedha atthi.
āveṭhiyāya.translation_2: You should speak to those with such views with an argument, with a refutation, with a rejoinder, with a distinction, with a counter-distinction, with a turning-around, with an unraveling, with a cutting, with a circle; they are your opponents, your rivals, your enemies, your adversaries—this is what is meant by “You should speak to them—there is none here.”

nibbeṭhiyāya.meaning_2: unravelling; disentangling; a way of escape (from); solving
nibbeṭhiyāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Part of a list of debate tactics (āveṭhiyā, nibbeṭhiyā, cheda, maṇḍala); instrumental singular in the text, coordinated with āveṭhiyāya.
nibbeṭhiyāya.example_1: te tvaṃ diṭṭhigatike vadassu vādena vādaṃ, niggahena niggahaṃ, paṭikammena paṭikammaṃ, visesena visesaṃ, paṭivisesena paṭivisesaṃ, āveṭhiyāya āveṭhiyaṃ, nibbeṭhiyāya nibbeṭhiyaṃ, chedena chedaṃ, maṇḍalena maṇḍalaṃ, te tuyhaṃ paṭisūrā paṭipurisā paṭisattū paṭimallāti—
nibbeṭhiyāya.example_2: Te tvaṃ diṭṭhigatike vadassu vādena vādaṃ, niggahena niggahaṃ, paṭikammena paṭikammaṃ, visesena visesaṃ, paṭivisesena paṭivisesaṃ, āveṭhiyāya āveṭhiyaṃ, nibbeṭhiyāya nibbeṭhiyaṃ, chedena chedaṃ, maṇḍalena maṇḍalaṃ, te tuyhaṃ paṭisūrā paṭipurisā paṭisattū paṭimallāti – te tvaṃ vadassū na hi tedha atthi.
nibbeṭhiyāya.translation_2: You should speak to those with such views with an argument, with a refutation, with a rejoinder, with a distinction, with a counter-distinction, with a turning-around, with an unraveling, with a cutting, with a circle; they are your opponents, your rivals, your enemies, your adversaries—this is what is meant by “You should speak to them—there is none here.”

paṭipurisā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominal plural in the text, in a list of adversaries alongside paṭisūrā, paṭisattū and paṭimallā.
paṭipurisā.example_1: te tvaṃ diṭṭhigatike vadassu vādena vādaṃ, niggahena niggahaṃ, paṭikammena paṭikammaṃ, visesena visesaṃ, paṭivisesena paṭivisesaṃ, āveṭhiyāya āveṭhiyaṃ, nibbeṭhiyāya nibbeṭhiyaṃ, chedena chedaṃ, maṇḍalena maṇḍalaṃ, te tuyhaṃ paṭisūrā paṭipurisā paṭisattū paṭimallāti—
paṭipurisā.example_2: Te tvaṃ diṭṭhigatike vadassu vādena vādaṃ, niggahena niggahaṃ, paṭikammena paṭikammaṃ, visesena visesaṃ, paṭivisesena paṭivisesaṃ, āveṭhiyāya āveṭhiyaṃ, nibbeṭhiyāya nibbeṭhiyaṃ, chedena chedaṃ, maṇḍalena maṇḍalaṃ, te tuyhaṃ paṭisūrā paṭipurisā paṭisattū paṭimallāti – te tvaṃ vadassū na hi tedha atthi.
paṭipurisā.translation_2: You should speak to those with such views with an argument, with a refutation, with a rejoinder, with a distinction, with a counter-distinction, with a turning-around, with an unraveling, with a cutting, with a circle; they are your opponents, your rivals, your enemies, your adversaries—this is what is meant by “You should speak to them—there is none here.”

nābhinivisitabbāti.meaning_2: should not be insisted upon; should not be clung to (thus)
nābhinivisitabbāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + abhinivisitabbā + iti. Quotative particle iti is joined; the main word is a negative potential participle agreeing with a feminine noun. The ti in the text is the sandhi form of iti.
nābhinivisitabbāti.example_1: atha vā na gaṇhitabbā na parāmasitabbā nābhinivisitabbāti.

upasantiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is accusative singular, paired with santi and vūpasanti (santiṃ upasantiṃ vūpasantiṃ). From upa + santa, the past participle of upasammati; the PEU entry upasanta gives 'calmness'.
upasantiṃ.example_1: makkhassa … paḷāsassa … issāya … macchariyassa … māyāya … sāṭheyyassa … thambhassa … sārambhassa … mānassa … atimānassa … madassa … pamādassa … sabbakilesānaṃ … sabbaduccaritānaṃ … sabbadarathānaṃ … sabbapariḷāhānaṃ … sabbasantāpānaṃ … sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārānaṃ santiṃ upasantiṃ vūpasantiṃ nibbutiṃ paṭippassaddhiṃ kittayissāmi pakittayissāmi ācikkhissāmi desessāmi paññapessāmi paṭṭhapessāmi vivarissāmi vibhajissāmi uttānīkarissāmi pakāsissāmīti—
upasantiṃ.example_2: ajjhattasantiṃ ajjhattaṃ rāgassa santiṃ, dosassa santiṃ, mohassa santiṃ, kodhassa … upanāhassa … makkhassa … paḷāsassa … issāya … macchariyassa … māyāya … sāṭheyyassa … thambhassa … sārambhassa … mānassa … atimānassa … madassa … pamādassa … sabbakilesānaṃ … sabbaduccaritānaṃ … sabbadarathānaṃ … sabbapariḷāhānaṃ … sabbasantāpānaṃ … sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārānaṃ santiṃ upasantiṃ vūpasantiṃ nibbutiṃ paṭipassaddhiṃ santiṃ.

vūpasantiṃ.meaning_2: complete peace; appeasement; relief; calmed state
vūpasantiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, in a series with santiṃ, upasantiṃ, nibbutiṃ, paṭippassaddhiṃ. Sometimes written vūpasama; the reading here points to a feminine noun santi with the vi+upa prefix.
vūpasantiṃ.example_1: makkhassa … paḷāsassa … issāya … macchariyassa … māyāya … sāṭheyyassa … thambhassa … sārambhassa … mānassa … atimānassa … madassa … pamādassa … sabbakilesānaṃ … sabbaduccaritānaṃ … sabbadarathānaṃ … sabbapariḷāhānaṃ … sabbasantāpānaṃ … sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārānaṃ santiṃ upasantiṃ vūpasantiṃ nibbutiṃ paṭippassaddhiṃ kittayissāmi pakittayissāmi ācikkhissāmi desessāmi paññapessāmi paṭṭhapessāmi vivarissāmi vibhajissāmi uttānīkarissāmi pakāsissāmīti—
vūpasantiṃ.example_2: ajjhattasantiṃ ajjhattaṃ rāgassa santiṃ, dosassa santiṃ, mohassa santiṃ, kodhassa … upanāhassa … makkhassa … paḷāsassa … issāya … macchariyassa … māyāya … sāṭheyyassa … thambhassa … sārambhassa … mānassa … atimānassa … madassa … pamādassa … sabbakilesānaṃ … sabbaduccaritānaṃ … sabbadarathānaṃ … sabbapariḷāhānaṃ … sabbasantāpānaṃ … sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārānaṃ santiṃ upasantiṃ vūpasantiṃ nibbutiṃ paṭipassaddhiṃ santiṃ.

phassituṃ.meaning_2: to touch; to attain; to realize
phassituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive in a list of purpose infinitives (pāpuṇituṃ, adhigantuṃ, phassituṃ, sacchikātuṃ). From √phus 1 'touch'. The form is phassituṃ with assimilation; related to phassita.
phassituṃ.example_1: api ca sambhārā ime dhammā honti ajjhattasantiṃ pāpuṇituṃ adhigantuṃ phassituṃ sacchikātunti—
phassituṃ.example_2: Api ca sambhārā ime dhammā honti ajjhattasantiṃ pāpuṇituṃ adhigantuṃ phassituṃ sacchikātunti – adiṭṭhiyā assutiyā añāṇā asīlatā abbatā nopi tena.
phassituṃ.translation_2: But these phenomena are the requisites for reaching, acquiring, touching, and realizing internal serenity—thus ‘without view, without hearsay, without knowledge, without moral virtue, without vows, nor by that’.

paṭisaññojeyya.meaning_2: would connect; would engage in; would fasten upon
paṭisaññojeyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular; paṭi- + saṃ- + causative of √yuj. In the text it is coordinated with paṭibaleyya, kareyya etc., meaning 'would take up / engage in (a dispute)'.
paṭisaññojeyya.example_1: So kena mānena, kāya diṭṭhiyā, kena vā puggalena vādaṃ paṭisaññojeyya paṭibaleyya kalahaṃ kareyya bhaṇḍanaṃ kareyya viggahaṃ kareyya vivādaṃ kareyya medhagaṃ kareyya –
paṭisaññojeyya.translation_1: With what conceit, view, or person would he engage in disputes, join in, fight, quarrel, contend, dispute, or wrangle,

paṭibaleyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] MS variant paṭibale; related to paṭibala. Appears in a list of hostile acts; optative 3rd singular.
paṭibaleyya.example_1: so kena mānena, kāya diṭṭhiyā, kena vā puggalena vādaṃ paṭisaṃyojeyya paṭibaleyya kalahaṃ kareyya bhaṇḍanaṃ kareyya viggahaṃ kareyya vivādaṃ kareyya medhagaṃ kareyya—
paṭibaleyya.example_2: So kena mānena, kāya diṭṭhiyā, kena vā puggalena vādaṃ paṭisaññojeyya paṭibaleyya kalahaṃ kareyya bhaṇḍanaṃ kareyya viggahaṃ kareyya vivādaṃ kareyya medhagaṃ kareyya –
paṭibaleyya.translation_2: With what conceit, view, or person would he engage in disputes, join in, fight, quarrel, contend, dispute, or wrangle,

haliddakānī.meaning_2: Hāliddakāni; name of a householder (in the Niddesa)
haliddakānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name, declined as an a-stem (hapax-like); the spelling in the text is haliddakānī, a variant of hāliddakāni. Nominative singular in the sentence.
haliddakānī.example_1: Atha kho hāliddakāni [haliddakānī (sī.)] gahapati yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkami;
haliddakānī.translation_1: Then the householder Hāliddakāni approached the venerable Mahākaccāna;

leṭṭūhipi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental plural in the text, with the particle -pi: "with clods too". The spelling leḍḍū (variant leṭṭhū) occurs elsewhere; the form here is a variant.
leṭṭūhipi.example_1: Te tattha kalahaviggahavivādamāpannā aññamaññaṃ pāṇīhipi upakkamanti, leḍḍūhipi [leṭṭūhipi (ka.)] upakkamanti, daṇḍehipi upakkamanti, satthehipi upakkamanti.
leṭṭūhipi.translation_1: Having fallen into quarrels, disputes, and conflict there, they attack one another with their hands, they attack with clods, they attack with sticks, they attack with weapons.

hanusañcopano.meaning_2: movement of the jaw; grinding of the teeth
hanusañcopano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it appears as hanusañcopano, with a variant nasal (cf. the PEU's hanasuṃ copana). Nominative singular.
hanusañcopano.example_1: atthi kañci kālaṃ kodho mukhakulānavikulānamatto hoti, na ca tāva hanusañcopano hoti.

disāvidisānuvilokano.meaning_2: looking around in all directions; glancing in every direction
disāvidisānuvilokano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominalised compound functioning as a predicate nominative in the sentence; describes the stage of anger when one has not yet begun looking around.
disāvidisānuvilokano.example_1: atthi kañci kālaṃ kodho pharusavācaṃ nicchāraṇamatto hoti, na ca tāva disāvidisānuvilokano hoti.

daṇḍasatthaabhinipātano.meaning_2: striking with rod and sword; coming to blows with stick and weapon
daṇḍasatthaabhinipātano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text nominative singular describing the stage of anger. The printed form has a single b (daṇḍasatthaabhinipātano), which is likely a spelling for daṇḍasatthābhinipātano; sandhi of sattha + abhinipātana.
daṇḍasatthaabhinipātano.example_1: atthi kañci kālaṃ kodho daṇḍasatthaabbhukkiraṇamatto hoti, na ca tāva daṇḍasatthaabhinipātano hoti.

ghāṭetvā.meaning_2: having destroyed; having ruined; having killed; having brought to ruin
ghāṭetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of the causative ghāṭeti (to destroy, ruin, kill). In the text it describes anger destroying another person and oneself.
ghāṭetvā.example_1: yato kodho parapuggalaṃ ghāṭetvā attānaṃ ghāṭeti, ettāvatā kodho paramussadagato paramavepullappatto hoti.

ghāṭeti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of √ghaṭ 1 (strike, kill); the text contrasts the destruction of oneself (attānaṃ ghāṭeti) with that of others. 3rd singular present.
ghāṭeti.example_1: yato kodho parapuggalaṃ ghāṭetvā attānaṃ ghāṭeti, ettāvatā kodho paramussadagato paramavepullappatto hoti.

tāsī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Predicate adjective modifying a person in the Niddesa gloss (tāsī hoti). The PEU entry suggests derivation from tasa + ṇī; nominative singular in -ī.
tāsī.example_1: asantāsīti idhekacco tāsī hoti uttāsī parittāsī, so tasati uttasati parittasati bhāyati santāsaṃ āpajjati.
tāsī.example_2: Asantāsīti idhekacco tāsī hoti uttāsī parittāsī, so tasati na uttasati parittasati bhāyati santāsaṃ āpajjati.
tāsī.translation_2: “Fearless” refers to the case where a certain person here is prone to fear, prone to extreme fear, or prone to terror. He trembles, is extremely agitated, and becomes terrified, falling into states of panic and terror.

korañjikakorañjiko.meaning_2: with a (horn-shaped) contraction (of the body); with a hunched posture
korañjikakorañjiko.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in the reduplicated compound korañjikakorañjiko (in some editions korajikakorajiko), describing a recluse whose limbs are drawn in like a horn (korañja = a kind of horned bird/fish?). Related to bhākuṭika (frowning). Nominative singular.
korañjikakorañjiko.example_1: Atha vā korajikakorajiko [korañjikakorañjiko (sī.)] bhākuṭikabhākuṭiko kuhakakuhako lapakalapako mukhasambhāviko,‘‘ ayaṃ samaṇo imāsaṃ evarūpānaṃ santānaṃ vihārasamāpattīnaṃ lābhī ’’ ti tādisaṃ gambhīraṃ gūḷhaṃ nipuṇaṃ paṭicchannaṃ lokuttaraṃ suññatāpaṭisaṃyuttaṃ kathaṃ kathesi.
korañjikakorañjiko.translation_1: Or, he speaks about deep, hidden, subtle, secret, supramundane, and void-related teachings, thinking, ‘This recluse is a recipient of such abidings and attainments,’ while being extremely contracting, having a habit of excessive frowning, causing extreme wonder, speaking excessively, and being honored through his own mouth.

labilaṃ.meaning_2: one of the six tastes; astringent?; acid?; sour?
labilaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Only occurs in the list of tastes (rasa) in Niddesa prose, where the editions differ: lambikaṃ (sī., syā.), lapilaṃ (sī.), labilaṃ (ka.). The text reading labilaṃ is probably a variant of lambikaṃ. The exact taste in the list of six (sour, sweet, bitter, pungent, salty, alkaline) is uncertain; some take it as astringent (kasāva is also listed after it).
labilaṃ.example_1: Rasoti mūlaraso khandharaso tacaraso pattaraso puppharaso phalaraso, ambilaṃ madhuraṃ tittakaṃ kaṭukaṃ loṇikaṃ khārikaṃ lambikaṃ [lapilaṃ (sī.), lambilaṃ (syā.), labilaṃ (ka.), āyatanavibhaṅge] kasāvo sādu asādu sītaṃ uṇhaṃ.
labilaṃ.translation_1: “Taste” means taste of roots, taste of trunks, taste of bark, taste of leaves, taste of flowers, taste of fruit, sour, sweet, bitter, pungent, salty, alkaline, lambika, astringent, tasty, not tasty, cool, and hot.

itonidānāti.meaning_2: having this as cause; originating from this; with this as source
itonidānāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form in the text is itonidānāti = itonidānā + iti; the -ti is the quotation particle and is not part of the word. Used in the Nikāyas and Niddesa in the phrase itonidānā dukkhā, 'suffering having this as cause'.

sadveḷhako.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] sandhi of saha + dveḷhaka; bahubbīhi compound describing an uncertain person; masculine nominative singular in the text
sadveḷhako.example_1: kathaṅkathī puggalo sakaṅkho savilekho sadveḷhako savicikiccho, ñāṇādhigamāya ñāṇaphusanāya ñāṇasacchikiriyāya adhisīlampi sikkheyya, adhicittampi sikkheyya, adhipaññampi sikkheyya;
sadveḷhako.example_2: Kathaṃkathī puggalo sakaṅkho savilekho sadveḷhako savicikiccho, ñāṇādhigamāya ñāṇaphusanāya ñāṇasacchikiriyāya adhisīlampi sikkheyya, adhicittampi sikkheyya, adhipaññampi sikkheyya;
sadveḷhako.translation_2: A perplexed person, who is doubtful, full of mental agitation, of two minds, full of uncertainty, should train in heightened virtue, in heightened mind, and in heightened discernment for the attainment of knowledge, for the realization of knowledge, for the actual realization of knowledge;

yaṃjātikaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yaṃ + jātikaṃ, in a list of parallel phrases (yaṃnidānaṃ, yaṃsamudayaṃ, yaṃpabhavanti). Accusative singular agreeing with the neuter subject.
yaṃjātikaṃ.example_2: Yatonidānanti yaṃnidānaṃ yaṃsamudayaṃ yaṃjātikaṃ yaṃpabhavanti – etaṃ me pabrūhi yatonidānaṃ.
yaṃjātikaṃ.translation_2: ‘What its source is’ (yatonidānaṃ)—that is, what is its source, what is its origin, what is its nature, what is its foundation. This is the meaning of the phrase ‘Explain to me what its source is.’

yaṃpabhavanti.meaning_2: from which they arise; whatever they originate from
yaṃpabhavanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yaṃ (relative pronoun, neuter accusative) + pabhavanti (present 3rd plural of pabhavati, 'to arise from, originate'). Part of a stock Niddesa gloss explaining yatonidānaṃ: 'whatever is its source, its origin, its nature, from which they arise'.
yaṃpabhavanti.example_2: Yatonidānanti yaṃnidānaṃ yaṃsamudayaṃ yaṃjātikaṃ yaṃpabhavanti – etaṃ me pabrūhi yatonidānaṃ.
yaṃpabhavanti.translation_2: ‘What its source is’ (yatonidānaṃ)—that is, what is its source, what is its origin, what is its nature, what is its foundation. This is the meaning of the phrase ‘Explain to me what its source is.’

vibhavite.meaning_2: destroyed; annihilated; brought to an end; passed away
vibhavite.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle of vibhavati, used in a string of synonyms (vibhūta, vibhavita, atikkanta) describing the cessation or passing away of something. Locative singular in the text.
vibhavite.example_1: kismiṃ vibhūte vibhavite atikkante samatikkante vītivatte phassā na phusantīti—
vibhavite.example_2: Kismiṃ vibhūte vibhavite atikkante samatikkante vītivatte phassā na phusantīti – kismiṃ vibhūte na phusanti phassā.
vibhavite.translation_2: When what has vanished, has passed away, has been transcended, has been completely transcended, has moved on—do contacts not touch? This is the meaning of the phrase ‘When what has vanished do contacts not touch?’

asantyā.meaning_2: not existing; non-existent; unmanifest; not present
asantyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Negative of santa (present participle of √as). Feminine instrumental singular asantyā in the text, agreeing with icchāya. Sometimes interpreted as a contraction of icchāya asantyā.
asantyā.example_1: icchāya asantyā asaṃvijjamānāya natthi anupalabbhamānāya mamattā natthi na santi na saṃvijjanti nupalabbhanti, pahīnā samucchinnā vūpasantā paṭipassaddhā abhabbuppattikā ñāṇagginā daḍḍhāti—
asantyā.example_2: Icchāya asantyā asaṃvijjamānāya natthi anupalabbhamānāya mamattā natthi na santi na saṃvijjanti nupalabbhanti, pahīnā samucchinnā vūpasantā paṭipassaddhā abhabbuppattikā ñāṇagginā daḍḍhāti – icchāyasantyā na mamattamatthi.
asantyā.translation_2: When craving is stilled, non-existent, not obtained, mine-making does not exist, is not found, is not present, is not attained, is abandoned, eradicated, stilled, calmed, has become incapable of arising, burned by the fire of knowledge—thus, when craving is stilled, there is no mine-making.

atikkamiyyati.meaning_2: is passed; is surpassed; is overcome; is transcended
atikkamiyyati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive of atikkamati; variant reading atikkamiyyati (= atikkamīyati) given in the text. Present indicative 3rd singular, passive.
atikkamiyyati.example_1: Kathaṃ sametassāti kathaṃ sametassa kathaṃ paṭipannassa kathaṃ iriyantassa kathaṃ vattentassa kathaṃ pālentassa kathaṃ yapentassa kathaṃ yāpentassa rūpaṃ vibhoti vibhāvīyati atikkamīyati samatikkamīyati [vibhāviyyati atikkamiyyati samatikkamiyyati (bahūsu)] vītivattīyatīti – kathaṃ sametassa vibhoti rūpaṃ.
atikkamiyyati.translation_1: ‘How for one who has entered upon’: How for one who has practiced in this way, how for one who has entered upon, how for one observing their bodily postures, how for one who regulates them, how for one who guards them, how for one who sustains them, how for one who is sustained—does form vanish, is it exterminated, is it surpassed, is it transcended, is it passed over? This is the meaning of the phrase ‘How for one who has entered upon does form vanish?’

topaccayantavasena.meaning_2: by way of the -to suffix ending; by means of the -to verbal termination
topaccayantavasena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in Sinhalese and Thai editions of the Niddesa gloss (masc. bālato etc.); paccayanta = 'ending in a suffix/affix', here the -to termination. A bahubbīhi in the instrumental, used adverbially as a gloss on the ablative-like -to forms.
topaccayantavasena.example_1: te aññamaññaṃ bālo [bālato (sī. ka.) evamaññesu chappadesupi topaccayantavasena] hīno nihīno omako lāmako chatukko parittoti, evamāhaṃsu evaṃ kathenti evaṃ bhaṇanti evaṃ dīpayanti evaṃ voharantīti – yamāhu bālā mithu aññamaññaṃ.
topaccayantavasena.translation_1: They say, express, state, preach, and declare to each other that the other is a fool, inferior, low, stunted, wretched, stunted-by-birth, or small—this is what is meant by ‘That which fools call ‘fool’ to each other.’

nānāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text nānāni is an adjective agreeing with saccāni (nominative plural neuter), glossed nānāni vividhāni aññoññāni. Variant reading nānā (ka.) in sentence 3.
nānāni.example_1: saccāni sutāni bahūni nānāti saccāni sutāni bahukāni nānāni vividhāni aññoññāni puthūnīti—
nānāni.example_2: na heva saccāni bahūni nānāti na heva saccāni bahukāni nānāni vividhāni aññoññāni puthūnīti—

takkayitvā.meaning_2: having thought; having reasoned; having considered; having pondered
takkayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -itvā from the causative-denominative takketi. In the text it is the first of three absolutives (takkayitvā vitakkayitvā saṅkappayitvā) describing the formation of views.
takkayitvā.example_1: takkaṃ vitakkaṃ saṅkappaṃ takkayitvā vitakkayitvā saṅkappayitvā diṭṭhigatāni janenti sañjanenti nibbattenti abhinibbattenti.

vitakkayitvā.meaning_2: having thought; having pondered; having reasoned (about)
vitakkayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is grouped with takkayitvā and saṅkappayitvā; causative/denominative form built on takka. The readings vitakketvā / vitakkayitvā alternate.
vitakkayitvā.example_1: takkaṃ vitakkaṃ saṅkappaṃ takkayitvā vitakkayitvā saṅkappayitvā diṭṭhigatāni janenti sañjanenti nibbattenti abhinibbattenti.

saṅkappayitvā.meaning_2: having intended; having thought out; having formed a concept
saṅkappayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in a series with takkayitvā and vitakkayitvā; causative of √kapp 2. The PEU split saṃ + kappa + ṇaya + tvā suggests the same analysis.
saṅkappayitvā.example_1: takkaṃ vitakkaṃ saṅkappaṃ takkayitvā vitakkayitvā saṅkappayitvā diṭṭhigatāni janenti sañjanenti nibbattenti abhinibbattenti.

abhinibbattetvā.meaning_2: produces; brings forth; generates; gives rise to
abhinibbattetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of abhinibbatteti (causative of abhinibbattati, from √vatt). Used in a series with janetvā, sañjanetvā, nibbattetvā to describe the arising of wrong views (diṭṭhigatāni). Some editions read abhinibbattetvā.
abhinibbattetvā.example_1: diṭṭhigatāni janetvā sañjanetvā nibbattetvā abhinibbattetvā “mayhaṃ saccaṃ tuyhaṃ musā”ti, evamāhaṃsu evaṃ kathenti evaṃ bhaṇanti evaṃ dīpayanti evaṃ voharantīti—
abhinibbattetvā.example_2: Diṭṭhigatāni janetvā sañjanetvā nibbattetvā abhinibbattetvā ‘‘ mayhaṃ saccaṃ tuyhaṃ musā ’’ ti, evamāhaṃsu evaṃ kathenti evaṃ bhaṇanti evaṃ dīpayanti evaṃ voharantīti – takkañca diṭṭhīsu pakappayitvā saccaṃ musāti dvayadhammamāhu.
abhinibbattetvā.translation_2: Having generated, given rise to, brought forth, and produced views, they say thus, they speak thus, they declare thus, they proclaim thus, and they describe thus: ‘My statement is true, yours is false.’ That is the meaning of ‘having generated conjectures in their views, they proclaim a dual standard.’

paminitvāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of pamāti, formed from √mā. The form paminitvāti is paminitvā (absolutive) + iti; the entry is for the verb. Absolutive in the text.
paminitvāti.example_1: ayaṃ maggo niyyāniko”ti sayaṃ pamāya paminitvāti—
paminitvāti.example_2: ‘‘ Ayaṃ satthā sabbaññū ’’ ti sayaṃ pamāya paminitvā,‘‘ ayaṃ dhammo svākkhāto … ayaṃ gaṇo suppaṭipanno … ayaṃ diṭṭhi bhaddikā … ayaṃ paṭipadā supaññattā … ayaṃ maggo niyyāniko ’’ ti sayaṃ pamāya paminitvāti – vinicchaye ṭhatvā sayaṃ pamāya.
paminitvāti.translation_2: Thinking ‘This teacher is omniscient,’ having measured and assessed it himself; ‘This Dhamma is well proclaimed... this community is practicing the good way... this view is excellent... this practice is well-enacted... this path leads out’—having measured and assessed it himself—this is standing on judgments, having measured it himself.

ugghātinigghāti.meaning_2: oppression and non-oppression; crushing and not crushing; exaltation and humiliation
ugghātinigghāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ugghāti (removal; crushing; exaltation) and nigghāti (non-removal; non-crushing). Part of a list of paired opposites in the Diṭṭhikathā of the Niddesa; nominative singular.
ugghātinigghāti.example_1: jayaparājayo hoti, lābhālābho hoti, yasāyaso hoti, nindāpasaṃso hoti, sukhadukkhaṃ hoti, somanassadomanassaṃ hoti, iṭṭhāniṭṭhaṃ hoti, anunayapaṭighaṃ hoti, ugghātinigghāti hoti, anurodhavirodho hoti.
ugghātinigghāti.example_2: Diṭṭhikalahassa diṭṭhibhaṇḍanassa diṭṭhiviggahassa diṭṭhivivādassa diṭṭhimedhagassa dve phalāni honti – jayaparājayo hoti, lābhālābho hoti, yasāyaso hoti, nindāpasaṃso hoti, sukhadukkhaṃ hoti, somanassadomanassaṃ hoti, iṭṭhāniṭṭhaṃ hoti, anunayapaṭighaṃ hoti, ugghātinigghāti hoti, anurodhavirodho hoti.
ugghātinigghāti.translation_2: There are two results of the dispute of view, the quarrel of view, the conflict of view, the altercation of view, the altercation of view—victory and defeat, gain and loss, fame and disrepute, blame and praise, pleasure and pain, joy and sadness, desirable and undesirable, attraction and aversion, oppression and non-oppression, compliance and contradiction.

parivisuddhiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, in a list with suddhi, visuddhi, mutti, vimutti, parivimutti.
parivisuddhiṃ.example_1: te sīlamattena saññamamattena saṃvaramattena avītikkamamattena suddhiṃ visuddhiṃ parivisuddhiṃ, muttiṃ vimuttiṃ parivimuttiṃ āhaṃsu vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharanti.
parivisuddhiṃ.example_2: te sīlamattena saññamamattena saṃvaramattena avītikkamamattena suddhiṃ visuddhiṃ parivisuddhiṃ, muttiṃ vimuttiṃ parivimuttiṃ āhu [āhaṃsu (sī. ka.)] vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharanti.
parivisuddhiṃ.translation_2: They speak of, declare, proclaim, preach, and treat purity, clarification, perfect purity, release, freedom, and total freedom as consisting merely of morality, restraint, discipline, and non-transgression.

parivimuttiṃ.meaning_2: complete liberation; total freedom; perfect release
parivimuttiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, in a list with suddhi, visuddhi, mutti, vimutti, all objects of āhu. The prefix pari- intensifies vimutti.
parivimuttiṃ.example_1: te sīlamattena saññamamattena saṃvaramattena avītikkamamattena suddhiṃ visuddhiṃ parivisuddhiṃ, muttiṃ vimuttiṃ parivimuttiṃ āhaṃsu vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharanti.
parivimuttiṃ.example_2: te sīlamattena saññamamattena saṃvaramattena avītikkamamattena suddhiṃ visuddhiṃ parivisuddhiṃ, muttiṃ vimuttiṃ parivimuttiṃ āhu [āhaṃsu (sī. ka.)] vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharanti.
parivimuttiṃ.translation_2: They speak of, declare, proclaim, preach, and treat purity, clarification, perfect purity, release, freedom, and total freedom as consisting merely of morality, restraint, discipline, and non-transgression.

parivicchindanāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text (parivicchindanāya). Abstract noun from parivicchindati; the sentence's sense is doubtful.
parivicchindanāya.translation_1: Thus one falls due to being cut off by others.

vuddhipārihāniṃ.meaning_2: growth and decline; increase and decrease; rise and fall
vuddhipārihāniṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in the phrase vuddhipārihāniṃ vītivatto, meaning one who has overcome growth and decline. The main reading has the compound vuddhipārihānivītivatto, with the variant reading vuddhipārihāniṃ vītivatto. The word vuddhi is from √vaddh. DPD has not yet recorded an entry for pārihāni.
vuddhipārihāniṃ.translation_1: The Arahant has transcended longing; they have evolved past growth and decline.

panā.meaning_2: but; however; moreover; further; and; now
panā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written panā before tatheva (metrical lengthening / sandhi). A particle, not a compound; the reading is saddhammapūjāpi pana tatheva. Also functions as an emphatic connective.
panā.example_1: 141. Saddhammapūjāpi [saddhammapūjā ca (sī. syā.)] panā tatheva , yathā pasaṃsanti sakāyanāni ;
panā.translation_1: 141. “Reverence for the true Dhamma occurs in the same way as they praise their own path;
panā.translation_2: “Reverence for the true Dhamma occurs in the same way”:

tathi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tathiyā with following bhaveyyuṃ in the text; alternative analysis tathi + vā (locative plural of tatha) is also given by the commentary tradition.
tathi.example_1: Sabbeva vādā [sabbe pavādā (syā.)] tathiyā [tathi vā (bahūsu)] bhaveyyuṃ , suddhī hi nesaṃ paccattameva .
tathi.translation_1: If all doctrines were true, their purity would only be personal.”

dubbinayo.meaning_2: difficult to discipline; hard to guide; difficult to admonish
dubbinayo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes a nivissavādī (dogmatist). Nominative singular in the text; du- here is the prefix 'difficult, bad'.
dubbinayo.example_1: nivissavādī dubbinayo duppaññāpayo dunnijjhāpayo duppekkhāpayo duppasādayoti—
dubbinayo.example_2: Nivissavādī dubbinayo duppaññāpayo [duppaññāpiyo (sī.) evamīdisesu ṭhānesu] dunnijjhāpayo duppekkhāpayo duppasādayoti – nivissavādī na hi subbināyo.
dubbinayo.translation_2: A dogmatist is difficult to guide, difficult to enlighten, difficult to make ponder, difficult to make see, and difficult to make confident—this is “a dogmatist is certainly not easily taught.”

ānissito.meaning_2: leaning on; relying on; clinging to; attached to
ānissito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is a past participle meaning 'leaned on; relied on', used as a synonym of nissito, allīno, upagato, ajjhosito. The initial ā- is the prefix ā (towards); some analyses take the form as ā + nissita rather than with ni-.
ānissito.example_1: yaṃ nissitoti yaṃ satthāraṃ dhammakkhānaṃ gaṇaṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭipadaṃ maggaṃ nissito ānissito allīno upagato ajjhosito adhimuttoti—
ānissito.example_2: Yaṃ nissitoti yaṃ satthāraṃ dhammakkhānaṃ gaṇaṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭipadaṃ maggaṃ nissito ānissito allīno upagato ajjhosito adhimuttoti – yaṃ nissito.
ānissito.translation_2: “Whatever he clings to” means the teacher, the doctrinal statement, the group, the view, the practice, or the path he relies on, leans on, resorts to, draws near to, is attached to, and is devoted to.

vibaddhe.meaning_2: bound fast; entangled; tied up; fastened
vibaddhe.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text. vi + baddha (pp of bandhati); literally 'bound in various ways'. Part of a list of synonyms for 'bound'.
vibaddhe.example_1: Atha vā ganthe gadhite ganthite [gathite gaṇṭhite (bahūsu) suddhaṭṭhakasutte sattamagāthāvaṇṇanā oloketabbā] bandhe vibandhe ābandhe [baddhe vibaddhe ābaddhe (sī.)] lagge laggite palibuddhe bandhane phoṭayitvā vissajja.
vibaddhe.translation_1: Or, having broken and discarded the knots that are connected, knotted, bound, bound in particular, bound in special ways, attached, clinging, and hindered with bindings.

ninahātapāpakanti.meaning_2: with evil washed away; whose wickedness is cleansed
ninahātapāpakanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternate form ninahātapāpaka; the text reads ninahātapāpakanti (sandhi of -pāpakaṃ + iti). The word appears in a quotation describing the muni as having washed away evil.
ninahātapāpakanti.translation_1: The sage possessing perfection, they call cleansed of evil.”

santiphusanāya.meaning_2: touching peace; attainment of peace; experiencing of peace
santiphusanāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Dative singular in the text. Part of a triplet with santādhigama and santisacchikiriyā, meaning the realisation of Nibbāna.
santiphusanāya.example_1: athāparenākārena ye dhammā santādhigamāya santiphusanāya santisacchikiriyāya saṃvattanti, seyyathidaṃ—
santiphusanāya.example_2: atha aparena ākārena ye dhammā santādhigamāya santiphusanāya santisacchikiriyāya saṃvattanti, seyyathidaṃ—
