abbhuhanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of abbūhanaṃ (Sī. Syā.) in the dogmatic passage on the Buddha's qualities; accusative singular in the text, object of esī. The prefix form is doubtful (abhi + ud + √vah or abhi + ava + √hā are also possible analyses).
abbhuhanaṃ.example_1: mahato tamokāyassa padālanaṃ, mahato vipallāsassa bhedanaṃ, mahato taṇhāsallassa abbahanaṃ [abbūhanaṃ (sī. syā.), abbhuhanaṃ (ka.)], mahato diṭṭhisaṅghātassa viniveṭhanaṃ, mahato mānadhajassa papātanaṃ [pavāhanaṃ (syā.)], mahato abhisaṅkhārassa vūpasamaṃ, mahato oghassa nittharaṇaṃ, mahato bhārassa nikkhepanaṃ, mahato saṃsāravaṭṭassa upacchedaṃ, mahato santāpassa nibbāpanaṃ, mahato pariḷāhassa paṭipassaddhiṃ, mahato dhammadhajassa ussāpanaṃ esī gavesī pariyesīti mahesi, mahante satipaṭṭhāne mahante sammappadhāne mahante iddhipāde mahantāni indriyāni mahantāni balāni mahante bojjhaṅge mahantaṃ ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ mahantaṃ paramatthaṃ amataṃ nibbānaṃ esī gavesī pariyesīti mahesi;
abbhuhanaṃ.translation_1: he is a Great Seer because he has searched for, sought, and pursued the destruction of the mass of darkness, the breaking of the perversions, the extraction of the dart of craving, the untying of the knot of views, the toppling of the banner of conceit, the appeasement of the volitional activities, the crossing of the flood, the dropping of the burden, the cutting off of the cycle of rebirth, the quenching of the burning, the subsiding of the fever, and the raising of the banner of the Dhamma; he is a Great Seer because he has searched for, sought, and pursued the great establishments of mindfulness, the great right strivings, the great bases for psychic potency, the great faculties, the great powers, the great factors of enlightenment, the great noble eightfold path, and the great ultimate meaning, the deathless Nibbāna;

agaṇhayamāno.meaning_2: not grasping; not seizing; not taking hold (of)
agaṇhayamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle of the negative verb na gaṇhāti (root √gah with the ṇhā sign). Nominative singular masculine in the text, in a list of synonyms for non-attachment alongside anupādiyamāna, aparāmasamāna and anabhinivisamāna.
agaṇhayamāno.example_1: catūhi upādānehi anupādiyamāno agaṇhayamāno aparāmasamāno anabhinivisamāno.

parikittayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Third singular aorist of parikittayati (causative of parikitteti); glossed in the text by akittayi, ācikkhi, desesi, etc.
parikittayi.example_1: akittayīti akittayi parikittayi ācikkhi desesi paññapesi paṭṭhapesi vivari vibhaji uttānimakāsi pakāsesīti akittayi.
parikittayi.example_2: Akittayīti kittitaṃ ācikkhitaṃ desitaṃ paññapitaṃ paṭṭhapitaṃ vivaṭaṃ vibhattaṃ uttānīkataṃ pakāsitanti – akittayi [akittayīti akittayi parikittayi ācikkhi desesi paññapesi paṭṭhapesi vivari vibhaji uttānimakāsi pakāsesīti akittayi (syā.)].
parikittayi.translation_2: “He declared” means it was praised, told, taught, prepared, established, opened, divided, made clear, and proclaimed.

cakkhuloliyaṃ.meaning_2: greediness of the eyes; unsteadiness of the eye; longing for visual stimulation
cakkhuloliyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Used in Niddesa prose as an object of pajaheyya; ablative cakkhuloliyā in the same passage. Related PEU entry takes it as cakkhu + loliya, 'unsteadiness of the eye'.
cakkhuloliyaṃ.example_1: cakkhuloliyaṃ pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyya, cakkhuloliyā ārato assa virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā vihareyyāti—
cakkhuloliyaṃ.example_2: Cakkhuloliyaṃ pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyya, cakkhuloliyā ārato assa virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā vihareyyāti – cakkhūhi neva lolassa.
cakkhuloliyaṃ.translation_2: One should abandon, dispel, put an end to, and make non-existent greed for the eyes; one should be desisted, abstinent, and having turned away from greed for the eyes; one should dwell having emerged, escaped, liberated, detached, and disconnected [from it] with a mind that has no limits—this is “with the eyes, one should not be greedy.”

cakkhuloliyā.meaning_2: greediness of the eyes; unsteadiness of the eye; covetousness with regard to the eyes
cakkhuloliyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound of cakkhu and loliya. In the text it occurs in the accusative singular (cakkhuloliyaṃ) and the ablative singular (cakkhuloliyā). Related to the description of 'cakkhūhi neva lolassa'.
cakkhuloliyā.example_1: cakkhuloliyaṃ pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyya, cakkhuloliyā ārato assa virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā vihareyyāti—
cakkhuloliyā.example_2: Cakkhuloliyaṃ pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyya, cakkhuloliyā ārato assa virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā vihareyyāti – cakkhūhi neva lolassa.
cakkhuloliyā.translation_2: One should abandon, dispel, put an end to, and make non-existent greed for the eyes; one should be desisted, abstinent, and having turned away from greed for the eyes; one should dwell having emerged, escaped, liberated, detached, and disconnected [from it] with a mind that has no limits—this is “with the eyes, one should not be greedy.”

suṃsukābhayaṃ.meaning_2: fear of fierce fish; danger from suṃsuka fish
suṃsukābhayaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of susukābhaya in a list of fears. Part of the compound suṃsukābhayaṃ in the text; accusative singular.
suṃsukābhayaṃ.example_1: Athāparena ākārena bhayaṃ vuccati ajjhattikaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ bhayaṃ bhayānakaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso cetaso ubbego utrāso, jātibhayaṃ jarābhayaṃ byādhibhayaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ rājabhayaṃ corabhayaṃ aggibhayaṃ udakabhayaṃ attānuvādabhayaṃ parānuvādabhayaṃ daṇḍabhayaṃ duggatibhayaṃ ūmibhayaṃ kumbhīlabhayaṃ āvaṭṭabhayaṃ susukābhayaṃ [suṃsukābhayaṃ (syā.)] ājīvikabhayaṃ asilokabhayaṃ parisāya sārajjabhayaṃ madanabhayaṃ duggatibhayaṃ bhayaṃ bhayānakaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso cetaso ubbego utrāso.
suṃsukābhayaṃ.translation_1: From another angle, fear is described as fear originating in the mind: fear as terror, as trembling, as hair-raising, as mental agitation, as terror, fear of birth, fear of old age, fear of illness, fear of death, fear of kings, fear of bandits, fear of fire, fear of floods, fear of self-reproach, fear of reproach by others, fear of punishment, fear of bad destinations, fear of waves, fear of crocodiles, fear of whirlpools, fear of fierce fish, fear of one’s livelihood, fear of ill-repute, fear of timidity in an assembly, fear of madness, fear of a bad destination, fear as terror, as trembling, as hair-raising, as mental agitation, as terror.

pāribhaṭayayatāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text, in a list of improper ways of obtaining requisites. The form is uncertain; possibly a corruption of pāribhaṭṭhatā or pāribhaṭayatā.
pāribhaṭayayatāya.example_1: Laddhāti laddhā labhitvā adhigantvā vinditvā paṭilabhitvā na kuhanāya, na lapanāya, na nemittikatāya, na nippesikatāya, na lābhena lābhaṃ nijigīsanatāya [nijigiṃsanatāya (sī. syā.)], na kaṭṭhadānena, na veḷudānena, na pattadānena, na pupphadānena, na phaladānena, na sinānadānena, na cuṇṇadānena, na mattikādānena, na dantakaṭṭhadānena, na mukhodakadānena, na cāṭukamyatāya, na muggasūpyatāya [na muggasuppatāya (sī.), na muggasūpatāya (syā.)], na pāribhaṭayayatāya, na pīṭhamaddikatāya [piṭṭhimaṃsikatāya (sī.), piṭṭhimaddikatāya (ka.)], na vatthuvijjāya, na tiracchānavijjāya, na aṅgavijjāya, na nakkhattavijjāya, na dūtagamanena, na pahiṇagamanena, na jaṅghapesaniyena, na vejjakammena, na navakammena, na piṇḍapaṭipiṇḍakena, na dānānuppadānena dhammena samena laddhā labhitvā adhigantvā vinditvā paṭilabhitvāti – laddhā.
pāribhaṭayayatāya.translation_1: Having obtained means having received, attained, experienced, [and] acquired in accordance with the law; not by deceit, not by wheedling, not by hint, not by belittling, not by seeking gain through gain, not by giving wood, not by giving bamboo, not by giving leaves, not by giving flowers, not by giving fruit, not by giving bath-powder, not by giving powder, not by giving clay, not by giving tooth-sticks, not by giving face-washing water, not by fawning, not by mung-bean soup behavior, not by fawning behavior, not by stool-cushion behavior, not by astrology, not by animal-knowledge, not by body-knowledge, not by constellation-knowledge, not by acting as a messenger, not by the going of one who is sent, not by running errands, not by the work of a physician, not by new construction, not by giving alms in return, not by giving back gifts — having obtained, attained, experienced, [and] acquired in accordance with the law — this is 'having obtained'.

pādaloliyena.meaning_2: restlessness of feet; footlooseness; wandering about
pādaloliyena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun formed from pādalola. In the text it appears in the instrumental singular: 'pādaloliyena samannāgato hoti' = 'possessed of footlooseness'. Some analyses may treat it as adj agreeing with bhikkhu, but the neuter abstract noun fits best.
pādaloliyena.example_1: idhekacco bhikkhu pādalolo pādaloliyena samannāgato hoti—
pādaloliyena.example_2: atha vā bhikkhu antosaṅghārāme pādalolo pādaloliyena samannāgato hoti, na atthahetu na kāraṇahetu uddhato avūpasantacitto pariveṇato pariveṇaṃ gacchati, vihārato vihāraṃ gacchati, aḍḍhayogato aḍḍhayogaṃ gacchati, pāsādato pāsādaṃ gacchati, hammiyato hammiyaṃ gacchati, guhato guhaṃ gacchati, leṇato leṇaṃ gacchati, kuṭiyā kuṭiṃ gacchati, kūṭāgārato kūṭāgāraṃ gacchati, aṭṭato aṭṭaṃ gacchati, māḷato māḷaṃ gacchati, uddaṇḍato uddaṇḍaṃ gacchati, upaṭṭhānasālato upaṭṭhānasālaṃ gacchati, maṇḍapato maṇḍapaṃ gacchati, rukkhamūlato rukkhamūlaṃ gacchati, yattha vā pana bhikkhū nisīdanti vā gacchanti vā, tattha ekassa vā dutiyo hoti, dvinnaṃ vā tatiyo hoti, tiṇṇaṃ vā catuttho hoti.

pādaloliyaṃ.meaning_2: restlessness of the feet; fidgeting with the feet; foot-restlessness
pādaloliyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun from pādalola (unstable on the feet). Accusative singular in the text, object of pajaheyya. Also occurs in the ablative pādaloliyā.
pādaloliyaṃ.example_1: pādaloliyaṃ pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyya, pādaloliyā ārato assa virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā vihareyya careyya vicareyya iriyeyya vatteyya pāleyya yapeyya yāpeyya, paṭisallānārāmo assa paṭisallānarato ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ jhāyī jhānarato ekattamanuyutto paramatthagarukoti—
pādaloliyaṃ.example_2: pādaloliyaṃ pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyya, pādaloliyā ārato assa virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā vihareyya, paṭisallānārāmo assa paṭisallānarato ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgāraṃ jhāyī jhānarato ekattamanuyutto sadatthagarukoti—

pādaloliyā.meaning_2: unsteadiness of the feet; restlessness of the feet; wandering about
pādaloliyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] pāda + lola + suffix ṇiya (see PEU), hence nt abstract noun. The form pādaloliyā in the text is ablative singular, 'away from restlessness of the feet', parallel to ārato. The compound pādalola occurs in the quoted phrase na ca pādalolo. Some analyses take pādaloliyā as fem.
pādaloliyā.example_1: na ca pādaloloti so paccekasambuddho pādaloliyā ārato virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā paṭisallānārāmo hoti paṭisallānarato ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgāraṃ jhāyī jhānarato ekattamanuyutto sadatthagarukoti—
pādaloliyā.example_2: pādaloliyaṃ pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyya, pādaloliyā ārato assa virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā vihareyya careyya vicareyya iriyeyya vatteyya pāleyya yapeyya yāpeyya, paṭisallānārāmo assa paṭisallānarato ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ jhāyī jhānarato ekattamanuyutto paramatthagarukoti—

dhurasampaggaho.meaning_2: grasping the yoke; undertaking the burden; taking up the task
dhurasampaggaho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text part of a list of terms for effort (vīriya), nominative singular. Likely a compound of dhura (yoke; burden) + sampaggaha (grasping, taking up).
dhurasampaggaho.example_1: yo cetasiko vīriyārambho nikkamo parakkamo uyyāmo vāyāmo ussāho ussoḷhī thāmo ṭhiti asithilaparakkamatā anikkhittacchandatā anikkhittadhuratā dhurasampaggaho vīriyaṃ vīriyindriyaṃ vīriyabalaṃ sammāvāyāmo.

parikeḷanā.meaning_2: play; amusement; dalliance; fondness for adornment
parikeḷanā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa list of a monastic's vain adornments, following keḷanā; the variant gedhitatā/gedhitattaṃ appears in some editions. Nominative singular in the text.
parikeḷanā.example_1: cīvaramaṇḍanā pattamaṇḍanā senāsanamaṇḍanā imassa vā pūtikāyassa bāhirānaṃ vā parikkhārānaṃ maṇḍanā vibhūsanā keḷanā parikeḷanā gaddhikatā gaddhikattaṃ capalatā cāpalyaṃ—
parikeḷanā.example_2: cīvaramaṇḍanā pattamaṇḍanā senāsanamaṇḍanā imassa vā pūtikāyassa bāhirānaṃ vā parikkhārānaṃ maṇḍanā vibhūsanā keḷanā parikeḷanā gedhitatā gedhitattaṃ capalatā cāpalyaṃ—

bhijjheyyuṃ.meaning_2: be broken up; be split; be divided; break apart
bhijjheyyuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd plural, used here with the sense 'might be split apart, be divided'. Passive/impersonal in form but active in sense in this context.
bhijjheyyuṃ.example_1: kathaṃ ime nānā assu vinā assu vaggā assu dvidhā assu dvejjhā assu dve pakkhā assu bhijjheyyuṃ na samāgaccheyyuṃ dukkhaṃ na phāsu vihareyyunti.
bhijjheyyuṃ.example_2: Kathaṃ ime nānā assu vinā assu vaggā assu dvedhā assu dvejjhā assu dve pakkhā assu bhijjheyyuṃ na samāgaccheyyuṃ dukkhaṃ na phāsu vihareyyunti.
bhijjheyyuṃ.translation_2: Thinking: “How might these people be separated, be without, be divided, become two-fold, become dual, become two factions, be broken up, not come together, and live in discomfort and unease?”

unnahanā.meaning_2: binding up; tying up; entangling (in flattery); encompassing
unnahanā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text a feminine abstract noun in a list of flattering behaviours (lapanā series). Part of the compound-style enumeration of cātukamyatā; formed with prefix u + √nah and the -anā suffix.
unnahanā.example_1: lābhasakkārasilokasannissitassa pāpicchassa icchāpakatassa āmisacakkhukassa lokadhammagarukassa yā paresaṃ ālapanā lapanā sallapanā ullapanā samullapanā unnahanā samunnahanā ukkācanā samukkācanā anupiyabhāṇitā cāṭukamyatā muggasūpyatā pāribhaṭyatā parapiṭṭhimaṃsikatā, yā tattha saṇhavācatā sakhilavācatā sithilavācatā apharusavācatā—
unnahanā.example_2: Lābhasakkārasilokasannissitassa pāpicchassa icchāpakatassa āmisacakkhukassa lokadhammagarukassa yā paresaṃ ālapanā lapanā sallapanā ullapanā samullapanā unnahanā samunnahanā ukkācanā samukkācanā [ukkāpanā samukkāpanā (syā.)] anupiyabhāṇitā cātukamyatā muggasūpyatā pāribhaṭayatā parapiṭṭhimaṃsikatā [piṭṭhimaṃsikatā (ka.) visuddhimagge sīlaniddesavaṇṇanā oloketabbā], yā tattha saṇhavācatā sakhilavācatā sithilavācatā [mettavācakatā (syā.)] apharusavācatā – ayaṃ vuccati lapanā.
unnahanā.translation_2: For a person with evil desires, who is characterized by desire, greedy for gains, regarding worldly phenomena as significant, and linked to gain, honor, and fame, whatever addressing of others, flattery, chatting, lifting up, lifting up completely, tying up, binding completely, illuminating, illuminating completely, speaking pleasing words, servility, fawning, cringing, or backbiting, along with whatever gentle speech, moderate speech, soft speech, or sweet speech is there—this is called flattery.

ukkācanā.meaning_2: praising; extolling; exalting; lifting up (in flattery)
ukkācanā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Listed among the ways of flattery (lapanā) in the Niddesa and Visuddhimagga; often paired with samukkācanā. The PEU analysis u + kaca + ṇe + yu is uncertain; the ending suggests the ā-feminine action-noun suffix -anā. Nominative singular in the text.
ukkācanā.example_1: lābhasakkārasilokasannissitassa pāpicchassa icchāpakatassa āmisacakkhukassa lokadhammagarukassa yā paresaṃ ālapanā lapanā sallapanā ullapanā samullapanā unnahanā samunnahanā ukkācanā samukkācanā anupiyabhāṇitā cāṭukamyatā muggasūpyatā pāribhaṭyatā parapiṭṭhimaṃsikatā, yā tattha saṇhavācatā sakhilavācatā sithilavācatā apharusavācatā—
ukkācanā.example_2: Lābhasakkārasilokasannissitassa pāpicchassa icchāpakatassa āmisacakkhukassa lokadhammagarukassa yā paresaṃ ālapanā lapanā sallapanā ullapanā samullapanā unnahanā samunnahanā ukkācanā samukkācanā [ukkāpanā samukkāpanā (syā.)] anupiyabhāṇitā cātukamyatā muggasūpyatā pāribhaṭayatā parapiṭṭhimaṃsikatā [piṭṭhimaṃsikatā (ka.) visuddhimagge sīlaniddesavaṇṇanā oloketabbā], yā tattha saṇhavācatā sakhilavācatā sithilavācatā [mettavācakatā (syā.)] apharusavācatā – ayaṃ vuccati lapanā.
ukkācanā.translation_2: For a person with evil desires, who is characterized by desire, greedy for gains, regarding worldly phenomena as significant, and linked to gain, honor, and fame, whatever addressing of others, flattery, chatting, lifting up, lifting up completely, tying up, binding completely, illuminating, illuminating completely, speaking pleasing words, servility, fawning, cringing, or backbiting, along with whatever gentle speech, moderate speech, soft speech, or sweet speech is there—this is called flattery.

ukkāpanā.meaning_2: lighting up; kindling; (in a list of flatteries) exalting; puffing up
ukkāpanā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading ukkācanā is more common in this stock list of lapanā; here glossed as a form of flattery. Feminine ā-stem in -anā.
ukkāpanā.example_1: Lābhasakkārasilokasannissitassa pāpicchassa icchāpakatassa āmisacakkhukassa lokadhammagarukassa yā paresaṃ ālapanā lapanā sallapanā ullapanā samullapanā unnahanā samunnahanā ukkācanā samukkācanā [ukkāpanā samukkāpanā (syā.)] anupiyabhāṇitā cātukamyatā muggasūpyatā pāribhaṭayatā parapiṭṭhimaṃsikatā [piṭṭhimaṃsikatā (ka.) visuddhimagge sīlaniddesavaṇṇanā oloketabbā], yā tattha saṇhavācatā sakhilavācatā sithilavācatā [mettavācakatā (syā.)] apharusavācatā – ayaṃ vuccati lapanā.
ukkāpanā.translation_1: For a person with evil desires, who is characterized by desire, greedy for gains, regarding worldly phenomena as significant, and linked to gain, honor, and fame, whatever addressing of others, flattery, chatting, lifting up, lifting up completely, tying up, binding completely, illuminating, illuminating completely, speaking pleasing words, servility, fawning, cringing, or backbiting, along with whatever gentle speech, moderate speech, soft speech, or sweet speech is there—this is called flattery.

cātukamyatā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun from cātukāma (desiring to please). Listed among forms of lapanā (flattery).
cātukamyatā.example_1: Lābhasakkārasilokasannissitassa pāpicchassa icchāpakatassa āmisacakkhukassa lokadhammagarukassa yā paresaṃ ālapanā lapanā sallapanā ullapanā samullapanā unnahanā samunnahanā ukkācanā samukkācanā [ukkāpanā samukkāpanā (syā.)] anupiyabhāṇitā cātukamyatā muggasūpyatā pāribhaṭayatā parapiṭṭhimaṃsikatā [piṭṭhimaṃsikatā (ka.) visuddhimagge sīlaniddesavaṇṇanā oloketabbā], yā tattha saṇhavācatā sakhilavācatā sithilavācatā [mettavācakatā (syā.)] apharusavācatā – ayaṃ vuccati lapanā.
cātukamyatā.translation_1: For a person with evil desires, who is characterized by desire, greedy for gains, regarding worldly phenomena as significant, and linked to gain, honor, and fame, whatever addressing of others, flattery, chatting, lifting up, lifting up completely, tying up, binding completely, illuminating, illuminating completely, speaking pleasing words, servility, fawning, cringing, or backbiting, along with whatever gentle speech, moderate speech, soft speech, or sweet speech is there—this is called flattery.

pāribhaṭayatā.meaning_2: fawning; cringing; servility; being a follower
pāribhaṭayatā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun in -tā from pāribhaṭaya. Listed among forms of flattery (lapanā) in the Niddesa. The exact sense is uncertain; it may denote acting as a follower or servant.
pāribhaṭayatā.example_1: Lābhasakkārasilokasannissitassa pāpicchassa icchāpakatassa āmisacakkhukassa lokadhammagarukassa yā paresaṃ ālapanā lapanā sallapanā ullapanā samullapanā unnahanā samunnahanā ukkācanā samukkācanā [ukkāpanā samukkāpanā (syā.)] anupiyabhāṇitā cātukamyatā muggasūpyatā pāribhaṭayatā parapiṭṭhimaṃsikatā [piṭṭhimaṃsikatā (ka.) visuddhimagge sīlaniddesavaṇṇanā oloketabbā], yā tattha saṇhavācatā sakhilavācatā sithilavācatā [mettavācakatā (syā.)] apharusavācatā – ayaṃ vuccati lapanā.
pāribhaṭayatā.translation_1: For a person with evil desires, who is characterized by desire, greedy for gains, regarding worldly phenomena as significant, and linked to gain, honor, and fame, whatever addressing of others, flattery, chatting, lifting up, lifting up completely, tying up, binding completely, illuminating, illuminating completely, speaking pleasing words, servility, fawning, cringing, or backbiting, along with whatever gentle speech, moderate speech, soft speech, or sweet speech is there—this is called flattery.

ākāsanañcāyatanasamāpattiyā.meaning_2: attainment of the sphere of infinite space; the base of infinite space attainment
ākāsanañcāyatanasamāpattiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text has ākāsanañcāyatanasamāpattiyā, a variant spelling of ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiyā (instrumental singular). First of the four immaterial attainments.
ākāsanañcāyatanasamāpattiyā.example_1: Idhekacco na uccā kulā pabbajito samāno uccā kulā pabbajitena saddhiṃ sadisaṃ attānaṃ karoti cittena, na mahābhogakulā pabbajito samāno mahābhogakulā pabbajitena saddhiṃ sadisaṃ attānaṃ karoti cittena, na uḷārabhogakulā pabbajito samāno uḷārabhogakulā pabbajitena saddhiṃ sadisaṃ attānaṃ karoti cittena, na suttantiko samāno suttantikena saddhiṃ sadisaṃ attānaṃ karoti cittena, na vinayadharo samāno vinayadharena … na dhammakathiko samāno dhammakathikena … na āraññiko samāno āraññakena … na piṇḍapātiko samāno piṇḍapātikena … na paṃsukūliko samāno paṃsukūlikena … na tecīvariko samāno tecīvarakena … na sapadānacāriko samāno sapadānacārikena … na khalupacchābhattiko samāno khalupacchābhattikena … na nesajjiko samāno nesaññikena … na yathāsanthatiko samāno yathāsanthatikena saddhiṃ sadisaṃ attānaṃ karoti cittena, na paṭhamassa jhānassa lābhī samāno paṭhamassa jhānassa lābhinā saddhiṃ sadisaṃ attānaṃ karoti cittena, na dutiyassa jhānassa lābhī samāno dutiyassa … na tatiyassa jhānassa lābhī samāno tatiyassa … na catutthassa jhānassa lābhī samāno lābhī samāno catutthassa … na ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiyā lābhī samāno ākāsanañcāyatanasamāpattiyā … na viññāṇañcāyatanasamāpattiyā lābhī samāno viññāṇañcāyatana samāpattiyā … na ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpattiyā lābhī samāno ākiñcaññāyatana samāpattiyā … na nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā lābhī samāno nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā lābhinā saddhiṃ sadisaṃ attānaṃ karoti cittena – idaṃ cetasikaṃ pāgabbhiyaṃ.
ākāsanañcāyatanasamāpattiyā.translation_1: Here, someone, although not gone forth from a high-status family, makes himself equal in mind to one who has gone forth from a high-status family; although not gone forth from a family of great wealth, he makes himself equal in mind to one who has gone forth from a family of great wealth; although not gone forth from a family of eminent wealth, he makes himself equal in mind to one who has gone forth from a family of eminent wealth; although not a reciter of the Suttas, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a reciter of the Suttas; although not an expert on the discipline, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is an expert on the discipline; although not a speaker on the Dhamma, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a speaker on the Dhamma; although not a forest dweller, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a forest dweller; although not an eater of almsfood, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is an eater of almsfood; although not a wearer of rag-robes, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a wearer of rag-robes; although not a wearer of the triple robe, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a wearer of the triple robe; although not a continuous alms-walker, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a continuous alms-walker; although not one who does not eat in the evening, he makes himself equal in mind to one who does not eat in the evening; although not a continuous sitter, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a continuous sitter; although not an any-bed user, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is an any-bed user; although not a recipient of the first jhāna, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a recipient of the first jhāna; [similarly for the other jhānas and immaterial attainments]—this is mental presumption.

parisaṭho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Intensive compound of saṭha; nominative singular in the text, describing a deceitful person.
parisaṭho.example_1: idhekacco saṭho hoti parisaṭho, yaṃ tattha saṭhaṃ saṭhatā sāṭheyyaṃ kakkaratā kakkariyaṃ parikkhattatā pārikkhattiyaṃ—
parisaṭho.example_2: Idhekacco saṭho hoti parisaṭho, yaṃ tattha saṭhaṃ saṭhatā sāṭheyyaṃ kakkaratā kakkariyaṃ parikkhattatā pārikkhattiyaṃ – idaṃ vuccati sāṭheyyaṃ.
parisaṭho.translation_2: Here, someone is deceitful and is deceitful in every respect; that which is in that individual—the deceit, the state of being deceitful, fraud, the harsh nature, the praiseful state, the entrenched, firm deception—this is called fraud.

khuṃsito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used as an adjective meaning 'insulted, reviled'. The root √khuṃs (insult) is rare; the PEU suggests khusi+ta. In the text it appears in a list of synonyms (dūsito, ghaṭṭito, vambhito, garahito, upavadito) describing one who is insulted or abused.
khuṃsito.example_1: rusitoti dūsito khuṃsito ghaṭṭito vambhito garahito upavadito.
khuṃsito.example_2: dūsito khuṃsito vambhito ghaṭṭito garahito upavadito pharusena kakkhaḷena nappaṭivajjā nappaṭibhaṇeyya, akkosantaṃ na paccakkoseyya, rosantaṃ nappaṭiroseyya, bhaṇḍantaṃ na paṭibhaṇḍeyya, na kalahaṃ kareyya, na bhaṇḍanaṃ kareyya, na viggahaṃ kareyya, na vivādaṃ kareyya, na medhagaṃ kareyya, kalahaṃ bhaṇḍanaṃ viggahaṃ vivādaṃ medhagaṃ pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyya, kalahabhaṇḍanaviggahavivādamedhagā ārato assa virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā vihareyyāti—

sakkhidhammamanītihamaddasīti.meaning_2: saw the state of a witness, free from led-astray views; saw the truth as a witness, not led astray
sakkhidhammamanītihamaddasīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sakkhidhamma + anītihaṃ + addasī + iti (or similar); a poetic/commentarial description of the Buddha seeing the truth; final -ti is the quotation particle.

napī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + pi, used for emphasis: 'not even, nor'. In the text: 'na bhasmā hoti napī masi' = 'there is no ash, nor even soot'. Sometimes written na pi.
napī.example_2: Passa kammānaṃ daḷhattaṃ, na bhasmā hoti napī masi.
napī.translation_2: See the firmness of their deeds, there is no ash, nor even soot.

disampi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular of disā. In the text it is followed by the sandhi -pi (disampi).
disampi.example_1: ‘‘ Yaṃ yaṃ disaṃ padhāvanti [disampi dhāvanti (syā.)], taṃ taṃ dvāraṃ pidhīyati [pithīyati (sī. syā.)];
disampi.translation_1: “To whatever direction they run, that door is closed;

āvīsīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form āvīsīti in the text is likely āvisi + iti, with the aorist āvisi, but the passage also cites āvisati. Commentarial gloss on āvisi.
āvīsīti.example_1: Disvāti disvā passitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā bhayaṃ pīḷanaṃ ghaṭṭanaṃ upaddavo upasaggo āvisīti [āvīsīti (sī.), āvisatīti (syā.)]– disvā maṃ bhayamāvisi.
āvīsīti.translation_1: “Seeing” means having seen, having perceived, having calculated, having judged, having clarified, having made evident—fear, oppression, agitation, danger, or misfortune entered (me)—thus: “Seeing, fear entered me.”

uppāṭayitvā.meaning_2: having pulled out; having torn out; having uprooted; having eradicated
uppāṭayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive, part of a series of synonyms (uddharitvā, samuddharitvā, pajahitvā) for eradicating a defilement. Sometimes analysed with √paṭh (paṭh + *aya), but √paṭ 1 is preferred here.
uppāṭayitvā.example_1: attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhaccāti attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhacca samūhacca uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvāti—
uppāṭayitvā.example_2: tameva rāgasallaṃ dosasallaṃ mohasallaṃ mānasallaṃ diṭṭhisallaṃ sokasallaṃ kathaṅkathāsallaṃ abbuyha abbuhitvā uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantiṃ karitvā anabhāvaṃ gametvā neva puratthimaṃ disaṃ dhāvati na pacchimaṃ disaṃ dhāvati na uttaraṃ disaṃ dhāvati na dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ dhāvati.

uppādayitvā.meaning_2: having caused to arise; having produced; having stirred up
uppādayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in a list of absolutives describing the removal of the dart (salla). Causes the arising (of something). Some editions read samuppādayitvā.
uppādayitvā.example_1: Tameva rāgasallaṃ dosasallaṃ mohasallaṃ mānasallaṃ diṭṭhisallaṃ sokasallaṃ kathaṃkathāsallaṃ abbuyha abbuhitvā uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā [uppādayitvā samuppādayitvā (syā. ka.)] pajahitvā vinodetvā byantiṃ karitvā anabhāvaṃ gametvā neva puratthimaṃ disaṃ dhāvati na pacchimaṃ disaṃ dhāvati na uttaraṃ disaṃ dhāvati na dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ dhāvati.
uppādayitvā.translation_1: Having drawn out, pulled out, removed, completely removed, struck out, completely struck out, abandoned, dispelled, made an end of, and reduced to non-existence that very dart of lust, dart of hatred, dart of delusion, dart of conceit, dart of view, dart of sorrow, and dart of uncertainty and wondering, he does not run east, does not run west, does not run north, does not run south.

samuppādayitvā.meaning_2: having caused to arise; having produced; having generated
samuppādayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for uppādayitvā (digital PDB marks the samuppādayitvā reading as the Siamese/Thai edition). Absolutive in a list of absolutives describing removing the darts of defilement.
samuppādayitvā.example_1: Tameva rāgasallaṃ dosasallaṃ mohasallaṃ mānasallaṃ diṭṭhisallaṃ sokasallaṃ kathaṃkathāsallaṃ abbuyha abbuhitvā uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā [uppādayitvā samuppādayitvā (syā. ka.)] pajahitvā vinodetvā byantiṃ karitvā anabhāvaṃ gametvā neva puratthimaṃ disaṃ dhāvati na pacchimaṃ disaṃ dhāvati na uttaraṃ disaṃ dhāvati na dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ dhāvati.
samuppādayitvā.translation_1: Having drawn out, pulled out, removed, completely removed, struck out, completely struck out, abandoned, dispelled, made an end of, and reduced to non-existence that very dart of lust, dart of hatred, dart of delusion, dart of conceit, dart of view, dart of sorrow, and dart of uncertainty and wondering, he does not run east, does not run west, does not run north, does not run south.

gīyanti.meaning_2: is sung; is recited; is taken and memorised
gīyanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive of gāyati. In the text gīyanti is glossed with niggīyanti, kathīyanti, bhaṇīyanti and, in the second sentence, with gaṇhīyanti uggaṇhīyanti (are taken up and memorised). 3rd plural present passive.
gīyanti.example_1: anugīyantīti gīyanti niggīyanti kathīyanti bhaṇīyanti dīpīyanti voharīyanti.
gīyanti.example_2: atha vā gīyanti gaṇhīyanti uggaṇhīyanti dhārīyanti upadhārīyanti upalakkhīyanti gadhitapaṭilābhāya.

niggīyanti.meaning_2: is sung; is uttered; is spoken; is proclaimed
niggīyanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of anugīyanti in the defining sentence of the Niddesa commentary; passive causative of ni + √gā, meaning 'is sung out; is said'. Present 3rd plural.
niggīyanti.example_1: anugīyantīti gīyanti niggīyanti kathīyanti bhaṇīyanti dīpīyanti voharīyanti.

saṃtiṭṭheyya.meaning_2: should stand firm (in); should remain (in); should persist (in)
saṃtiṭṭheyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular of saṃtiṭṭhati, negated with na in the text: na saṃtiṭṭheyya, 'should not remain in'. Saṃtiṭṭheyya and tiṭṭheyya are used together, both negated with atimāne ('in conceit').
saṃtiṭṭheyya.example_1: Atimāne na tiṭṭheyya na saṃtiṭṭheyya, atimānaṃ pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyya, atimānā ārato assa virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā vihareyyāti – atimāne na tiṭṭheyya.
saṃtiṭṭheyya.translation_1: One should not remain or stand in conceit; one should abandon, dispel, put an end to, and bring to non-existence conceit; one should be one who has desisted, turned away, abstained, emerged, is freed, is released, is detached, and lives with a mind free of boundaries—that is “one should not remain in conceit.”

paṭivāsetvā.meaning_2: having turned away; having turned back; having withdrawn
paṭivāsetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of paṭivāpetvā; the commentator's gloss takes it as 'having turned away (the mind)'. Absolutive of the causative paṭivāseti.
paṭivāsetvā.example_1: Atha vā sabbasaṅkhāradhātuyā cittaṃ paṭivāpetvā [paṭivāsetvā (ka.)] amatāya dhātuyā cittaṃ upasaṃharati –
paṭivāsetvā.translation_1: Alternatively, having turned the mind away from the element of all volitional formations, one inclines the mind toward the deathless property—

nibbuttiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine i-stem noun; accusative singular in the text. The form is from nibbuti, meaning peace or Nibbāna. PEU also connects it with √vā (to blow) and ni (out).
nibbuttiṃ.example_1: ‘‘ Te nibbuttiṃ āsisamānasā [āsiṃsamānā (sī.), abhimānā (syā.)] dadanti, tanninnacittā [tanninnā tañcittā (ka.)] tadadhimuttā;
nibbuttiṃ.translation_1: “Desiring peace, they give gifts, with minds slanting toward that, and devoted to that;

vuttaṃñhetaṃ.meaning_2: for this is said; for this was said
vuttaṃñhetaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vuttaṃ (past participle of vadati, 'said') + hi (emphatic, 'for; indeed') + etaṃ (pronoun, 'this'). Opening of a quotation; the final -ṃ of vuttaṃ is replaced by ñ before hi.
vuttaṃñhetaṃ.translation_1: This has been said by the Blessed One—

visaritaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular agreeing with taṇhājāliniṃ; visaritaṃ visattikaṃ describes the craving-net as spread out and clinging.
visaritaṃ.example_1: so evaṃ eko adutiyo appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto mahāpadhānaṃ padahanto māraṃ sasenakaṃ namuciṃ kaṇhaṃ pamattabandhuṃ vidhametvā ca taṇhājāliniṃ visaritaṃ visattikaṃ pajahi vinodesi byantīakāsi anabhāvaṅgamesi.
visaritaṃ.example_2: so evaṃ eko adutiyo appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto najjā nerañjarāya tīre bodhirukkhamūle mahāpadhānaṃ padahanto māraṃ sasenaṃ kaṇhaṃ namuciṃ pamattabandhuṃ vidhamitvā taṇhājāliniṃ visaritaṃ visattikaṃ pajahasi vinodesi byantiṃ akāsi anabhāvaṃ gamesi.

sambujjhitabbaṃ.meaning_2: to be fully understood; to be comprehended; to be awakened to
sambujjhitabbaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle used in the Niddesa alongside bujjhitabba, anubujjhitabba, paṭibujjhitabba. Neuter nominative singular in the text.
sambujjhitabbaṃ.example_1: atha vā yaṃ bujjhitabbaṃ anubujjhitabbaṃ paṭibujjhitabbaṃ sambujjhitabbaṃ adhigantabbaṃ phassitabbaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ tena bodhiñāṇena bujjhi anubujjhi paṭibujjhi sambujjhi adhigacchi phassesi sacchākāsi.
sambujjhitabbaṃ.example_2: atha vā yaṃ bujjhitabbaṃ anubujjhitabbaṃ paṭibujjhitabbaṃ sambujjhitabbaṃ adhigantabbaṃ phassitabbaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ tena paccekabodhiñāṇena bujjhi anubujjhi paṭibujjhi sambujjhi adhigacchi phassesi sacchākāsīti evaṃ so paccekasambuddho eko anuttaraṃ paccekasambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti—

ugghātinigghātivītivatto.meaning_2: who has passed beyond vexation and non-vexation; gone beyond agitation and quieting
ugghātinigghātivītivatto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Attributive compound describing one free from attraction and aversion; nominative singular in the text.
ugghātinigghātivītivatto.example_1: ekacce bāhaṃ gandhena limpeyyuṃ, ekacce bāhaṃ vāsiyā taccheyyuṃ, amukasmiṃ natthi rāgo, amukasmiṃ natthi paṭighaṃ, anunayapaṭighavippahīno ugghātinigghātivītivatto anurodhavirodhaṃ samatikkanto.

paṭibāhirā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of paribāhirā in the sentence; nominative plural masculine agreeing with tumhe. Possibly from paṭi + bāhira, 'turned outside, excluded'.
paṭibāhirā.example_1: Sace ahaṃ na paṭiggahessāmi, evaṃ tumhe puññena paribāhirā [paṭibāhirā (ka.)] bhavissatha, na mayhaṃ iminā attho, api ca tumhākaṃyeva anukampāya paṭiggaṇhāmī ’’ ti.
paṭibāhirā.translation_1: If I do not accept, then you will be deprived of merit; I have no need for this, yet I accept it out of compassion for you.’

kivantoti.meaning_2: how much; how great; how many
kivantoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is kivanto with the quotation particle -ti: kivanto iti. Interrogative adjective meaning 'how much; how many'.

isivātapaṭivātāni.meaning_2: exposed to the winds of the sages; (unaffected by) the winds of the sages?; protected from the winds of the sages
isivātapaṭivātāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa list of families worthy of resort. The reading and sense are uncertain; the PEU entry suggests isi + vāta + paṭivāta. The context is a stock list, so it is likely a stock positive epithet. Neuter plural in the text.
isivātapaṭivātāni.example_1: yāni vā pana tāni kulāni saddhāni pasannāni opānabhūtāni kāsāvapajjotāni isivātapaṭivātāni atthakāmāni hitakāmāni phāsukāmāni yogakkhemakāmāni bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ, tathārūpāni kulāni sevati bhajati payirupāsati—
isivātapaṭivātāni.example_2: Yāni vā pana tāni kulāni saddhāni pasannāni opānabhūtāni kāsāvapajjotāni isivātapaṭivātāni atthakāmāni hitakāmāni phāsukāmāni yogakkhemakāmāni bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ, tathārūpāni kulāni sevati bhajati payirupāsati – ayampi vuccati gocaro.
isivātapaṭivātāni.translation_2: Whatever those families are that are faithful, serene, acting as a source of support, radiant with the robes, protected by the winds of the sages, desiring what is worthwhile, desiring what is beneficial, desiring what is comfortable, desiring what is safe from the four yokes, toward bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, laymen, and laywomen—he relies on, approaches, and pays homage to such families—this too is called a suitable resort.

paṭibujjhitukāmassa.meaning_2: desiring to awaken (to); wanting to understand; wishing to penetrate
paṭibujjhitukāmassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular in the text, agreeing with the seeker of sambodhi; the -tuṃ infinitive inside the compound is from paṭibujjhati.
paṭibujjhitukāmassa.example_1: taṃ sambodhiṃ bujjhitukāmassa anubujjhitukāmassa paṭibujjhitukāmassa sambujjhitukāmassa adhigantukāmassa phassitukāmassa sacchikātukāmassāti—
paṭibujjhitukāmassa.example_2: Taṃ sambodhiṃ bujjhitukāmassa anubujjhitukāmassa paṭibujjhitukāmassa sambujjhitukāmassa adhigantukāmassa phassitukāmassa sacchikātukāmassāti – sambodhikāmassa.
paṭibujjhitukāmassa.translation_2: For one who wishes to awaken to that enlightenment, who wishes to know through appropriate practice, who wishes to penetrate it, who wishes to awaken rightly, who wishes to reach it, who wishes to touch it, and who wishes to realize it—that is “for one who desires enlightenment.”

sambujjhitukāmassa.meaning_2: desiring to awaken fully; wishing to attain full enlightenment
sambujjhitukāmassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular in the text, qualifying one who desires sambodhi. Compound of the infinitive sambujjhituṃ and kāma; the form sambujjhitukāmassa is the genitive singular of the compound as a whole.
sambujjhitukāmassa.example_1: taṃ sambodhiṃ bujjhitukāmassa anubujjhitukāmassa paṭibujjhitukāmassa sambujjhitukāmassa adhigantukāmassa phassitukāmassa sacchikātukāmassāti—
sambujjhitukāmassa.example_2: Taṃ sambodhiṃ bujjhitukāmassa anubujjhitukāmassa paṭibujjhitukāmassa sambujjhitukāmassa adhigantukāmassa phassitukāmassa sacchikātukāmassāti – sambodhikāmassa.
sambujjhitukāmassa.translation_2: For one who wishes to awaken to that enlightenment, who wishes to know through appropriate practice, who wishes to penetrate it, who wishes to awaken rightly, who wishes to reach it, who wishes to touch it, and who wishes to realize it—that is “for one who desires enlightenment.”

phassitukāmassa.meaning_2: wishing to touch; desiring to experience; wanting to contact
phassitukāmassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Desiderative compound with infinitive phassituṃ (from phusati, √phus 1). Genitive singular in the text, qualifying one who wishes to attain sambodhi.
phassitukāmassa.example_1: taṃ sambodhiṃ bujjhitukāmassa anubujjhitukāmassa paṭibujjhitukāmassa sambujjhitukāmassa adhigantukāmassa phassitukāmassa sacchikātukāmassāti—
phassitukāmassa.example_2: Taṃ sambodhiṃ bujjhitukāmassa anubujjhitukāmassa paṭibujjhitukāmassa sambujjhitukāmassa adhigantukāmassa phassitukāmassa sacchikātukāmassāti – sambodhikāmassa.
phassitukāmassa.translation_2: For one who wishes to awaken to that enlightenment, who wishes to know through appropriate practice, who wishes to penetrate it, who wishes to awaken rightly, who wishes to reach it, who wishes to touch it, and who wishes to realize it—that is “for one who desires enlightenment.”

madditabbāni.meaning_2: to be crushed; to be trampled; to be destroyed
madditabbāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter nominative plural in -āni, agreeing with the preceding gerundives. Part of a list of things to be overcome and crushed.
madditabbāni.example_1: athāparānipi atthi abhisambhotabbāni abhibhavitabbāni ajjhottharitabbāni pariyādiyitabbāni madditabbāni.

abhisambhavैyyāti.meaning_2: could overcome; would be able to endure
abhisambhavैyyāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written abhisambhavaiyyāti, an alternative optative spelling of abhisambhaveyya with quotative ti. From abhisambhavati, optative 3rd singular. No sentences were found; optative form assumed.

visaṅghacārino.meaning_2: not moving in herds; wandering alone; not gregarious
visaṅghacārino.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (syā.) of asaṅghacārino; nominative plural in the text, agreeing with bhikkhavo. Also resolvable as vi + saṅghacārī.
visaṅghacārino.example_1: Migā viya asaṅghacārino [māgadhā visaṅghacārino (syā.)], aniketā viharanti bhikkhavo.
visaṅghacārino.translation_1: “Like animals, they are non-obstructive wanderers; the bhikkhus dwell without abode.”

cātukamyatāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text, listed among wrong ways of obtaining requisites. The word is an abstract noun from cātukamma, itself a compound of cātu and kamma.
cātukamyatāya.example_1: Cīvaraṃ labhitvā piṇḍapātaṃ labhitvā na kuhanāya, na lapanāya, na nemittikatāya, na nippesikatāya, na lābhena lābhaṃ nijigīsanatāya, na dārudānena, na veḷudānena, na pattadānena, na pupphadānena, na phaladānena, na sinānadānena, na cuṇṇadānena, na mattikādānena, na dantakaṭṭhadānena, na mukhodakadānena, na cātukamyatāya, na muggasūpyatāya, na pāribhaṭyatāya, na pīṭhamaddikatāya, na vatthuvijjāya, na tiracchānavijjāya, na aṅgavijjāya, na nakkhattavijjāya, na dūtagamanena, na pahiṇagamanena, na jaṅghapesanikena, na vejjakammena, na piṇḍapaṭipiṇḍakena, na dānānuppadānena dhammena samena laddhā labhitvā adhigantvā vinditvā paṭilabhitvāti – annañca laddhā vasanañca kāle.
cātukamyatāya.translation_1: Having received a robe, having received almsfood, not for the sake of flattery, not for the sake of deception, not for the sake of omens, not for the sake of hints, not for the sake of seeking gain with gain, not by giving wood, not by giving bamboo, not by giving leaves, not by giving flowers, not by giving fruits, not by giving water for bathing, not by giving powders, not by giving clay, not by giving tooth-sticks, not by giving water for the face, not for the sake of flattery, not for the sake of curry, not for the sake of gossip, not for the sake of supporting others, not by astrology, not by base arts, not by interpreting bodily marks, not by auspicious signs, not by acting as an emissary, not by going on errands, not by serving as a messenger, not by practicing medicine, not by returning alms for alms, not by giving gifts in return for gifts—having obtained them lawfully and righteously, having received them, having reached them, having found them, having acquired them—that is “having received almsfood and clothing in season.”

paṭivinoditvā.meaning_2: having driven away; having dispelled; having removed
paṭivinoditvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of vippajahitvā in these verses; the absolutive of paṭivinodeti, formed from the past participle stem paṭivinodita. No simplex paṭivinodati is attested.
paṭivinoditvā.example_1: Etaṃ rajaṃ vippajahitvā [paṭivinoditvā (ka.)] paṇḍitā, viharanti te vigatarajassa sāsane.
paṭivinoditvā.translation_1: having abandoned this dust, the wise dwell in the Dispensation of the dustless one.
paṭivinoditvā.example_2: Etaṃ rajaṃ vippajahitvā [paṭivinoditvā (ka.) mahāni.209] cakkhumā, tasmā jino vigatarajoti vuccati.
paṭivinoditvā.translation_2: Since the Clear-eyed One has abandoned this corruption, the Victorious Buddha is called ‘one whose corruption has faded away.’

puramāhiyati.meaning_2: Pura (city) and Māhissati (name of a city); to the city of Māhissatī
puramāhiyati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the text for puramāhissati; the second element is probably the name Māhissatī rather than a verb, though the spelling with -y- is irregular.
puramāhiyati.translation_1: 36. They went to Patiṭṭhāna of the city of Aḷaka, then to Māhissati,

pimpati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for lippati at this line, glossed by the commentary as sticking or being smeared. 3rd singular present in the text.
pimpati.example_1: Ko ubhantamabhiññāya, majjhe mantā na lippati [na pimpati (bahūsu)];
pimpati.translation_1: Who, having comprehended the two ends, is not stuck in the middle with wisdom?

yāvapārāyanānugītigātāpariyosānā.meaning_2: from the beginning of the Ajitamāṇavapucchā through to the end of the Pārāyanānugītigāthā
yāvapārāyanānugītigātāpariyosānā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yāva + pārāyanānugītigātāpariyosānā. The second member is a compound meaning 'ending with the Pārāyanānugītigāthā'. Commentarial citation indicating a range of text, parenthesised in the manuscript; not part of the verse.
yāvapārāyanānugītigātāpariyosānā.example_1: Addhā gamissāmi na mettha kaṅkhā, evaṃ maṃ dhārehi adhimuttacittan ’’ ti [ajitamāṇavapucchāya paṭṭhāya yāvapārāyanānugītigātāpariyosānā syā.… potthake natthi].
yāvapārāyanānugītigātāpariyosānā.translation_1: I will surely go there; I have no doubt about this. Consider me one whose mind is thus inclined.”

palippati.meaning_2: is smeared (with); is stained (by); is defiled (by)
palippati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present of palippati, used in the Niddesa gloss as a synonym of lippati and upalippati; the prefix pa- is intensive.
palippati.example_1: so ubhantamabhiññāya, majjhe mantā na lippatīti so ubho ca ante majjhañca mantāya abhiññāya jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā na lippati na palippati na upalippati, alitto asaṃlitto anupalitto nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā viharatīti—
palippati.example_2: So ubhantamabhiññāya , majjhe mantā na lippatīti so ubho ca ante majjhañca mantāya abhiññāya jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā na lippati na palippati na upalippati, alitto asaṃlitto anupalitto nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā viharatīti – so ubhantamabhiññāya majjhe mantā na lippati.
palippati.translation_2: ‘One who, having directly known both ends and the middle, is not stained by them’ means that having known, calculated, judged, clarified, and made evident both the ends and the middle with wisdom, he is not stained, not smeared, not defiled; he is untainted, escaped, released, detached, and dwells with a mind unconstrained by boundaries.

vidhūmito.meaning_2: smoke-free; freed from smoke; purged; destroyed; done away with
vidhūmito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle in -ita of vidhūmeti ('to free from smoke; to purge'), used figuratively in the Niddesa for defilements being burnt away. Appears in the text in nominative singular masculine (rāgo ... vidhūmito) and in neuter forms (kāyaduccaritaṃ ... vidhūmitaṃ), agreeing with its subject. Sometimes analysed as vidhūma + ta.
vidhūmito.example_1: manoduccaritaṃ vidhūmitaṃ vidhamitaṃ sositaṃ visositaṃ byantīkataṃ, rāgo … doso … moho vidhūmito vidhamito sosito visosito byantīkato, kodho … upanāho … makkho … paḷāso … issā … macchariyaṃ … māyā … sāṭheyyaṃ … thambho … sārambho … māno … atimāno … mado … pamādo … sabbe kilesā sabbe duccaritā sabbe darathā sabbe pariḷāhā sabbe santāpā sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārā vidhūmitā vidhamitā sositā visositā byantīkatā.
vidhūmito.example_2: vidhūmoti kāyaduccaritaṃ vidhūmitaṃ vidhamitaṃ sositaṃ visositaṃ byantīkataṃ [byantikataṃ (ka.)], vacīduccaritaṃ … pe … manoduccaritaṃ vidhūmitaṃ vidhamitaṃ sositaṃ visositaṃ byantīkataṃ, rāgo … doso … moho vidhūmito vidhamito sosito visosito byantīkato, kodho … upanāho … makkho … paḷāso … issā … macchariyaṃ … māyā … sāṭheyyaṃ … thambho … sārambho … māno … atimāno … mado … pamādo … sabbe kilesā sabbe duccaritā sabbe darathā sabbe pariḷāhā sabbe santāpā sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārā vidhūmitā vidhamitā sositā visositā byantīkatā.
vidhūmito.translation_2: ‘Smoke-free’ means bodily misconduct is smoke-free, destroyed, withered, fully withered, and made smoke-free; verbal misconduct... mental misconduct... lust, hatred, delusion, anger, resentment, denigration, insolence, envy, avarice, deceit, fraud, obstinacy, rivalry, conceit, excessive conceit, intoxication, negligence, all defilements, all misconducts, all troubles, all fevers, all burnings, and all unwholesome formative actions are smoke-free, destroyed, withered, fully withered, and made smoke-free.

vidhūmitā.meaning_2: smoke-free; freed from smoke; destroyed; cleared away
vidhūmitā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used adjectivally in the Niddesa gloss of vidhūmo, agreeing with duccarita, rāga and other masculine and neuter nouns, and in the plural with sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārā.
vidhūmitā.example_1: manoduccaritaṃ vidhūmitaṃ vidhamitaṃ sositaṃ visositaṃ byantīkataṃ, rāgo … doso … moho vidhūmito vidhamito sosito visosito byantīkato, kodho … upanāho … makkho … paḷāso … issā … macchariyaṃ … māyā … sāṭheyyaṃ … thambho … sārambho … māno … atimāno … mado … pamādo … sabbe kilesā sabbe duccaritā sabbe darathā sabbe pariḷāhā sabbe santāpā sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārā vidhūmitā vidhamitā sositā visositā byantīkatā.
vidhūmitā.example_2: vidhūmoti kāyaduccaritaṃ vidhūmitaṃ vidhamitaṃ sositaṃ visositaṃ byantīkataṃ [byantikataṃ (ka.)], vacīduccaritaṃ … pe … manoduccaritaṃ vidhūmitaṃ vidhamitaṃ sositaṃ visositaṃ byantīkataṃ, rāgo … doso … moho vidhūmito vidhamito sosito visosito byantīkato, kodho … upanāho … makkho … paḷāso … issā … macchariyaṃ … māyā … sāṭheyyaṃ … thambho … sārambho … māno … atimāno … mado … pamādo … sabbe kilesā sabbe duccaritā sabbe darathā sabbe pariḷāhā sabbe santāpā sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārā vidhūmitā vidhamitā sositā visositā byantīkatā.
vidhūmitā.translation_2: ‘Smoke-free’ means bodily misconduct is smoke-free, destroyed, withered, fully withered, and made smoke-free; verbal misconduct... mental misconduct... lust, hatred, delusion, anger, resentment, denigration, insolence, envy, avarice, deceit, fraud, obstinacy, rivalry, conceit, excessive conceit, intoxication, negligence, all defilements, all misconducts, all troubles, all fevers, all burnings, and all unwholesome formative actions are smoke-free, destroyed, withered, fully withered, and made smoke-free.

dhammasaṅgaṇiye.meaning_2: Dhamma enumeration; Dhammasaṅgaṇī (first book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka)
dhammasaṅgaṇiye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the commentarial phrase dhammasaṅgaṇiye, cited as the source of the variant reading lāpo palāpo. Title of the first Abhidhamma book.
dhammasaṅgaṇiye.example_1: Paridevoti ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa sīlabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa diṭṭhibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa aññataraññatarena byasanena vā samannāgatassa aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena vā phuṭṭhassa ādevo paridevo ādevanā paridevanā ādevitattaṃ paridevitattaṃ vācā palāpo [lāpo palāpo (syā.) dhammasaṅgaṇiye] vippalāpo lālappo lālappanā lālappitattaṃ [lālappāyanā lālappāyitattaṃ (bahūsu) jarāsuttaniddesaṭṭhakathā oloketabbā].
dhammasaṅgaṇiye.translation_1: Paridevoti: of one struck by the loss of relatives ... or by any other painful phenomenon—lamentation, great lamentation, act of lamenting, great act of lamenting, state of lamenting, state of great lamenting, verbal babble, erratic babble, babbling, act of babbling, state of babbling.

dhammamuttaṃmaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of dhammamuttaman in the text, resolved as dhamma + uttamaṃ and glossed as amataṃ nibbānaṃ. Could also be read as dhammamuttaṃ + amataṃ, but the gloss points to uttamaṃ (or uttama).
dhammamuttaṃmaṃ.translation_1: “Supreme Dhamma” refers to the Deathless Nibbāna.

ākiñcanaṃ.meaning_2: having nothing; possessionless; free from worldly ties
ākiñcanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, qualifying brāhmaṇaṃ. It is a negative compound in na-a, a- + kiñcana, with lengthening of the initial vowel. The related abstract noun ākiñcañña is a different word.

pamuñcituṃ.meaning_2: to release; to set free; to let loose
pamuñcituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive in a string of glosses on pamocanāya (muñcituṃ, pamuñcituṃ, mocetuṃ, pamocetuṃ ...). Causative-like sense 'to set free'. Root √muc (release, free); pa + √muc with -c- in the base.
pamuñcituṃ.example_1: nāhaṃ sahissāmi pamocanāyāti nāhaṃ taṃ sakkomi muñcituṃ pamuñcituṃ mocetuṃ pamocetuṃ uddharituṃ samuddharituṃ uṭṭhāpetuṃ samuṭṭhāpetuṃ kathaṅkathāsallatoti.
pamuñcituṃ.example_2: Nāhaṃ sahissāmi [samīhāmi (ka.)] pamocanāyāti nāhaṃ taṃ sakkomi muñcituṃ pamuñcituṃ mocetuṃ pamocetuṃ uddharituṃ samuddharituṃ uṭṭhāpetuṃ samuṭṭhāpetuṃ kathaṃkathāsallatoti.
pamuñcituṃ.translation_2: “I cannot release” means: I cannot liberate, set free, loosen, set quite free, lift up, rescue, set up, or set properly from the arrow of doubt.

akiliyamāno.meaning_2: not becoming defiled; not being soiled; not becoming stained
akiliyamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for akilissamāno; alternative form akiliyamāno. Present participle, nominative singular, negated with na. See kilissati.
akiliyamāno.example_1: Yathā ākāso na rajjati lākhāya vā haliddiyā [haliddena (syā.)] vā nīliyā [nīlena (syā.)] vā mañjeṭṭhāya vā evaṃ arajjamāno adussamāno amuyhamāno akilissamānoti [akiliyamāno (syā.)]– evampi ākāsova abyāpajjamāno.
akiliyamāno.translation_1: Just as space is not stained by lacquer, turmeric, indigo, or madder, so not becoming attached, not becoming angry, not becoming deluded, and not becoming defiled—in this way too, it is “Like space, not becoming affected.”

mābhinibbattesi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text mābhinibbattesi (mā + abhinibbattesi) is a prohibitive aorist-like form meaning 'do not generate'; the entry is for the present 3rd singular. Causative of abhinibbattati; cf. nibbatteti.
mābhinibbattesi.example_1: bhavābhavāyāti bhavābhavāya kammabhavāya punabbhavāya kāmabhavāya, kammabhavāya kāmabhavāya punabbhavāya rūpabhavāya, kammabhavāya rūpabhavāya punabbhavāya arūpabhavāya, kammabhavāya arūpabhavāya punabbhavāya punappunabbhavāya, punappunagatiyā punappunaupapattiyā punappunapaṭisandhiyā punappunaattabhāvābhinibbattiyā taṇhaṃ mākāsi mā janesi mā sañjanesi mā nibbattesi mābhinibbattesi, pajaha vinodehi byantīkarohi anabhāvaṃ gamehīti—
mābhinibbattesi.example_2: idaṃ kiñcanaṃ tuyhaṃ mā ahu mā ahosi mā janesi mā sañjanesi mābhinibbattesi pajaha vinodehi byantīkarohi anabhāvaṃ gamehīti—

patarituṃ.meaning_2: to cross over; to pass beyond; to traverse
patarituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of patarati, listed with synonyms tarituṃ, uttarituṃ, samatikkamituṃ in a series describing crossing the floods. Probably a variant of patarati.
patarituṃ.example_1: anissitoti puggalaṃ vā anissito dhammaṃ vā anissito no visahāmi na ussahāmi na sakkomi na paṭibalo mahantaṃ kāmoghaṃ bhavoghaṃ diṭṭhoghaṃ avijjoghaṃ tarituṃ uttarituṃ patarituṃ samatikkamituṃ vītivattitunti—
patarituṃ.example_2: Anissitoti puggalaṃ vā anissito dhammaṃ vā anissito no visahāmi na ussahāmi na sakkomi na paṭibalo mahantaṃ kāmoghaṃ bhavoghaṃ diṭṭhoghaṃ avijjoghaṃ tarituṃ uttarituṃ patarituṃ samatikkamituṃ vītivattitunti – anissito no visahāmi tārituṃ.
patarituṃ.translation_2: “Without a support” means: not relying on a person and not relying on a Dhamma, I am not able, not striving, not capable, not qualified to cross, go across, pass beyond, or fully transcend the great flood of sensual desires, the flood of existence, the flood of views, or the flood of ignorance; this is the meaning of “Without a support, I am unable to cross.”

dakkhamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle of dakkhati (irregular present of √dis). Nominative singular masculine, used in a string of synonyms for seeing in the Niddesa.
dakkhamāno.example_1: nissaraṇato pekkhamāno dakkhamāno olokayamāno nijjhāyamāno upaparikkhamāno.
dakkhamāno.example_2: pekkhamānoti pekkhamāno dakkhamāno dissamāno passamāno olokayamāno nijjhāyamāno upaparikkhamānoti—

khambhitā.meaning_2: checked; restrained; held back; blocked; made stiff
khambhitā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Only the plural form khambhitā is found in the text, where it sits in a list of words meaning 'shaken, driven away'. The PEU entry takes the root as 'khabhi', but √khambh (prop, be stiff) is the usual analysis. Nom. pl. in the text.
khambhitā.example_1: vātavegena khittāti vātavegena khittā ukkhittā nunnā paṇunnā khambhitā vikkhambhitāti—
khambhitā.example_2: Vātavegena khittāti vātavegena khittā [khittaṃ (syā.) evamaññesu padesu niggahītantavasena] ukkhittā nunnā paṇunnā khambhitā vikkhambhitāti – acci yathā vātavegena khittā.
khambhitā.translation_2: “Cast by a gust of wind” means: shaken, extremely shaken, driven away, removed to a distance, checked, or not kept in the vicinity; thus it is “like a flame cast by a gust of wind.”

anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhaj.meaning_2: devotion to a harsh life of many and various extreme austerities and difficult practices
anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhaj.construction: aneka + vividha + atiparama + dukkara + kārika + lūkha + jīvita + anuyoga
anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhaj.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Long bahubbīhi compound describing the ascetic; instrumental singular in the text, qualifying upetaṃ muniṃ. The segmentation of the middle members is uncertain (atiparama + dukkara + kārika is one possibility).
anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhaj.example_1: udāhu ve jīvitenūpapannanti udāhu anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhajīvitānuyogena upetaṃ samupetaṃ upāgataṃ samupāgataṃ upapannaṃ samupapannaṃ samannāgataṃ muniṃ vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharantīti—
anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhaj.example_2: Udāhu ve jīvitenūpapannanti udāhu anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhajīvitānuyogena upetaṃ samupetaṃ upāgataṃ samupāgataṃ upapannaṃ samupapannaṃ samannāgataṃ muniṃ vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharantīti – udāhu ve jīvitenūpapannaṃ.
anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhaj.translation_2: “Or do they call him one endowed with a [specific] livelihood?”: Or do they call, speak of, declare, explain, and designate a person as a sage because he is endowed with a livelihood that consists of various kinds of austerity and difficult practices—that is what is meant by ‘or do they call him one endowed with a livelihood.’

tireti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of tarati in the sense of penetrating, examining throughly. Variant reading tīreti in the text. 3rd singular present; used of judging craving by the forty aspects; tīraṇapariññā.
tireti.example_1: Evaṃ ñātaṃ katvā taṇhaṃ tīreti [tireti (syā.)] aniccato dukkhato rogato gaṇḍato sallato aghato ābādhato parato palokato ītito upaddavato bhayato upasaggato calato pabhaṅguto addhuvato atāṇato aleṇato asaraṇato asaraṇībhūtato rittato tucchato suññato anattato ādīnavato vipariṇāmadhammato asārakato aghamūlato vadhakato vibhavato sāsavato saṅkhatato mārāmisato jātidhammato jarādhammato byādhidhammato maraṇadhammato sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammato saṃkilesadhammato samudayato atthaṅgamato assādato ādīnavato nissaraṇato tīreti – ayaṃ tīraṇapariññā.
tireti.translation_1: Having made it known in this way, one judges craving as inconstant, as suffering, as a disease, as a cancer, as an arrow, as a misery, as an affliction, as alien, as a disintegration, as a calamity, as trouble, as peril, as oppression, as fluctuating, as dissolving, as transient, as shelterless, as no-shelter, as no refuge, as without protection, as empty, as bare and void, as the void, as not-self, as danger, as subject to change, as having no core, as a root of evil, as a killer, as non-existence, as tainted, as conditioned, as Māra’s bait, as subject to birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and despair, as subject to defilement, as having an arising, as having a passing away, as gratification, as danger, as escape—this is the full understanding as judged.

paṭippasaddhattā.meaning_2: because of being tranquillised; due to being stilled; through being calmed
paṭippasaddhattā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative singular in -ttā of the abstract noun paṭippasaddhatta (from paṭippassaddha, pp of paṭippassambhati), used in a list of synonyms for nibbuta. Note the spelling with single -s- here beside paṭippassaddhā in the same sentence.
paṭippasaddhattā.example_1: Abhinibbutāti rāgassa nibbāpitattā nibbutā, dosassa nibbāpitattā nibbutā, mohassa nibbāpitattā nibbutā, kodhassa … pe … upanāhassa … sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārānaṃ santattā samitattā vūpasamitattā nijjhātattā nibbutattā vigatattā paṭippasaddhattā santā upasantā vūpasantā nibbutā paṭippassaddhāti – diṭṭhadhammābhinibbutā.
paṭippasaddhattā.translation_1: “Extinguished” means they are extinguished because they have quenched greed, quenched hatred, quenched delusion, quenched anger, and so on, up to quenching all unwholesome volitional formations; they are peaceful, calmed, stilled, quenched, and tranquilized; this is the meaning of “Having seen the Dhamma, they are extinguished.”
paṭippasaddhattā.example_2: Upasantāti rāgassa upasamitattā nibbāpitattā upasantā … pe … dosassa … mohassa … kodhassa … upanāhassa … pe … sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārānaṃ santattā samitattā vūpasamitattā nijjhātattā nibbutattā vigatattā paṭippasaddhattā santā upasantā vūpasantā nibbutā paṭippassaddhāti upasantā.
paṭippasaddhattā.translation_2: “Calmed” means they are calmed because greed, hatred, delusion, anger, and so on, up to all unwholesome volitional formations are calmed, stilled, quenched, and tranquilized; they are peaceful, calmed, stilled, quenched, and tranquilized.

santāpayitvā.meaning_2: having scorched; having burned; having heated; having tormented
santāpayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of the causative santāpeti (from √tap 1). In the texts it describes the sun scorching the earth before dispelling darkness.
santāpayitvā.example_1: yathā sūriyo tejī tejena samannāgato pathaviṃ abhibhuyya abhibhavitvā ajjhottharitvā pariyādiyitvā santāpayitvā sabbaṃ ākāsagataṃ tamagataṃ abhivihacca andhakāraṃ vidhamitvā ālokaṃ dassayitvā ākāse antalikkhe gaganapathe gacchati, evameva bhagavā ñāṇatejī ñāṇatejena samannāgato sabbaṃ abhisaṅkhārasamudayaṃ …pe…
santāpayitvā.example_2: Yathā sūriyo tejī tejena samannāgato pathaviṃ abhibhuyya abhibhavitvā ajjhottharitvā pariyādiyitvā santāpayitvā sabbaṃ ākāsagataṃ tamagataṃ abhivihacca andhakāraṃ vidhamitvā ālokaṃ dassayitvā ākāse antalikkhe gaganapathe [gamanapathe (syā.) aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā] gacchati, evameva bhagavā ñāṇatejī ñāṇatejena samannāgato sabbaṃ abhisaṅkhārasamudayaṃ … pe … kilesatamaṃ avijjandhakāraṃ vidhamitvā ñāṇālokaṃ dassetvā vatthukāme parijānitvā kilesakāme pahāya abhibhuyya abhibhavitvā ajjhottharitvā pariyādiyitvā madditvā carati viharati iriyati vatteti pāleti yapeti yāpetīti – ādiccova pathaviṃ tejī tejasā.
santāpayitvā.translation_2: Just as the sun, possessed of heat and radiance, having overwhelmed the earth, having surged over, having surged above, having consumed, and having scorched it, having destroyed all darkness that has gone into space, having driven away the darkness, having revealed light, goes into the sky, the empty space, the path of the gods; just so, the Blessed One, possessed of the radiance of knowledge and the heat of knowledge, having destroyed the origin of all volitional formations … having destroyed the darkness of defilement and the darkness of ignorance, having revealed the light of knowledge, having fully understood the sensual objects, having abandoned the defiling sensual pleasures, having overcome, having overwhelmed, having surged over, having consumed, and having crushed them, conducts himself, dwells, continues, proceeds, guards, nourishes, and sustains himself—this is the meaning of ‘just as the sun with its heat shines while overwhelming the earth.’

saraṇībhūtato.meaning_2: as having become a refuge; as a shelter
saraṇībhūtato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative of comparison in -to, from saraṇībhūta (saraṇī + bhūta), in the series khemato ... saraṇībhūtato in the Niddesa commentary.
saraṇībhūtato.example_1: nekkhammanti sammāpaṭipadaṃ anulomapaṭipadaṃ apaccanīkapaṭipadaṃ anvatthapaṭipadaṃ dhammānudhammapaṭipadaṃ sīlesu paripūrakāritaṃ indriyesu guttadvārataṃ bhojane mattaññutaṃ jāgariyānuyogaṃ satisampajaññaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhāne cattāro sammappadhāne cattāro iddhipāde pañcindriyāni pañca balāni satta bojjhaṅge ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ nibbānañca nibbānagāminiñca paṭipadaṃ khemato tāṇato leṇato saraṇato saraṇībhūtato abhayato accutato amatato nibbānato daṭṭhuṃ passitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvāti—
saraṇībhūtato.example_2: Nekkhammanti sammāpaṭipadaṃ anulomapaṭipadaṃ apaccanīkapaṭipadaṃ anvatthapaṭipadaṃ dhammānudhammapaṭipadaṃ sīlesu paripūrakāritaṃ indriyesu guttadvārataṃ bhojane mattaññutaṃ jāgariyānuyogaṃ satisampajaññaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhāne cattāro sammappadhāne cattāro iddhipāde pañcindriyāni pañca balāni satta bojjhaṅge ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ nibbānañca nibbānagāminiñca paṭipadaṃ khemato tāṇato leṇato saraṇato saraṇībhūtato abhayato accutato amatato nibbānato daṭṭhuṃ passitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvāti – nekkhammaṃ daṭṭhu khemato.
saraṇībhūtato.translation_2: “Renunciation”: the path of practice, the compliant path, the non-obstructive path, the path in accordance with the goal, the path of Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, perfect conduct in virtue, guarding the doors of the faculties, moderation in eating, the practice of wakefulness, mindfulness and clear comprehension, the four applications of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four foundations for supernormal power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, the noble eightfold path, Nibbāna, and the path of practice leading to Nibbāna—having seen them as secure, as a sanctuary, as a refuge, as a protection, as having no fear, as deathless, as the unmoving, as Nibbāna, having calculated, judged, examined, clarified, and made evident—this is “Having seen renunciation as secure.”

pavijjittha.meaning_2: entered; arrived (with mā: may it not enter; may it not arrive)
pavijjittha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Second person singular aorist in the prohibitive phrase mā pavijjittha, parallel to mā vijjittha and mā saṃvijjittha. Probably from pa + √vis with assimilation of s to jj; the v.l. is paviṭṭha.
pavijjittha.example_1: idaṃ kiñcanaṃ tuyhaṃ mā vijjittha mā pavijjittha mā saṃvijjittha pajaha vinodehi byantīkarohi anabhāvaṃ gamehīti—
pavijjittha.example_2: Idaṃ kiñcanaṃ [ime kiñcanā (ka.)] tuyhaṃ mā vijjittha mā pavijjittha mā saṃvijjittha pajaha vinodehi byantīkarohi anabhāvaṃ gamehīti – mā te vijjittha kiñcanaṃ.
pavijjittha.translation_2: This baggage—let it not be for you, not arrive for you, not exist for you; abandon it, cast it aside, make it to be gone, bring it to non-existence—this is “Let not such baggage be yours.”

jāguṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, listed in a string of synonyms for 'being' (satta, jana, nara, puggala, jīva). The PEU suggests an analysis jāti + gamu, but it is uncertain; possibly related to jantu.
jāguṃ.example_1: jantunti sattaṃ janaṃ naraṃ mānavaṃ posaṃ puggalaṃ jīvaṃ jāguṃ jantuṃ indaguṃ manujanti—
jāguṃ.example_2: Jantunti sattaṃ janaṃ naraṃ māṇavaṃ [mānavaṃ (syā.)] posaṃ puggalaṃ jīvaṃ jāguṃ jantuṃ indaguṃ manujanti – teneva māro anveti jantuṃ.
jāguṃ.translation_2: “The person” means the being, the man, the human, the fellow, the individual, the living being, the creature, the person, the mortal—this is the meaning of “by that, Māra follows the person.”

paṭivicāraṇaṃ.meaning_2: wandering about; roaming; going to and fro
paṭivicāraṇaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is part of a gloss explaining vicāraṇa: cāraṇaṃ vicāraṇaṃ paṭivicāraṇaṃ. Nominative singular neuter, in apposition.
paṭivicāraṇaṃ.example_1: kiṃsu tassa vicāraṇanti kiṃsu tassa cāraṇaṃ vicāraṇaṃ paṭivicāraṇaṃ.

paṭivicāraṇā.meaning_2: ranging over; turning over; reflection; consideration
paṭivicāraṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun from pati + vi + carati; listed among the nine vitakkas as vicāraṇā / paṭivicāraṇā. Nominative singular in the text.
paṭivicāraṇā.example_1: ime nava vitakkā lokassa cāraṇā vicāraṇā paṭivicāraṇā.

uparujjhatī.meaning_2: stops; comes to an end; ceases; is cut off
uparujjhatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present of upa + √rudh 1 (obstruct, stop). The text glosses it with nirujjhati, vūpasammati, atthaṃ gacchati, paṭippassambhati. In pada 2 the finite verb stands for a relative clause with yattha.
uparujjhatī.example_2: yattha nāmañca rūpañca, asesaṃ uparujjhatīti nāmanti cattāro arūpino khandhā.

antonimmuggaposīni.meaning_2: thriving (while) completely submerged (under water); growing underneath (the water's surface)
antonimmuggaposīni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads antonimuggaposīni (variant antonimuggaposīni); the entry takes the stem antonimuggaposī. Describes lotuses that grow entirely underwater, in contrast to those on the surface and those standing above the water. Here it is nominative plural neuter modifying uppalāni, padumāni, puṇḍarīkāni. The word is a compound of anto, nimugga, and posī.
antonimmuggaposīni.example_1: Seyyathāpi nāma uppaliniyaṃ vā paduminiyaṃ vā puṇḍarīkiniyaṃ vā appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakānuggatāni antonimuggaposīni [antonimmuggaposīni (ka.)], appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni samodakaṃ ṭhitāni, appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakā accuggamma tiṭṭhanti anupalittāni udakena;
antonimmuggaposīni.translation_1: Just as in a pool of blue, red, or white lotuses, some blue, red, or white lotuses are born in the water, thrive in the water, not rising above the water, thriving underwater; some blue, red, or white lotuses are born in the water, thrive in the water, resting on the water's surface; and some blue, red, or white lotuses are born in the water, thrive in the water, and stand lifted up far above the water, untouched by it;

samuhacca.meaning_2: having completely uprooted; having entirely removed; having destroyed
samuhacca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Glossed in the text by uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvā; variant reading uhacca samuhacca. Companion absolutive to ūhacca in the phrase attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhacca samuhacca.
samuhacca.example_1: Attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhaccāti attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhacca samūhacca [uhacca samuhacca (ka.) saddanītiyā pana sameti] uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvāti – attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhacca.
samuhacca.translation_1: “Having uprooted the identity-view” means having pulled up, completely pulled up, removed, completely removed, cleared, completely cleared, abandoned, dispelled, made an end of, and reduced to non-existence the identity-view—thus, ‘having uprooted the identity-view.’

mohamuho.meaning_2: deluded by ignorance; confused by delusion; one whose mouth is folly
mohamuho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A bahubbīhi compound, glossed in the text as moha-mukha: 'one whose mouth is delusion'. The reading momuho is likely a misreading for mohamuho. Nominative singular in the sentence.

ītijāte.meaning_2: afflicted with calamity; fallen into distress; beset by misfortune
ītijāte.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa passage it glosses santāpajāte, describing one afflicted by illness and calamity; locative singular in the text.
ītijāte.example_1: diṭṭhibyasanena dukkhena santāpajāte ītijāte upaddavajāte upasaggajāteti—
ītijāte.example_2: Santāpajāteti jātiyā santāpajāte, jarāya santāpajāte, byādhinā santāpajāte, maraṇena santāpajāte, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi santāpajāte, nerayikena dukkhena santāpajāte … pe … diṭṭhibyasanena dukkhena santāpajāte ītijāte upaddavajāte upasaggajāteti – santāpajāte.
ītijāte.translation_2: “Tormented” means: tormented by birth, tormented by decay, tormented by illness, tormented by death, tormented by sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair, tormented by the suffering of the hells... tormented by the suffering of wrong views; with illness that has arisen, with dangers that have arisen, with suffering that has arisen. This is the meaning of “tormented.”

uttānīākāsi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular aorist (with the ā augment) of uttānīkaroti, 'makes clear'; one item in a list of synonyms for byākāsi. Prefixed form of karoti, so the root fields are given; uttānī- corresponds to uttāna ('clear, plain') plus the denominative suffix -ī.
uttānīākāsi.example_1: pañhaṃ byākāsīti pañhaṃ byākāsi ācikkhi desesi paññapesi paṭṭhapesi vivari vibhaji uttānīākāsi pakāsesīti—
uttānīākāsi.example_2: Pañhaṃ byākāsīti pañhaṃ byākāsi ācikkhi desesi paññapesi paṭṭhapesi vivari vibhaji uttānīākāsi pakāsesīti – ajjhiṭṭho puṭṭho puṭṭho pañhaṃ byākāsi.
uttānīākāsi.translation_2: “Answered their questions” means he answered the question, explained, taught, prepared, established, opened up, analyzed, clarified, and proclaimed. Thus: “Having been requested, and having been asked repeatedly, he answered their questions.”

vitosesi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it appears as vitosesi, the aorist 3rd singular meaning 'gladdened; pleased; delighted'. The sekhiya passage glosses tosesi with tosesi vitosesi pasādesi ārādhesi attamane akāsi, treating the forms as synonyms. For the same passage the PEU gives vitoseti [vi+tusa+ṇe+ti], causative of √tus; the form is also written vitosesi.
vitosesi.example_1: tosesīti tosesi vitosesi pasādesi ārādhesi attamane akāsi.

vitositā.meaning_2: gladdened; caused to rejoice; satisfied; delighted
vitositā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used adjectivally in the Niddesa gloss; nominative plural masculine agreeing with tositā in the text.
vitositā.example_1: tositāti tositā vitositā pasāditā ārādhitā attamanā katāti—
vitositā.example_2: Tositāti tositā vitositā pasāditā ārādhitā attamanā katāti – te tositā.
vitositā.translation_2: “Delighted” means delighted, caused to rejoice, caused to be clear, satisfied, and made joyful—this is “delighted.”

vivano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it occurs in a string of epithets of the Buddha, probably glossing nibbāna from the root √van (desire/forest) with the prefix vi-. Nominative singular.
vivano.example_1: tasmā buddho avano vivano nibbano vanāpagato vanavippahīno vanavimutto sabbavanavītivattoti—
vivano.example_2: Tasmā buddho avano vivano nibbano vanāpagato vanavippahīno vanavimutto sabbavanavītivattoti – nibbano.
vivano.translation_2: Therefore the Buddha is without forest, free from forest, gone out, gone from the forest, has abandoned the forest, is freed from the forest, and has crossed over all forests—this is “gone out.”

nitthuriyakammaṃ.meaning_2: harsh act; act of harshness; cruel deed
nitthuriyakammaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading nitthuriyakammaṃ for niṭṭhuriyakammaṃ. Nominative singular in the text, listed as a synonym of makkha.
nitthuriyakammaṃ.example_1: Makkhoti yo makkho makkhāyanā makkhāyitattaṃ niṭṭhuriyaṃ niṭṭhuriyakammaṃ [nitthuriyakammaṃ (ka.) passa vibha.892]– ayaṃ vuccati makkho.
nitthuriyakammaṃ.translation_1: “Contempt” means: whatever contempt, disparaging, disparagement, harshness, or harsh act there is—this is called contempt.

paripañhitoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is part of an -ti quotation ending (paripañhito ti). Past participle used passively in a list of honours paid to the Buddha: āsito upāsito payirupāsito paripucchito paripañhito.
paripañhitoti.example_1: brahme upāsito meti so mayā bhagavā āsito upāsito payirupāsito paripucchito paripañhitoti—
paripañhitoti.example_2: Brahme upāsito meti so mayā bhagavā āsito upāsito payirupāsito paripucchito paripañhitoti – saccavhayo brahme upāsito me.
paripañhitoti.translation_2: “I have approached, O Brahmin” means that Blessed One has been approached, attended to, deeply attended to, questioned, and cross-examined by me — this is “rightly named, I have approached, O Brahmin”.

ītippahānaṃ.meaning_2: removal of calamity; elimination of danger; abandoning of distress
ītippahānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of īti (calamity, affliction) + pahāna (abandoning). In the text it is nominative singular in a list of epithets of Nibbāna.
ītippahānaṃ.example_1: ītippahānaṃ ītivūpasamaṃ ītipaṭinissaggaṃ ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—

ītivūpasamaṃ.meaning_2: calming of distress; appeasement of calamity; pacification of affliction
ītivūpasamaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, in a list of epithets of Nibbāna. Sometimes printed ītivūpassama; the second member is vūpasama (from upa + √sam 1).
