ītivūpasamaṃ.example_1: ītippahānaṃ ītivūpasamaṃ ītipaṭinissaggaṃ ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—

ītipaṭinissaggaṃ.meaning_2: relinquishment of calamity; abandoning of distress
ītipaṭinissaggaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text; part of a list of epithets of Nibbāna.
ītipaṭinissaggaṃ.example_1: ītippahānaṃ ītivūpasamaṃ ītipaṭinissaggaṃ ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—
ītipaṭinissaggaṃ.example_2: Ītippahānaṃ ītivūpasamaṃ ītipaṭinissaggaṃ ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti – taṇhakkhayamanītikaṃ.
ītipaṭinissaggaṃ.translation_2: The abandonment of trouble, the calming of trouble, the relinquishment of trouble, the complete cessation of trouble, the deathless Nibbāna — thus [it is] destruction of craving, free of trouble.

ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ.meaning_2: complete cessation of trouble; calming of misfortune
ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, in a list of epithets of Nibbāna. Sometimes written ītivūpasama in the same list. The related PEU entry gives ītipaṭippassaddhi as feminine.
ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ.example_1: ītippahānaṃ ītivūpasamaṃ ītipaṭinissaggaṃ ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—

natohamasmīti.meaning_2: not so I am not (such like that); I am not like that
natohamasmīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Quotation in the text breaks as na tiha maṃ iti, tiha being a particle variant of taha; sandhi chanda-vaṭṭa maybe uncertain, written natohamasmīti without spacing.

sampamuñcassu.meaning_2: release; let go; give up completely; place (faith)
sampamuñcassu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd singular imperative of sampamuñcati, glossed in the text by pamuñcassu, adhimuñcassu, okappehi; used with saddhaṃ in a series of synonyms.
sampamuñcassu.example_1: evameva tvampi pamuñcassu saddhanti evameva tvaṃ saddhaṃ muñcassu pamuñcassu sampamuñcassu adhimuñcassu okappehi.
sampamuñcassu.example_2: “sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā”ti saddhaṃ muñcassu pamuñcassu sampamuñcassu adhimuñcassu okappehi.

sammabhidevā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads sammabhidevā, a variant reading (syā.) for sammutidevā. Nominative plural in -ā in the list of three devas.
sammabhidevā.translation_1: “Devas” means there are three [types of] devas: conventional devas, born devas, and purity devas.

aphassi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the third verb of a series vedi / aññāsi / aphassi / paṭivijjhi, meaning 'knew, understood, experienced, penetrated'. The initial a- is the augment of the aorist, not a negative prefix (contrast aphassaka). Sinhala-script editions often read phassi.
aphassi.example_1: sabbaṃ vedi paroparanti bhagavā attano ca paresañca adhidevakare dhamme vedi aññāsi aphassi paṭivijjhi.
aphassi.example_2: evaṃ bhagavā attano ca paresañca adhidevakare dhamme vedi aññāsi aphassi paṭivijjhīti—

nidveḷahakā.meaning_2: free from duplicity; without deceit; not double-tongued
nidveḷahakā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative plural in the text, paired with sadveḷhaka (those who are duplicitous) and explained by nillekhā (settled). Probably a v.l. or commentarial formation for niddeḷhaka; the reading dveḷaha- for dveḷhaka- is uncertain.
nidveḷahakā.example_1: Kaṅkhīnaṃ paṭijānatanti sakaṅkhā āgantvā nikkaṅkhā sampajjanti, sallekhā āgantvā nillekhā sampajjanti, sadveḷhakā āgantvā nidveḷahakā sampajjanti, savicikicchā āgantvā nibbicikicchā sampajjanti, sarāgā āgantvā vītarāgā sampajjanti, sadosā āgantvā vītadosā sampajjanti, samohā āgantvā vītamohā sampajjanti, sakilesā āgantvā nikkilesā sampajjantīti – kaṅkhīnaṃ paṭijānataṃ.
nidveḷahakā.translation_1: “For those who are perplexed who acknowledge” means those who are perplexed come and become free of doubt, those who are scattered come and become settled, those who have two minds come and become of one mind, those who are in doubt come and become free of doubt, those who are full of lust come and become free of lust, those who are full of hatred come and become free of hatred, those who are full of delusion come and become free of delusion, those who are defiled come and become free of defilements—that is “for those who are perplexed who acknowledge.”

adduyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (ka.) for anduya/aruya, instrumental singular adduyā; the PEU gloss 'Knee' is doubtful.
adduyā.example_1: Aviheṭhayaṃ aññatarampi tesanti ekamekampi sattaṃ pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā anduyā [aruyā (syā.), adduyā (ka.)] vā rajjuyā vā aviheṭhayanto, sabbepi satte pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā anduyā vā rajjuyā vā aviheṭhayantoti – aviheṭhayaṃ aññatarampi tesaṃ.
adduyā.translation_1: “Not harming even one of them” means: not harming even one single being—whether with a hand, a clod, a staff, a blade, a snare, or a rope—not harming any of all beings with a hand, a clod, a staff, a blade, a snare, or a rope—this is “not harming even one of them.”

khiṭṭā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading khiṭṭā for khiḍḍā; the passage glosses it with ratī (delight). Nominative singular, subject of hoti.
khiṭṭā.example_1: 127. Khiḍḍā [khiṭṭā (ka.)] ratī hoti sahāyamajjhe , puttesu ca vipulaṃ hoti pemaṃ ;
khiṭṭā.translation_1: 127. There is playing and delight amidst companions, and there is great affection for children;

mukhabherukaṃ.meaning_2: mouth-drum; vocal drumming; making drum sounds with the mouth
mukhabherukaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of mukhakeraka in the Niddesa list of performing arts. Accusative singular in the text; part of a list of playful vocal and musical performances.
mukhabherukaṃ.example_1: Mukhabherikaṃ mukhālambaraṃ mukhaḍiṇḍimakaṃ [mukhadeṇḍimakaṃ (syā.), mukhadindimakaṃ (ka.)] mukhacalimakaṃ mukhakerakaṃ [mukhabherukaṃ (syā.)] mukhadaddarikaṃ nāṭakaṃ lāsaṃ gītaṃ davakammaṃ.
mukhabherukaṃ.translation_1: Making drum sounds with the mouth, blowing through the mouth, making trumpet sounds, tongue-clicking, making mouth-music, reciting poetry, acting, dancing, singing, and comedic skits.

hotiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text hotiṃ is a sandhi variant of hoti (before pemaṃ); the -ṃ belongs to the following word.
hotiṃ.example_1: Puttesu ca vipulaṃ hotiṃ pemanti puttesu ca adhimattaṃ hoti pemanti – puttesu ca vipulaṃ hoti pemaṃ.
hotiṃ.translation_1: “And there is great affection for children” means there is intense affection for children—and there is great affection for children.

appaṭikulā.meaning_2: not unpleasant; agreeable; pleasing; not repulsive
appaṭikulā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has appaṭikulā as a variant reading of appaṭikūlā, nominative plural agreeing with sattā. The na prefix has assimilated to the following p.
appaṭikulā.example_1: Cātuddiso appaṭigho ca hotīti mettāya bhāvitattā ye puratthimāya disāya sattā te appaṭikūlā [appaṭikulā (bahūsu)] honti, ye dakkhiṇāya disāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye pacchimāya disāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye uttarāya disāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye puratthimāya anudisāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye dakkhiṇāya anudisāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye pacchimāya anudisāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye uttarāya anudisāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye heṭṭhimāya disāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye uparimāya disāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye disāsu vidisāsu sattā te appaṭikūlā honti;
appaṭikulā.translation_1: “Global in outlook and unobstructed” means because he has developed loving-kindness, the beings in the east, south, west, north, and the intermediate directions, as well as those below and above, are not hindered; they are not obstructed.

paṭinissatāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Commentary gloss, nominative singular masculine agreeing with sahitā and listed with past participles ārādhitā, ajjhottharitā, pariyāditā. The -ti at the end is a quotation marker.
paṭinissatāti.example_1: parissayānaṃ sahitāti parissaye sahitā ārādhitā ajjhottharitā pariyāditā paṭinissatāti—
paṭinissatāti.example_2: Parissayānaṃ sahitāti parissaye sahitā ārādhitā ajjhottharitā pariyāditā paṭinissatāti – parissayānaṃ sahitā.
paṭinissatāti.translation_2: “Enduring troubles” means having endured, overcome, overwhelmed, depleted, and abandoned troubles—enduring troubles.

paṭipassambhayitvāti.meaning_2: having pacified; having calmed down; having subsided
paṭipassambhayitvāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Formation is doubtful: the Commentary glosses it with nikkhipitvā, so it is taken here as a causative absolutive of paṭipassambhati (√sambh 1), with the -aya- of the causative. The -ti belongs to the quotation (paṭipassambhayitvāti) and is not part of the word.
paṭipassambhayitvāti.example_1: oropayitvā gihibyañjanānīti gihibyañjanāni oropayitvā samoropayitvā nikkhipitvā paṭipassambhayitvāti—
paṭipassambhayitvāti.example_2: Oropayitvā gihibyañjanānīti gihibyañjanāni oropayitvā samoropayitvā nikkhipitvā paṭipassambhayitvāti – oropayitvā gihibyañjanāni.
paṭipassambhayitvāti.translation_2: “Having removed the attributes of the householder life” means having removed, thoroughly removed, laid down, and pacified the attributes of the householder life — that is 'having removed the attributes of the householder life'.

saṃhāyaṃ.meaning_2: companion who is wise; sagacious companion; intelligent friend
saṃhāyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is used as a gloss for nipakaṃ sahāyaṃ ('wise companion'), so it is treated here as an adjective. Could also be analysed as saha + aya, or as a commentarial variant of sahāya.
saṃhāyaṃ.example_1: Sace labhetha nipakaṃ sahāyanti sace nipakaṃ paṇḍitaṃ paññavantaṃ buddhimantaṃ ñāṇiṃ vibhāviṃ medhāviṃ sahāyaṃ labheyya paṭilabheyya adhigaccheyya vindeyyāti – sace labhetha nipakaṃ saṃhāyaṃ.
saṃhāyaṃ.translation_1: “If one should find a skillful companion” means if one should find, encounter, acquire, or experience a skillful, wise, intelligent, learned, knowledgeable, brilliant, and sagacious companion — that is 'if one should find a skillful companion'.

vīharaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads vīharaṃ, a variant of viharaṃ (present participle of viharati) with lengthened i; it agrees with the subject and means 'living, dwelling'. It is glossed alternatively as vihare, an optative.
vīharaṃ.translation_1: Lives in the wilderness as long as he wants, one should wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.

abhivajjetvā.meaning_2: having avoided; having shunned; having abandoned
abhivajjetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text glossing vivajjayitvā alongside parivajjetvā and abhinivajjetvā; absolutive in -tvā.
abhivajjetvā.example_1: nāgova yūthāni vivajjayitvāti yathā so hatthināgo yūthāni vivajjetvā parivajjetvā abhinivajjetvā ekova araññavanamajjhogāhetvā carati viharati iriyati vatteti pāleti yapeti yāpeti, paccekasambuddhopi gaṇaṃ vivajjetvā parivajjetvā abhivajjetvā eko araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevati appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni.
abhivajjetvā.example_2: Nāgova yūthāni vivajjayitvāti yathā so hatthināgo yūthāni vivajjetvā parivajjetvā abhinivajjetvā ekova araññavanamajjhogāhetvā [araññe vanamajjhassa ajjhogāhetvā (syā.)] carati viharati iriyati vatteti pāleti yapeti yāpeti, paccekasambuddhopi gaṇaṃ vivajjetvā parivajjetvā abhivajjetvā eko [eko care khaggavisāṇakappo (syā.)] araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevati appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni.
abhivajjetvā.translation_2: “Like an elephant, having abandoned the herds” — just as an elephant, having abandoned the herds, repeatedly avoiding, and constantly avoiding them, plunged into the forest, wanders, dwells, conducts itself, operates, keeps, lives, and survives, so too does a Solitary Awakened One, having abandoned the group, repeatedly avoiding, and constantly avoiding it, alone frequent the forest wildernesses, remote resting places, free from noise, free from sound, with their atmosphere devoid of people, appropriately secluded for resting undisturbed by human beings, and appropriate for seclusion.

āpātakajjhāyī.meaning_2: seeming to be absorbed in meditation; one who is like a meditator
āpātakajjhāyī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has āpāthakajjhāyī, but the variant reading āpātakajjhāyī (as given) is chosen. A compound describing someone who only appears to be meditating. The ending -ī is adjectival, referring to a person.
āpātakajjhāyī.example_1: Idhekacco pāpiccho icchāpakato sambhāvanādhippāyo ‘‘ evaṃ maṃ jano sambhāvessatī ’’ ti gamanaṃ saṇṭhapeti ṭhānaṃ saṇṭhapeti nisajjaṃ [nisajjanaṃ (ka.)] saṇṭhapeti sayanaṃ saṇṭhapeti, paṇidhāya gacchati paṇidhāya tiṭṭhati paṇidhāya nisīdati paṇidhāya seyyaṃ kappeti samāhito viya gacchati samāhito viya tiṭṭhati samāhito viya nisīdati samāhito viya seyyaṃ kappeti, āpāthakajjhāyīva [āpātakajjhāyī ca (ka.)] hoti.
āpātakajjhāyī.translation_1: Here, some person with evil desires, overwhelmed by greed, desiring to be admired, sets up his walking, sets up his standing, sets up his sitting, sets up his lying down; he walks having directed, stands having directed, sits having directed, lies down having directed, walks like someone composed, stands like someone composed, sits like someone composed, lies down like someone composed, and acts as one in meditative absorption.

saṃvantā.meaning_2: fully vomited; completely ejected; spewed out
saṃvantā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative plural masculine, qualifying makkho, kasāvo and moho: 'makkho ca ... moho ca ... vantā saṃvantā ...'. The PEU suggests saṃ + vamita, but the form is probably a prefix saṃ + vanta (pp of vamati), meaning 'fully vomited out'. The sandhi form saṃvantā is used.
saṃvantā.example_1: tassa paccekasambuddhassa makkho ca kasāvo ca moho ca vantā saṃvantā niddhantā pahīnā samucchinnā vūpasantā paṭippassaddhā abhabbuppattikā ñāṇagginā daḍḍhāti.

tannino.meaning_2: inclined to that; disposed towards that; bent on that
tannino.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the nominative singular form is tannino; the compound repeats the demonstrative taṃ of the preceding series (taccarito ... tadadhipateyyo), pointing back to kāme.
tannino.example_1: Pasutanti yopi kāme esati gavesati pariyesati taccarito tabbahulo taggaruko tannino tappoṇo tappabbhāro tadadhimutto tadadhipateyyo, sopi kāmappasuto.
tannino.translation_1: ‘Engaged’ means: whoever searches for, seeks, and hunts for sensual pleasures, and is thus behaving, is thus habituated, is thus attentive, is thus inclined, is thus leaning, is thus leaning toward, is thus resolved, is thus subjected — he is engaged in sensuality.

saṃbhajeyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular. In the text it glosses 'bhajeyya' as one of a series of near-synonyms (bhajeyya, seveyya, niseveyya, saṃseveyya, paṭiseveyya). Causative form, so the -e- before the optative ending.
saṃbhajeyya.example_1: Bahussutaṃ dhammadharaṃ bhajethāti bahussutañca dhammadharañca mittaṃ bhajeyya saṃbhajeyya seveyya niseveyya saṃseveyya paṭiseveyyāti – bahussutaṃ dhammadharaṃ bhajetha.
saṃbhajeyya.translation_1: “You should follow a learned one, a holder of the Dhamma” means you should follow, associate with, serve, wait upon, keep company with, retreat with a friend who is both learned and a holder of the Dhamma — therefore one should follow a learned one, a holder of the Dhamma.

vibhūsaṇaṭṭhānā.meaning_2: place of adornment; occasion for decoration; cause of ornamentation
vibhūsaṇaṭṭhānā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative singular (or possibly a contraction of vibhūsanāya ṭhānā) in the verses; v.l. vibhūsaṭṭhānā, vibhūsanaṭṭhānā. Means grounds for adorning oneself, which one abstains from.
vibhūsaṇaṭṭhānā.example_1: Vibhūsaṭṭhānā [vibhūsanaṭṭhānā (syā. ka.), vibhūsaṇaṭṭhānā (sī. aṭṭha.)] virato saccavādī , eko care khaggavisāṇakappo .
vibhūsaṇaṭṭhānā.translation_1: Renounced from places of adornment, speaker of the truth, one should wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.

gaddhikatā.meaning_2: state of being greedy (for); craving; longing; attachment
gaddhikatā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Listed in a pejorative series describing anāgārikavibhūsā (homeless vanity); variant reading gedhikatā. Nominative singular in the text.
gaddhikatā.example_1: cīvaramaṇḍanā pattamaṇḍanā senāsanamaṇḍanā imassa vā pūtikāyassa bāhirānaṃ vā parikkhārānaṃ maṇḍanā vibhūsanā keḷanā parikeḷanā gaddhikatā gaddhikattaṃ capalatā cāpalyaṃ—
gaddhikatā.example_2: Cīvaramaṇḍanā pattamaṇḍanā senāsanamaṇḍanā imassa vā pūtikāyassa bāhirānaṃ vā parikkhārānaṃ maṇḍanā vibhūsanā keḷanā parikeḷanā gaddhikatā gaddhikattaṃ [gedhikatā gedhikattaṃ (syā.) passa vibha.854] capalatā [capalanā (syā.)] cāpalyaṃ – ayaṃ anāgārikavibhūsā.
gaddhikatā.translation_2: Decoration of robes, decoration of the bowl, decoration of the lodging, decoration of this corpse-body or of external items, adornment, decoration, playing, playing in every way, yearning, bondage, frivolity, vanity — this is homeless adornment.

khetrajo.meaning_2: field-born son; son born from the field (i.e. of a wife of lower status); illegitimate son
khetrajo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternative spelling (with r) of khettaja in the list of four kinds of sons; nominative singular in the text. The Thai edition reads khettajo.
khetrajo.example_1: Puttāti cattāro puttā – atrajo putto, khettajo [khetrajo (syā. ka.)] putto, dinnako putto, antevāsiko putto.
khetrajo.translation_1: “Sons” means there are four types of sons: the legitimate son, the field-born son, the adopted son, and the pupil son.

paṭippassambhitvāti.meaning_2: having calmed down; having become quiet; having subsided
paṭippassambhitvāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is followed by the enclitic -ti: paṭippassambhitvāti = paṭippassambhitvā + iti.
paṭippassambhitvāti.example_1: oropayitvā samoropayitvā nikkhipitvā paṭippassambhitvāti sabbesu bhūtesu nidhāya daṇḍaṃ.
paṭippassambhitvāti.example_2: ohārayitvā gihibyañjanānīti gihibyañjanāni oropayitvā samoropayitvā nikkhipitvā paṭippassambhitvāti—

akuṭakaṃ.meaning_2: not bitter; free from bitterness; (what is) not acrid
akuṭakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Negative compound (na + kaṭuka, 'not bitter'); accusative singular neuter agreeing with the contrasted kaṭukaṃ. The na- prefix becomes a- before a consonant.
akuṭakaṃ.example_1: kaṭukaṃ labhitvā akuṭakaṃ pariyesanti, akuṭakaṃ labhitvā kaṭukaṃ pariyesanti;

udakummikajātaṃ.meaning_2: become like a water-wave; continuous like waves on water
udakummikajātaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant udakūmikajāta; explained in the gloss as poṅkhānupoṅkhaṃ, i.e. continuous, wave upon wave. Nominative singular agreeing with dhammesu? no, with the practitioner; neuter/accusative usage uncertain, listed as adj.
udakummikajātaṃ.example_1: Dhammesu niccaṃ anudhammacārīti dhammesu niccakālaṃ dhuvakālaṃ satataṃ samitaṃ avokiṇṇaṃ poṅkhānupoṅkhaṃ udakūmikajātaṃ [udakummijātaṃ (syā.), udakummikajātaṃ (ka.)]
udakummikajātaṃ.translation_1: “Constantly living in conformity with the Teaching” means, regarding those teachings, constantly, continuously, persistently, and without a break, one after another, like the waves on water,

paṭinisaṭṭhattā.meaning_2: state of having relinquished; state of having given up; detachment
paṭinisaṭṭhattā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative singular in -ā (paṭinisaṭṭhattā); abstract noun formed from the past participle paṭinisaṭṭha (relinquished, given up) + -tta, used here with diṭṭhilepa (taint of views).
paṭinisaṭṭhattā.example_1: taṇhālepassa pahīnattā diṭṭhilepassa paṭinisaṭṭhattā so paccekasambuddho rūpe na limpati sadde na limpati …pe…
paṭinisaṭṭhattā.example_2: Taṇhālepassa pahīnattā diṭṭhilepassa paṭinisaṭṭhattā so paccekasambuddho rūpe na limpati sadde na limpati … pe … diṭṭhasutamutaviññātabbesu dhammesu na limpati na palimpati na upalimpati, alitto apalitto anupalitto nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā viharatīti – padumaṃva toyena alimpamāno, eko care khaggavisāṇakappo.
paṭinisaṭṭhattā.translation_2: Because the taint of craving is abandoned and the taint of views is relinquished, that Solitary Awakened One does not taint forms, does not taint sounds… does not taint things seen, heard, sensed, and cognized, he does not taint, does not smear, does not adhere, untainted, undefiled, and untarnished; emerging, escaped, released, and detached, he dwells with a mind that has no limits—this is “like a lotus not soiled by water, one should wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.”

iccā.meaning_2: having come; having arrived; thus; so
iccā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Usually written with the emphatic particle -ā as iccā; the entry is for the bare absolutive. In the text it introduces a quotation or explanation.
iccā.example_1: iccāti padasandhi padasaṃsaggo padapāripūrī akkharasamavāyo byañjanasiliṭṭhatā padānupubbatāpetaṃ iccāti.

brūsī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd person singular of brūti, used in the gloss brūsi ācikkhasi ...; the text's brūsī (with ī) is the same form under sandhi or mètre. The PEU notes the spelling brūsi.
brūsī.example_1: kissābhilepanaṃ brūsīti kiṃ lokassa lepanaṃ lagganaṃ bandhanaṃ upakkileso.
brūsī.example_2: brūsīti brūsi ācikkhasi desesi paññapesi paṭṭhapesi vivarasi vibhajasi uttānīkarosi pakāsesīti—

mahabbhayan.meaning_2: great fear; great danger; great peril
mahabbhayan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative singular, glossed by bhayaṃ mahabbhayaṃ in the Niddesa. Sometimes treated as masculine.
mahabbhayan.example_1: kiṃsu tassa mahabbhayanti kiṃ lokassa bhayaṃ mahabbhayaṃ pīḷanaṃ ghaṭṭanaṃ upaddavo upasaggoti—

brūmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 1st person singular brūmi, used in the text as an author's declaration, 'I say; I call'. Forms of √brū replace the root with brū- (brūmi, brūma, brūhi); related to bravīti.
brūmī.example_2: sotānaṃ saṃvaraṃ brūmīti sotānaṃ āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ saṃvaraṇaṃ rakkhanaṃ gopanaṃ brūmi ācikkhāmi …pe… uttānīkaromi pakāsemīti—

dukkhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written dukkhan before ti (dukkhanti); the niggahīta is represented by n. Neuter accusative singular used as a quoted term in the Niddesa gloss.
dukkhan.example_1: dukkhanti jātidukkhaṃ jarādukkhaṃ byādhidukkhaṃ maraṇadukkhaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadukkhaṃ nerayikaṃ dukkhaṃ tiracchānayonikaṃ dukkhaṃ pettivisayikaṃ dukkhaṃ mānusikaṃ dukkhaṃ gabbhokkantimūlakaṃ dukkhaṃ gabbhaṭṭhitimūlakaṃ dukkhaṃ gabbhavuṭṭhānamūlakaṃ dukkhaṃ jātassūpanibandhakaṃ dukkhaṃ jātassa parādheyyakaṃ dukkhaṃ attūpakkamaṃ dukkhaṃ parūpakkamaṃ dukkhaṃ saṅkhāradukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadukkhaṃ cakkhurogo sotarogo ghānarogo jivhārogo kāyarogo sīsarogo kaṇṇarogo mukharogo dantarogo kāso sāso pināso ḍāho jaro kucchirogo mucchā pakkhandikā sūlā visūcikā kuṭṭhaṃ gaṇḍo kilāso soso apamāro daddu kaṇḍu kacchu rakhasā vitacchikā lohitapittaṃ madhumeho aṃsā piḷakā bhagandalā pittasamuṭṭhānā ābādhā semhasamuṭṭhānā ābādhā vātasamuṭṭhānā ābādhā sannipātikā ābādhā utupariṇāmajā ābādhā visamaparihārajā ābādhā opakkamikā ābādhā kammavipākajā ābādhā sītaṃ uṇhaṃ jighacchā pipāsā uccāro passāvo ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassaṃ dukkhaṃ mātumaraṇaṃ dukkhaṃ pitumaraṇaṃ dukkhaṃ bhātumaraṇaṃ dukkhaṃ bhaginimaraṇaṃ dukkhaṃ puttamaraṇaṃ dukkhaṃ dhītumaraṇaṃ dukkhaṃ ñātibyasanaṃ dukkhaṃ rogabyasanaṃ dukkhaṃ bhogabyasanaṃ dukkhaṃ sīlabyasanaṃ dukkhaṃ diṭṭhibyasanaṃ dukkhaṃ yesaṃ dhammānaṃ ādito samudāgamanaṃ paññāyati.
dukkhan.example_2: jātiṃ jaraṃ sokapariddavañca, idheva vidvā pajaheyya dukkhanti.

nivāraṇan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] This is the form nivāraṇaṃ with the final nasal left unassimilated before ti (nivāraṇanti); neuter nominative singular. In the text it glosses āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ saṃvaraṇaṃ rakkhanaṃ gopanaṃ.
nivāraṇan.example_1: sotānaṃ kiṃ nivāraṇanti sotānaṃ kiṃ āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ saṃvaraṇaṃ rakkhanaṃ gopananti—

brūhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form brūhī is the 2nd person singular imperative of brūti (with the imperative ending -hi). In the passage it is glossed by ācikkha, desa, paññapehi etc.: 'tell, explain'. Used in the sense of 'preach, proclaim'.
brūhī.example_1: sotānaṃ saṃvaraṃ brūhīti sotānaṃ āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ saṃvaraṇaṃ rakkhanaṃ gopanaṃ brūhi ācikkha desehi paññapehi paṭṭhapehi vivarāhi vibhajāhi uttānīkarohi pakāsehīti—
brūhī.example_2: aññaṃ taṃ pucchāma tadiṅgha brūhīti aññaṃ taṃ pucchāma, aññaṃ taṃ yācāma, aññaṃ taṃ ajjhesāma, aññaṃ taṃ pasādema, uttari taṃ pucchāma.

lokasmin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, with the sandhi -smin (-smiṃ). In the Niddesa gloss it is defined as apāyaloka, manussaloka, devaloka, khandhaloka, dhātuloka, āyatanaloka.
lokasmin.example_1: yāni sotāni lokasminti yāni etāni sotāni mayā kittitāni pakittitāni ācikkhitāni desitāni paññapitāni paṭṭhapitāni vivaritāni vibhajitāni uttānīkatāni pakāsitāni, seyyathidaṃ—
lokasmin.example_2: lokasminti apāyaloke manussaloke devaloke khandhaloke dhātuloke āyatanaloketi—

cāpī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the sandhi form ca + api, often written cāpi. Here spelled cāpī, likely for metrical reasons. In sentence 1, ca + api fits the context better than a noun meaning 'bow'. It appears in the stock list of castes and people.
cāpī.example_2: te cāpīti khattiyā ca brāhmaṇā ca vessā ca suddā ca gahaṭṭhā ca pabbajitā ca devā ca manussā ca.

nāman.meaning_2: name; designation; mental phenomenon; mentality; the four immaterial aggregates
nāman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa passages nāman is glossed both as the four immaterial aggregates and as name/designation. Accusative singular nāmaṃ appears in the quoted verse; the entry form nāman is the stem. The PEU entry derives nāma from √nam with the suffix -a, but the stem nāman is the citation form here.
nāman.example_2: yattha nāmañca rūpañca, asesaṃ uparujjhatīti nāmanti cattāro arūpino khandhā.

rūpan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In these sentences rūpa refers to physical form or matter; the text form rūpan is a sandhi variant of rūpaṃ before ti. The PEU entry connects it to √rūp (form, produce).
rūpan.example_1: rūpanti cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpaṃ.
rūpan.example_2: jahassu rūpanti jahassu rūpaṃ, pajahassu rūpaṃ, vinodehi rūpaṃ, byantīkarohi rūpaṃ, anabhāvaṃ gamehi rūpaṃ.

pabrūhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative 2nd singular, glossed in the text with brūhi, ācikkhāhi, paññapehi etc. The text's pabrūhīti = pabrūhi + iti.
pabrūhī.example_2: pabrūhīti brūhi ācikkhāhi desehi paññapehi paṭṭhapehi vivarāhi vibhajāhi uttānīkarohi pakāsehīti—

yametan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text yametan is a sandhi of yameti + iti (the -ti being the quotative). The word quoted is yameti, 3rd singular causative present. The PEU entry suggests a causative of √yam; the meaning 'restrains, controls' fits the causative sense best.

vadāmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular present in the text (vadāmi), but lemma is the present 3rd singular. In the second sentence 'idaṃ vadāmi' means 'I call this'. The first sentence glosses vadāmi with ācikkhāmi etc.
vadāmī.example_1: vadāmīti vadāmi ācikkhāmi desemi paññapemi paṭṭhapemi vivarāmi vibhajāmi uttānīkaromi pakāsemīti—
vadāmī.example_2: idaṃ vadāmīti idaṃ vadāmi, etaṃ vadāmi, ettakaṃ vadāmi, ettāvatā vadāmi, idaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ vadāmi—

asesan.meaning_2: without remainder; without residue; complete; total; leaving nothing left
asesan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text asesaṃ (accusative singular, m/f/nt, agreeing with sabbaṃ) is glossed in the Niddesa by nissesaṃ pariyādiyanavacanaṃ, "without residue, a term of total exhaustion". Often in the phrase asesaṃ (adv.), "entirely". Accusative singular in the text.
asesan.example_1: asesanti sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ asesaṃ nissesaṃ pariyādiyanavacanametaṃ asesanti.
asesan.example_2: Asesanti sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ asesaṃ nissesaṃ pariyādiyanavacanametaṃ [pariyādāyavacanametaṃ (syā. ka.)] asesanti.
asesan.translation_2: “Without remainder” means entirely, totally, in every way, without residue, without exception; this is a term that encompasses everything.

idhā.meaning_2: here; in this world; in this teaching
idhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written idhā before ti. The gloss explains it as 'in this view ... in this human world'. A sandhi form of idha + ti.
idhā.example_1: ye ca saṅkhātadhammāse, ye ca sekhā puthū idhāti.
idhā.example_2: idhāti imissā diṭṭhiyā imissā khantiyā imissā ruciyā imasmiṃ ādāye imasmiṃ dhamme imasmiṃ vinaye imasmiṃ dhammavinaye imasmiṃ pāvacane imasmiṃ brahmacariye imasmiṃ satthusāsane imasmiṃ attabhāve imasmiṃ manussaloketi—

sabbadhammānan.meaning_2: all phenomena; all things; all states
sabbadhammānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text sabbadhammānaṃ (genitive plural) is written sabbadhammānan before ti. Occurs in the phrase kusalo sabbadhammānaṃ and in the epithet pāragū sabbadhammānaṃ.
sabbadhammānan.example_2: pāraguṃ sabbadhammānanti bhagavā sabbadhammānaṃ abhiññāpāragū pariññāpāragū pahānapāragū bhāvanāpāragū sacchikiriyāpāragū samāpattipāragū.

ubhantamabhiññāyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ubhantaṃ (accusative singular of ubhanta, nt) and abhiññāya, the absolutive of abhijānāti. The commentary explains it as ubho ante abhiññāya jānitvā. Quoted and glossed in the text.
ubhantamabhiññāyā.example_1: ko ubhantamabhiññāyāti ko ubho ante abhiññāya jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvāti—
ubhantamabhiññāyā.example_2: Ko ubhantamabhiññāyāti ko ubho ante abhiññāya jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvāti – ko ubhantamabhiññāya.
ubhantamabhiññāyā.translation_2: “Who, having directly known the two extremes” means: who, having directly known, having known, having calculated, having judged, having clarified, and having made evident the two extremes—this is the meaning of “Who, having directly known the two extremes.”

saṅkhāyā.meaning_2: having calculated; having considered; having discriminated; having comprehended
saṅkhāyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text saṅkhāyāti = saṅkhāya + iti, the -ti of the quotation being sandhied to -yā. The gloss explains it with jānitvā, tulayitvā, tīrayitvā, vibhāvayitvā. PEU takes it from sa + khā + tvā.
saṅkhāyā.example_1: saṅkhāyāti saṅkhāya jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā, “sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā”ti saṅkhāya jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā,
saṅkhāyā.example_2: Saṅkhāyāti saṅkhāya jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā,‘‘ sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā ’’ ti saṅkhāya jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā,‘‘ sabbe saṅkhārā dukkhā ’’ ti … pe …‘‘ sabbe dhammā anattā ’’ ti …‘‘ avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā ’’ ti …‘‘ yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamman ’’ ti saṅkhāya jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā.
saṅkhāyā.translation_2: “Through reflection” means: having investigated through reflection, having known, having calculated, having judged, having clarified, and having made evident that “all volitional formations are impermanent,” having known, having calculated, having judged, having clarified, and having made evident that “all volitional formations are suffering,” that “all phenomena are non-self,” that “with ignorance as condition, volitional formations arise,” ... that “whatever is subject to origination, all that is subject to cessation,” having known, having calculated, having judged, having clarified, and having made evident.

mūladassāvin.meaning_2: seeing the root; knowing the root cause; who sees the origin
mūladassāvin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound of mūla and dassāvī (from √dis 1). In the text it describes the Buddha (bhagavā), who sees the root, the cause, the origin, etc. The form is the nominative singular; the quote anejaṃ mūladassāvin shows the same stem with -i, a variant ending.
mūladassāvin.example_2: mūladassāvinti bhagavā mūladassāvī hetudassāvī nidānadassāvī sambhavadassāvī pabhavadassāvī samuṭṭhānadassāvī āhāradassāvī ārammaṇadassāvī paccayadassāvī samudayadassāvī.

āgaman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written without the final vowel before 'ti' (āgaman-ti) for sandhi. It occurs in the phrase 'atthi pañhena āgamanaṃ', meaning 'there is a coming (arrival) with a question' — i.e., 'is there a purpose in your coming?'. Part of āgama family.
āgaman.example_1: atthi pañhena āgamanti pañhena atthiko āgatomhi, pañhaṃ pucchitukāmo āgatomhi, pañhaṃ sotukāmo āgatomhīti—
āgaman.example_2: atthi pañhena āgamanti pañhena atthiko āgatomhi, pañhaṃ pucchitukāmo āgatomhi, pañhaṃ sotukāmo āgatomhīti, evampi atthi pañhena āgamaṃ.

devatānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text devatānan is genitive plural (devatānaṃ), the form before ti showing the niggahīta. The Niddesa passage explains that people regard whatever they are devoted to (ājīvakas, nigaṇṭhas, animals, gods) as their devatā.
devatānan.example_2: devatānanti ājīvakasāvakānaṃ ājīvakā devatā, nigaṇṭhasāvakānaṃ nigaṇṭhā devatā, jaṭilasāvakānaṃ jaṭilā devatā, paribbājakasāvakānaṃ paribbājakā devatā, aviruddhakasāvakānaṃ aviruddhakā devatā, hatthivatikānaṃ hatthī devatā, assavatikānaṃ assā devatā, govatikānaṃ gāvo devatā, kukkuravatikānaṃ kukkurā devatā, kākavatikānaṃ kākā devatā, vāsudevavatikānaṃ vāsudevo devatā, baladevavatikānaṃ baladevo devatā, puṇṇabhaddavatikānaṃ puṇṇabhaddo devatā, maṇibhaddavatikānaṃ maṇibhaddo devatā, aggivatikānaṃ aggi devatā, nāgavatikānaṃ nāgā devatā, supaṇṇavatikānaṃ supaṇṇā devatā, yakkhavatikānaṃ yakkhā devatā, asuravatikānaṃ asurā devatā, gandhabbavatikānaṃ gandhabbā devatā, mahārājavatikānaṃ mahārājāno devatā, candavatikānaṃ cando devatā, sūriyavatikānaṃ sūriyo devatā, indavatikānaṃ indo devatā, brahmavatikānaṃ brahmā devatā, devavatikānaṃ devo devatā, disāvatikānaṃ disā devatā, ye yesaṃ dakkhiṇeyyā te tesaṃ devatāti—

yaññamakappayiṃsū.meaning_2: they prepared a sacrifice; they arranged a sacrificial offering; they made (it) a sacrifice
yaññamakappayiṃsū.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yaññaṃ + akappayiṃsu (aorist 3rd plural of kappeti). The Niddesa glosses it as yaññaṃ kappenti and, in the third quote, as jarānissitā etc. The -ti is a quotation marker and is not part of the word.
yaññamakappayiṃsū.example_1: yaññamakappayiṃsūti yepi yaññaṃ esanti gavesanti pariyesanti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ, tepi yaññaṃ kappenti.
yaññamakappayiṃsū.example_2: yaññamakappayiṃsūti yepi yaññaṃ esanti gavesanti pariyesanti …pe… seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ, tepi yaññaṃ kappenti.

metan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of me (enclitic dative/genitive of ahaṃ) and etaṃ (nominative/accusative neuter of eta). In the text brūhi metan ti = "tell me this". The n is the sandhi consonant before ti.
metan.example_2: brūhi metanti brūhi ācikkhāhi desehi paññapehi paṭṭhapehi vivarāhi vibhajāhi uttānīkarohi pakāsehīti—

itthattan.meaning_2: this state of existence; the state of being thus; this life; this present condition
itthattan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form itthattan is the sandhi of itthattaṃ before ti. In the Niddesa it glosses attabhāvābhinibbatti, the production of a state of being.
itthattan.example_2: puṇṇaka itthattanti ettha attabhāvābhinibbattiṃ āsīsamānā ettha khattiyamahāsālakule attabhāvābhinibbattiṃ āsīsamānā …pe…

kaccisū.meaning_2: perhaps; I wonder; surely not; question (of doubt)
kaccisū.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text kaccisū is kacci + su, the enclitic su being a quotation marker? Actually the sandhi is kacci + iti > kaccīti? But the form kaccisū is glossed as a question expressing doubt, so the lemma is kacci and the -sū is part of an old sandhi or emphatic particle; see comment. Here it introduces synonyms for a doubtful question (saṃsayapucchā etc.).

thomayantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form thomayantī is quoted in the text, possibly as an accusative singular of a present participle thomayanta (praising) or as a variant reading for thomayanti (3rd plural present). The sentence glosses it with the 3rd plural thomenti. Causative of thomati.
thomayantī.example_1: thomayantīti yaññaṃ vā thomenti phalaṃ vā thomenti dakkhiṇeyye vā thomenti.

abhijappantī.meaning_2: desires; wishes for; prays for; longs for
abhijappantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form abhijappantī is a sandhi of abhijappanti + iti. The gloss explains it with āsīsanti and thomayanti.
abhijappantī.example_1: abhijappantīti rūpapaṭilābhaṃ abhijappanti, saddapaṭilābhaṃ abhijappanti, gandhapaṭilābhaṃ abhijappanti, rasapaṭilābhaṃ abhijappanti …pe…
abhijappantī.example_2: Abhijappantīti rūpapaṭilābhaṃ abhijappanti, saddapaṭilābhaṃ abhijappanti, gandhapaṭilābhaṃ abhijappanti, rasapaṭilābhaṃ abhijappanti … pe … brahmakāyikesu devesu attabhāvapaṭilābhaṃ abhijappantīti – āsīsanti thomayanti abhijappanti.
abhijappantī.translation_2: ‘They pray to’ means they desire the acquisition of form, they desire the acquisition of sound... they desire the acquisition of individuality in the realm of the Brahmā-hosts—this is the meaning of ‘they hope, they praise, they pray to.’

lābhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (lābhan = lābhaṃ, sandhi before ti). Explained in the Niddesa gloss by paṭilābha, acquisition; often paired with kāma (kāmābhijappanti paṭicca lābhaṃ).
lābhan.example_1: kāmābhijappanti paṭicca lābhanti rūpapaṭilābhaṃ paṭicca kāme abhijappanti, saddapaṭilābhaṃ paṭicca kāme abhijappanti …pe…
lābhan.example_2: Kāmābhijappanti paṭicca lābhanti rūpapaṭilābhaṃ paṭicca kāme abhijappanti, saddapaṭilābhaṃ paṭicca kāme abhijappanti … pe … brahmakāyikesu devesu attabhāvapaṭilābhaṃ paṭicca kāme abhijappanti pajappantīti – kāmābhijappanti paṭicca lābhaṃ.
lābhan.translation_2: ‘They pray to sensual pleasures dependent on gain’ means they pray to sensual pleasures for the acquisition of form... they pray to sensual pleasures for the acquisition of individuality in the realm of the Brahmā-hosts; they wish for, they greatly wish for them—this is the meaning of ‘they pray to sensual pleasures dependent on gain.’

yaññehī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental plural in the text (yaññehi), with -īti sandhi from yaññehi iti; glossed by yaññehi pahūtehi etc.
yaññehī.example_1: yaññehīti yaññehi pahūtehi yaññehi vividhehi yaññehi puthūhi.

paroparānī.meaning_2: others and (these); other and (this); beyond and (this side)
paroparānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa the word is analysed as paroparāni, neuter plural of ”para” + ”upara” (= beyond and this side), glossed by aniccato dukkhato etc. Written paroparāni after sandhi of -a + u-. The text's ”paroparānī” shows a niggahīta before ti; possible alternative analysis: para + upara in the sense of ”higher and lower”. Locative absolute in the verse quotation.
paroparānī.example_1: saṅkhāya lokasmi paroparānīti saṅkhā vuccati ñāṇaṃ yā paññā pajānanā …pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi.

iñjitan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text as iñjitan (sandhi of iñjitaṃ before ti). Used in a word-play on taṇhā, diṭṭhi, māna, kilesa and kāma. The quotation mark joined to the word is dropped in lemma_1.

kuhiñcī.meaning_2: anywhere; in something; in anything whatsoever
kuhiñcī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi form of kuhiñci before a vowel, quoted and glossed in the text as kuhiñci kismiñci katthaci, 'anywhere, in something, in anything'. Also occurs in the verse tasmā munī natthi khilo kuhiñci. See kuhiñci.
kuhiñcī.example_1: kuhiñcīti kuhiñci kismiñci katthaci ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā ajjhattabahiddhā vā.

pucchāmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 1st person singular present of pucchati, ending -mi. In the Niddesa it introduces a quotation and is glossed with the three kinds of questions (pucchā).
pucchāmī.example_2: Pucchāmīti tisso pucchā – adiṭṭhajotanā pucchā, diṭṭhasaṃsandanā pucchā, vimaticchedanā pucchā.
pucchāmī.translation_2: ‘I ask’ — there are three types of questions: the question illuminating the unseen, the question verifying what is seen, and the question cutting off doubt.

bhāvitattan.meaning_2: with a developed self; with a cultivated mind; whose self is developed
bhāvitattan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the compound appears as bhāvitattan, the accusative singular of the adjective used to describe the vedagū. Sometimes analysed as bhāvita + atta (developed self) rather than attan; the meaning is the same.
bhāvitattan.translation_2: ‘I think him a knowledge master with a composed mind’.

pajānan.meaning_2: knowing; understanding; discerning; penetrating with wisdom
pajānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form pajānan is the lengthened sandhi variant of pajānanto, nominative singular masculine of the present participle. The commentarial gloss explains it with ājānanto vijānanto paṭivijānanto.
pajānan.example_2: yathā pajānanti yathā pajānanto ājānanto vijānanto paṭivijānanto paṭivijjhanto.

karotī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present 3rd singular. In the text, karotīti is karoti + iti; the final ī is sandhi. The word is used with upadhiṃ (upadhiṃ karoti) meaning 'makes a basis' or 'creates a support', and with nissayaṃ (nissayaṃ na karoti) meaning 'does not make a dependence'.
karotī.example_2: upadhiṃ karotīti taṇhūpadhiṃ karoti, diṭṭhūpadhiṃ karoti, kilesūpadhiṃ karoti, kammūpadhiṃ karoti, duccaritūpadhiṃ karoti, āhārūpadhiṃ karoti, paṭighūpadhiṃ karoti, catasso upādinnadhātuyo upadhī karoti, cha ajjhattikāni āyatanāni upadhī karoti, cha viññāṇakāye upadhī karoti janeti sañjaneti nibbatteti abhinibbattetīti—

sokapariddavañcā.meaning_2: sorrow and lamentation too; sorrow and wailing (and)
sokapariddavañcā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sokapariddavaṃ + ca (or sokapariddava + ca), with the final -aṃ of the accusative optionally left out; the commentary glosses sokañca paridevañca. Accusative singular in the verse.
sokapariddavañcā.example_1: kathaṃ nu dhīrā vitaranti oghaṃ, jātiṃ jaraṃ sokapariddavañcāti.
sokapariddavañcā.example_2: kathaṃ nu dhīrā vitaranti oghaṃ, jātiṃ jaraṃ sokapariddavañcāti dhīrā kathaṃ oghañca jātiñca jarañca sokañca paridevañca taranti uttaranti pataranti samatikkamanti vītivattantīti—

oghan.meaning_2: flood; torrent; stream; (figuratively) the four floods (of sensual desire, existence, wrong views, ignorance)
oghan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (oghan ti = oghaṃ). In the Niddesa it is glossed as the four oghas: kāmogha, bhavogha, diṭṭhogha, avijjogha.
oghan.example_2: natthīti nissāya tarassu oghanti natthi kiñcīti ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpatti.

viyākarohī.meaning_2: explain; declare; answer; elucidate; make clear
viyākarohī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative 2nd singular of viyākaroti, here with the emphatic -ti: 'please explain (it)'. The sandhi vi + ā > viyā. In the Niddesa glossed by ācikkhāhi, desehi, paññapehi, etc.
viyākarohī.example_2: sādhu viyākarohīti taṃ sādhu ācikkhāhi desehi paññapehi paṭṭhapehi vivarāhi vibhajāhi uttānīkarohi pakāsehīti—

dhamman.meaning_2: teaching; doctrine; the Dhamma; (in this context) the good doctrine, i.e. the holy life together with the 37 requisites of awakening and nibbāna
dhamman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular with sandhi -n for -ṃ (dhammaṃ) before ti. In the text it is the object of kittayissāmi, 'I will proclaim the Dhamma'; the Niddesa glosses it widely as the brahmacariya and the 37 bodhipakkhiyā dhammā.
dhamman.example_2: dhammanti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, cattāro satipaṭṭhāne, cattāro sammappadhāne, cattāro iddhipāde, pañcindriyāni, pañca balāni, satta bojjhaṅge, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ, nibbānañca, nibbānagāminiñca paṭipadaṃ kittayissāmi ācikkhissāmi desessāmi paññapessāmi paṭṭhapessāmi vivarissāmi vibhajissāmi uttānīkarissāmi pakāsissāmīti—

anītihan.meaning_2: not based on hearsay; personally verified; not from tradition
anītihan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is part of the phrase diṭṭhe dhamme anītihan, meaning 'in the present life, personally verified'. The ending -n is the accusative singular case ending, with the final vowel of the stem shortened before it.
anītihan.example_2: anītihanti na itihītihaṃ na itikirāya na paramparāya na piṭakasampadāya na takkahetu na nayahetu na ākāraparivitakkena na diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā, sāmaṃ sayamabhiññātaṃ attapaccakkhadhammaṃ, taṃ kathayissāmīti—

caran.meaning_2: walking; wandering; moving about; living; behaving
caran.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle of carati, nominative singular masculine in the text (caran). Used of one who lives or conducts themselves, with verbs viharanto, iriyanto, vattento in the gloss.
caran.example_1: yaṃ viditvā sato caranti yaṃ viditaṃ katvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā, “sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā”ti viditaṃ katvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā,
caran.example_2: caranti caranto viharanto iriyanto vattento pālento yapento yāpentoti—

visattikan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text visattikan is accusative singular of the adjective visattika, agreeing with loke in the phrase tare loke visattikaṃ. There is also a feminine noun visattikā, 'clinging, craving, attachment' (explained as taṇhā in the Niddesa), and some analyses may take visattikaṃ there as a noun.
visattikan.example_2: tare loke visattikanti loke vesā visattikā, loke vetaṃ visattikaṃ sato tareyya uttareyya patareyya samatikkameyya vītivatteyyāti—

abhinandāmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text abhinandāmi is 1st singular present with the emphatic -i (abhinandāmīti, sandhi of abhinandāmi + iti).

dhammamuttaman.meaning_2: supreme in dhamma; highest teaching; supreme state
dhammamuttaman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the final -ṃ of the accusative has been assimilated to the following ti (dhammamuttamaṃ iti). Explained in the Niddesa as a name for amata nibbāna.

uttaman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is uttaman ti, i.e. uttamaṃ with sandhi, accusative singular agreeing with dhammaṃ; the glosses in the quotation are agga, seṭṭha, viseṭṭha, pāmokkha, pavara.
uttaman.example_1: uttamanti aggaṃ seṭṭhaṃ viseṭṭhaṃ pāmokkhaṃ uttamaṃ pavaraṃ dhammanti—
uttaman.example_2: uttamanti aggaṃ seṭṭhaṃ viseṭṭhaṃ pāmokkhaṃ uttamaṃ pavaranti—

uddhan.meaning_2: above; upwards; beyond; higher (world); the beyond
uddhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written as uddhan before ti, from uddhaṃ (ind, 'above; upwards; beyond') + iti. In the Niddesa it is glossed in several ways: anāgataṃ ('the future'), devaloko ('the heavenly world'), kusalā dhammā ('wholesome states'). The form is a sandhi of uddhaṃ + iti, not a separate word.

etesū.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural of eta (a pronoun), with -su written as -sū due to sandhi before the quotation marker ti. In the Niddesa it refers back to the things just explained and to the five sense objects.
etesū.example_1: etesu nandiñca nivesanañca, panujja viññāṇaṃ bhave na tiṭṭheti etesūti ācikkhitesu desitesu paññapitesu paṭṭhapitesu vivaritesu vibhajitesu uttānīkatesu pakāsitesu.

nivesanan.meaning_2: tangle; attachment; clinging; adherence; abode; dwelling
nivesanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is part of the compound nivesanā in taṇhānivesanā and diṭṭhinivesanā, meaning 'tangle of craving' and 'tangle of views'. The form nivesanan is nominative singular neuter, but here it is used as a neuter plural? Actually the commentary glosses nivesanan ti dve nivesanā, treating it as a collective. The PTS gives nivesana as neuter, sometimes masculine. The root √vis with prefix ni gives 'to enter, to settle', hence 'abode' and metaphorically 'attachment'.
nivesanan.example_2: Nivesananti dve nivesanā – taṇhānivesanā ca diṭṭhinivesanā ca.
nivesanan.translation_2: “Tangles” means there are two tangles: the tangle of craving and the tangle of views.

viññāṇan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads viññāṇan, a quotation with the m-final sandhi of viññāṇaṃ, accusative singular in "panujja viññāṇaṃ" and nominative in "saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ". viññāṇa is formed from vi + √ñā.
viññāṇan.example_1: panujja viññāṇanti puññābhisaṅkhārasahagataṃ viññāṇaṃ, apuññābhisaṅkhārasahagataṃ viññāṇaṃ, āneñjābhisaṅkhārasahagataṃ viññāṇaṃ.
viññāṇan.example_2: ‘‘ Saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇan ’’ ti … pe …‘‘ viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpan ’’ ti …‘‘ nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanan ’’ ti …‘‘ saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso ’’ ti …‘‘ phassapaccayā vedanā ’’ ti …‘‘ vedanāpaccayā taṇhā ’’ ti …‘‘ taṇhāpaccayā upādānan ’’ ti …‘‘ upādānapaccayā bhavo ’’ ti …‘‘ bhavapaccayā jātī ’’ ti …‘‘ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇan ’’ ti jānato passato paññāyete sotā pidhīyanti pacchijjanti na savanti na āsavanti na sandanti nappavattanti.
viññāṇan.translation_2: For one who knows and sees that “with volitional formations as condition, consciousness arises”... up to “with birth as condition, old age and death arise,” by wisdom these streams are dammed up, cut off, and do not persist.

mamāyitānī.meaning_2: cherished; held dear; clung to as mine; appropriated
mamāyitānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter nominative/accusative plural in the text (mamāyitāni), from the quotation 'hitvā mamāyitāni'; formed from mama ('mine') with the denominative suffix -āya, meaning 'things held as mine'.

jaran.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written as jaran, niggahīta assimilated before ti (jarā + ti); glossed in the Niddesa to the ageing of beings. Some sources treat jara as a by-form.
jaran.example_2: Jātīti yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ … pe … jaranti yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ … pe … sokoti ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa … pe … paridevoti ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa … pe … idhāti imissā diṭṭhiyā … pe … imasmiṃ manussaloke.
jaran.translation_2: “Birth” refers to the birth of various beings... “aging” refers to the aging of various beings... “sorrow” refers to one touched by the loss of relatives... “lamentation” refers to one touched by the loss of relatives... “right here” means in this view... in this human world.

etan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text etan is sandhi for etaṃ, the demonstrative pronoun, used in glosses to point back to the preceding word. The same form is given as etanti in some editions.
etan.example_1: etanti tuyhaṃ vacanaṃ byappathaṃ desanaṃ anusāsanaṃ anusiṭṭhaṃ nandāmi abhinandāmi modāmi anumodāmi icchāmi sādiyāmi patthayāmi pihayāmi abhijappāmi.

gotamanūpadhīkan.meaning_2: having the Gotama's defilements?; (commentarial explanation) connected with the Gotama's attachments
gotamanūpadhīkan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears twice in the same passage, in the phrase sukittitaṃ gotamanūpadhīkaṃ, with the gloss upadhī vuccanti kilesā ca khandhā ca abhisaṅkhārā ca, so the word is being analysed in connection with upadhi. The text may be corrupt: perhaps gotamanūpadhīkaṃ = gotama + anūpadhīka ("without attachment")? The form here shows -ka-, not an-; accusative singular neuter in the text. Uncertain.
gotamanūpadhīkan.example_2: gotamanūpadhīkanti upadhī vuccanti kilesā ca khandhā ca abhisaṅkhārā ca.

sukittitan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the headword of a gloss (sukittitan ti), nominative singular in -aṃ (sandhi -n- before ti). The glosses explain it with suācikkhita, sudesita and similar terms. The PEU connects it with kittita from √kitt, but the root fields are left empty here since this is a compound.
sukittitan.example_1: sukittitanti sukittitaṃ suācikkhitaṃ sudesitaṃ supaññapitaṃ supaṭṭhapitaṃ suvivaritaṃ suvibhajitaṃ suuttānīkataṃ supakāsitanti—
sukittitan.example_2: sukittitanti sukittitaṃ suācikkhitaṃ sudesitaṃ supaññapitaṃ supaṭṭhapitaṃ suvivaṭaṃ suvibhattaṃ suuttānīkataṃ supakāsitaṃ.

tvan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a sandhi contraction of tvaṃ with a following word (e.g. tvaṃ + an?); the commentarial gloss bhagavantaṃ bhaṇati 'says to the Buddha' treats tvan as a word by itself, but the exact split is uncertain.

sameccā.meaning_2: having met; having approached; having realized; having fully understood
sameccā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text glossed by samecca abhisamecca samāgantvā abhisamāgantvā, and followed by namassāmi. Sometimes written as samecca from sameti; alternative analysis as saṃ + ā + i + tvā. Absolutive form, indeclinable.
sameccā.example_1: sameccāti samecca abhisamecca samāgantvā abhisamāgantvā sammukhā taṃ namassāmi.

asattan.meaning_2: unattached (to); not clinging (to); free from attachment (to)
asattan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text asattan is used before the quotative ti; it is the accusative singular of the adjective asatta (na + satta, 'not attached'), describing a person free from attachment to sensual pleasures and existence.
asattan.example_2: akiñcanaṃ kāmabhave asattanti akiñcanaṃ puggalaṃ kāmabhave ca asattaṃ alaggaṃ alaggitaṃ apalibuddhaṃ nikkhantaṃ nissaṭaṃ vippamuttaṃ visaññuttaṃ vimariyādikatena cetasā viharantanti—

akiñcanan.meaning_2: having nothing; free from impediments; without possessions; (in the text) free from the stains of defilements
akiñcanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The word occurs as akiñcanan ti, i.e. akiñcanaṃ followed by the quotative ti. The commentary explains kiñcana as rāga, dosa, moha, etc., and akiñcana as one in whom these kiñcanas are abandoned. The form in the text is nominative singular neuter or masculine, quoted as a lemma.
akiñcanan.example_1: akiñcananti rāgakiñcanaṃ dosakiñcanaṃ mohakiñcanaṃ mānakiñcanaṃ diṭṭhikiñcanaṃ kilesakiñcanaṃ duccaritakiñcanaṃ, yassete kiñcanā pahīnā samucchinnā vūpasantā paṭipassaddhā abhabbuppattikā ñāṇagginā daḍḍhā, so vuccati akiñcano.
akiñcanan.example_2: akiñcananti rāgakiñcanaṃ dosakiñcanaṃ mohakiñcanaṃ mānakiñcanaṃ diṭṭhikiñcanaṃ kilesakiñcanaṃ duccaritakiñcanaṃ, te kiñcanā buddhassa bhagavato pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā, tasmā buddho akiñcano.

pāran.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text pāran is a sandhi form (pāraṃ before ti). It refers to Nibbāna as the far shore, the goal to be reached.
pāran.example_1: tiṇṇo ca pāranti pāraṃ vuccati amataṃ nibbānaṃ.
pāran.example_2: gaccheyyeva jarāmaraṇassa pāranti jarāmaraṇassa pāraṃ vuccati amataṃ nibbānaṃ.

visajjā.meaning_2: having abandoned; having let loose; having released; having given up
visajjā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive used in the Niddesa (e.g. bhavābhave saṅgamimaṃ visajjā); the same form glossed as visajja. Alternative to the -tvā absolutive visajjetvā.

tuyhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written tuyhan before the following mahesi by sandhi. Genitive singular of the pronoun tvaṃ; commented on with vacanaṃ byappathaṃ desanaṃ anusāsanaṃ.
tuyhan.example_1: vācābhikaṅkhāmi mahesi tuyhanti tuyhaṃ vacanaṃ byappathaṃ desanaṃ anusāsanaṃ anusiṭṭhaṃ kaṅkhāmi abhikaṅkhāmi icchāmi sādiyāmi patthayāmi pihayāmi abhijappāmi.

nigghosan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it occurs in the accusative singular (nigghosaṃ). The gloss explains it as vacana, byappatha, desanā, anusāsanā, anusiṭṭha, i.e. words, expressions, teaching or instruction, so 'roar' here is metaphorical.
nigghosan.example_1: tava sutvāna nigghosanti tuyhaṃ vacanaṃ byappathaṃ desanaṃ anusāsanaṃ anusiṭṭhaṃ sutvā suṇitvā uggahetvā upadhārayitvā upalakkhayitvāti—
nigghosan.example_2: ito sutvāna nigghosanti ito mayhaṃ vacanaṃ byappathaṃ desanaṃ anusāsanaṃ anusiṭṭhaṃ sutvā suṇitvā uggaṇhitvā upadhārayitvā upalakkhayitvāti—

karohī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd singular imperative of karoti (karohi), quoted in a commentarial gloss: 'tenahātappaṃ karohī' ti ātappaṃ karohi. The final -ī is the sandhi of -i before ti.
karohī.example_1: tenahātappaṃ karohīti ātappaṃ karohi, ussāhaṃ karohi, ussoḷhiṃ karohi, thāmaṃ karohi, dhitiṃ karohi, vīriyaṃ karohi, chandaṃ janehi sañjanehi upaṭṭhapehi samuṭṭhapehi nibbattehi abhinibbattehīti—
karohī.example_2: Tenahātappaṃ karohīti ātappaṃ karohi, ussāhaṃ karohi, ussoḷhiṃ karohi, thāmaṃ karohi, dhitiṃ karohi, vīriyaṃ karohi, chandaṃ janehi sañjanehi upaṭṭhapehi samuṭṭhapehi nibbattehi abhinibbattehīti – tenahātappaṃ karohi.
karohī.translation_2: “Perform ardor” means: perform striving, perform urgency, perform powerful energy, perform steadfastness, perform firmness, perform energy; generate desire, bring forth inclination, establish, set up, produce, and specifically produce the skillful desire to perform the task — this is “Perform ardor.”

brāhmaṇamiriyamānan.meaning_2: not moving like a brahmin; wandering without possessions
brāhmaṇamiriyamānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Difficult and uncertain; the context ākiñcanaṃ suggests a brahmin free of possessions. Possibly a sandhi or compound including mi; accusative singular in the text.

kathaṅkathāhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form is kathaṅkathāhī, probably an exclamation or address ('O Sakka, [you who are] a doubter?'), but it could also be an instrumental form of the compound. The compound is kathaṃ + kathā, but with the vikāra kathaṅkathā. Alternative: some trace it to kathaṅkathā + ahiṃsā or similar, but the compound kathaṃ + kathā is standard.
kathaṅkathāhī.example_2: pamuñca maṃ sakka kathaṅkathāhīti muñca maṃ pamuñca maṃ mocehi maṃ pamocehi maṃ uddhara maṃ samuddhara maṃ vuṭṭhāpehi maṃ kathaṅkathāsallatoti—

pamocanāyā.meaning_2: for the purpose of releasing; in order to set free
pamocanāyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Dative or genitive singular of pamocana as a feminine abstract noun, used with sahissāmi (can). The commentarial gloss explains it as muñcituṃ etc.; possibly an instrumental or a form with svarabhakti vowel (pamocanāyā).
pamocanāyā.example_1: nāhaṃ sahissāmi pamocanāyāti nāhaṃ taṃ sakkomi muñcituṃ pamuñcituṃ mocetuṃ pamocetuṃ uddharituṃ samuddharituṃ uṭṭhāpetuṃ samuṭṭhāpetuṃ kathaṅkathāsallatoti.
pamocanāyā.example_2: Nāhaṃ sahissāmi [samīhāmi (ka.)] pamocanāyāti nāhaṃ taṃ sakkomi muñcituṃ pamuñcituṃ mocetuṃ pamocetuṃ uddharituṃ samuddharituṃ uṭṭhāpetuṃ samuṭṭhāpetuṃ kathaṃkathāsallatoti.
pamocanāyā.translation_2: “I cannot release” means: I cannot liberate, set free, loosen, set quite free, lift up, rescue, set up, or set properly from the arrow of doubt.

kañcī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text kañcīti is kañci + iti, the quotation particle. kañci is the accusative of the indefinite pronoun kaṃci (kiṃ + ci), 'someone; anyone'. The reading -ī- is sandhi for kañci iti.
kañcī.example_1: kañcīti kañci khattiyaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā vessaṃ vā suddaṃ vā gahaṭṭhaṃ vā pabbajitaṃ vā devaṃ vā manussaṃ vā.

vijaññan.meaning_2: would know; should know; could know; would understand
vijaññan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 1st singular vijaññaṃ, written vijaññan before the quotation ti; the -n belongs to the sandhi. In the text it introduces the definition: 'that I would know (to be) the state of seclusion'. The PEU also records a separate adjective vijañña ('very wise'), not relevant here.
vijaññan.example_1: vivekadhammaṃ yamahaṃ vijaññanti vivekadhammaṃ vuccati amataṃ nibbānaṃ.
vijaññan.example_2: yamahaṃ vijaññanti yamahaṃ jāneyyaṃ ājāneyyaṃ vijāneyyaṃ paṭivijāneyyaṃ paṭivijjheyyaṃ adhigaccheyyaṃ phasseyyaṃ sacchikareyyanti—

careyyan.meaning_2: may live; may dwell; may maintain oneself
careyyan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 1st singular of carati in the Niddesa gloss. The form careyyan is sandhi for careyyaṃ.
careyyan.example_2: careyyanti careyyaṃ vihareyyaṃ iriyeyyaṃ vatteyyaṃ pāleyyaṃ yapeyyaṃ yāpeyyanti—

santin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text; part of a quotation meaning 'I will proclaim your peace'. Alternative analysis: from √sam 1 with suffix -ti.
santin.example_1: kittayissāmi te santinti rāgassa santiṃ, dosassa santiṃ, mohassa santiṃ, kodhassa santiṃ, upanāhassa …pe…
santin.example_2: Kittayissāmi te santinti rāgassa santiṃ, dosassa santiṃ, mohassa santiṃ, kodhassa santiṃ, upanāhassa … pe … makkhassa … paḷāsassa … issāya … macchariyassa … māyāya … sāṭheyyassa … thambhassa … sārambhassa … mānassa … atimānassa … madassa … pamādassa … sabbakilesānaṃ … sabbaduccaritānaṃ … sabbadarathānaṃ … sabbapariḷāhānaṃ … sabbasantāpānaṃ … sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārānaṃ santiṃ upasantiṃ vūpasantiṃ nibbutiṃ paṭippassaddhiṃ kittayissāmi pakittayissāmi ācikkhissāmi desessāmi paññapessāmi paṭṭhapessāmi vivarissāmi vibhajissāmi uttānīkarissāmi pakāsissāmīti – kittayissāmi te santiṃ.
santin.translation_2: “I will proclaim the peace for you” means I will proclaim, announce, explain, teach, make known, establish, open up, analyze, clarify, and make evident the peace—the cessation of greed, the cessation of hatred, the cessation of delusion, the cessation of anger, the cessation of hostility, the cessation of denigration, the cessation of insolence, the cessation of envy, the cessation of miserliness, the cessation of deceitfulness, the cessation of craftiness, the cessation of obstinacy, the cessation of vehemence, the cessation of conceit, the cessation of arrogance, the cessation of intoxication, the cessation of heedlessness—the cessation, deep calming, profound calming, extinguishment, and revocation of all defilements, all misconduct, all disturbances, all burnings, all torments, and all unwholesome volitional formations. This is “I will proclaim the peace for you.”

mahesisantimuttaman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi form in a gloss: mahesi + santimuttamaṃ ('great sage, the highest peace'), with final -n for -ṃ. Probably quoted from a verse; the spelling is uncertain.

santimuttaman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text glossed with 'santi vuccati amataṃ nibbānaṃ'. Explained in the Niddesa as santi + mutto; possibly santimuttaman = santiṃ uttamaṃ = santi + uttamaṃ (cf. sabbe sattā bhavantu sukhitattā santimuttaman ti); glossed in DPD as sandhi of santa + uttamaṃ = completely ended is the highest / best possible sanity; the sandhi of santi + uttamaṃ perhaps.

taṇhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text taṇhan is taṇhaṃ, accusative singular, with the final consonant assimilated before ti. The sandhi word taṇhan is not a separate entry; the dictionaries list taṇhā.
taṇhan.example_2: jahassu taṇhanti jahassu taṇhaṃ pajahassu taṇhaṃ vinodehi taṇhaṃ byantīkarohi taṇhaṃ anabhāvaṃ gamehi taṇhaṃ.

mahantamoghan.meaning_2: great flood; mighty torrent; vast stream
mahantamoghan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of mahant + ogha with the n assimilated to m before o; vocative singular in the text (sakka mahantamogha).

tāritun.meaning_2: to overcome; to cross over; to get across
tāritun.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi form of tārituṃ in the text; infinitive of the causative tāreti, used with visahāmi ('I dare to cross over'). The PEU analysis tara + ṇe + tuṃ agrees with this.

tareyyan.meaning_2: might cross (to); might get across (to); might overcome
tareyyan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 1st singular of tarati; the sandhi form tareyyan is tareyyaṃ before ti. Here with oghaṃ: 'might cross this flood'.
tareyyan.example_2: Ārammaṇaṃ brūhi samantacakkhu, yaṃ nissito oghamimaṃ tareyyan ’’ ti.
tareyyan.translation_2: Tell me a support, All-seer, depending on which, I might cross this flood.”

kathāhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in the commentarial phrase kathaṅkathā vuccati vicikicchā. The form kathāhī is analysed as kathā + āhī (2nd sg. aor. of √ah 'to speak'), i.e. 'you spoke words'; it is a sandhi-compound, not a simple noun. The PEU entry kathā is a feminine noun from √kath.

maññan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the accusative singular, written maññan before the line break (maññanaṃ). PEU also records a feminine maññanā of the same meaning; the neuter fits the compound-breaking gloss hitvā maññanaṃ.

tatthā.meaning_2: there; in that (case); in that state
tatthā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form used in the commentarial glosses to introduce a quoted phrase; often equivalent to tattha but with lengthened final vowel.
tatthā.example_2: tatthāti sakāya diṭṭhiyā sakāya khantiyā sakāya ruciyā sakāya laddhiyā.

vassānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vassāni is accusative plural, part of the gloss phrase pūgampi vassāni ("for many years"). The printed pada is sometimes read as vassāni or vassānaṃ.
vassānī.example_1: pūgampi vassānīti pūgampi vassāni bahūni vassāni bahūni vassasatāni bahūni vassasahassāni bahūni vassasatasahassāni bahūni kappāni bahūni kappasatāni bahūni kappasahassāni bahūni kappasatasahassāni.
vassānī.example_2: Pūgampi vassānīti pūgampi vassāni bahūni vassāni [bahunnaṃ vassānaṃ (syā.)] bahūni vassasatāni bahūni vassasahassāni bahūni vassasatasahassāni bahūni kappāni bahūni kappasatāni bahūni kappasahassāni bahūni kappasatasahassāni.
vassānī.translation_2: “For many years” means for many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, many hundreds of thousands of years, many eons, many hundreds of eons, many thousands of eons, many hundreds of thousands of eons.

saṅkhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the accusative singular saṅkhaṃ (= saṅkhan by sandhi before ti) in the phrase na upeti saṅkhaṃ, 'does not go into reckoning; is beyond enumeration'. Some analyses take it as saṅkhā, others relate it to saṅkhyā; the PEU entry saṅkha (conch) does not fit here.
saṅkhan.example_2: na upeti saṅkhanti saṅkhaṃ na upeti, uddesaṃ na upeti, gaṇanaṃ na upeti, paṇṇattiṃ na upeti, “puratthimaṃ vā disaṃ gatā, pacchimaṃ vā disaṃ gatā, uttaraṃ vā disaṃ gatā, dakkhiṇaṃ vā disaṃ gatā uddhaṃ vā gatā, adho vā gatā, tiriyaṃ vā gatā, vidisaṃ vā gatā”ti, so hetu natthi, paccayo natthi, kāraṇaṃ natthi, yena saṅkhaṃ gaccheyyāti—

paletī.meaning_2: goes away; passes away; vanishes; ceases
paletī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Glossed in the text as gameti, gacchati, nirujjhati etc., and explained as parinibbāyati. Third person singular; the -ti is separated in atthaṃ paletīti.
paletī.example_1: atthaṃ paletīti atthaṃ paleti, atthaṃ gameti, atthaṃ gacchati nirujjhati vūpasamati paṭippassambhati.

evan.meaning_2: thus; so; in this way; like this
evan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written evan before a vowel (sandhi of evaṃ + iti). In these sentences it introduces and quotes the preceding word: 'evan ti' = 'evaṃ (thus)'. Here it glosses the sense of the quotation, in the phrase evanti opammasampaṭipādanaṃ.

kathaṃsū.meaning_2: how?; how is this?; in what way?
kathaṃsū.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Interrogative particle iva/su added to kathaṃ, used in the set phrase 'tayidaṃ kathaṃsū' quoted in the Niddesa as a question of doubt (saṃsayapucchā).
kathaṃsū.example_2: tayidaṃ kathaṃsūti saṃsayapucchā vimatipucchā dveḷhakapucchā anekaṃsapucchā “evaṃ nu kho, na nu kho, kiṃ nu kho, kathaṃ nu kho”ti—

jīvitenūpapannan.meaning_2: endowed with a livelihood; furnished with a way of living
jīvitenūpapannan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of jīvitena + upapanna; accusative singular in the text, agreeing with muniṃ. The Niddesa glosses it as jīvitānuyogena upetaṃ samannāgataṃ.
jīvitenūpapannan.example_1: udāhu ve jīvitenūpapannanti udāhu anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhajīvitānuyogena upetaṃ samupetaṃ upāgataṃ samupāgataṃ upapannaṃ samupapannaṃ samannāgataṃ muniṃ vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharantīti—
jīvitenūpapannan.example_2: Udāhu ve jīvitenūpapannanti udāhu anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhajīvitānuyogena upetaṃ samupetaṃ upāgataṃ samupāgataṃ upapannaṃ samupapannaṃ samannāgataṃ muniṃ vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharantīti – udāhu ve jīvitenūpapannaṃ.
jīvitenūpapannan.translation_2: “Or do they call him one endowed with a [specific] livelihood?”: Or do they call, speak of, declare, explain, and designate a person as a sage because he is endowed with a livelihood that consists of various kinds of austerity and difficult practices—that is what is meant by ‘or do they call him one endowed with a livelihood.’

ñāṇenā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text (ñāṇena, sandhi ñāṇenā with following ti).
ñāṇenā.example_2: na ñāṇenāti napi aṭṭhasamāpattiñāṇena napi pañcābhiññāñāṇena napi micchāñāṇenāti—

suddhin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text suddhin is an accusative singular of suddhi; the form shows sandhi with the following -ti (suddhiṃ + iti).
suddhin.example_1: diṭṭhassutenāpi vadanti suddhinti diṭṭhenāpi suddhiṃ visuddhiṃ parisuddhiṃ muttiṃ vimuttiṃ parimuttiṃ vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharanti;
suddhin.example_2: sīlabbatenāpi vadanti suddhinti sīlenapi suddhiṃ visuddhiṃ parisuddhiṃ muttiṃ vimuttiṃ parimuttiṃ vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharanti;

kiñcāpī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text quoted as an example of padasandhi (a sandhi of words); the spelling kiñcāpī adds a lengthened final -ī.
kiñcāpī.example_1: kiñcāpīti padasandhi padasaṃsaggo padapāripūrī akkharasamavāyo byañjanasiliṭṭhatā padānupubbatāpetaṃ—
kiñcāpī.example_2: Kiñcāpīti padasandhi padasaṃsaggo padapāripūrī akkharasamavāyo byañjanasiliṭṭhatā padānupubbatāpetaṃ – kiñcāpīti.
kiñcāpī.translation_2: “Kiñcāpī” is a conjunction, a particle, a word-filler, an amalgamation of sounds, a refinement of syllables, a sequence of words — thus, “kiñcāpī”.

sabban.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text sabban is sandhi for sabbaṃ (accusative singular), the object of pahāya: 'having abandoned all'. The PEU entry suggests a derivation sara + va, which is doubtful.
sabban.example_1: ye sīdha diṭṭhaṃ va sutaṃ mutaṃ vā, sīlabbataṃ vāpi pahāya sabbanti ye sabbā diṭṭhasuddhiyo pahāya jahitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvā.
sabban.example_2: anekarūpampi pahāya sabbanti anekavidhakotūhalamaṅgalena suddhiṃ visuddhiṃ parisuddhiṃ muttiṃ vimuttiṃ parimuttiṃ pahāya jahitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvāti—

pariññāyā.meaning_2: having fully understood; having known thoroughly
pariññāyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written pariññāyā before ti (pariññāyāti), the absolutive of parijānāti. The three pariññā are ñāta, tīraṇa and pahāna.
pariññāyā.example_2: taṇhaṃ pariññāyāti taṇhaṃ imāhi tīhi pariññāhi parijānitvā.

viyākaṃsū.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd plural of viyākaroti (vi + ā + karoti), with the ending -uṃ; the text glosses it by byākaṃsu, ācikkhiṃsu, etc. The form viyākaṃsu is the same aorist without the final nasal.
viyākaṃsū.example_1: ye me pubbe viyākaṃsūti yo ca bāvarī brāhmaṇo ye caññe tassa ācariyā, te sakaṃ diṭṭhiṃ sakaṃ khantiṃ sakaṃ ruciṃ sakaṃ laddhiṃ sakaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ sakaṃ adhippāyaṃ byākaṃsu ācikkhiṃsu desayiṃsu paññapiṃsu paṭṭhapiṃsu vivariṃsu vibhajiṃsu uttānīakaṃsu pakāsesunti—

itihītihan.meaning_2: such and such; of this and that kind; regarded as "so it was, so it was"; consisting of hearsay, oral tradition
itihītihan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] "Sabbaṃ taṃ itihītihan" is a stock phrase quoted in the Niddesa for what is merely hearsay (itikirāya, paraṃparāya, piṭakasampadāya). In the text it is the accusative singular -aṃ of the neuter adjective used nominally; the -n is sandhi before ti. The PEU analyses it as itiha + itiha + ṇa.
itihītihan.example_1: sabbaṃ taṃ itihītihanti sabbaṃ taṃ itihītihaṃ itikirāya paraṃparāya piṭakasampadāya takkahetu nayahetu ākāraparivitakkena diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā na sāmaṃ sayamabhiññātaṃ na attapaccakkhadhammaṃ kathayiṃsūti—
itihītihan.example_2: sabbaṃ taṃ itihītihanti sabbaṃ taṃ itihītihaṃ itikirāya paramparāya piṭakasampadāya takkahetu nayahetu ākāraparivitakkena diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā na sāmaṃ sayamabhiññātaṃ na attapaccakkhaṃ dhammaṃ yaṃ kathayiṃsūti—

takkavaḍḍhanan.meaning_2: increase of speculation; growth of reasoning; augmentation of thought
takkavaḍḍhanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is written takkavaḍḍhanan, a sandhi form (m final) before ti; the commentary glosses it with vitakkavaḍḍhana etc. The word is quoted in Niddesa 2 as part of itihītihaṃ.
takkavaḍḍhanan.example_1: sabbaṃ taṃ takkavaḍḍhananti sabbaṃ taṃ takkavaḍḍhanaṃ vitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ saṅkappavaḍḍhanaṃ kāmavitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ byāpādavitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ ñātivitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ janapadavitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ amarāvitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ parānudayatāpaṭisaṃyuttavitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ lābhasakkārasilokapaṭisaṃyuttavitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ anavaññattipaṭisaṃyuttavitakkavaḍḍhananti—
takkavaḍḍhanan.example_2: Sabbaṃ taṃ takkavaḍḍhananti sabbaṃ taṃ takkavaḍḍhanaṃ vitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ saṅkappavaḍḍhanaṃ kāmavitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ byāpādavitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ ñātivitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ janapadavitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ amarāvitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ parānudayatāpaṭisaṃyuttavitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ lābhasakkārasilokapaṭisaṃyuttavitakkavaḍḍhanaṃ anavaññattipaṭisaṃyuttavitakkavaḍḍhananti – sabbaṃ taṃ takkavaḍḍhanaṃ.
takkavaḍḍhanan.translation_2: “Sabbaṃ taṃ takkavaḍḍhanan” (all that is the augmentation of speculation) means: all that is the augmentation of speculation, the augmentation of thoughts, the augmentation of intentions, the augmentation of sensual thoughts, the augmentation of thoughts of ill-will, the augmentation of thoughts of harming, the augmentation of thoughts about relatives, the augmentation of thoughts about regions, the augmentation of thoughts about immortality, the augmentation of thoughts associated with concern for others, the augmentation of thoughts associated with gain, honor, and fame, and the augmentation of thoughts associated with wishing to be unregarded—this is 'all that is the augmentation of speculation'.

abhiramin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular aorist in the quoted verse nāhaṃ tattha abhiramin. The commentary glosses it with abhiramiṃ, then na vindiṃ, nādhigacchiṃ, na paṭilabhiṃ. The negative na combines with the verb, giving 'I did not delight (in)'.
abhiramin.example_1: nāhaṃ tattha abhiraminti nāhaṃ tattha abhiramiṃ na vindiṃ nādhigacchiṃ na paṭilabhinti—
abhiramin.example_2: Nāhaṃ tattha abhiraminti nāhaṃ tattha abhiramiṃ na vindiṃ nādhigacchiṃ na paṭilabhinti – nāhaṃ tattha abhiramiṃ.
abhiramin.translation_2: “Nāhaṃ tattha abhiramin” (I do not delight in that) means: I did not delight, I did not find, I did not attain, I did not obtain in that—this is 'I do not delight in that'.

dhammamakkhāhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of dhammaṃ + akkhāhi, imperative 2nd singular of akkhāti with the assimilated prefix ā; the pada is tvañca me dhammaṃ akkhāhi, 'you must declare the Dhamma to me'. The headword is given as the present 3rd singular akkhāti.

diṭṭhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text diṭṭhan is a sandhi form of diṭṭhaṃ, the nominative singular neuter, glossed by cakkhunā diṭṭhaṃ. The past participle is from √dis 1 (see), root sign ta.

sutan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text sutan ti, sandhi of sutaṃ + iti. Quotation of a phrase heard; here the sutaṃ is singular nominative/accusative neuter of suta as 'heard (thing)'.
sutan.example_2: yāvatatiyañca devīsi, byākarotīti me sutanti yāvatatiyaṃ buddho sahadhammikaṃ pañhaṃ puṭṭho byākaroti no saṃsāretīti—

mutan.meaning_2: known; sensed; perceived; (as a category of experience) what is known by the mind; the sensed
mutan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the sentence mutan is quoted as a form glossed by ghānena ghāyitaṃ jivhāya sāyitaṃ kāyena phuṭṭhaṃ; the -n is a sandhi consonant before ti (mutaṃ ti), so the word is mutaṃ, nominative/accusative singular neuter. Often listed with diṭṭha, suta, viññāta; PEU's muta entry gives a different, likely folk-etymological, analysis.
mutan.example_1: mutanti ghānena ghāyitaṃ jivhāya sāyitaṃ kāyena phuṭṭhaṃ;

viññātan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Here it is the past participle used as a neuter noun ('what is known'), in the phrase diṭṭhasutamutaviññātesu. The -n is the sandhi of -nti (viññātanti = viññātaṃ iti); the entry is for the main word.
viññātan.translation_2: “Thought” means what is known by the mind; this is the meaning of “in regard to things seen, heard, sensed, and thought.”

chandarāgavinodanan.meaning_2: removal of desire and lust; dispelling of sensual desire
chandarāgavinodanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the word being glossed (chandarāgavinodananti), nominative singular in the gloss - chandarāgavinodanaṃ. Used as a name for Nibbāna.
chandarāgavinodanan.example_2: chandarāgavinodananti chandarāgappahānaṃ chandarāgavūpasamaṃ chandarāgapaṭinissaggaṃ chandarāgapaṭippassaddhaṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—

nibbānapadamaccutan.meaning_2: the deathless state of Nibbāna; the unchanging path to Nibbāna
nibbānapadamaccutan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Commentarial gloss of nibbānapadamaccutaṃ; part of a compound (bahubbīhi) meaning the deathless state of Nibbāna. The form in the text is sandhi for nibbānapadaṃ + amaccutaṃ or a compound with maccuta.
nibbānapadamaccutan.translation_2: The removal of desire and lust is the unchanging state of Nibbāna.”

accutan.meaning_2: not falling; imperishable; immortal; unchanging; everlasting
accutan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text accutan is the accusative singular of the neuter noun accutaṃ in the phrase accutaṃ nibbānapadaṃ; the gloss explains accuta as niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ avipariṇāmadhammaṃ. Sometimes accuta is analysed as a + cuta ('not fallen'), i.e. na + cuta with vowel coalescence.
accutan.translation_2: “Unchanging” means it is constant, everlasting, eternal, and not subject to change; this is the meaning of “the unchanging state of Nibbāna.”

yasmin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular of the relative pronoun ya; sandhi of yasmiṃ. In the text it introduces a relative clause, glossed by the commentary as puggale and sacce.
yasmin.example_2: yasminti yasmiṃ puggale arahante khīṇāsave sadisohamasmīti māno natthi, seyyohamasmīti māno natthi, hīnohamasmīti omāno natthi na santi na saṃvijjati nupalabbhati, pahīnaṃ samucchinnaṃ vūpasantaṃ paṭipassaddhaṃ abhabbuppattikaṃ ñāṇagginā daḍḍhanti—

tiṭṭhatan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text tiṭṭhatan is a sandhi of tiṭṭhataṃ (present participle, genitive plural) + ti? The sentence majjhe sarasmiṃ tiṭṭhatan looks like a quotation tiṭṭhataṃ (of those standing) in the middle of the stream. The PEU entries suggest tiṭṭhatha/tiṭṭhate, but the form is likely tiṭṭhataṃ in the text.
tiṭṭhatan.example_1: majjhe sarasmiṃ tiṭṭhatanti saro vuccati saṃsāro āgamanaṃ gamanaṃ gamanāgamanaṃ kālaṃ gati bhavābhavo cuti ca upapatti ca nibbatti ca bhedo ca jāti ca jarā ca maraṇañca.

jarāmaccuparetānan.meaning_2: oppressed by old age and death; afflicted by ageing and death
jarāmaccuparetānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is genitive plural (jarāmaccuparetānaṃ, with sandhi -nan for -naṃ). The Niddesa glosses it with jarāya phuṭṭhānaṃ ... maccunā phuṭṭhānaṃ.
jarāmaccuparetānan.example_2: jarāmaccuparetānanti jarāya phuṭṭhānaṃ paretānaṃ samohitānaṃ samannāgatānaṃ, maccunā phuṭṭhānaṃ paretānaṃ samohitānaṃ samannāgatānaṃ jātiyā anugatānaṃ jarāya anusaṭānaṃ byādhinā abhibhūtānaṃ maraṇena abbhāhatānaṃ atāṇānaṃ aleṇānaṃ asaraṇānaṃ asaraṇībhūtānanti—
