dīpamakkhāhī.meaning_2: explain the refuge (to me); tell me the shelter
dīpamakkhāhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of dīpaṃ (accusative singular of dīpa, 'refuge') and akkhāhi (imperative of akkhāti, 'explain'). The Niddesa glosses it with dīpaṃ ... akkhāhi.
dīpamakkhāhī.example_2: dīpamakkhāhīti dīpaṃ tāṇaṃ leṇaṃ saraṇaṃ gatiṃ parāyanaṃ akkhāhi ācikkhāhi desehi paññapehi paṭṭhapehi vivarāhi vibhajāhi uttānīkarohi pakāsehīti—

anādānan.meaning_2: not grasping; not taking; without clinging; free from attachment
anādānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the accusative singular anādānaṃ, glossed by the Niddesa as ādānaṃ vuccati taṇhā, i.e. the absence of craving's grasping. na + ādāna with the two words fused.

kiñcanan.meaning_2: something; anything; impediment; obstacle; (in compounds) bondage (of); entanglement (of)
kiñcanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the final -ṃ is changed to -n by sandhi before 'ti' (kiñcanaṃ + iti → kiñcananti). Used in the Niddesa in the sense of the bonds of lust, hatred, delusion, etc.; see rāgakiñcana etc.
kiñcanan.example_2: mā te vijjittha kiñcananti rāgakiñcanaṃ dosakiñcanaṃ mohakiñcanaṃ mānakiñcanaṃ diṭṭhikiñcanaṃ kilesakiñcanaṃ duccaritakiñcanaṃ.

anāparan.meaning_2: having nothing beyond; having nothing other than this; unsurpassed (in the phrase etaṃ dīpaṃ anāparan)
anāparan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa gloss: tamhā paro añño dīpo natthi, i.e. there is no other island beyond it. Accusative singular here, qualifying dīpaṃ.
anāparan.example_1: etaṃ dīpaṃ anāparanti etaṃ dīpaṃ tāṇaṃ leṇaṃ saraṇaṃ gati parāyanaṃ.

itī.meaning_2: thus; so; like this; (marker of quotation or end of a phrase)
itī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text itī is iti lengthened before ti (itīti) as a quotation marker; the entry is for the word iti itself. Often used to close a quoted term or definition.
itī.example_1: itīti padasandhi padasaṃsaggo padapāripūrī akkharasamavāyo byañjanasiliṭṭhatā padānupubbatāpetaṃ—

jarāmaccuparikkhayan.meaning_2: destruction of old age and death; end of aging and death; exhaustion of aging and death
jarāmaccuparikkhayan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, glossed by the Niddesa as jarāmaraṇassa pahānaṃ ... nibbānaṃ. The text spells maccu where the gloss has maraṇa. In the quotation the following -ti is sandhi.
jarāmaccuparikkhayan.example_1: jarāmaccuparikkhayanti jarāmaraṇassa pahānaṃ vūpasamaṃ paṭinissaggaṃ paṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—
jarāmaccuparikkhayan.example_2: Jarāmaccuparikkhayanti jarāmaraṇassa pahānaṃ vūpasamaṃ paṭinissaggaṃ paṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti – jarāmaccuparikkhayaṃ.
jarāmaccuparikkhayan.translation_2: 'The destruction of aging and death': the abandoning, the quelling, the relinquishing, the revocation, the Deathless Nibbāna of aging and death—that is 'the destruction of aging and death'.

vīramakāmakāmin.meaning_2: O hero, not desiring desire; O hero, free from craving for the desirable
vīramakāmakāmin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vīra (vocative) and akāmakāmin; the context (sutvā) suggests a quoted phrase or address. The pada is unsure.
vīramakāmakāmin.example_1: sutvānahaṃ vīramakāmakāminti sutvā suṇitvā uggahetvā upadhāretvā upalakkhayitvā.

vīran.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In vīranti the -an- is a sandhi liaison (vīraṃ ti) before ti; the gloss explains it as vīro bhagavā, i.e. the Buddha as hero. Sometimes analysed as the Sanskrit-style strong stem vīran, but here it is the nominative vīro in quotation.

akāmakāmin.meaning_2: free of sensual desire; without craving
akāmakāmin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An epithet of the Buddha (a + kāma + kāmin, "not desiring sensual pleasures" with the na-prefix). Vocative singular in the quoted verse (sutvānahaṃ vīra akāmakāmin ti); in the Niddesa gloss it is quoted and glossed. Related PEU entry akāmakāmī is a variant.
akāmakāmin.example_2: Sutvānahaṃ vīra akāmakāminti sutvā suṇitvā uggahetvā upadhāretvā upalakkhayitvā.
akāmakāmin.translation_2: “Having heard, O Hero, of one who has no desires”: having heard, listened to, learned, retained, and identified—

puṭṭhumakāmamāgaman.meaning_2: the arrival of those desiring to ask about the crossing of the flood
puṭṭhumakāmamāgaman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound of puṭṭhuṃ (infinitive 'to ask') + kāma ('desire') + āgamana ('coming'); the final form in the text is a sandhi (n + ti).

oghātigan.meaning_2: one who has overcome the flood; one who has crossed beyond the flood
oghātigan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, quoted and glossed as oghaṃ atikkantaṃ vītivattaṃ.
oghātigan.example_2: Oghātiganti oghātigaṃ oghaṃ atikkantaṃ samatikkantaṃ vītivattanti – oghātigaṃ.
oghātigan.translation_2: “Overcome the flood” means having overcome, completely overcome, crossed beyond the flood—this is the meaning of ‘overcome the flood’.

puṭṭhun.meaning_2: to ask; to question; to beg; to request
puṭṭhun.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text puṭṭhun is a sandhi variant of puṭṭhuṃ before ti. Explained by pucchituṃ yācituṃ ajjhesituṃ pasādetuṃ.

akāmamāgaman.meaning_2: coming to one who has no desires; approaching the desireless
akāmamāgaman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A commentarial gloss (as if akāmaṃ + āgamana) explaining the phrase akāmamāgamaṃ in the verse 'oghātigaṃ puṭṭhumakāmamāgamaṃ'. The form akāmamāgaman is quoted with the -ti and treated as an indeclinable gloss; the standard compound analysis is akāma + āgamana.
akāmamāgaman.example_1: akāmamāgamanti akāmaṃ puṭṭhuṃ nikkāmaṃ cattakāmaṃ vantakāmaṃ muttakāmaṃ pahīnakāmaṃ paṭinissaṭṭhakāmaṃ vītarāgaṃ vigatarāgaṃ cattarāgaṃ vantarāgaṃ muttarāgaṃ pahīnarāgaṃ paṭinissaṭṭharāgaṃ āgamhā āgatamhā upāgatamhā sampattamhā tayā saddhiṃ samāgatamhāti—
akāmamāgaman.example_2: Akāmamāgamanti akāmaṃ puṭṭhuṃ nikkāmaṃ cattakāmaṃ vantakāmaṃ muttakāmaṃ pahīnakāmaṃ paṭinissaṭṭhakāmaṃ vītarāgaṃ vigatarāgaṃ cattarāgaṃ vantarāgaṃ muttarāgaṃ pahīnarāgaṃ paṭinissaṭṭharāgaṃ āgamhā āgatamhā upāgatamhā sampattamhā tayā saddhiṃ samāgatamhāti – oghātigaṃ puṭṭhumakāmamāgamaṃ.
akāmamāgaman.translation_2: “Having come to one who has no desires” means having come to one who is without desire, who has gone beyond desire, who has cast off desire, who has vomited out desire, who is released from desire, who has abandoned desire, who has relinquished desire, who is free of lust, who has discarded lust, who has cast off lust, who has vomited out lust, who is released from lust, who has abandoned lust, and who has relinquished lust; having approached him, having reached him, having arrived at him, and having come together with him—this is the meaning of ‘having come to ask one who has overcome the flood and who has no desires.’

vippahānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it appears as vippahānan, which is the accusative singular in sandhi (vippahānaṃ). The compound is glossed in the Niddesa as pahāna, vūpasama, paṭinissagga, paṭippassaddhi, amataṃ nibbāna.
vippahānan.example_1: jātijarāya idha vippahānanti idheva jātijarāya maraṇassa pahānaṃ vūpasamaṃ paṭinissaggaṃ paṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—
vippahānan.example_2: jātijarāya idha vippahānanti idheva jātijarāmaraṇassa pahānaṃ vūpasamaṃ paṭinissaggaṃ paṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—

gedhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. PEU suggests root gidh + ṇa, giving gedha.

nekkhamman.meaning_2: renunciation; giving up; escape (from); the practice of renunciation
nekkhamman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form is nekkhamman, a sandhi variant of nekkhammaṃ (accusative singular) before ti. The Niddesa glosses it very broadly with the whole graduated path up to Nibbāna.
nekkhamman.example_1: nekkhammanti sammāpaṭipadaṃ anulomapaṭipadaṃ apaccanīkapaṭipadaṃ anvatthapaṭipadaṃ dhammānudhammapaṭipadaṃ sīlesu paripūrakāritaṃ indriyesu guttadvārataṃ bhojane mattaññutaṃ jāgariyānuyogaṃ satisampajaññaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhāne cattāro sammappadhāne cattāro iddhipāde pañcindriyāni pañca balāni satta bojjhaṅge ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ nibbānañca nibbānagāminiñca paṭipadaṃ khemato tāṇato leṇato saraṇato saraṇībhūtato abhayato accutato amatato nibbānato daṭṭhuṃ passitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvāti—
nekkhamman.example_2: Nekkhammanti sammāpaṭipadaṃ anulomapaṭipadaṃ apaccanīkapaṭipadaṃ anvatthapaṭipadaṃ dhammānudhammapaṭipadaṃ sīlesu paripūrakāritaṃ indriyesu guttadvārataṃ bhojane mattaññutaṃ jāgariyānuyogaṃ satisampajaññaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhāne cattāro sammappadhāne cattāro iddhipāde pañcindriyāni pañca balāni satta bojjhaṅge ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ nibbānañca nibbānagāminiñca paṭipadaṃ khemato tāṇato leṇato saraṇato saraṇībhūtato abhayato accutato amatato nibbānato daṭṭhuṃ passitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvāti – nekkhammaṃ daṭṭhu khemato.
nekkhamman.translation_2: “Renunciation”: the path of practice, the compliant path, the non-obstructive path, the path in accordance with the goal, the path of Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, perfect conduct in virtue, guarding the doors of the faculties, moderation in eating, the practice of wakefulness, mindfulness and clear comprehension, the four applications of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four foundations for supernormal power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, the noble eightfold path, Nibbāna, and the path of practice leading to Nibbāna—having seen them as secure, as a sanctuary, as a refuge, as a protection, as having no fear, as deathless, as the unmoving, as Nibbāna, having calculated, judged, examined, clarified, and made evident—this is “Having seen renunciation as secure.”

uggahitan.meaning_2: taken; grasped; grasped wrongly; clung to; seized (by craving or views)
uggahitan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form is uggahitan-ti, an accusative singular neuter agreeing with the quoted word; the -n is sandhi before ti. The gloss explains it as taken and clung to by craving (taṇhāvasena) and by views (diṭṭhivasena).
uggahitan.example_1: uggahitanti taṇhāvasena diṭṭhivasena gahitaṃ parāmaṭṭhaṃ abhiniviṭṭhaṃ ajjhositaṃ adhimuttaṃ.

visosehī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative 2nd singular visosehi in the text (vi + sosehi). Causative of visussati; glossed by sosehi, sukkhāpehi, etc.
visosehī.example_1: yaṃ pubbe taṃ visosehīti atīte saṅkhāre ārabbha ye kilesā uppajjeyyuṃ te kilese sosehi visosehi sukkhāpehi visukkhāpehi abījaṃ karohi pajaha vinodehi byantīkarohi anabhāvaṃ gamehīti—

carissasī.meaning_2: will walk; will wander; will live; will practise
carissasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Future 2nd singular in -ssasi (carissasi) from carati; written carissasī before ti. In the text it is quoted as part of the phrase upasanto carissasī ti.
carissasī.example_1: upasanto carissasīti rāgassa upasamitattā upasanto carissasi, dosassa …pe…

anejan.meaning_2: without shaking; free from craving; free from defilement
anejan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Adjective qualifying okañjaham and taṇhacchidam in the verse quotation. The text has anejan, which would be the masculine accusative singular, but the lemma is aneja.

okañjahan.meaning_2: abandons the abode; gives up the dwelling
okañjahan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form is okañjahan ti, with -ti (iti) marking a quotation and the -n representing the verb's -ti ending in sandhi; a compound verb of okaṃ (abode) + jahati (abandons), glossed in the Niddesa as abandoning desire, lust, delight and craving in the material realm.
okañjahan.example_1: okañjahanti rūpadhātuyā yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te buddhassa bhagavato pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā.
okañjahan.example_2: Okañjahanti rūpadhātuyā yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upāyupādānā [upayupādānā (ka.)] cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te buddhassa bhagavato pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā.
okañjahan.translation_2: “Having abandoned the abode” means: whatever desire, whatever lust, whatever delight, whatever craving, and whatever engagement and clinging, mental standpoints, adherences, and underlying tendencies there are in the material realm, the Blessed One has abandoned them, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, done away with them, and they are no longer subject to future arising.

taṇhacchidan.meaning_2: who has cut off craving; with craving destroyed
taṇhacchidan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the accusative singular taṇhacchidaṃ, quoted in the Niddesa as taṇhacchidanti (an epithet of one who has destroyed craving). The final -a of the compound is elided before -ti.

vimuttan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form in the text is vimuttaṃ (nominative/accusative singular neuter, agreeing with cittaṃ). The final -n is due to sandhi before ti: vimuttaṃ + ti > vimuttanti (the text writes vimuttan ti).
vimuttan.example_2: vimuttanti bhagavato rāgā cittaṃ muttaṃ vimuttaṃ suvimuttaṃ, dosā cittaṃ … mohā cittaṃ …pe…

oghatiṇṇan.meaning_2: having crossed the flood; one who has crossed the flood (of saṃsāra)
oghatiṇṇan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An epithet of the Buddha. In the text it is written oghatiṇṇan, representing oghatiṇṇaṃ (nominative singular, sandhi with ti), the form being glossed in the Niddesa. Some editors take oghatiṇṇa as a bahubbīhi compound.
oghatiṇṇan.example_1: oghatiṇṇanti bhagavā kāmoghaṃ tiṇṇo bhavoghaṃ tiṇṇo diṭṭhoghaṃ tiṇṇo avijjoghaṃ tiṇṇo sabbasaṃsārapathaṃ tiṇṇo uttiṇṇo nitthiṇṇo atikkanto samatikkanto vītivatto.

sumedhan.meaning_2: wise; of good understanding; having excellent wisdom
sumedhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (sumedhan); a bahubbīhi compound of su + medhā, used as a masc noun for a wise man.

tesan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi form of tesaṃ (dative/genitive plural of ta) with -ti: tesaṃ + iti → tesanti, written tesan in the text. In the Niddesa it introduces a gloss ('of those, namely ...'). Genitive plural.
tesan.example_1: tesanti tesaṃ khattiyānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vessānaṃ suddānaṃ gahaṭṭhānaṃ pabbajitānaṃ devānaṃ manussānaṃ.

tuvan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Quotation mark -ti is attached in the text. Probably tu + ivan ("but this"), or tu + evaṃ; the commentarial gloss bhagavantaṃ bhaṇati suggests a particle of address; uncertain, so both parts are given as indeclinables.

jantun.meaning_2: creature; being; person; man; living being
jantun.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (jantuṃ, with sandhi jantun ti). The PEU relates it to √jan (be born) with suffix -tu, and also mentions √jar; treated here as a u-stem masculine noun.
jantun.example_1: teneva māro anveti jantunti teneva kammābhisaṅkhāravasena paṭisandhiko khandhamāro dhātumāro āyatanamāro gatimāro upapattimāro paṭisandhimāro bhavamāro saṃsāramāro vaṭṭamāro anveti anugacchati anvāyiko hoti.
jantun.example_2: jantunti sattaṃ janaṃ naraṃ mānavaṃ posaṃ puggalaṃ jīvaṃ jāguṃ jantuṃ indaguṃ manujanti—

upādiyethā.meaning_2: would grasp; would cling to; would take up; would become attached to
upādiyethā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd person singular optative of upādiyati, used impersonally in the text (na upādiyethā = one should not grasp). The PEU gloss 'upādiyetha' is the same form; the ending -etha is 2sg optative. In the commentary it is glossed by nādiyeyya, na gaṇheyya, na parāmaseyya, nābhiniviseyya.
upādiyethā.example_2: na upādiyethāti rūpaṃ nādiyeyya na upādiyeyya na gaṇheyya na parāmaseyya nābhiniviseyya;

visattan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form in text visattan is accusative singular of visatta used adjectivally with pajaṃ, agreeing with it: 'this people clinging in the realm of death'. Alternative: visattaṃ with sandhi -aṃ > -an before ti.
visattan.example_2: Ādānasatte iti pekkhamāno, pajaṃ imaṃ maccudheyye visattan ’’ ti.
visattan.translation_2: observing this multitude in the realm of death [as] adhering to acquisition.”

virajamāsīnan.meaning_2: dwelling free from dust; sitting without impurity
virajamāsīnan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound with āsīna, present participle of āsati; accusative singular agreeing with jhāyiṃ. The ending -n is sandhi of -ntaṃ; the sense is 'seated free from dust (defilement)'.

jhāyin.meaning_2: meditating; absorbed in jhāna; one who meditates
jhāyin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An agent noun from jhāyati. In the text it is nominative singular, glossed by jhāyī bhagavā.

virajan.meaning_2: free from dust; free from impurity; without passion; stainless
virajan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text virajan is the accusative singular of the adjective viraja, used in the explanation virajanti rāgo rajo... ("free from dust: passion is dust..."). The vi- prefix here carries a privative sense.
virajan.example_1: virajanti rāgo rajo, doso rajo, moho rajo, kodho rajo, upanāho rajo …pe… sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārā rajā.

āsīnan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle of āsati (sit). In the text it is the word being glossed (āsīnanti), and the gloss itself uses the nominative singular āsīno.
āsīnan.translation_2: ‘Sitting’ (āsīnaṃ) means the Blessed One is seated at the Pāsāṇaka Shrine, thus he is ‘sitting’ (āsīno).

anāsavan.meaning_2: without influxes; free from taints; taintless
anāsavan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Used in the stock phrase katakiccaṃ anāsavaṃ (one who has done the task, taintless). In the text it appears as anāsavan due to sandhi (anāsavaṃ ti / anāsavaṃ). Accusative singular in the sentence.
anāsavan.example_1: katakiccaṃ anāsavanti buddhassa bhagavato kiccākiccaṃ karaṇīyākaraṇīyaṃ pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṅkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ.

pabhedanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text pabhedanan ti with sandhi for pabhedanaṃ, nominative or accusative singular, glossed by the commentary as pahānaṃ vūpasamaṃ paṭinissaggaṃ.
pabhedanan.example_1: avijjāya pabhedananti avijjāya bhedanaṃ pabhedanaṃ pahānaṃ vūpasamaṃ paṭinissaggaṃ paṭippassaddhaṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—

kāmacchandānan.meaning_2: sensual desire; desire for sense pleasures
kāmacchandānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form in the text is kāmacchandānaṃ (genitive plural), written with a single n at the end in the sandhi. It is glossed by the commentator as pahānaṃ vūpasamaṃ paṭinissaggaṃ paṭippassaddhiṃ.
kāmacchandānan.example_2: pahānaṃ kāmacchandānanti kāmacchandānaṃ pahānaṃ vūpasamaṃ paṭinissaggaṃ paṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—

cūbhayan.meaning_2: overcoming of both; vanquishing of both
cūbhayan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text cūbhayan is accusative singular, in apposition to domanassāna; glossed in the commentary as ubhinnaṃ pahānaṃ vūpasamaṃ paṭinissaggaṃ paṭippassaddhiṃ. The form is cited both as cūbhayan and cūbhayaṃ. Possibly a sandhi/contraction of ca + ubhaya.
cūbhayan.example_2: domanassāna cūbhayanti kāmacchandassa ca domanassassa ca ubhinnaṃ pahānaṃ vūpasamaṃ paṭinissaggaṃ paṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—

panūdanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text is a variant with -n, perhaps a reading 'panūdananti'. It glosses the removal and abandoning of sluggardedness (thinassa).
panūdanan.example_2: panūdananti thinassa ca panūdanaṃ pahānaṃ vūpasamaṃ paṭinissaggaṃ paṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—

thinan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text thinan is sandhi for thinaṃ, the object of the definition. The PEU entry thinana may be a related variant.
thinan.example_1: thinanti yā cittassa akalyatā akammaññatā olīyanā sallīyanā līnā līyanā līyitattaṃ thinaṃ thiyanā thiyitattaṃ cittassa.
thinan.example_2: Thinanti yā cittassa akalyatā akammaññatā olīyanā sallīyanā līnā līyanā līyitattaṃ thinaṃ thiyanā [thīnaṃ thīyanā (syā.)] thiyitattaṃ cittassa.
thinan.translation_2: “Sluggishness” (thinan) is the mind’s lack of well-being, incapacity, backsliding, shrinking, the mode of backsliding, the mode of stupor, or the state of remaining in a dense, unexpanded condition.

kukkuccan.meaning_2: worry; scruple; remorse; doubt (about what is proper)
kukkuccan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In these Niddesa passages kukkucca is defined by hatthakukkucca, pādakukkucca, etc. The form kukkuccan is nominative singular in -n (an alternative to kukkuccaṃ), used before ti in the gloss.
kukkuccan.example_1: kukkuccanti hatthakukkuccampi kukkuccaṃ, pādakukkuccampi kukkuccaṃ, hatthapādakukkuccampi kukkuccaṃ.
kukkuccan.example_2: kukkuccanti hatthakukkuccampi kukkuccaṃ, pādakukkuccampi kukkuccaṃ, hatthapādakukkuccampi kukkuccaṃ, akappiye kappiyasaññitā kappiye akappiyasaññitā, vikāle kālasaññitā kāle vikālasaññitā, avajje vajjasaññitā vajje avajjasaññitā;

upekkhāsatisaṃsuddhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes the fourth jhāna. In the text it is the accusative singular of the quoted phrase, written upekkhāsatisaṃsuddhan before ti.
upekkhāsatisaṃsuddhan.example_2: upekkhāsatisaṃsuddhanti catutthe jhāne upekkhā ca sati ca suddhā honti visuddhā saṃsuddhā parisuddhā pariyodātā anaṅgaṇā vigatūpakkilesā mudubhūtā kammaniyā ṭhitā āneñjappattāti—

dhammatakkapurejavan.meaning_2: preceded by right thought; having right intention as forerunner
dhammatakkapurejavan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is accusative singular (dhammatakkapurejavan) modifying a noun. The gloss explains dhammatakka as sammāsaṅkappa, 'right thought'; purejava means 'going before, forerunner'.

pabrūmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present 1st singular in the text, glossed with brūmi ācikkhāmi desemi. Part of the phrase etaṃ te pabrūmi.
pabrūmī.example_2: pabrūmīti brūmi ācikkhāmi desemi paññapemi paṭṭhapemi vivarāmi vibhajāmi uttānīkaromi pakāsemīti—

vicāraṇan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vicāraṇan (with nasal assimilation, for vicāraṇaṃ) is accusative singular. It glosses vitakka ('applied thought') in the Niddesa; the passage analyses it as cāraṇaṃ vicāraṇaṃ paṭivicāraṇaṃ.
vicāraṇan.example_1: kiṃsu tassa vicāraṇanti kiṃsu tassa cāraṇaṃ vicāraṇaṃ paṭivicāraṇaṃ.

tavā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular of the pronoun 'tvaṃ'. Here followed by the emphatic/sandhi particle -ā (tavā = tava + ā), written as one word in the text.
tavā.example_2: Bhagavantaṃ puṭṭhumāgamā, taṃ suṇoma vaco tavā ’’ ti.
tavā.translation_2: We have come to ask the Blessed One; we wish to hear your words.”

kiñcī.meaning_2: something; anything; a little; even a thing
kiñcī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The final -ī in the text is sandhi for kiñci before an initial vowel or a quotation particle (kiñcīti = kiñci + iti). Occurs in the phrase natthi kiñci "there is nothing" and yaṃ kiñci "whatever". Perhaps an emphatic particle -ci.
kiñcī.example_2: yaṃ kiñcīti sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ asesaṃ nissesaṃ pariyādiyanavacanametaṃ—

sakkānupucchāmī.meaning_2: knowing that, I ask; I ask Sakka about knowledge
sakkānupucchāmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Quoted sandhi in the Niddesa gloss (ñāṇaṃ sakkānupucchāmī ti), analysed in the commentary as ñāṇaṃ pucchāmi. Alternative segmentation: sakkā + anupucchāmi, or sandhi of sakka (Sakka, lord of the devas) with anupucchāmi. Appears as the first-person verb in -ti. The text uses extra sandhi vowels.
sakkānupucchāmī.example_2: ñāṇaṃ sakkānupucchāmīti tassa ñāṇaṃ pucchāmi, paññaṃ pucchāmi, sambuddhaṃ pucchāmi.

abhijānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular ending -an is used adverbially, meaning 'while knowing' or 'knowing'. Abhijānanti in the sentence glosses it as abhijānanto vijānanto paṭivijānanto.

tapparāyaṇan.meaning_2: having that as one's refuge; intent on that; devoted to that
tapparāyaṇan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written with a final n (tapparāyaṇan), reflecting the sandhi for -aṃ. In sentence 2 it refers to the goal of the saṅkhāras: taṃ + parāyaṇa, 'that is its support'. PEU suggests ta + parāyaṇa.
tapparāyaṇan.example_2: tapparāyaṇanti ākiñcaññāyatanamayaṃ tapparāyaṇaṃ kammaparāyaṇaṃ vipākaparāyaṇaṃ kammagarukaṃ paṭisandhigarukaṃ.

dhimuttan.meaning_2: resolved upon; intent on; fixed on; attached to
dhimuttan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi form of adhimutta (adhi + mutta with the initial vowel elided). Niddesa commentarial spelling with initial dh; the text glosses it as ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ. Nominative singular in -an rather than the usual -o.

abhiññāyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it appears as abhiññāyā, the -ā being sandhi for abhiññāya or an emphatic ending; some manuscripts read abhiññāya. The word is glossed in the Niddesa with jānitvā, tulayitvā, tīrayitvā, vibhāvayitvā.
abhiññāyā.example_1: evametaṃ abhiññāyāti evaṃ etaṃ abhiññāya jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvāti—

apucchissan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular aorist in the quotation dvāhaṃ sakkaṃ apucchissaṃ; the text explains it with apucchiṃ, ayācissaṃ and ajjhesissaṃ. Written apucchissan before the quotation particle ti.
apucchissan.example_1: dvāhaṃ sakkaṃ apucchissanti so brāhmaṇo dvikkhattuṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pañhaṃ apucchi.
apucchissan.example_2: dvāhaṃ sakkaṃ apucchissanti dvāhaṃ sakkaṃ apucchissaṃ ayācissaṃ ajjhesissaṃ pasādayissanti—

sakkan.meaning_2: Sakka; king of the gods; epithet of Inda
sakkan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text sakkanti sakko, a gloss explaining sakka as sakko. Accusative singular form sakkan is unusual here; possibly a quotation or variant reading. Sakka is the god king also called Inda.

byākāsī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of byākaroti (vi + ā + √kar), used repeatedly in the Niddesa glosses for explaining or answering a question; the -s- form stands beside the more regular byākāsi.
byākāsī.example_1: na me byākāsīti na me byākāsi na ācikkhi na desesi na paññapesi na paṭṭhapesi na vivari na vibhaji na uttānīakāsi na pakāsesi.

nābhijānātī.meaning_2: does not know; does not understand; is not aware (of)
nābhijānātī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Negative of abhijānāti, with na joined by sandhi. 3rd singular present in the text. The gloss explains it as loko na jānāti.
nābhijānātī.example_1: diṭṭhiṃ te nābhijānātīti tuyhaṃ diṭṭhiṃ khantiṃ ruciṃ laddhiṃ ajjhāsayaṃ adhippāyaṃ loko na jānāti—

abhikkantadassāvin.meaning_2: one who sees the supreme; seer of the excellent; one whose vision is outstanding
abhikkantadassāvin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the -ī stem appears as the sandhi form abhikkantadassāvin (before ti), with the base abhikkanta + dassāvī. The Niddesa glosses it with aggadassāviṃ, seṭṭhadassāviṃ, paramadassāviṃ etc. (accusative singular). Sometimes analysed as abhikkanta + disa + āvī.
abhikkantadassāvin.example_1: evaṃ abhikkantadassāvinti evaṃ abhikkantadassāviṃ aggadassāviṃ seṭṭhadassāviṃ viseṭṭhadassāviṃ pāmokkhadassāviṃ uttamadassāviṃ paramadassāvinti—
abhikkantadassāvin.example_2: Evaṃ abhikkantadassāvinti evaṃ abhikkantadassāviṃ aggadassāviṃ seṭṭhadassāviṃ viseṭṭhadassāviṃ pāmokkhadassāviṃ uttamadassāviṃ paramadassāvinti – evaṃ abhikkantadassāviṃ.
abhikkantadassāvin.translation_2: “One who sees in this way” (evaṃ abhikkantadassāvin) means one who sees the supreme, the best, the excellent, the eminent, the principal, the highest, the ultimate, the paramount — this is [the meaning of] “One who sees in this way.”

avekkhantan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle in accusative singular (avekkhantaṃ) in the text, agreeing with lokaṃ. Variants: avekkhantaṃ, avekkhantanti.
avekkhantan.example_1: kathaṃ lokaṃ avekkhantanti kathaṃ lokaṃ avekkhantaṃ paccavekkhantaṃ tulayantaṃ tīrayantaṃ vibhāvayantaṃ vibhūtaṃ karontanti—
avekkhantan.example_2: evaṃ lokaṃ avekkhantanti evaṃ lokaṃ avekkhantaṃ paccavekkhantaṃ tulayantaṃ tīrayantaṃ vibhāvayantaṃ vibhūtaṃ karontanti—

ūhaccā.meaning_2: having pulled up; having uprooted; having removed
ūhaccā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -cca (cf. hacca), glossed in the Niddesa by uddharitvā, uppāṭetvā, pajahitvā. The form ūhaccā in the text has a lengthened final vowel before ti; similar to uhacca, a variant reading noted by the commentary. Often spelt uhacca.
ūhaccā.example_2: attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhaccāti attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhacca samūhacca uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvāti—

jiṇṇohamasmī.meaning_2: I am old; I am aged
jiṇṇohamasmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of jiṇṇo ahaṃ asmi iti, quoting the phrase jiṇṇohamasmi. The Niddesa glosses it with jiṇṇo vuḍḍho mahallako ... vīsavassasatiko jātiyā.
jiṇṇohamasmī.example_1: jiṇṇohamasmīti jiṇṇo vuḍḍho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto vīsavassasatiko jātiyā.

nassan.meaning_2: would perish; would be lost; would be destroyed
nassan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 1st singular nassaṃ in the phrase māhaṃ nassaṃ; the text also has the variant nassan, apparently a sandhi or scribal form of nassaṃ. Same optative is found in the parallel passage.
nassan.example_1: māhaṃ nassanti māhaṃ nassaṃ māhaṃ vinassaṃ māhaṃ panassaṃ.
nassan.example_2: Māhaṃ nassanti māhaṃ nassa māhaṃ vinassaṃ māhaṃ panassaṃ.
nassan.translation_2: ‘Let me not be lost’ means: let me not perish, let me not be destroyed, let me not vanish.

brāhmaṇānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive plural of brāhmaṇa in the compound paricārakasoḷasānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ; the text has the eastern form -ānan for -ānaṃ. Part of a compound with paricārakasoḷasānaṃ, quoted as an explanation of Piṅgiya's relationship to Bāvarī.
brāhmaṇānan.example_1: paricārakasoḷasānaṃ brāhmaṇānanti piṅgiyo brāhmaṇo bāvarissa brāhmaṇassa paddho paddhacaro paricārako sisso.
brāhmaṇānan.example_2: Paricārakasoḷasānaṃ brāhmaṇānanti piṅgiyo [siṅgiyo (ka.)] brāhmaṇo bāvarissa brāhmaṇassa paddho paddhacaro paricārako [paricāriko (syā. ka.)] sisso.
brāhmaṇānan.translation_2: “Of the sixteen attendants” means: Piṅgiya the brahmin was a servant, a follower, an attendant, and a pupil of the brahmin Bāvarī.

paṭipajjeyyā.meaning_2: should practise; should follow; should walk (on); should undertake
paṭipajjeyyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular, spelled paṭipajjeyyā before ti. In the text it glosses dhammānudhammaṃ paṭipajjati, i.e. practising in accordance with the Dhamma; the -ā is the sandhi form of -a before ti.
paṭipajjeyyā.example_1: dhammānudhammaṃ paṭipajjeyyāti sammāpaṭipadaṃ anulomapaṭipadaṃ apaccanīkapaṭipadaṃ anvatthapaṭipadaṃ dhammānudhammapaṭipadaṃ paṭipajjeyyāti—
paṭipajjeyyā.example_2: tathā yo paṭipajjeyyāti sammāpaṭipadaṃ anulomapaṭipadaṃ apaccanīkapaṭipadaṃ anvatthapaṭipadaṃ dhammānudhammapaṭipadaṃ paṭipajjeyyāti—

adhivacanan.meaning_2: designation; term; name; label; conventional expression
adhivacanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the headword of a gloss (adhivacananti …), so it is quoted in the nominative singular without the -ti; the niggahīta is restored as -aṃ. Glossed with saṅkhā, samaññā, paññatti, vohāra, nāma, etc.; often refers to the designation 'pārāyana' in the phrase pārāyananteva adhivacanaṃ.
adhivacanan.example_1: pārāyananteva adhivacananti pāraṃ vuccati amataṃ nibbānaṃ …pe… nirodho nibbānaṃ.
adhivacanan.example_2: adhivacananti saṅkhā samaññā paññatti vohāro nāmaṃ nāmakammaṃ nāmadheyyaṃ nirutti byañjanaṃ abhilāpoti—

upāgacchun.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has upāgacchun, a variant spelling of upāgacchuṃ, the 3rd plural aorist. The commentary explains it with upāgamiṃsu, upasaṅkamiṃsu.
upāgacchun.example_2: ete buddhaṃ upāgacchunti ete buddhaṃ upāgamiṃsu upasaṅkamiṃsu payirupāsiṃsu paripucchiṃsu paripañhiṃsūti—

isin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text isin is the accusative singular of isi, used in the phrase sampannacaraṇaṃ isiṃ. The sandhi form -n is due to the following ti (isinti).
isin.translation_2: “The Sage accomplished in conduct” means conduct is called the production of virtuous behavior.

sampannacaraṇan.meaning_2: accomplished in conduct; perfect in behaviour
sampannacaraṇan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written as sampannacaran with niggahīta before ti (sampannacaraṇanti); explained in the Niddesa by seṭṭhacaraṇaṃ etc. Quoted and glossed in the second sentence.
sampannacaraṇan.example_1: sampannacaraṇanti sampannacaraṇaṃ seṭṭhacaraṇaṃ viseṭṭhacaraṇaṃ pāmokkhacaraṇaṃ uttamacaraṇaṃ pavaracaraṇaṃ.
sampannacaraṇan.example_2: Sampannacaraṇanti sampannacaraṇaṃ seṭṭhacaraṇaṃ viseṭṭhacaraṇaṃ [visiṭṭhacaraṇaṃ (ka.)] pāmokkhacaraṇaṃ uttamacaraṇaṃ pavaracaraṇaṃ.
sampannacaraṇan.translation_2: “Accomplished in conduct” means accomplished in conduct, supreme in conduct, superior in conduct, foremost in conduct, best in conduct, most excellent in conduct.

upāgamun.meaning_2: they approached; they drew near (Best of Buddhas)
upāgamun.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] upāgamuṃ + iti, with the final nasal of the aorist written 'n' before 'ti' (as often in verse). Variant of upāgamuṃ, aorist 3rd plural of upāgacchati (upa + ā + gamu + uṃ). Appears only in the phrase buddhaseṭṭhaṃ upāgamun ti; the PEU entry upāgamuṃ is the same word.
upāgamun.example_2: Pucchantā nipuṇe pañhe, buddhaseṭṭhaṃ upāgamun ’’ ti.
upāgamun.translation_2: Inquiring about subtle questions, they approached the Best of Buddhas.”

pabyākāsī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of pabyākaroti, used in the Niddesa commentary. The form pabyākāsī is the same word with a sandhi -ī before ti.
pabyākāsī.example_2: pabyākāsīti tesaṃ buddho pabyākāsi ācikkhi desesi paññapesi paṭṭhapesi vivari vibhaji uttānīakāsi pakāsesīti—

yathātathan.meaning_2: exactly as it is; in accordance with the truth; as things really are
yathātathan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form yathātathan is sandhi for yathātathaṃ, accusative singular, used adverbially in the phrase pañhaṃ puṭṭho yathātathaṃ (answering a question exactly as it is). The Niddesa glosses it with yathā ... tathā clauses.
yathātathan.example_2: yathātathanti yathā ācikkhitabbaṃ tathā ācikkhi, yathā desitabbaṃ tathā desesi, yathā paññapetabbaṃ tathā paññapesi, yathā paṭṭhapetabbaṃ tathā paṭṭhapesi, yathā vivaritabbaṃ tathā vivari, yathā vibhajitabbaṃ tathā vibhaji, yathā uttānīkātabbaṃ tathā uttānīakāsi, yathā pakāsitabbaṃ tathā pakāsesīti—

veyyākaraṇenā.meaning_2: answer; explanation; exposition; elucidation (of a question)
veyyākaraṇenā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text, in the phrase pañhānaṃ veyyākaraṇena, glossed by ācikkhana, desanā, etc. From vyākaraṇa; the root connection is somewhat doubtful.
veyyākaraṇenā.example_1: pañhānaṃ veyyākaraṇenāti pañhānaṃ veyyākaraṇena ācikkhanena desanena paññapanena paṭṭhapanena vivaraṇena vibhajanena uttānīkammena pakāsanenāti—
veyyākaraṇenā.example_2: Pañhānaṃ veyyākaraṇenāti pañhānaṃ veyyākaraṇena ācikkhanena desanena paññapanena paṭṭhapanena vivaraṇena vibhajanena uttānīkammena pakāsanenāti – pañhānaṃ veyyākaraṇena.
veyyākaraṇenā.translation_2: “By answering the questions” means by declaring, teaching, making known, establishing, opening up, analyzing, clarifying, and revealing the answers to the questions—this is “by answering the questions.”

brahmacariyamacariṃsū.meaning_2: they lived the holy life; they practised the spiritual path
brahmacariyamacariṃsū.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of brahmacariyaṃ + acariṃsu (aorist of carati). Quoted in the Niddesa as a gloss on practicing the holy life; -ti is the quotation marker and is not part of the word.
brahmacariyamacariṃsū.example_1: brahmacariyamacariṃsūti brahmacariyaṃ vuccati asaddhammasamāpattiyā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī viramaṇaṃ akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto.

desitan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it appears as desitan (sandhi for desitaṃ), accusative singular referring to the Buddha's teaching; the gloss in the Niddesa lists synonyms such as desita, paññapita, pakāsita.
desitan.example_2: yathā buddhena desitanti yathā buddhena ācikkhitaṃ desitaṃ paññapitaṃ paṭṭhapitaṃ vivaritaṃ vibhajitaṃ uttānīkataṃ pakāsitanti—

maggamuttaman.meaning_2: foremost path; supreme path; highest path
maggamuttaman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, but the sandhi form maggamuttaman stands for maggamuttamaṃ before ti. Compound of magga + uttama; glossed in the Niddesa as maggaṃ aggaṃ seṭṭhaṃ viseṭṭhaṃ pāmokkhaṃ uttamaṃ pavaraṃ.
maggamuttaman.example_1: bhāvento maggamuttamanti maggamuttamaṃ vuccati ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ—
maggamuttaman.example_2: maggamuttamanti maggaṃ aggaṃ seṭṭhaṃ viseṭṭhaṃ pāmokkhaṃ uttamaṃ pavaraṃ.

gamanāyā.meaning_2: for reaching; for going (to); for arriving (at)
gamanāyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Dative singular of gamana; the -āya ending draws out -āya, and the text glosses it as pāraṃ gamanāya. Often used idiomatically after pāraṃ.
gamanāyā.example_2: pāraṃ gamanāyāti pāraṃ gamanāya pāraṃ sampāpanāya pāraṃ samanupāpanāya jarāmaraṇassa taraṇāyāti—

pārāyanamanugāyissan.meaning_2: will sing after the Pārāyana; will recite in sequence the Pārāyana
pārāyanamanugāyissan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text pārāyanamanugāyissan ti stands for the 1st singular pārāyanamanugāyissaṃ, glossed by gītamanugāyissaṃ (quoted in the 3rd plural bhāsitamanubhāsissanti in sentence 1, which looks stray). Compound verb; the form is 1sg and the headword is the 3sg future of the compound verb pārāyanamanugāyati.
pārāyanamanugāyissan.example_2: Pārāyanamanugāyissanti gītamanugāyissaṃ kathitamanukathayissaṃ [kathitamanugāyissaṃ (syā.) evaṃ sabbapadesu anugāyissanti āgataṃ] bhaṇitamanubhaṇissaṃ lapitamanulapissaṃ bhāsitamanubhāsissanti – pārāyanamanugāyissaṃ.
pārāyanamanugāyissan.translation_2: “I will sing after the Pārāyana” means I will sing in sequence the song [taught by the Blessed One], I will recite in sequence what was told, I will repeat in sequence what was spoken, I will recount in sequence what was spoken—this is “I will sing after the Pārāyana.”

tathākkhāsī.meaning_2: as he saw, so he told
tathākkhāsī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi resolution given in the gloss: tathā + akkhāsi (aorist of akkhāti). The formula yathāddakkhi tathākkhāsi is a stock description of the Buddha's speech.
tathākkhāsī.example_1: yathāddakkhi tathākkhāsīti yathā addakkhi tathā akkhāsi ācikkhi desesi paññapesi paṭṭhapesi vivari vibhaji uttānīakāsi pakāsesi.

malan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text malan is a sandhi form of malaṃ before ti; nominative singular used in a definition of defilements.
malan.example_1: malanti rāgo malaṃ, doso malaṃ, moho malaṃ, māno malaṃ, diṭṭhi malaṃ, kileso malaṃ, sabbaduccaritaṃ malaṃ, sabbabhavagāmikammaṃ malaṃ.

vaṇṇūpasañhitan.meaning_2: connected with colour; endowed with beauty; possessing (pleasing) appearance; accompanied by praise
vaṇṇūpasañhitan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular modifying giraṃ in the text. Variant upasañhita for upasaṃhita (with ṃ > ñ).
vaṇṇūpasañhitan.example_2: kittayissāmi giraṃ vaṇṇūpasañhitanti vaṇṇena upetaṃ samupetaṃ upāgataṃ samupāgataṃ upapannaṃ samupapannaṃ samannāgataṃ vācaṃ giraṃ byappathaṃ udīraṇaṃ kittayissāmi desessāmi paññapessāmi paṭṭhapessāmi vivarissāmi vibhajissāmi uttānīkarissāmi pakāsessāmīti—

handāhan.meaning_2: come now!; well then!; here, take this!
handāhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The Niddesa analyses handāhan as a padasandhi: handa + ahan. handa is an emphatic particle, "come! come now!"; ahan (or haṃ) is an exclamation, "here! look here!" (cf. the canonical handa and haṃ). The text resolves handāhan as handāhaṃ or handa haṃ. Treated here as a sandhi of two indeclinables.
handāhan.example_1: handāhanti padasandhi padasaṃsaggo padapāripūrī akkharasamavāyo byañjanasiliṭṭhatā padānupubbatāpetaṃ—
handāhan.example_2: Handāhanti padasandhi padasaṃsaggo padapāripūrī akkharasamavāyo byañjanasiliṭṭhatā padānupubbatāpetaṃ – handāhanti.
handāhan.translation_2: “Now” is a junction of words, a connection of words, a completion of words, a collection of letters, the smoothness of syllables, and the sequential order of words.

sandiṭṭhikamakālikan.meaning_2: visible in this life and not subject to time; immediately effective and timeless
sandiṭṭhikamakālikan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sandiṭṭhikaṃ + akālikaṃ, quoted and glossed in the Niddesa as sandiṭṭhikaṃ akālikaṃ; an epithet of the Dhamma. Sandhi form in the text.
sandiṭṭhikamakālikan.example_1: sandiṭṭhikamakālikanti sandiṭṭhikaṃ akālikaṃ ehipassikaṃ opaneyyikaṃ paccattaṃ veditabbaṃ viññūhīti—
sandiṭṭhikamakālikan.example_2: sandiṭṭhikamakālikanti sandiṭṭhikaṃ akālikaṃ ehipassikaṃ opaneyyikaṃ paccattaṃ veditabbaṃ viññūhīti, evaṃ sandiṭṭhikaṃ.

akālikan.meaning_2: timeless; not related to time; immediate; not delayed
akālikan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is written akālikanti, i.e. akālikaṃ + iti, and is glossed as a Dhamma not dependent on time, unlike wealth given for a specific period.
akālikan.example_1: akālikanti yathā manussā kālikaṃ dhanaṃ datvā anantarā na labhanti kālaṃ āgamenti, nevāyaṃ dhammo.

taṇhakkhayamanītikan.meaning_2: having the destruction of craving as its guidance; led by the ending of craving
taṇhakkhayamanītikan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, followed by ti as a quotation marker. taṇhakkhaya and manītika are compounds; manītika presumably from √nī with a manī- form, but uncertain.

taṇhakkhayan.meaning_2: destruction of craving; extinction of craving; end of craving
taṇhakkhayan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (taṇhakkhayaṃ); the form taṇhakkhayan is the same accusative with sandhi -ṃ > -n before ti. In the Niddesa gloss it is equated with Nibbāna and with rāgakkhaya, dosakkhaya, mohakkhaya.
taṇhakkhayan.example_1: taṇhakkhayanti taṇhakkhayaṃ rāgakkhayaṃ dosakkhayaṃ mohakkhayaṃ gatikkhayaṃ upapattikkhayaṃ paṭisandhikkhayaṃ bhavakkhayaṃ saṃsārakkhayaṃ vaṭṭakkhayaṃ.
taṇhakkhayan.example_2: taṇhakkhayanti rāgakkhayaṃ dosakkhayaṃ mohakkhayaṃ gatikkhayaṃ upapattikkhayaṃ paṭisandhikkhayaṃ bhavakkhayaṃ saṃsārakkhayaṃ vaṭṭakkhayaṃ patthayanto icchanto sādiyanto pihayanto abhijappantoti—

anītikan.meaning_2: free of trouble (from defilements, aggregates, and volitional formations); suffering no calamity; (as noun) Nibbāna
anītikan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text, the form is the accusative singular anītikan, likely used as a nominative in the gloss? The word is glossed with īti (trouble). Sometimes analyzed as na + nīti + ka.
anītikan.example_1: anītikanti īti vuccanti kilesā ca khandhā ca abhisaṅkhārā ca.
anītikan.example_2: Anītikanti īti vuccanti kilesā ca khandhā ca abhisaṅkhārā ca.
anītikan.translation_2: “Free of trouble” means: defilements, aggregates, and volitional formations are called “trouble.”

kvacī.meaning_2: somewhere; anywhere; in some place; wherever
kvacī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written kvacī before ti (kvacīti) and glossed in the text as kvaci kimhici katthaci, i.e. ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā ajjhattabahiddhā vā.
kvacī.example_2: kvacīti kvaci kimhici katthaci ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā ajjhattabahiddhā vāti—

rattin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text form rattin is accusative singular (niṃ > n Middle Indic); some texts write rattiṃ. Also found as rattiyaṃ and ratto. It is the object of vivasemi ('I dwell/live') in the quoted verse, meaning 'I spend the night'.

avippavāsan.meaning_2: not being separated (from); not living apart (from); non-separation
avippavāsan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the final -aṃ is a sandhi form before ti (avippavāsan ti). Used of not being separated from the Buddha through constant recollection (buddhānussati).
avippavāsan.example_1: teneva maññāmi avippavāsanti tāya buddhānussatiyā bhāvento avippavāsoti taṃ maññāmi, avippavuṭṭhoti taṃ maññāmi jānāmi.
avippavāsan.example_2: Namassamāno vivasemi rattiṃ, teneva maññāmi avippavāsan ’’ ti.
avippavāsan.translation_2: paying homage, I spend the night, and thus I think there is no separation.”

disan.meaning_2: direction; quarter; point of the compass
disan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text disan is the accusative singular of disa (a-stem, niggahīta before ti: disaṃ ti > disan ti). Sentence 1 refers to the eastern, western, southern and northern quarters; sentence 2 means 'not going in the direction of one who is going'. The related entry disa looks corrupt (perhaps for disā); the meaning 'direction' is the one required here.
disan.example_1: yaṃ yaṃ disanti puratthimaṃ vā disaṃ pacchimaṃ vā disaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ vā disaṃ uttaraṃ vā disaṃ vajati gacchati kamati abhikkamati.

natohamasmī.meaning_2: I am inclined toward that; I am bent toward that
natohamasmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of nato (past participle of namati, 'inclined; bent') + ahaṃ + asmi. Occurs in the refrain sa tena teneva natohamasmī ti, quoted to explain inclination toward the Buddha. Sometimes written natohamasmi.
natohamasmī.example_1: sa tena teneva natohamasmīti so yena buddho tena teneva nato tanninno tappoṇo tappabbhāro tadadhimutto tadadhipateyyoti—
natohamasmī.example_2: Sa tena teneva natohamasmīti so yena buddho tena teneva nato tanninno tappoṇo tappabbhāro tadadhimutto tadadhipateyyoti – sa tena teneva natohamasmi.
natohamasmī.translation_2: “I am inclined toward that very side” means: wherever the Buddha is, I am inclined, bent toward, sloped toward, intent on, and have that as my sovereign — thus “I am inclined toward that very side.”

niccan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text niccan is sandhi for niccaṃ (always) before the quotation, the same word glossed as niccaṃ in the second version. Sometimes classed as an adjective nicca (permanent), but here it functions as an adverb.
niccan.example_1: saṅkappayantāya vajāmi niccanti saṅkappagamanena vitakkagamanena ñāṇagamanena paññāgamanena buddhigamanena vajāmi gacchāmi atikkamāmīti—
niccan.example_2: Saṅkappayantāya vajāmi niccanti saṅkappagamanena vitakkagamanena ñāṇagamanena paññāgamanena buddhigamanena vajāmi gacchāmi atikkamāmīti – saṅkappayantāya vajāmi niccaṃ.
niccan.translation_2: “By intending, I always go” means: by the movement of intention, by the movement of thought, by the movement of knowledge, by the movement of wisdom, by the movement of understanding, I go, I proceed, I surpass — thus “by intending, I always go.”

upallavin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular, quoted in the Niddesa to explain upallaviṃ. Doubtful derivation; possibly from √plu (float, swim), with the doubled l and v. Same meaning as upallaviṃ in the following gloss.
upallavin.example_1: dīpā dīpaṃ upallavinti satthārato satthāraṃ dhammakkhānato dhammakkhānaṃ gaṇato gaṇaṃ diṭṭhiyā diṭṭhiṃ paṭipadāya paṭipadaṃ maggato maggaṃ pallaviṃ upallaviṃ sampallavinti—
upallavin.example_2: Dīpā dīpaṃ upallavinti satthārato satthāraṃ dhammakkhānato dhammakkhānaṃ gaṇato gaṇaṃ diṭṭhiyā diṭṭhiṃ paṭipadāya paṭipadaṃ maggato maggaṃ pallaviṃ upallaviṃ sampallavinti – dīpā dīpaṃ upallaviṃ.
upallavin.translation_2: “I swam from island to island” means: from one teacher to another teacher, from one Dhamma-preacher to another, from one group to another, from one view to another, from one practice to another, from one path to another, I swam, swam across, and swam thoroughly — thus “I swam from island to island.”

sambuddhan.meaning_2: fully awakened one; the Buddha; perfectly enlightened one
sambuddhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (sambuddhaṃ with sandhi -n before t-); an epithet of the Buddha. Could also be analysed as saṃ + √budh + ta.

athā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of atha + a; the text glosses it as padasandhi etc. Alternative: atha + iti? No, it is atha + a (vowel sandhi).
athā.example_1: athāti padasandhi padasaṃsaggo padapāripūrī akkharasamavāyo byañjanasiliṭṭhatā padānupubbatāpetaṃ—

addasāsin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 2nd singular form, used in the string addasaṃ addakkhiṃ apassiṃ paṭivijjhiṃ explaining addasāsi; the text's addasāsin is addasāsi + ni (or an emphatic variant).

saddhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (saddhan = saddhaṃ). The sandhi -n is m before muñcassu; the glossing prose explains it with saddhaṃ muñcassu. Sometimes written saddhā (fem); here masculine accusative.
saddhan.example_1: evameva tvampi pamuñcassu saddhanti evameva tvaṃ saddhaṃ muñcassu pamuñcassu sampamuñcassu adhimuñcassu okappehi.

pasīdāmī.meaning_2: trusts; has confidence (in); is pleased (with); believes
pasīdāmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 1st person singular in the text (pasīdāmi), glossed by saddahāmi, okappemi, adhimuccāmi. Headword given as the present 3rd singular.
pasīdāmī.example_1: esa bhiyyo pasīdāmīti esa bhiyyo pasīdāmi, bhiyyo bhiyyo saddahāmi, bhiyyo bhiyyo okappemi, bhiyyo bhiyyo adhimuccāmi;

chadanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is used in a gloss (chadananti) and nominative singular (chadanan-ti = chadanaṃ iti). The five veils are taṇhāchadana, diṭṭhichadana, kilesachadana, duccaritachadana, avijjāchadana. The sandhi -an before ti is resolved as -aṃ.
chadanan.example_2: Chadananti pañca chadanāni – taṇhāchadanaṃ, diṭṭhichadanaṃ, kilesachadanaṃ, duccaritachadanaṃ, avijjāchadanaṃ.
chadanan.translation_2: “Veil” means: the veil of craving, the veil of views, the veil of defilements, the veil of misconduct, the veil of ignorance.

paroparan.meaning_2: higher and lower; other and further; superior and inferior
paroparan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi form of paroparaṃ; the -ṃ has been assimilated to the initial b- of the following bhagavā? Here it stands at the end of the verse 'sabbaṃ vedi paroparan ti'. The word means 'the higher and the lower' (i.e., all things), and is glossed by attano ca paresañca adhidevakare dhamme.
paroparan.example_1: sabbaṃ vedi paroparanti bhagavā attano ca paresañca adhidevakare dhamme vedi aññāsi aphassi paṭivijjhi.

paṭijānatan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In 'kaṅkhīnaṃ paṭijānatan', genitive plural (skr. -atām); some editions read paṭijānataṃ. The phrase is a quotation glossed in the Niddesa.
paṭijānatan.example_1: kaṅkhīnaṃ paṭijānatanti sakaṅkhā āgantvā nikkaṅkhā sampajjanti, sallekhā āgantvā nillekhā sampajjanti, sadveḷhakā āgantvā nidveḷhakā sampajjanti, savicikicchā āgantvā nibbicikicchā sampajjanti, sarāgā āgantvā vītarāgā sampajjanti, sadosā āgantvā vītadosā sampajjanti, samohā āgantvā vītamohā sampajjanti, sakilesā āgantvā nikkilesā sampajjantīti—
paṭijānatan.example_2: Kaṅkhīnaṃ paṭijānatanti sakaṅkhā āgantvā nikkaṅkhā sampajjanti, sallekhā āgantvā nillekhā sampajjanti, sadveḷhakā āgantvā nidveḷahakā sampajjanti, savicikicchā āgantvā nibbicikicchā sampajjanti, sarāgā āgantvā vītarāgā sampajjanti, sadosā āgantvā vītadosā sampajjanti, samohā āgantvā vītamohā sampajjanti, sakilesā āgantvā nikkilesā sampajjantīti – kaṅkhīnaṃ paṭijānataṃ.
paṭijānatan.translation_2: “For those who are perplexed who acknowledge” means those who are perplexed come and become free of doubt, those who are scattered come and become settled, those who have two minds come and become of one mind, those who are in doubt come and become free of doubt, those who are full of lust come and become free of lust, those who are full of hatred come and become free of hatred, those who are full of delusion come and become free of delusion, those who are defiled come and become free of defilements—that is “for those who are perplexed who acknowledge.”

nidveḷhakā.meaning_2: free from doubt; without hesitation; devoid of perplexity
nidveḷhakā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it stands for nidveḷhakā, nominative plural, in the list of contrasts (sadveḷhakā → nidveḷhakā). The prefix ni- negates dveḷhaka (doubt, hesitation).
nidveḷhakā.example_1: kaṅkhīnaṃ paṭijānatanti sakaṅkhā āgantvā nikkaṅkhā sampajjanti, sallekhā āgantvā nillekhā sampajjanti, sadveḷhakā āgantvā nidveḷhakā sampajjanti, savicikicchā āgantvā nibbicikicchā sampajjanti, sarāgā āgantvā vītarāgā sampajjanti, sadosā āgantvā vītadosā sampajjanti, samohā āgantvā vītamohā sampajjanti, sakilesā āgantvā nikkilesā sampajjantīti—

asaṅkuppan.meaning_2: immovable; unshakeable; not to be stirred
asaṅkuppan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Glossed with amataṃ nibbānaṃ. In the text it is a quotation form (asaṅkuppan ti), possibly a sandhi of asaṅkuppaṃ; nominative/accusative neuter singular.

asaṃhīran.meaning_2: not able to be shaken; immovable; unshakeable
asaṃhīran.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text asaṃhīran is a sandhi of asaṃhīraṃ (nominative/accusative neuter agreeing with nibbānaṃ); the gloss is asaṃhāriyaṃ. The na + saṃhīra compound with the negative na.
asaṃhīran.example_1: asaṃhīranti rāgena dosena mohena kodhena upanāhena makkhena paḷāsena issāya macchariyena māyāya sāṭheyyena thambhena sārambhena mānena atimānena madena pamādena sabbakilesehi sabbaduccaritehi sabbapariḷāhehi sabbāsavehi sabbadarathehi sabbasantāpehi sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārehi asaṃhāriyaṃ nibbānaṃ niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ avipariṇāmadhammanti—
asaṃhīran.example_2: Asaṃhīranti rāgena dosena mohena kodhena upanāhena makkhena paḷāsena issāya macchariyena māyāya sāṭheyyena thambhena sārambhena mānena atimānena madena pamādena sabbakilesehi sabbaduccaritehi sabbapariḷāhehi sabbāsavehi sabbadarathehi sabbasantāpehi sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārehi asaṃhāriyaṃ nibbānaṃ niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ avipariṇāmadhammanti – asaṃhīraṃ.
asaṃhīran.translation_2: “Unshakable” means it is Nibbāna that cannot be shaken by lust, hatred, delusion, anger, resentment, smearing, disparagement, envy, selfishness, deceit, dissimulation, stubbornness, haughtiness, conceit, arrogance, intoxication, carelessness, all defilements, all misconduct, all burning, all taints, all fever, all heating, all unwholesome volitional formations; it is constant, everlasting, eternal, and not subject to change—that is “unshakable.”

etthā.meaning_2: here; in this place; in this regard; herein
etthā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form in the text is etthā, a sandhi variant of ettha before the quotation marker ti (etthāti). The Niddesa glosses it with different senses: 'in nibbāna', 'in one's own view', 'in beings'. Indeclinable.
etthā.example_1: etthāti nibbāne kaṅkhā natthi, vicikicchā natthi, dveḷhakaṃ natthi, saṃsayo natthi, na atthi na saṃvijjati nupalabbhati, pahīno samucchinno vūpasanto paṭippassaddho abhabbuppattiko ñāṇagginā daḍḍhoti—
etthā.example_2: etthāti sakāya diṭṭhiyā sakāya khantiyā sakāya ruciyā sakāya laddhiyā paraṃ bālato hīnato nihīnato omakato lāmakato chatukkato parittato kaṃ daheyya kaṃ passeyya kaṃ dakkheyya kaṃ olokeyya kaṃ nijjhāyeyya kaṃ upaparikkheyyāti—

adhimuttacittan.meaning_2: with a mind inclined (towards); whose mind is devoted (to); intent in mind
adhimuttacittan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the final consonant is niggahīta (adhimuttacittan) and the word is in the accusative singular, agreeing with maṃ in the Niddesa quotation; the commentarial gloss explains it as nibbānādhimutta, "inclined towards nibbāna".

dhārehī.meaning_2: hold; bear in mind; remember; acknowledge
dhārehī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative 2nd singular of dhāreti (causative of dharati) with the ending -hi. In the text 'evaṃ maṃ dhārehīti' means 'thus you should remember me' or 'bear it in mind thus'. Some analyses take it as a causative imperative meaning 'cause to hold; establish'.

daṇḍan.meaning_2: stick; rod; staff; punishment; violence; force
daṇḍan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular with niggahīta (daṇḍaṃ) in the text. In the phrase nidhāya daṇḍaṃ it means laying aside violence or the rod towards all beings.

sahāyan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (sahāyan). In the verse na puttamiccheyya kuto sahāyan and the Niddesa gloss; the gloss explains sahāya as one with whom coming and going, sitting, lying down, and conversing are easy.
sahāyan.example_2: sahāyanti sahāyā vuccanti yehi saha āgamanaṃ phāsu, gamanaṃ phāsu, gamanāgamanaṃ phāsu, ṭhānaṃ phāsu, nisajjanaṃ phāsu, sayanaṃ phāsu, ālapanaṃ phāsu, sallapanaṃ phāsu, ullapanaṃ phāsu, samullapanaṃ phāsu.

atthan.meaning_2: goal; benefit; welfare; good; purpose; meaning
atthan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Here the form is atthaṃ, accusative singular (written atthan before ti by sandhi). The commentary glosses it with attattha, parattha, diṭṭhadhammika attha, samparāyika attha and paramattha, i.e. 'goal; benefit'.
atthan.example_1: mitte suhajje anukampamāno hāpeti atthanti mitte ca suhajje ca sandiṭṭhe ca sambhatte ca sahāye ca anukampamāno anupekkhamāno anugaṇhamāno attatthampi paratthampi ubhayatthampi hāpeti, diṭṭhadhammikampi atthaṃ hāpeti, samparāyikampi atthaṃ hāpeti, paramatthampi hāpeti pahāpeti parihāpeti paridhaṃseti parivajjeti antaradhāpetīti—
atthan.example_2: Mitte suhajje anukampamāno hāpeti atthanti mitte ca suhajje ca sandiṭṭhe ca sambhatte ca sahāye ca anukampamāno anupekkhamāno anugaṇhamāno attatthampi paratthampi ubhayatthampi hāpeti, diṭṭhadhammikampi atthaṃ hāpeti, samparāyikampi atthaṃ hāpeti, paramatthampi hāpeti pahāpeti parihāpeti paridhaṃseti parivajjeti [parisajjeti (syā.)] antaradhāpetīti – mitte suhajje anukampamāno hāpeti atthaṃ.
atthan.translation_2: “Compassionate to friends and well-wishers, one puts off the goal” means: being compassionate, observant, and supportive toward friends, well-wishers, those seen together, those associated together, and companions, one ruins, destroys, and loses one's own goal, another's goal, and both goals; one ruins, destroys, loses, abandons, and causes to disappear the goal pertaining to the present life, the goal pertaining to the future life, and the ultimate goal—thus, “compassionate to friends and well-wishers, one puts off the goal.”

bhayan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written as bhayan before ti (bhayaṃ + iti). Neuter noun; nominative singular with niggahīta.
bhayan.example_1: bhayanti jātibhayaṃ jarābhayaṃ byādhibhayaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ rājabhayaṃ corabhayaṃ aggibhayaṃ udakabhayaṃ attānuvādabhayaṃ parānuvādabhayaṃ daṇḍabhayaṃ duggatibhayaṃ ūmibhayaṃ kumbhilabhayaṃ āvaṭṭabhayaṃ susumārabhayaṃ ājīvikabhayaṃ asilokabhayaṃ parisasārajjabhayaṃ madanabhayaṃ bhayānakaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso cetaso ubbego utrāso.

gocarāyā.meaning_2: for grazing; for pasture; for food
gocarāyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Dative form of gocara used adverbially in the text; possibly a sandhi variant of gocarāya. The related entry gocara (masc) means 'grazing; pasture; attention'. Here in the poetic simile it means 'for grazing'.
gocarāyā.example_1: migo araññamhi yathā abaddho, yenicchakaṃ gacchati gocarāyāti.

cārikāyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa verse cārikāyā is ablative/genitive singular governed by vāse ṭhāne gamane; the commentary glosses it with the locative cārikāyapi.
cārikāyā.example_1: āmantanā hoti sahāyamajjhe, vāse ṭhāne gamane cārikāyāti sahāyā vuccanti yehi saha āgamanaṃ phāsu gamanaṃ phāsu gamanāgamanaṃ phāsu ṭhānaṃ phāsu nisajjanaṃ phāsu sayanaṃ phāsu ālapanaṃ phāsu sallapanaṃ phāsu ullapanaṃ phāsu samullapanaṃ phāsu.
cārikāyā.example_2: āmantanā hoti sahāyamajjhe, vāse ṭhāne gamane cārikāyāti sahāyamajjhe vāsepi ṭhānepi gamanepi cārikāyapi attatthamantanā paratthamantanā ubhayatthamantanā diṭṭhadhammikatthamantanā samparāyikatthamantanā paramatthamantanā ti—

peman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text spelled peman (and once pemaṃ), probably sandhi for pemaṃ before 'ti'. Locative plural puttesu expresses the object of affection.
peman.example_2: puttesu ca vipulaṃ hoti pemanti puttesu ca adhimattaṃ hoti pemanti—

gihibyañjanānī.meaning_2: layperson's mark; sign of a householder; layman's adornment
gihibyañjanānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative plural in the text (gihibyañjanāni), object of oropayitvā / ohārayitvā. Glossed in the Niddesa with hairdressing, garlands, ornaments, weapons etc.
gihibyañjanānī.example_1: oropayitvā gihibyañjanānīti gihibyañjanāni vuccanti kesā ca massū ca mālā ca gandhañca vilepanañca ābharaṇañca pilandhanañca vatthañca pārupanañca veṭhanañca ucchādanaṃ parimaddanaṃ nhāpanaṃ sambāhanaṃ ādāsaṃ añjanaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ mukhacuṇṇaṃ mukhalepanaṃ hatthabandhaṃ sikhābandhaṃ daṇḍaṃ nāḷikaṃ khaggaṃ chattaṃ citrupāhanaṃ uṇhīsaṃ maṇiṃ vāḷabījaniṃ odātāni vatthāni dīghadasāni iti vā.
gihibyañjanānī.example_2: oropayitvā gihibyañjanānīti gihibyañjanāni oropayitvā samoropayitvā nikkhipitvā paṭipassambhayitvāti—

gihibandhanānī.meaning_2: bond of household life; fetter of a householder; tie of sense desire
gihibandhanānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the accusative plural gihibandhanāni (with the sandhi -ānī before ti). The Niddesa explains it as gihibandhanāni chinditvā. Bandhana from √bandh is added to gihi as a compound member.
gihibandhanānī.example_2: chetvāna vīro gihibandhanānīti so paccekasambuddho vīro gihibandhanāni chinditvā samucchinditvā jahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvāti—

dhīran.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular of dhīra used adverbially in the text (dhīraṃ), with the niggahīta assimilated to the following t (dhīran ti = dhīraṃ + iti). Explained by the gloss paṇḍitaṃ paññavantaṃ buddhimantaṃ ñāṇiṃ vibhāviṃ medhāviṃ.
dhīran.example_2: dhīranti dhīraṃ paṇḍitaṃ paññavantaṃ buddhimantaṃ ñāṇiṃ vibhāviṃ medhāvinti—

sādhuvihārin.meaning_2: living well; dwelling well; one who lives well
sādhuvihārin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the accusative singular sādhuvihāriṃ, quoted and glossed in the Niddesa as one who dwells well through the jhānas, the divine abidings and the attainments. The alternative stem sādhuvihārin is also found; cf. the PEU entry sādhuvihārī.

sahāyasampadan.meaning_2: possession of a friend; the good fortune of having a companion
sahāyasampadan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has sahāyasampadan, which the commentary explains as sahāyasampadaṃ, accusative singular of sahāyasampadā. It is used in the sense of the blessing of having a good friend (sahāya) who possesses the virtue, concentration, wisdom, liberation and knowledge of liberation of an arahant. The form may also be analysed as sahāya + sampada (masc/nt).
sahāyasampadan.example_2: sahāyasampadanti sahāyasampadā vuccati yo so sahāyo asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena samādhikkhandhena …

pabhassarānī.meaning_2: very bright; radiant; shining; luminous; pure and clear
pabhassarānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is neuter plural (pabhassarāni), agreeing with suvaṇṇassa (bracelets of gold); glossed parisuddhāni pariyodātāni. Occasionally taken as pa + bhā + sara.
pabhassarānī.example_1: disvā suvaṇṇassa pabhassarānīti disvā passitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā.

suniṭṭhitānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Grammatically neuter plural in the text, agreeing with the implied items made by the smith.

bhujasmin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular bhujasmin in the gloss bhujo vuccati hattho (the arm is called the hand). Root doubtful; possibly √bhuj 2 (bend).

cittan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written cittan before ti (cittaṃ). Object of mathenti in the text; also appears as cittaṃ in the gloss.
cittan.example_2: Virūparūpena mathenti cittanti nānāvaṇṇehi rūpehi … pe … nānāvaṇṇehi phoṭṭhabbehi cittaṃ mathenti tosenti pahāsentīti – virūparūpena mathenti cittaṃ.
cittan.translation_2: “Through their diverse forms, they crush the mind” means through diverse forms... through diverse tangibles, they crush, gladden, and refresh the mind—this is the meaning of ‘through their diverse forms, they crush the mind’.

pipāsan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, the object of khudaṃ together with it: 'cold and heat, hunger and thirst'. The related PEU entry gives pipāsa as a feminine/neuter noun in -ā; here it is treated as an a-stem masculine. The sandhi -aṃ before the quotation -ti is written as the accusative ending.

sītan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text sītan is the sandhi form of sītaṃ (nominative singular neuter), quoted and glossed by the commentary. Also occurs as a neuter noun meaning cold, coolness.
sītan.example_2: Sītanti dvīhi kāraṇehi sītaṃ hoti – abbhantaradhātuppakopavasena [abbhantaradhātusaṅkopavasena (syā.)] vā sītaṃ hoti, bahiddhā utuvasena vā sītaṃ hoti.
sītan.translation_2: “Cold” occurs for two reasons: cold happens due to the disturbance of the internal elements, or cold happens due to external seasons.

uṇhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text uṇhan ti is the citation form uṇhaṃ with the quotation enclitic -ti assimilated; the gloss explains heat as arising from internal elements or external seasons.
uṇhan.example_2: Uṇhanti dvīhi kāraṇehi uṇhaṃ hoti – abbhantaradhātuppakopavasena vā uṇhaṃ hoti, bahiddhā utuvasena vā uṇhaṃ hotīti – sītaṃ athuṇhaṃ.
uṇhan.translation_2: “Heat” occurs for two reasons: heat happens due to the disturbance of the internal elements, or heat happens due to external seasons—this is “cold and heat.”

vimuttin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vimuttin is the accusative singular of this ī-stem noun (vimuttiṃ). It occurs in a quotation of a verse: 'sāmayikaṃ vimuttiṃ'.
vimuttin.example_1: aṭṭhānataṃ saṅgaṇikāratassa, yaṃ phassaye sāmayikaṃ vimuttinti vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā—

parivajjayethā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text as parivajjayethā, which is the optative 2nd person plural with a middle/reflexive ending, though the form is quoted inside a sentence with ti; the present 3rd singular is used as headword. Cf. the related root vajj (turn, avoid).

niviṭṭhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular qualifying visame and anatthadassiṃ; in the gloss repeated with kāyakamme etc. it means 'engaged in, given over to'. Doubtful root: √vis 1 (enter) fits the sense 'settled in'.
niviṭṭhan.example_1: anatthadassiṃ visame niviṭṭhanti anatthadassī vuccati yo so sahāyo dasavatthukāya micchādiṭṭhiyā samannāgato—
niviṭṭhan.example_2: visame niviṭṭhanti visame kāyakamme niviṭṭhaṃ, visame vacīkamme niviṭṭhaṃ, visame manokamme niviṭṭhaṃ, visame pāṇātipāte niviṭṭhaṃ, visame adinnādāne niviṭṭhaṃ, visame kāmesumicchācāre niviṭṭhaṃ, visame musāvāde niviṭṭhaṃ, visamāya pisuṇāya vācāya niviṭṭhaṃ, visamāya pharusāya vācāya niviṭṭhaṃ, visame samphappalāpe niviṭṭhaṃ, visamāya abhijjhāya niviṭṭhaṃ, visame byāpāde niviṭṭhaṃ, visamāya micchādiṭṭhiyā niviṭṭhaṃ, visamesu saṅkhāresu niviṭṭhaṃ visamesu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu niviṭṭhaṃ, visamesu pañcasu nīvaraṇesu niviṭṭhaṃ viniviṭṭhaṃ sattaṃ allīnaṃ upagataṃ ajjhositaṃ adhimuttanti—

pamattan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Secondary sandhi form of pamattaṃ, accusative singular agreeing with pasutaṃ; glossed in the Niddesa with pamattañca.

pasutan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used adjectivally, agreeing with kāmappasuto (nom sg masc). The Niddesa glosses it with esati gavesati pariyesati, i.e. 'one who seeks'.
pasutan.example_1: pasutanti yopi kāme esati gavesati pariyesati taccarito tabbahulo taggaruko tanninno tappoṇo tappabbhāro tadadhimutto tadadhipateyyo, sopi kāmappasuto.
pasutan.example_2: Pasutanti yopi kāme esati gavesati pariyesati taccarito tabbahulo taggaruko tannino tappoṇo tappabbhāro tadadhimutto tadadhipateyyo, sopi kāmappasuto.
pasutan.translation_2: ‘Engaged’ means: whoever searches for, seeks, and hunts for sensual pleasures, and is thus behaving, is thus habituated, is thus attentive, is thus inclined, is thus leaning, is thus leaning toward, is thus resolved, is thus subjected — he is engaged in sensuality.

bhajethā.meaning_2: should associate with; should keep company with; should resort to
bhajethā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optional 2nd person singular (bhajetha) used imperatively; the gloss explains it with bhajeyya. From the quotation bahussutaṃ dhammadharaṃ bhajethā ti.
bhajethā.example_1: bahussutaṃ dhammadharaṃ bhajethāti bahussuto hoti mitto sutadharo sutasannicayo.
bhajethā.example_2: bahussutaṃ dhammadharaṃ bhajethāti bahussutañca dhammadharañca mittaṃ bhajeyya sambhajeyya seveyya niseveyya saṃseveyya paṭiseveyyāti—

dhammadharan.meaning_2: one who holds the Dhamma; bearer of the teachings
dhammadharan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular masculine in the text (dhammadharaṃ); compounded of dhamma + dhara.
dhammadharan.example_2: Dhammadharanti dhammaṃ dhārentaṃ [dhāreti (ka.)]– suttaṃ geyyaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ gāthaṃ udānaṃ itivuttakaṃ jātakaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ vedallaṃ.
dhammadharan.translation_2: “Holder of the Dhamma” means one who holds the Dhamma — the discourse, the stanzas, the exposition, the verse, the solemn utterance, the sayings, the birth stories, the marvels, and the answers to questions.

paṭibhānavantan.meaning_2: possessing wisdom; endowed with ready wit; eloquent
paṭibhānavantan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (mittaṃ ... paṭibhānavantaṃ). The Niddesa glosses it with uḷāro and explains three kinds of paṭibhāna.
paṭibhānavantan.example_1: mittaṃ uḷāraṃ paṭibhānavantanti uḷāro hoti mitto sīlena samādhinā paññāya vimuttiyā vimuttiñāṇadassanena.

kaṅkhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text kaṅkhan is a sandhi form of kaṅkhaṃ, the accusative singular of kaṅkhā (doubt), as the gloss kaṅkhaṃ vineyya confirms; the reading without sandhi would be kaṅkhaṃ. Sometimes analysed as kaṅkhā + aṃ.
kaṅkhan.example_1: aññāya atthāni vineyya kaṅkhanti attatthaṃ aññāya paratthaṃ aññāya ubhayatthaṃ aññāya diṭṭhadhammikatthaṃ aññāya samparāyikatthaṃ aññāya paramatthaṃ aññāya abhiññāya jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā kaṅkhaṃ vineyya paṭivineyya pajaheyya vinodeyya byantīkareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyyāti—
kaṅkhan.example_2: Aññāya atthāni vineyya kaṅkhanti attatthaṃ aññāya paratthaṃ aññāya ubhayatthaṃ aññāya diṭṭhadhammikatthaṃ aññāya samparāyikatthaṃ aññāya paramatthaṃ aññāya abhiññāya jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā kaṅkhaṃ vineyya paṭivineyya pajaheyya vinodeyya byantīkareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyyāti – aññāya atthāni vineyya kaṅkhaṃ, eko care khaggavisāṇakappo.
kaṅkhan.translation_2: “Having known beneficial things, having abandoned doubt” means having known one’s own benefit, having known the benefit of others, having known both, having known the benefit of the present life, having known the benefit of the next life, having known the ultimate benefit, having known with direct knowledge, having calculated, having judged, having clarified, having made evident, having abandoned, having dispelled, having destroyed, having eradicated, having driven out, having caused the non-existence of doubt — thus, having known beneficial things, having abandoned doubt, one should wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.

kāmasukhan.meaning_2: sensual pleasure; pleasure of the senses; happiness from sense desires
kāmasukhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is quoted as kāmasukhan ti (sandhi for kāmasukhaṃ iti), introducing a quotation from the Buddha. Accusative singular.
kāmasukhan.translation_2: “Sensual pleasure” is what the Blessed One said —

mātaran.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Irregular accusative singular of mātā (from mātar), used in the compound phrase puttañca dāraṃ pitarañca mātaran; the form mātaran is the accusative of mātar at the end of the quotative clause.

bandhavānī.meaning_2: relatives and wealth; kinsmen and treasures
bandhavānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is explained as dhanāni dhaññāni ca bandhavānī ti, and then glossed as cattāro bandhavā. Possibly a sandhi of bandhavā (nominative plural of bandhava) + ānī, or a textual variant for bandhavāni (neut nom pl).
bandhavānī.example_1: dhanāni dhaññāni ca bandhavānīti dhanāni vuccanti hiraññaṃ suvaṇṇaṃ muttā maṇi veḷuriyo saṅkho silā pavāḷaṃ rajataṃ jātarūpaṃ lohitaṅgo masāragallaṃ.

yathodhikānī.meaning_2: according to one's share; as allocated; in accordance with one's portion
yathodhikānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is neuter nominative/accusative plural, agreeing with kāmāni ('sense pleasures as allotted'). Commentarial gloss on the verse; sandhi yathā + odhika > yathodhika.
yathodhikānī.example_2: hitvāna kāmāni yathodhikānīti sotāpattimaggena ye kilesā pahīnā, te kilese na puneti na pacceti na paccāgacchati;

kāmānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative plural kāmāni in the quoted phrase hitvāna kāmānī ti (Niddesa); the -ī is sandhi for -i before ti. The word is glossed with vatthukāme and kilesakāme.
kāmānī.example_1: hitvāna kāmānīti vatthukāme parijānitvā, kilesakāme pahāya pajahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvā.

sokhyan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form in the text (sokhyan) shows sandhi -ṃ + vowel. PEU suggests sukha + ṇya; DPD analysis uncertain.
sokhyan.example_1: saṅgo eso parittamettha sokhyanti saṅgoti vā baḷisanti vā āmisanti vā laggananti vā palibodhoti vā, pañcannetaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ adhivacanaṃ.

saṃyojanānī.meaning_2: fetter; bond; tie that binds (to existence)
saṃyojanānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is plural (dasa saṃyojanāni, the ten fetters) with -ī as a sandhi variant of -āni before the quotative ti (saṃyojanānī ti).
saṃyojanānī.example_2: sandālayitvāna saṃyojanānīti dasa saṃyojanāni dālayitvā sandālayitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvāti—

sinehadosan.meaning_2: fault of affection; defect of fondness
sinehadosan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of sineha (affection, fondness) and dosa (fault, defect). The text has the accusative singular sinehadosaṃ (written sinehadosan before ti). The commentary explains it as taṇhāsneha, diṭṭhisneha and dosa.
sinehadosan.example_2: anissito chetva sinehadosanti so paccekasambuddho taṇhāsnehañca diṭṭhisnehañca dosañca chetvā ucchinditvā samucchinditvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvā cakkhuṃ anissito,

somanassadomanassan.meaning_2: joy and distress; pleasure and displeasure; happiness and sadness
somanassadomanassan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse the final -ṃ is elided before ti (somanassadomanassanti). Elsewhere in the same passage the full form somanassadomanassānaṃ (genitive plural) occurs.
somanassadomanassan.example_1: vipiṭṭhikatvāna sukhaṃ dukhañca, pubbeva ca somanassadomanassanti so paccekasambuddho sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharatīti—
somanassadomanassan.example_2: Vipiṭṭhikatvāna sukhaṃ dukhañca , pubbeva ca somanassadomanassanti so paccekasambuddho sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharatīti – vipiṭṭhikatvāna sukhaṃ dukhañca, pubbeva ca somanassadomanassaṃ.
somanassadomanassan.translation_2: “Having put aside happiness and suffering beforehand, and joy and distress beforehand as well” means that Solitary Awakened One, through the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of suffering, and through the prior dying away of joy and distress, enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which is without ease and without pain, and possesses complete purity of mindfulness owing to equanimity—this is the meaning of “having put aside happiness and suffering beforehand, and joy and distress beforehand as well.”

visuddhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is visuddhaṃ, accusative singular agreeing with samathaṃ; the sandhi with the following quote gives visuddhan ti. From the root √sudh with the prefix vi, as in visujjhati.
visuddhan.example_2: laddhānupekkhaṃ samathaṃ visuddhanti catutthajjhānaṃ upekkhañca samathañca laddhā labhitvā vinditvā paṭilabhitvāti—

senāsanānī.meaning_2: dwelling; lodging; resting place; secluded abode
senāsanānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural forms senāsanāni (nom/acc). In the text senāsanānī is sandhi with following ti, i.e. senāsanāni + iti. Often in the phrase pantāni senāsanāni, secluded dwellings.
senāsanānī.example_1: sevetha pantāni senāsanānīti yathā sīho migarājā araññavanamajjhogāhetvā carati viharati iriyati vatteti pāleti yapeti yāpeti, paccekasambuddhopi araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevati appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni.

mohan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is written mohan before ti (mohaṃ + iti). It is the accusative singular in the phrase rāgañca dosañca mohan ti = rāgaṃ ca dosaṃ ca mohaṃ. The commentary explains it as rāgaṃ ca dosaṃ ca mohaṃ.
mohan.example_2: rāgañca dosañca pahāya mohanti so paccekasambuddho rāgañca dosañca mohañca pahāya pajahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvāti—

samijjhatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present 3rd singular of samijjhati (saṃ + idh + ya). The text glosses it with ijjhati, labhati, paṭilabhati, adhigacchati, vindati. The Niddesa quote is "tassa ce taṃ samijjhatīti".
samijjhatī.example_2: samijjhatīti ijjhati samijjhati labhati paṭilabhati adhigacchati vindatīti—

parihāyantī.meaning_2: falls away (from); declines; is lost; dwindles
parihāyantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the subject is kāmā, so the plural parihāyantī (with sandhi -īti) means 'those sensual pleasures fall away'; the gloss also shows the person falls away from them (kāmehi parihāyati). Present 3rd plural form.
parihāyantī.example_2: Te kāmā parihāyantīti – te vā kāmā parihāyanti, so vā kāmehi parihāyati.
parihāyantī.translation_2: “If those sensual pleasures fall away” means either those sensual objects fall away, or that person falls away from the sensual pleasures.

parivajjetī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present of the causative parivajjeti; in the text it occurs in the quoted phrase kāme parivajjetīti (before -iti).

taṇhāgaddūlaṃ.meaning_2: net of craving; snare of craving
taṇhāgaddūlaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, in a list of synonyms for craving. PEU gives both masculine and neuter; the Pāḷi form with -aṃ is ambiguous. gaddūla is usually 'creeper, creeper-net'; the PEU gloss 'bondage' is doubtful.
