taṇhāgaddūlaṃ.example_1: yo rāgo sārāgo anunayo anurodho nandī nandirāgo, cittassa sārāgo icchā mucchā ajjhosānaṃ gedho paligedho saṅgo paṅko, ejā māyā janikā sañjananī sibbinī jālinī saritā visattikā, suttaṃ visatā āyūhinī dutiyā paṇidhi bhavanetti, vanaṃ vanatho sandhavo sneho apekkhā paṭibandhu, āsā āsīsanā āsīsitattaṃ, rūpāsā saddāsā gandhāsā rasāsā phoṭṭhabbāsā, lābhāsā dhanāsā puttāsā jīvitāsā, jappā pajappā abhijappā jappanā jappitattaṃ loluppaṃ loluppāyanā loluppāyitattaṃ pucchañjikatā sādhukamyatā, adhammarāgo visamalobho nikanti nikāmanā patthanā pihanā sampatthanā, kāmataṇhā bhavataṇhā vibhavataṇhā, rūpataṇhā arūpataṇhā nirodhataṇhā, rūpataṇhā saddataṇhā gandhataṇhā rasataṇhā phoṭṭhabbataṇhā dhammataṇhā, ogho yogo gantho upādānaṃ āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ chadanaṃ bandhanaṃ, upakkileso anusayo pariyuṭṭhānaṃ latā vevicchaṃ, dukkhamūlaṃ dukkhanidānaṃ dukkhappabhavo mārapāso mārabaḷisaṃ māravisayo, taṇhānadī taṇhājālaṃ taṇhāgaddūlaṃ taṇhāsamuddo abhijjhā lobho akusalamūlaṃ.

khettan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text khettan is a sandhi form of khettaṃ (accusative singular) before ti, in a gloss listing types of fields.
khettan.example_1: khettanti sālikkhettaṃ vīhikkhettaṃ muggakkhettaṃ māsakkhettaṃ yavakkhettaṃ godhumakkhettaṃ tilakkhettaṃ.
khettan.example_2: Khettanti sālikhettaṃ vīhikhettaṃ muggakhettaṃ māsakhettaṃ yavakhettaṃ godhumakhettaṃ tilakhettaṃ.
khettan.translation_2: 'Field' means rice fields, barley fields, mung bean fields, bean fields, barley fields, wheat fields, sesame fields.

vatthun.meaning_2: thing; matter; case; object; subject; dwelling; place; basis
vatthun.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vatthun is a sandhi form of vatthuṃ (accusative singular) before ti; the quotation glosses it with gharavatthuṃ etc. PED analyses it as from √vas with suffix -tu (Rū.681).
vatthun.example_1: vatthunti gharavatthuṃ koṭṭhakavatthuṃ purevatthuṃ pacchāvatthuṃ ārāmavatthuṃ vihāravatthuṃ.
vatthun.example_2: vatthunti gharavatthuṃ koṭṭhavatthuṃ purevatthuṃ pacchāvatthuṃ ārāmavatthuṃ vihāravatthuṃ.

hiraññan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written hiraññan (niggahīta before ti) and glossed with kahāpaṇa; nominative/accusative singular.
hiraññan.example_2: Hiraññanti hiraññaṃ vuccati kahāpaṇoti – khettaṃ vatthuṃ hiraññaṃ vā.
hiraññan.translation_2: 'Wealth' is what is called gold or coins — thus, “to a field, property, or wealth.”

dāsaporisan.meaning_2: slaves and servants; male and female slaves
dāsaporisan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of dāsa and porisa (man; servant). Accusative singular in the text, in a list of possessions.

gavan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form gavan is a sandhi of gavo + ti (or an archaic accusative). It is glossed as 'gavā vuccanti'. The word belongs to the go declension.

anugijjhatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Third person singular present of anugijjhāti, glossed by gijjhati, paligijjhati and palibajjhati. In the text the form is quoted and explained in the Niddesa.
anugijjhatī.example_2: anugijjhatīti kilesakāmena vatthukāmesu gijjhati anugijjhati paligijjhati palibajjhatīti—

balīyantī.grammar: pr, 3rd pl of balīyati; or caus of balati
balīyantī.meaning_2: are overpowered; are subdued; are strong
balīyantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text as balīyantīti (balīyanti + iti), 3rd plural. The PEU gives two families: denominal from bala ('are powerful') and passive/causative ('are overpowered'); the gloss abalā naṃ suggests the passive sense 'the powerless overpower him'?

dukkhamanvetī.meaning_2: suffering follows that; pain follows it
dukkhamanvetī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of dukkhaṃ (accusative of dukkha) + anveti (anu + eti, follows). Quoted in the text as a definition; the word is analysed as dukkha + anveti.

bhinnamivodakan.meaning_2: like water in a broken boat; like a broken boat's water
bhinnamivodakan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of bhinnaṃ ivodakaṃ found in the Dhammapada verse (Dhp 118 in some editions). Sandhi of bhinnaṃ, iva and udakaṃ, with the final m assimilating to the following vowel.
bhinnamivodakan.example_2: Tato naṃ dukkhamanveti, nāvaṃ bhinnamivodakan ’’ ti.
bhinnamivodakan.translation_2: “From that, suffering follows him, like water entering a broken boat.”

guhāyan.meaning_2: cave; cavity; hiding place; (in this context) the body
guhāyan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular guhāyaṃ, written guhāyan before ti. The gloss explains it as guhāyaṃ satto visatto āsatto laggo laggito palibuddho (a being stuck, clinging, entangled in the cave/body).
guhāyan.example_1: satto guhāyanti guhāyaṃ satto visatto āsatto laggo laggito palibuddho.

jappan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has jappan, which looks like a present participle (jappanta) rather than a finite verb. It is glossed as yearning for sensual pleasures. Sandhi with the preceding va makes the form ambiguous.
jappan.example_2: Pacchā pure vāpi apekkhamānā, ime va kāme purime va jappan ’’ ti.
jappan.translation_2: “Looking to the future or the past, yearning for these same sensual pleasures or those of the past.”

paridevayantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present 3rd plural in the text: paridevayantī (with paridevayantīti in the quotation). Causal form of paridevati. In the gloss it is explained by lapanti, lālapanti, socanti, kilamanti, paridevanti, urattāḷiṃ kandanti, sammohaṃ āpajjanti.
paridevayantī.example_2: paridevayantīti lapanti lālapanti, socanti kilamanti paridevanti urattāḷiṃ kandanti sammohaṃ āpajjantīti—

sikkhethā.meaning_2: should train; should practise; should learn
sikkhethā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 2nd plural, used in the Niddesa to gloss a quotation: 'sikkhethāti ... sikkheyya ācareyya'. The ending -etha is an alternative to -eyyātha. The form could also be 3rd singular of the optative, but the context is 2nd plural addressing the audience.

jīvitan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text jīvitan is a sandhi form of jīvitaṃ before ti. The quotation glosses āyu and jīvitindriya.
jīvitan.example_1: jīvitanti āyu ṭhiti yapanā yāpanā iriyanā vattanā pālanā jīvitaṃ jīvitindriyaṃ.
jīvitan.example_2: ‘‘ manussānaṃ appakaṃ jīvitaṃ, parittakaṃ jīvitaṃ, thokaṃ jīvitaṃ, khaṇikaṃ jīvitaṃ, lahukaṃ jīvitaṃ, ittaraṃ jīvitaṃ, anaddhanīyaṃ jīvitaṃ, naciraṭṭhitikaṃ jīvitan ’’ ti.
jīvitan.translation_2: “The lifespan of humans is scant, is a little life, is a slight life, is a momentary life, is a light life, is a brief life, is a life that does not last, is a life that does not stand long.”

pariphandamānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text: pariphandamānan ti = pariphandamānaṃ iti. Used to describe beings in the world trembling with craving, views, etc. The sandhi -an before ti is resolved in the commentary.

passāmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present 3rd singular of passati, quoted in the text as passāmīti (passāmi + iti), with the quotation marker dropped in the lemma. The 1st person singular passāmi is formed from the same stem.
passāmī.example_1: passāmīti maṃsacakkhunāpi passāmi, dibbacakkhunāpi passāmi, paññācakkhunāpi passāmi, buddhacakkhunāpi passāmi, samantacakkhunāpi passāmi dakkhāmi olokemi nijjhāyāmi upaparikkhāmi.
passāmī.example_2: passāmīti maṃsacakkhunā vā passāmi, dibbena cakkhunā vā passāmi.

taṇhagatan.meaning_2: gone to craving; overcome by craving; fallen into craving
taṇhagatan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is accusative singular neuter modifying cittaṃ, part of a gloss on taṇhāgata (with single ṇhā). The commentarial explanation links gata with anugata, anusaṭa and pātita.
taṇhagatan.example_1: taṇhagatanti taṇhāgataṃ taṇhānugataṃ taṇhāyānusaṭaṃ taṇhāyāsannaṃ taṇhāya pātitaṃ abhibhūtaṃ pariyādinnacittaṃ.

lapantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present 3rd plural lapantī in the text, with the plural subject narā; the gloss explains it as wailing in the face of death.

chandan.meaning_2: desire; wish; attachment; seeking (of a sense object)
chandan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (chandan = chandaṃ, sandhi of chandaṃ). In the Niddesa, glossed as chandaṃ vineyya paṭivineyya etc.
chandan.example_2: ubhosu antesu vineyya chandanti ubhosu antesu chandaṃ vineyya paṭivineyya pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyyāti—

sallan.meaning_2: dart; arrow; barb; (figuratively) sting, thorn (of defilements)
sallan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa text sallan is the accusative singular (with sandhi -n for -ṃ) of salla, glossed by satta sallāni, the seven darts of rāga, dosa, moha, māna, diṭṭhi, soka and kathaṃkathā. Written sallaṃ in normal orthography.

parañcā.meaning_2: and the next; and the other world
parañcā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of paraṃ (this-worldly/next-worldly, accusative) + ca. Alternate resolution: para + añcā, but the gloss paralokaṃ nāsīsati parattabhāvaṃ supports paraṃ + ca. Occurs in the phrase lokamimaṃ parañcā.
parañcā.example_1: nāsīsatī lokamimaṃ parañcāti imaṃ lokaṃ nāsīsati sakattabhāvaṃ, paralokaṃ nāsīsati parattabhāvaṃ;
parañcā.example_2: Abbūḷhasallo caramappamatto, nāsīsatī lokamimaṃ parañcā ’’ ti.
parañcā.translation_2: ‘Having the dart extracted, he dwells diligent, and he does not long for this world or the next.’

upetī.meaning_2: approaches; draws near; becomes involved (with); attaches (to)
upetī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular of upeti; in the verse muni no upetīti, negated by no and joined to -ti (vādañca jātaṃ muni no upetīti). The underlying form is upeti.

sīlavatānī.meaning_2: virtue and observance; ethics and (religious) practices; moral conduct and vows
sīlavatānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text sīlavatānīti is sīlavatāni + iti, nominative plural, glossed by atthi sīlañceva vatañca. Some editions read sīlabbata here (the well-known sīlabbata-pāramāsa, 'attachment to rites and rituals'); the manuscript variants sīlavattha and sīlabbata are worth noting.
sīlavatānī.example_1: sīlavatānīti atthi sīlañceva vatañca, atthi vataṃ na sīlaṃ.
sīlavatānī.example_2: Sīlavatānīti atthi sīlañceva vatañca [vattañca (syā.), evamuparipi], atthi vataṃ na sīlaṃ.
sīlavatānī.translation_2: “Ethics and observances” (sīlavatāni) means that there is both virtue and observance; there is also observance that is not virtue.

paresan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive plural of para. Sandhi -ṃ before ti becomes -n. Glossed in the text with paresaṃ, used distributively with khattiyānaṃ etc.
paresan.example_1: paresanti paresaṃ khattiyānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vessānaṃ suddānaṃ gahaṭṭhānaṃ pabbajitānaṃ devānaṃ manussānaṃ.
paresan.example_2: paresanti upajjhāyā vā ācariyā vā samānupajjhāyakā vā samānācariyakā vā mittā vā sandiṭṭhā vā sambhattā vā sahāyā vā codenti—

tamāhū.meaning_2: that they call; that is called
tamāhū.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of taṃ + āhu, perfect 3rd plural of brūti, 'they say'; the form is used in a definitional clause.

ānisaṃsan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads ānisaṃsan, which is probably a sandhi or textual variant for ānisaṃsaṃ (accusative singular).

kuppapaṭiccasantin.meaning_2: relying on a shaky peace; dependent on a peace that is liable to waver
kuppapaṭiccasantin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of kuppa (shaky, liable to shake), paṭicca (dependent on), santin (peace). The readings kuppapaṭiccasantin and kuppaṭiccasantin occur; commentarial gloss, syntactic form uncertain.
kuppapaṭiccasantin.example_2: Yadattani passati ānisaṃsaṃ, taṃ nissito kuppapaṭiccasantin ’’ ti.
kuppapaṭiccasantin.translation_2: He sees an advantage in himself, and dependent on that, he holds to a peace that is shaky and dependent.”

samuggahītan.meaning_2: grasped; seized; taken hold of; comprehended; clung to
samuggahītan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter accusative singular form used in the text (samuggahītan = samuggahītaṃ). Quoted and explained in the Niddesa as grasping (odhiggāho etc.).
samuggahītan.example_2: samuggahītanti nivesanesu odhiggāho bilaggāho varaggāho koṭṭhāsaggāho uccayaggāho samuccayaggāho.

vādan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vādan is the accusative singular (sometimes written vādaṃ); it is the object of upeti. The PEU entry derives it from vada + ṇa. Printed as vādan at the end of a verse line, so possibly a sandhi form.

arogan.meaning_2: free from disease; healthy; sound; untainted; free from corruption
arogan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In these Niddesa contexts it refers to Nibbāna, glossed as ārogyappattaṃ. Accusative singular in the text.
arogan.example_2: paramaṃ aroganti paramaṃ ārogyappattaṃ tāṇappattaṃ leṇappattaṃ saraṇappattaṃ abhayappattaṃ accutappattaṃ amatappattaṃ nibbānappattanti—

suddhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text suddhan is a sandhi form of suddhaṃ (accusative singular), formed before the quotative ti: suddhan ti. The form suddhan recurs several times in the sentence.
suddhan.example_1: passāmi suddhanti passāmi suddhaṃ, dakkhāmi suddhaṃ, olokemi suddhaṃ, nijjhāyāmi suddhaṃ, upaparikkhāmi suddhaṃ.

ñāṇan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text ñāṇan is ñāṇaṃ with sandhi -ṃ before ti: 'pacceti ñāṇaṃ' + iti. Object of pacceti; the commentary glosses it as cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, i.e. what is taken to be knowledge.
ñāṇan.example_2: yo suddhaṃ passati, so suddhānupassī, pacceti ñāṇanti cakkhuviññāṇaṃ rūpadassanena ñāṇanti pacceti, maggoti pacceti, pathoti pacceti, niyyānanti paccetīti—

vadānan.meaning_2: speaking; talking; preaching; one who speaks
vadānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular of vadāna, a present participle from vadati; glossed by the commentary as vadantaṃ kathentaṃ bhaṇantaṃ. Sometimes analysed with māna changed to āna.
vadānan.example_2: tathā vadānanti tathā vadantaṃ kathentaṃ bhaṇantaṃ dīpayantaṃ voharantaṃ.

suddhimāhā.meaning_2: he did not bring purity from anything else; he did not call purity from anything other than
suddhimāhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of suddhiṃ (accusative of suddhi, purity) and āhā, the aorist (used as an imperfect) of āharati, bring. The final -aṃ of suddhiṃ is elided before the initial ā-.

saṅgan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (saṅgaṃ, with sandhi -n before t-). The Niddesa glosses it with rāgasaṅga, dosasaṅga, etc., i.e. attachment of various kinds.
saṅgan.example_2: te na taranti saṅganti rāgasaṅgaṃ dosasaṅgaṃ mohasaṅgaṃ mānasaṅgaṃ diṭṭhisaṅgaṃ kilesasaṅgaṃ duccaritasaṅgaṃ na taranti na uttaranti na pataranti na samatikkamanti na vītivattantīti—

nirassajantī.meaning_2: abandons; gives up; lets go of; releases
nirassajantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text nirassajantī is present participle feminine nominative plural (nirassajantī), from the same verb; sentence glosses it with muñcitvā (having released) and gaṇhanti (they take).
nirassajantī.example_1: te uggahāyanti nirassajantīti satthāraṃ gaṇhanti, taṃ muñcitvā aññaṃ satthāraṃ gaṇhanti;

vatānī.meaning_2: vow; religious observance; practice; rule of conduct
vatānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vatānī is the plural (nominative/accusative) of vata, glossed by the commentary with compounds such as hatthivataṃ, assavataṃ, etc. Printed with -ī for the plural ending -āni.
vatānī.example_1: vatānīti hatthivataṃ vā assavataṃ vā govataṃ vā kukkūravataṃ vā kākavataṃ vā vāsudevavataṃ vā baladevavataṃ vā puṇṇabhaddavataṃ vā maṇibhaddavataṃ vā aggivataṃ vā nāgavataṃ vā supaṇṇavataṃ vā yakkhavataṃ vā asuravataṃ vā …pe…
vatānī.example_2: Vatānīti hatthivataṃ vā assavataṃ vā govataṃ vā kukkūravataṃ vā kākavataṃ vā vāsudevavataṃ vā baladevavataṃ vā puṇṇabhaddavataṃ vā maṇibhaddavataṃ vā aggivataṃ vā nāgavataṃ vā supaṇṇavataṃ vā yakkhavataṃ vā asuravataṃ vā … pe … disāvataṃ vā ādāya samādāya ādiyitvā samādiyitvā gaṇhitvā parāmasitvā abhinivisitvā.
vatānī.translation_2: ‘Vows’ means: elephant-vows, horse-vows, ox-vows, dog-vows, crow-vows, Vāsudeva-vows, Baladeva-vows, Puṇṇabhadda-vows, Maṇibhadda-vows, Agni-vows, Naga-vows, Supaṇṇa-vows, Yakkha-vows, Asura-vows... or directional-vows, having taken up, undertaken, accepted, initiated, mastered, displayed, and stood upon.

vedehī.meaning_2: possessor of knowledge; one who has the Vedas (i.e. knowledge); (in commentarial gloss) one endowed with knowledge of the four paths
vedehī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Commentarial wordplay: vedehī is explained as vedā (knowledge) + ī (possessor). In the text the word is glossed by vedā vuccanti ... ñāṇaṃ, i.e. the four paths. Nominative singular.
vedehī.example_1: vedehīti vedā vuccanti catūsu maggesu ñāṇaṃ paññā paññindriyaṃ paññābalaṃ dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo vīmaṃsā vipassanā sammādiṭṭhi.

carantan.meaning_2: walking; moving about; wandering; behaving; living
carantan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular of the present participle of carati, used in the Niddesa to gloss carantaṃ; the -n is the sandhi form before a vowel-initial word.
carantan.example_2: carantanti carantaṃ vicarantaṃ viharantaṃ iriyantaṃ vattentaṃ pālentaṃ yapentaṃ yāpentanti—

vivaṭan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vivaṭan is a sandhi form of vivaṭaṃ (accusative singular) before ti. Here it explains the opening or removal of the coverings of taṇhā, diṭṭhi, kilesa, duccarita and avijjā.

purekkharontī.meaning_2: puts in front; prefers; esteems; pays respect (to)
purekkharontī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd plural present in the text, negated by na; the gloss translates it as "they do not prefer". Written as purekkharontī before ti.

paramuggahītan.meaning_2: taken as supreme; held as highest; regarded as ultimate
paramuggahītan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of parama + uggahīta. Nominative singular ending -ṃ in the text (paramuggahītan before ti).

sabbamāhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is part of the compound string sabbamāhā (sabbaṃ + āhā); the quotation is corrupt: sabbaṃ is accusative singular, not part of a compound. āhā is taken as an aorist of āharati.
sabbamāhā.example_1: hīnāti aññe tato sabbamāhāti attano satthāraṃ dhammakkhānaṃ gaṇaṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭipadaṃ maggaṃ ṭhapetvā sabbe parappavāde khipati ukkhipati parikkhipati.

vivādānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vivādānīti = vivādāni + iti, nominative plural neuter form of vivāda used adjectivally with diṭṭhikalahāni etc.; the sandhi -āni + iti > -ānīti. The headword is the masculine noun vivāda.
vivādānī.example_1: vivādānīti diṭṭhikalahāni diṭṭhibhaṇḍanāni diṭṭhiviggahāni diṭṭhivivādāni diṭṭhimedhagāni ca.

tadevā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text tadevāti = tadeva + iti; glossed as taṃ diṭṭhigataṃ, so tadeva = 'that very (wrong view)'. The -ā belongs to the -ti of iti, not to the sandhi itself.

sabbamaññan.meaning_2: all (is) another's; all else belonging to others
sabbamaññan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sabbaṃ + aññaṃ (or sabba + aññan). Occurs in a commentarial quotation on the papañca views: 'sees all else as inferior' (nihīnato passati); the editor's sandhi form, sandhi dissolution uncertain.
sabbamaññan.example_2: Tadeva so tattha samuggahāya, nihīnato passati sabbamaññan ’’ ti.
sabbamaññan.translation_2: That very person, having firmly adopted the view regarding that [object], sees all else as inferior.”

hīnamaññan.meaning_2: considering as inferior; who regards as low; deemed inferior by another
hīnamaññan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of hīna and mañña, from maññati. In the text it appears as hīnamaññan. This is sometimes read as the masculine accusative singular of the adjective hīnamañña, and sometimes as the nominative singular of a masculine agent noun (hīnamañño), in the idiom 'yaṃ nissito passati hīnamaññaṃ/ hīnamaññan'. The commentary glosses the form with hīnato.
hīnamaññan.example_2: passati hīnamaññanti aññaṃ satthāraṃ dhammakkhānaṃ gaṇaṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭipadaṃ maggaṃ hīnato nihīnato omakato lāmakato chatukkato parittato dissati passati dakkhati oloketi nijjhāyati upanijjhāyati upaparikkhatīti—

diṭṭhimanādiyānan.meaning_2: not holding (to) views; not grasping views
diṭṭhimanādiyānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of diṭṭhiṃ + anādiyāna (negative present participle of ādāti, 'not taking up, not grasping'). The form in the text is accusative singular, qualifying brāhmaṇaṃ; quoted with ti in the Niddesa.

paccetī.meaning_2: goes back (to); returns (to); falls back (on); comes back
paccetī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Third person singular present of paṭi + √i; the text glosses it with na puneti na paccāgacchati, 'does not return to'. Written paccetī before ti.
paccetī.example_1: na paccetīti sotāpattimaggena ye kilesā pahīnā, te kilese na puneti na pacceti na paccāgacchati.

idan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi form of idaṃ before a vowel (idanti = idaṃ + iti; idan ti = idaṃ + ti). The -ṃ becomes -n in the text; entry is under the base pronoun idaṃ.
idan.example_2: Yassa ‘‘ mayhaṃ vā idaṃ paresaṃ vā idan ’’ ti kiñci rūpagataṃ vedanāgataṃ saññāgataṃ saṅkhāragataṃ viññāṇagataṃ gahitaṃ parāmaṭṭhaṃ abhiniviṭṭhaṃ ajjhositaṃ adhimuttaṃ atthi, tassa jāni atthi.
idan.translation_2: Whoever has any grasping, holding, insistence, accepted view, or devotion—thinking ‘this is mine’ or ‘this is another's’—in regards to form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, or consciousness, for him there is a penalty.

santamevidan.meaning_2: but this is absent; but this does not exist
santamevidan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of santaṃ (present participle of atthi, 'being, existing'), eva ('only, just') and idaṃ ('this'). Found in a Niddesa gloss explaining vinābhāva ('absence, separation'). The final -aṃ of santaṃ is assimilated before eva, and idaṃ is reduced to idan before the quotative ti. Alternative resolution: santaṃ eva idaṃ.

pahīyatī.meaning_2: is abandoned; is given up; is left behind; is lost; disappears
pahīyatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive of pajahati (√hā 1 with pa-). 3rd singular passive in the text; glossed by jahīyati, vijahīyati, antaradhāyati, vippalujjati.

maraṇan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text maraṇan is a sandhi form of maraṇaṃ before ti (maraṇaṃ + iti). It heads a definition of death in the Niddesa. The PEU entry suggests analysis as mara + yu, but the standard derivation is from √mar.
maraṇan.example_1: maraṇanti yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhā tamhā sattanikāyā cuti cavanatā bhedo antaradhānaṃ maccumaraṇaṃ kālaṅkiriyā khandhānaṃ bhedo kaḷevarassa nikkhepo jīvitindriyassupacchedo.
maraṇan.example_2: Maraṇanti yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhā tamhā sattanikāyā cuti cavanatā bhedo antaradhānaṃ maccumaraṇaṃ kālaṃkiriyā khandhānaṃ bhedo kaḷevarassa nikkhepo jīvitindriyassupacchedo.
maraṇan.translation_2: “Death” is the passing away, falling away, breaking up, disappearance, death by the Ender, ending of time, breaking up of the aggregates, throwing off of the corpse, and cutting off of the life faculty of these various beings from their respective groups of beings.

yan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text yanti is yaṃ + iti. Here yaṃ introduces a list or explanation, 'namely'. Sometimes treated as a nipāta.

saṅgatan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text saṅgatan is accusative singular of the past participle, in the phrase supinena yathāpi saṅgataṃ, comparing something to meeting in a dream. Some editions read saṅgataṃ.

janan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular of jana with the -aṃ ending assimilated to the following consonant (janan ti = janaṃ iti); the same sandhi form occurs three times in these sentences. In sentence 2 the gloss is mamāyitaṃ janaṃ, 'cherished person'; in sentence 3 the word stands for various kinds of people.
janan.example_2: piyāyitaṃ jananti mamāyitaṃ janaṃ mātaraṃ vā pitaraṃ vā bhātaraṃ vā bhaginiṃ vā puttaṃ vā dhītaraṃ vā mittaṃ vā amaccaṃ vā ñātiṃ vā sālohitaṃ vāti—

pavuccatī.meaning_2: is spoken; is called; is stated; is said; is expressed
pavuccatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive of pavadati. The -ī- in the text is the sandhi of pavuccati + iti. In the gloss it is explained by vuccati, kathīyati, bhaṇīyati, dīpīyati, voharīyati.
pavuccatī.example_2: pavuccatīti vuccati pavuccati kathīyati bhaṇīyati dīpīyati voharīyatīti—

yesan.meaning_2: of those whose; of whatever; of which
yesan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of the dative/genitive plural pronoun yesaṃ with the quotative -ti; in the text it answers yesaṃ, meaning 'of those whose ...'.
yesan.example_1: yesanti yesaṃ khattiyānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vessānaṃ suddānaṃ gahaṭṭhānaṃ pabbajitānaṃ devānaṃ manussānaṃ.

akkheyyan.meaning_2: expressible; nameable; that can be called; reckoned as
akkheyyan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text akkheyyaṃ, nominative singular neuter. Often used in the phrase nāmaṃ yeva avasissati akkheyyaṃ, meaning only the name remains to be expressed.

macchariyan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text macchariyan is a sandhi form of macchariyaṃ before ti. The Niddesa explains it as the five kinds of stinginess.
macchariyan.example_2: Macchariyanti pañca macchariyāni – āvāsamacchariyaṃ, kulamacchariyaṃ, lābhamacchariyaṃ, vaṇṇamacchariyaṃ, dhammamacchariyaṃ.
macchariyan.translation_2: “Stinginess” means the five forms of stinginess: stinginess as to one’s monastery, family, gains, status, and Dhamma.

vivittamāsanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Part of the quoted phrase bhajamānassa vivittamāsanaṃ; accusative singular (vivittamāsanaṃ) in the text, dissolved as vivitta + āsana. Vivitta is a past participle of √vic (separate).
vivittamāsanan.example_2: Bhajamānassa vivittamāsananti āsanaṃ vuccati yattha nisīdanti – mañco pīṭhaṃ bhisi taṭṭikā cammakhaṇḍo tiṇasanthāro paṇṇasanthāro palālasanthāro.
vivittamāsanan.translation_2: “Associating with a solitary seat”: “A seat” is so called because one sits down upon it—a bed, a chair, a mattress, matting, a piece of hide, a grass spread, a leaf spread, or a straw spread.

appiyan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text appiyan is a sandhi form of appiyaṃ (before the following vowel), accusative singular neuter agreeing with piyaṃ; the phrase na piyaṃ kubbati nopi appiyan means 'does not do what is liked nor what is disliked'.

tasmin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text tasmin ti = tasmiṃ iti, with ti marking the quoted word. Locative singular of ta(d).

vighātan.meaning_2: distress; affliction; oppression; destruction; harm; suffering (of body and mind)
vighātan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vighātan ti is vighātaṃ + iti, with the niggahīta assimilated to the following t. The Niddesa glosses it with upaghāta, pīḷana, ghaṭṭana, upaddava, upasagga. Instrumental singular vighātena is attested elsewhere.
vighātan.example_1: vighātanti vighātaṃ upaghātaṃ pīḷanaṃ ghaṭṭanaṃ upaddavaṃ upasaggaṃ brūhi ācikkha desehi paññapehi paṭṭhapehi vivara vibhaja uttānīkarohi pakāsehi.
vighātan.example_2: Vighātanti vighātaṃ upaghātaṃ pīḷanaṃ ghaṭṭanaṃ upaddavaṃ upasaggaṃ brūhi ācikkha desehi paññapehi paṭṭhapehi vivara vibhaja uttānīkarohi [uttāniṃ karohi (ka.)] pakāsehi.
vighātan.translation_2: “Distress” means oppression, destruction, friction, danger, or calamity; “speak” means tell, show, make known, establish, open up, divide, make plain, or reveal.

sāsanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in both sentences. The readings sāsanan and sāsanaṃ are the same form; the -n is sandhi or a variant ending.

anāriyan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text etaṃ tasmiṃ anāriyan ti, anāriyaṃ is nominative singular neuter agreeing with etaṃ; the -n is sandhi before ti.
anāriyan.example_2: Micchā ca paṭipajjati, etaṃ tasmiṃ anāriyan ’’ ti.
anāriyan.translation_2: And he proceeds wrongly; this is ignoble in him.”

yānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yānaṃ + iti (with the -ṃ assimilated to -n), used in the gloss to quote the word being explained. The entry could instead be given under the main word yāna.
yānan.example_1: yānanti hatthiyānaṃ assayānaṃ goyānaṃ ajayānaṃ meṇḍayānaṃ oṭṭhayānaṃ kharayānaṃ bhantaṃ adantaṃ akāritaṃ avinītaṃ uppathaṃ gaṇhāti, visamaṃ khāṇumpi pāsāṇampi abhiruhati, yānampi ārohanakampi bhañjati, papātepi papatati.

puthujjanan.meaning_2: ordinary person; common worldling; run-of-the-mill person
puthujjanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the final -a is changed to -n before the quotation ti (puthujjanti). Accusative singular, governed by āhu.
puthujjanan.example_2: Yānaṃ bhantaṃva taṃ loke, hīnamāhu puthujjanan ’’ ti.
puthujjanan.translation_2: Like a wild vehicle in the world, they call a run-of-the-mill person lesser.”

satthānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form satthānī is the nominative plural, glossed tīṇi satthāni. Here applied figuratively to kāyasattha, vacīsattha and manosattha. Sometimes derived from √sas 2 (slaughter) with the -tha suffix; compare Sanskrit śastra.
satthānī.translation_2: “Swords” means three swords: the sword of the body, the sword of speech, and the sword of the mind.

parikissatī.meaning_2: is exhausted; is worn out; is overcome; is spent
parikissatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Third person singular present of pari + √kis (be thin, be weak). In the text it is used idiomatically of one overcome by sexual indulgence, 'he is worn out / overcome just like a fool'. Contracted from parikissati.
parikissatī.example_2: Sa cāpi methune yutto, mandova parikissatī ’’ ti.
parikissatī.translation_2: If he engages in sexual intercourse, he is overcome just like a fool.”

methunan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular object of na nisevetha in the quoted verse. DPD's related entry methunaka is a derivative; here methuna means sexual intercourse.
methunan.example_2: Ekaccariyaṃ daḷhaṃ kayirā, na nisevetha methunan ’’ ti.
methunan.translation_2: He should keep the solitary life firm, and should not engage in sexual intercourse.”

ariyānamuttaman.meaning_2: highest of the noble ones; supreme among the noble ones
ariyānamuttaman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ariyānaṃ + uttama (genitive plural + adjective). In the text the quotation marker -ti is attached (ariyānamuttanti); here the accusative neuter singular form. An epithet of the Buddha or of Nibbāna.

maññethā.meaning_2: should think; should consider; should regard (as)
maññethā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 2nd plural in the text (maññethā), used in the sense 'one should not consider oneself superior because of that'.

vādayantī.meaning_2: asserts; declares; claims; (or) causes to sound; plays (a musical instrument)
vādayantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vādayantī is sandhi for vādayanti + iti (3rd plural present). The commentarial gloss takes it from √vad in the sense 'to assert, declare' (idheva suddhiṃ, idameva saccaṃ), but the form is formally the causative of vadati 'to make sound, play (an instrument)'. Both analyses are possible.

vigayhā.meaning_2: having entered; having plunged into; having penetrated
vigayhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -ya of vigāhati (vi + √gāh). In the text the absolutive is written vigayhā before ti (vigayhāti), and the gloss explains it with vigayha, ogayha, ajjhogāhetvā, pavisitvā. The form with -yā is a sandhi variant before the quotative ti.
vigayhā.example_2: parisaṃ vigayhāti khattiyaparisaṃ brāhmaṇaparisaṃ gahapatiparisaṃ samaṇaparisaṃ vigayha ogayha ajjhogāhetvā pavisitvāti—

aññamaññan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form aññamaññan is likely a sandhi variant for aññamaññaṃ (nominative/accusative singular neuter), used adverbially in the phrase mithu aññamaññaṃ ('mutually, one another').

mithū.meaning_2: mutually; with each other; in pairs; in opposition
mithū.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text glossed with dve janā and explained as two people quarrelling, arguing, disputing; a synonym of mitho. Sometimes written mithu.
mithū.example_1: mithūti dve janā dve kalahakārakā dve bhaṇḍanakārakā dve bhassakārakā dve vivādakārakā dve adhikaraṇakārakā dve vādino dve sallāpakā;
mithū.example_2: mithūti dve janā, dve kalahakārakā, dve bhaṇḍanakārakā, dve bhassakārakā, dve vivādakārakā, dve adhikaraṇakārakā, dve vādino, dve sallapakā;

kathojjan.meaning_2: argument; quarrel; dispute; contentious speech; useless words
kathojjan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text kathojjan is an accusative ending (nirutti/poetic), with -ojja in the old -ya ending. The Niddesa explains it as anojavantī kathā, i.e. a quarrelsome or pointless way of speaking; glossed kalaha, bhaṇḍana, viggaha, vivāda, medhaga. The PeU entry lists it as neuter (na).
kathojjan.example_2: atha vā kathojjanti anojavantī sā kathā kathojjaṃ vadanti, kalahaṃ vadanti, bhaṇḍanaṃ vadanti, viggahaṃ vadanti, vivādaṃ vadanti, medhagaṃ vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharantīti—

pasaṃsamicchan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of pasaṃsaṃ + icchanta, glossed by icchanto, sādiyanto, patthayanto etc. Nominative singular here.
pasaṃsamicchan.example_1: pasaṃsamicchanti pasaṃsaṃ thomanaṃ kittiṃ vaṇṇahāriyaṃ icchanto sādiyanto patthayanto pihayanto abhijappanto.

anutthunātī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present 3rd singular. In the text it introduces the quoted phrase 'upaccagā maṃ ti', i.e. he repeats 'he has passed beyond me'.
anutthunātī.example_2: Paridevati socati hīnavādo, upaccagā manti anutthunātī ’’ ti.
anutthunātī.translation_2: He sorrows and grieves, his doctrine degraded, bemoaning, ‘He has passed beyond me’.”

ṃ.meaning_2: the letter ṃ; niggahīta (the nasal sound represented by the sign ṃ)
ṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] This is not a word but the niggahīta sign ṃ, shown in the source as a separate token (its preceding vowel is written apart, e.g. kathojjaṃ and paṇṇaṃ). In the sentences it is the final nasal of the accusative singular.
ṃ.example_1: kathojjaṃ vuccati kalaho bhaṇḍanaṃ viggaho vivādo medhagaṃ.

tenā.meaning_2: thereby; by that; on account of that; for that reason
tenā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the final -ā is the prolongation before the quotative ti (tenā ti). Instrumental singular of the demonstrative ta, used adverbially as a causal particle.
tenā.example_2: so hassatī unnamatī ca tenāti so tena jayatthena unnato hoti unnamo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassāti—

vivādayethā.grammar: only in comp with na; opt of vivādayati
vivādayethā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Negated optative in the text: na vivādayethāti, glossed na kalahaṃ kareyya. The form shows the causative sign -aya-; the PEU splits it as Vi+vada+ṇaya+etha.
vivādayethā.example_2: na vivādayethāti na kalahaṃ kareyya na bhaṇḍanaṃ kareyya na viggahaṃ kareyya na vivādaṃ kareyya, na medhagaṃ kareyya, kalahabhaṇḍanaviggahavivādamedhagaṃ pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyya, kalahabhaṇḍanaviggahavivādamedhagā ārato assa virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippayutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā vihareyyāti—

paṭisūramicchan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The quoted Pāḷi abhigajjameti is glossed with paṭisūramicchan ('desiring to rival the brave') in the Niddesa commentarial prose. The lemma is taken as the causative present 3rd singular; if the form is instead the ending -m-etaṃ at a sandhi boundary, the entry would be abhigajjam etaṃ.

yudhāyā.meaning_2: for battle; for war; for fighting
yudhāyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Dative of yuddha, glossed in the text by yuddhatthāya kalahatthāya etc.; the printed form is yuddhāya, written yudhāyā before ti.
yudhāyā.example_2: yadidaṃ yudhāyāti yadidaṃ yuddhatthāya kalahatthāya bhaṇḍanatthāya viggahatthāya vivādatthāya medhagatthāyāti—

vivādayantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of vivadati. In the text vivādayantī is the unelided form of vivādayanti (present 3rd plural) before ti.
vivādayantī.example_1: ye diṭṭhimuggayha vivādayantīti ye dvāsaṭṭhidiṭṭhigatānaṃ aññataraññataraṃ diṭṭhigataṃ gahetvā gaṇhitvā uggaṇhitvā parāmasitvā abhinivisitvā vivādayanti kalahaṃ karonti, bhaṇḍanaṃ karonti, viggahaṃ karonti, vivādaṃ karonti, medhagaṃ karonti—

methunasmin.meaning_2: sexual intercourse; copulation; in sexual union
methunasmin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text. Cited as part of a quotation.
methunasmin.example_1: disvāna taṇhaṃ aratiṃ ragañca, nāhosi chando api methunasminti.

adassan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular aorist of dassati (see), negated a-dassaṃ 'I did not see'? In the text adassan is glossed by adassaṃ adakkhiṃ apassiṃ; the sandhi form adassaṃ before ti. The PEU entry adassana is a different word (na + dassana).

pacinan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle of pacinati, here in the commentarial explanation of 'pacinaṃ' with the sense of investigating or contemplating. In the text it appears as pacinan (sandhi form of pacinantaṃ).
pacinan.example_1: pacinanti pacinanto vicinanto pavicinanto tulayanto tīrayanto vibhāvayanto vibhūtaṃ karonto,
pacinan.example_2: Pacinanti pacinanto vicinanto pavicinanto tulayanto tīrayanto vibhāvayanto vibhūtaṃ karonto,‘‘ sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā ’’ ti pacinanto vicinanto pavicinanto tulayanto tīrayanto vibhāvayanto vibhūtaṃ karonto,‘‘ sabbe saṅkhārā dukkhā ’’ ti …‘‘ sabbe dhammā anattā ’’ ti pacinanto vicinanto pavicinanto …‘‘ yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamman ’’ ti pacinanto vicinanto pavicinanto tulayanto tīrayanto vibhāvayanto vibhūtaṃ karonto.
pacinan.translation_2: “Investigated” means, while investigating, seeking, searching, weighing, judging, clarifying, and making evident: while investigating, seeking, searching, weighing, judging, clarifying, and making evident [the truth that] “All conditioned things are impermanent,” [or] “All conditioned things are suffering,” or [the truth that] “All phenomena are nonself,” or [while] investigating, seeking, searching, weighing, judging, clarifying, and making evident [that] “Whatever is subject to origination, all that is subject to cessation.”

pakappitānī.meaning_2: arranged; designed; intended; planned; contrived; considered
pakappitānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter nominative plural in the text (pakappitāni), agreeing with yāni. Glossed in the Niddesa with kappitā, abhisaṅkhatā, saṇṭhapitā.

yametamatthan.meaning_2: which is this matter; namely this point; this very matter
yametamatthan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yaṃ + etad + atthaṃ; the text writes yametamatthan before -ti. In the Niddesa it introduces a gloss on the meaning of the preceding words.
yametamatthan.example_1: te ve munī brūsi anuggahāya, ajjhattasantīti yametamatthanti.

dhīrehī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumentative plural in the text (dhīrehi), glossed by paṇḍitehi etc. Sometimes analysed as √dhī + ra.
dhīrehī.example_1: dhīrehīti dhīrehi paṇḍitehi paññavantehi buddhimantehi ñāṇīhi vibhāvīhi medhāvīhi.
dhīrehī.example_2: Dhīrehīti dhīrehi paṇḍitehi paññavantehi [paññāvantehi (sī. syā.)] buddhimantehi ñāṇīhi vibhāvīhi medhāvīhi.
dhīrehī.translation_2: ‘By the sages’ (dhīrehi) means by the astute, the wise, the prudent, the intelligent, the knowledgeable, the brilliant, the sagacious.

paveditan.meaning_2: declared; made known; proclaimed; taught; revealed
paveditan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text paveditan is sandhi for paveditaṃ, the accusative singular, glossed by veditaṃ ācikkhitaṃ desitaṃ. The PEU splits it as pa + vida + ṇe + ta; the causative base is pavede/vede from √vid.
paveditan.example_1: paveditanti veditaṃ paveditaṃ ācikkhitaṃ desitaṃ paññāpitaṃ paṭṭhapitaṃ vivaṭaṃ vibhattaṃ uttānīkataṃ pakāsitanti—
paveditan.example_2: Paveditanti veditaṃ paveditaṃ ācikkhitaṃ desitaṃ paññāpitaṃ paṭṭhapitaṃ vivaṭaṃ vibhattaṃ uttānīkataṃ pakāsitanti – kathaṃ nu dhīrehi paveditaṃ taṃ.
paveditan.translation_2: ‘Declared’ (paveditaṃ) means known, explicitly known, told, taught, designated, established, uncovered, well-divided, made clear, and revealed—thus: ‘How then was that declared by the sages?’

anissāyā.meaning_2: not relying (on); not clinging (to); not depending (on)
anissāyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text anissāyā is the form before ti (anissāya + iti), with a long ā at the sandhi. The gloss explains that there are two reliances, craving (taṇhānissaya) and view (diṭṭhinissaya).
anissāyā.example_2: Anissāyāti dve nissayā – taṇhānissayo ca diṭṭhinissayo ca … pe … ayaṃ taṇhānissayo … pe … ayaṃ diṭṭhinissayo.
anissāyā.translation_2: ‘Without relying’ (anissāya) means there are two reliances—the reliance of craving and the reliance of view… this is the reliance of craving… this is the reliance of view.

saññan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Poetic accusative singular (saññaṃ → saññan) in the Niddesa verse, meaning perception or consciousness; the ending -an is m.c.

dahāsī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text, dahāsīti = dahāsi + iti in a quotation. Form is 2nd person singular present indicative of dahati, meaning 'you see/regard/consider' (cf. PED dahati 3). Translation 'you see it as deluded' is idiomatic.
dahāsī.example_2: Ito ca nāddakkhi aṇumpi saññaṃ, tasmā tuvaṃ momuhato dahāsī ’’ ti.
dahāsī.translation_2: You do not see even a tiny bit of perception from this, therefore you see it as [highly] deluded.”

kenā.meaning_2: with whom?; by what? (with -ci: anyone; something)
kenā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi in the text (kenā = kena + ā). Part of the phrase kenāti (kena + āti, 'by what?' as quoted question); kena is the instrumental of kiṃ, and the related entry kenaci (= kena + ci) shows the same base with the indefinite particle.

paṭisaṃyujeyyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular of a causative-denominative verb, with the ending -eyya like kareyya. Text form paṭisaṃyujeyyā at the end of the line, with -iti sandhi.
paṭisaṃyujeyyā.example_2: Yasmiṃ samaṃ visamaṃ vāpi natthi, sa kena vādaṃ paṭisaṃyujeyyā ’’ ti.
paṭisaṃyujeyyā.translation_2: In one for whom there is no ‘equal’ or ‘unequal,’ with whom would he engage in disputes?”

paṭisaṃyojeyya.meaning_2: could connect; could engage; could join (with)
paṭisaṃyojeyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular in the text, in a series with paṭibaleyya, kareyya. Denotes ability or possibility: 'could he engage in debate with whom?'.
paṭisaṃyojeyya.example_1: so kena mānena, kāya diṭṭhiyā, kena vā puggalena vādaṃ paṭisaṃyojeyya paṭibaleyya kalahaṃ kareyya bhaṇḍanaṃ kareyya viggahaṃ kareyya vivādaṃ kareyya medhagaṃ kareyya—

yehī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text yehī is the instrumental plural of the relative pronoun ya, with the emphatic particle ti (yehi + ti). It introduces the clause yehi diṭṭhigatehi, correlating with tehi understood.

canūpalittan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ca na upalitta; the text reads canūpalittan before ti. Past participle used adjectivally agreeing with the subject.

mānametī.meaning_2: comes to conceit; arrives at pride; attains conceit
mānametī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound verb: mānaṃ (accusative of māna) + eti (√i 1). Quotation from a verse, third person singular. Alternative analysis: māna + √i with -ṃ sandhi.
mānametī.example_1: na vedagū diṭṭhiyāyako na mutiyā, sa mānametīti.
mānametī.example_2: Na vedagū diṭṭhiyā na mutiyā , sa mānametīti.
mānametī.translation_2: “He is not a master of knowledge through view or through perception, he does not come to conceit.”

naran.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (naran, uttamaṃ naran ti). Sometimes nara is derived from √nar 'lead' as well.
naran.example_2: uttamaṃ naranti aggaṃ seṭṭhaṃ visiṭṭhaṃ pāmokkhaṃ uttamaṃ pavaraṃ naranti—

purakkhatan.meaning_2: placed in front; honoured; preferred; surrounded
purakkhatan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has purakkhatan, which is purakkhataṃ (nominative neuter singular) with the final nipphanna (ṃ) shown as n before a vowel. It is the past participle of purakkhati, meaning 'placed in front' or 'honoured'. The form is neuter singular.
purakkhatan.translation_2: For him there is nothing preferred.”

nīyatī.meaning_2: is led; is carried away; is guided (by); is moved (by)
nīyatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive (kamma) of neti; literary 3sg present. In the text na nīyati, 'is not led (by views)'.
nīyatī.example_2: Vivekadassī phassesu, diṭṭhīsu ca na nīyatī ’’ ti.
nīyatī.translation_2: one who sees detachment in contacts, and is not led by views.”

pāgabbhiyan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative singular (pāgabbhiyan is sandhi for pāgabbhiyaṃ before ti). The Niddesa lists three kinds: kāyika, vācasika and cetasika.
pāgabbhiyan.example_2: Pāgabbhiyanti tīṇi pāgabbhiyāni – kāyikaṃ pāgabbhiyaṃ, vācasikaṃ pāgabbhiyaṃ, cetasikaṃ pāgabbhiyaṃ.
pāgabbhiyan.translation_2: Presumption refers to three types of presumption: bodily presumption, verbal presumption, and mental presumption.

pesuññan.meaning_2: malicious speech; slander; tale-bearing; divisive speech
pesuññan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written pesuññan before ti (sandhi for pesuññaṃ). One of the four verbal faults (vacīduccarita). In the text it is glossed by pisuṇavācā.
pesuññan.example_1: pesuññanti idhekacco pisuṇavāco hoti, ito sutvā amutra akkhātā imesaṃ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā imesaṃ akkhātā amūsaṃ bhedāya.

nānugijjhatī.meaning_2: does not covet; does not hanker (after); is not greedy (for)
nānugijjhatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + anugijjhati. 3rd singular present in the quoted verse; the na negates the whole verb.
nānugijjhatī.example_2: Aviruddho ca taṇhāya, rasesu nānugijjhatī ’’ ti.
nānugijjhatī.translation_2: and, being unopposed by craving, he does not covet tastes.”

saman.meaning_2: calm; peaceful; tranquil; one who is at peace
saman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text 'saman' is the accusative singular of sama (masc) used as a substantive: 'they do not conceive one who is calm in the world'. The form is sandhi for samaṃ before a following consonant; the related PEU entry samaṃ confirms the base sama. Sometimes taken as samaṇa (ascetic), but the context and commentary support sama.

bhavāyā.meaning_2: for existence; for continued existence; to becoming (towards)
bhavāyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Dative or genitive singular of bhava used adverbially in the Niddesa as a gloss on 'bhavāya' (and 'vibhavāya' in the parallel phrase), explained as diṭṭhiyā and as punappunabbhavāya. Final -ā is the sandhi form before 'ti; the headword is given without it.

anapekkhinan.meaning_2: not expecting; not longing (for); free from desire (for)
anapekkhinan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant spelling of anapekkhī. Locative plural in the text: kāmesu anapekkhinaṃ 'without longing for sensual pleasures'. Form anapekkhinan in the text is probably a sandhi variant of anapekkhinaṃ; the lemma could also be read as anapekkhī.

apurakkhatan.meaning_2: not placed in front; not made the forerunner; not put forward
apurakkhatan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is a sandhi form apurakkhataṃ, accusative singular agreeing with taṃ. Formed with the negative prefix na + purakkhata, a past participle of purakkharoti.

nejatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present, negated by na (na ... nejatī); the word is cited in the Niddesa as vādesu nejatī ti, glossing a term meaning 'does not waver in arguments'. Causative form of √ej with the meaning of the simplex.
nejatī.example_2: Taṃ tassa apurakkhataṃ, tasmā vādesu nejatī ’’ ti.
nejatī.translation_2: That is not held in front of him; therefore he does not quake in regard to arguments.”

maccharan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text maccharaṃ (nominative/accusative singular) is glossed by the commentarial 'pañca macchariyāni'. Sometimes written macchariya; here the shorter form is used.
maccharan.example_2: Maccharanti pañca macchariyāni – āvāsamacchariyaṃ, kulamacchariyaṃ, lābhamacchariyaṃ, vaṇṇamacchariyaṃ, dhammamacchariyaṃ.
maccharan.translation_2: 'Avarice' (macchariyaṃ) means: there are five forms of stinginess — stinginess as to one’s monastery, stinginess as to one’s family, stinginess as to one’s gains, stinginess as to one’s status, and stinginess as to the Dhamma.

pesuṇānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural form of pesuṇāni (slanderous words). In the text it is part of a quoted passage explaining when backbiting arises. Could be nominative or accusative plural.
pesuṇānī.translation_2: And backbiting occurs when disputes have arisen.'

piyānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text glossed as dve piyā, i.e. the plural neuter piyāni (piya + āni) in sandhi; the commentary treats it as a nominative plural neuter. Sandhi of separate words, so no root fields.
piyānī.example_2: Piyānīti dve piyā – sattā vā saṅkhārā vā … pe … ime sattā piyā … pe … ime saṅkhārā piyā.
piyānī.translation_2: 'Dear things' (piyāni) refers to two types of dear things: either beings or volitional formations... these beings are dear... these volitional formations are dear.

sātan.meaning_2: pleasant; agreeable; pleasant feeling; desirable object
sātan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An idiomatic and grammatical explanation of pleasure: pleasant feeling and a desirable object. The form sātan is the nominative/accusative singular used in the gloss. See sāta.
sātan.example_2: Sātanti sukhā ca vedanā, iṭṭhañca vatthu [vatthuṃ (sī. ka.)].
sātan.translation_2: Pleasant means pleasant feeling and desirable objects.

asātan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In these sentences asāta is used as an adjective modifying vatthu ('unpleasant thing') and to describe unpleasant feeling. The given form asātan is a sandhi alteration of asātaṃ, the nominative singular in -aṃ. Some sources treat it as a noun ('unpleasantness').

bhavañcā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Quotation form in the Niddesa, glossed by bhavañca vibhavañca; the sandhi replaces the final ṃ of bhavaṃ with ñ before c. Alternative split: bhavaṃ + ca with metrical lengthening of the final vowel.
bhavañcā.example_2: rūpesu disvā vibhavaṃ bhavañcāti rūpesu bhavañca vibhavañca disvā passitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvāti—

yatonidānan.meaning_2: from whatever cause; having whatever source; with whatever origin
yatonidānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In these Niddesa passages the form is a sandhi/compound of yato and nidānaṃ, meaning 'from whatever source' or 'whatever its source'; the text also has yatonidānaṃ as a compound adjective.

itonidānan.meaning_2: having its source here; originating from this; caused by this
itonidānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form is itonidānaṃ, accusative singular neuter used adverbially as 'its source'. The Niddesa glosses it with phassanidānaṃ etc., taking ito as referring to contact (phassa).

pariggahānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text pariggahāni is nominative plural neuter, agreeing with icchānidānāni. The word is from pari + grah, likely via Sanskrit; not included in the root list. Could also be masc plural pariggahā, but the neuter form is used here.

vibhotī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text glosses it with vibhāvīyati, atikkamīyati, etc. The PEU suggests an alternative analysis vi + bhū + ya + te, i.e. a passive vibhūyati contracted to vibhoti. Appears in verse as the final word of the line.
vibhotī.example_1: sukhaṃ dukhañcāpi kathaṃ vibhotīti sukhañca dukkhañca kathaṃ vibhoti vibhāvīyati atikkamīyati samatikkamīyati vītivattīyatīti—

vivādametī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound verb vivādaṃ + eti (√i 1). 3rd singular present. Commentarial gloss: na kalahaṃ karoti, na vivādaṃ karoti. The sandhi -am- is vivādaṃ eti.
vivādametī.example_1: ñatvā vimutto na vivādametīti ñatvā jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā.
vivādametī.example_2: na vivādametīti na kalahaṃ karoti, na bhaṇḍanaṃ karoti, na viggahaṃ karoti, na vivādaṃ karoti, na medhagaṃ karoti.

viggayhā.meaning_2: having grasped; having taken hold of; having seized; having settled upon
viggayhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text viggayhāti = viggayha + iti, the absolutive used in the Niddesa explanation of disputatious speech; the gloss gives gahetvā, uggahetvā, gaṇhitvā, parāmasitvā, abhinivisitvā. The absolutive ending -ya here follows the form viggayha (cf. PEU viggayha [vi+gaha+tvā]).
viggayhā.example_1: viggayhāti gahetvā uggahetvā gaṇhitvā parāmasitvā abhinivisitvā nānā vadanti vividhaṃ vadanti aññoññaṃ vadanti puthu vadanti, na ekaṃ vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharanti.
viggayhā.example_2: Viggayhāti gahetvā uggahetvā gaṇhitvā parāmasitvā abhinivisitvā nānā vadanti vividhaṃ vadanti aññoññaṃ vadanti puthu [puthuṃ (sī.)] vadanti, na ekaṃ vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharanti.
viggayhā.translation_2: “Striving” means having taken up, having grabbed, having seized, having grasped, having settled into, they speak in many ways, they speak in diverse ways, they speak differently, they speak in many ways; they do not speak, talk, tell, or declare as one thing.

cāhū.meaning_2: and they said; and they called
cāhū.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ca + āhu. In the text cāhūti = ca + āhu + iti. The final -ū is m.c. (metri causa) for the original -u; see CPD s.v. āha. The translation 'and they said' fits the gloss for bālo paro akusalo.

imesan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of imesaṃ + nu? Actually imesan ti = imesaṃ + iti, showing -aṃ + iti sandhi. Genitive/dative plural demonstrative pronoun. Possibly influenced by neuter r-stem declension? (Buddhavaṃsa 2.2 uses imesan).

dhammamanānujānan.meaning_2: not approving of the teaching; not consenting to the doctrine
dhammamanānujānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, from the phrase parassa ce dhammaṃ ananujānanto. Sandhi of dhammaṃ + ananujānanta. The negative an- is joined to anujānanta.

saccan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of saccaṃ iti with the final consonant assimilated: saccaṃ + iti > saccan ti. In the text it appears in the phrase saccan ti, where it is the object of āhu ('they call it the truth'). The sandhi (-ṃ + i- > -n-) is common in verse and commentarial prose.

musātī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form musātī is musā with the quotative ti attached (musā + ti); entry given for musā alone. Used with tucchaṃ (vainly, falsely).

cāhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ca + āhā (perfect of āha, 'said'), used in commentarial quotations: ... iti cāhā ti, '... and he said'. Sometimes written as one word with the quotation marker.

dahātī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present of √dhā ("place, put"). In the text it follows paraṃ in the Niddesa gloss of bālo. Variant readings dahatīti etc. are the same verb with the quotative -ti.

bālamasuddhidhamman.meaning_2: of a fool with impure doctrine; of a foolish person with an impure teaching
bālamasuddhidhamman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of bālaṃ + asuddhidhammaṃ; the -n is a commentarial mis-sandhi for -ṃ. Found in a verse quoted in the Niddesa.
bālamasuddhidhamman.example_2: Sayaṃva so medhagamāvaheyya, paraṃ vadaṃ bālamasuddhidhamman ’’ ti.
bālamasuddhidhamman.translation_2: He would bring contention upon himself, while speaking of the other as a fool with impure doctrine.”

nindamanvānayantī.meaning_2: all of them follow censuring; all of them bring censure upon themselves
nindamanvānayantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a sandhi of nindantaṃ (or nindaṃ) + anvānayantī; alternatively analysed as nindaṃ + anvānayantī. Final -ī is nom. pl. feminine of anvānayantī, agreeing with a feminine subject; but the first part is uncertain, and *nindAM* or nindanto also possible.

avivādabhūmin.meaning_2: ground of non-dispute; sphere free from dispute; state without contention
avivādabhūmin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An epithet of Nibbāna. Accusative singular in the text.
avivādabhūmin.example_2: Etampi disvā na vivādayetha, khemābhipassaṃ avivādabhūmin ’’ ti.
avivādabhūmin.translation_2: Having seen this, one should not dispute, seeing Nibbāna as the ground of no-dispute.”

kācī.meaning_2: any; whatever; some; any at all
kācī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Indefinite pronoun, feminine nominative singular of kiñci in the phrase yā kāci, 'whatever (woman/feminine thing); any at all'. Sometimes written as kāci with the emphatic -ci; in the text it follows the relative yā, giving the generalising sense 'whatever'.
kācī.example_1: yā kācīti sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ asesaṃ nissesaṃ pariyādiyanavacanametaṃ—
kācī.example_2: Yā kācīti sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ asesaṃ nissesaṃ pariyādiyanavacanametaṃ – yā kācīti.
kācī.translation_2: “Whatever” means: in all respects, in every way, entirely, without remainder—this is a term for all-inclusiveness.

vatan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vatan ti stands for vataṃ, nominative singular, quoted and glossed with various vows (hatthivata etc.). Not the emphatic particle vata.
vatan.example_1: vatanti hatthivataṃ vā assavataṃ vā govataṃ vā kukkuravataṃ vā kākavataṃ vā vāsudevavataṃ vā baladevavataṃ vā puṇṇabhaddavataṃ vā maṇibhaddavataṃ vā aggivataṃ vā nāgavataṃ vā supaṇṇavataṃ vā yakkhavataṃ vā asuravataṃ vā gandhabbavataṃ vā mahārājavataṃ vā candavataṃ vā sūriyavataṃ vā indavataṃ vā brahmavataṃ vā devavataṃ vā disāvataṃ vā ādāya samādāya ādiyitvā samādiyitvā gaṇhitvā parāmasitvā abhinivisitvā upaṭṭhitā paccupaṭṭhitā allīnā upagatā ajjhositā adhimuttāti—
vatan.example_2: Vatanti hatthivataṃ vā assavataṃ vā govataṃ vā kukkuravataṃ vā kākavataṃ vā vāsudevavataṃ vā baladevavataṃ vā puṇṇabhaddavataṃ vā maṇibhaddavataṃ vā aggivataṃ vā nāgavataṃ vā supaṇṇavataṃ vā yakkhavataṃ vā asuravataṃ vā gandhabbavataṃ vā mahārājavataṃ vā candavataṃ vā sūriyavataṃ vā indavataṃ vā brahmavataṃ vā devavataṃ vā disāvataṃ vā ādāya samādāya ādiyitvā samādiyitvā gaṇhitvā parāmasitvā abhinivisitvā upaṭṭhitā paccupaṭṭhitā allīnā upagatā ajjhositā adhimuttāti – vataṃ samādāya upaṭṭhitāse.
vatan.translation_2: “Vows” are the vow of the elephant, the horse, the cow, the dog, the crow... the vow of the gods, the vow of the quarters; having taken, undertaken, assumed, accepted, grasped, held as a base, conceived, and become attached to them, they remain, are ready, adhere, are committed, and are deeply involved in them; thus, “having undertaken vows, they remain established in them.”

sāvajjanavajjametan.meaning_2: this is blameworthy and blameless; this is faulty and faultless
sāvajjanavajjametan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sāvajjanavajjaṃ (sa + avajja + avajja) and etaṃ. Part of the compound kammañca sāvajjanavajjametaṃ; the text's -an is a variant spelling of the sandhi.

asuddhin.meaning_2: impurity; that which is impure; unwholesome state
asuddhin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text asuddhinti, i.e. asuddhiṃ, accusative singular after patthenti. Commentarial gloss explains asuddhi as akusale dhamme. The na prefix is assimilated to a- before the noun.

jappitānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter plural nominative/accusative in -āni in the text; a past participle used as a noun meaning 'murmurings; longings'.

tathevā.meaning_2: in the same way; just so; likewise
tathevā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text tathevā is tatheva before a quotation ti (tathevāti); the -ā belongs to the quotative particle, not the word. The commentary glosses tathā tacchā bhūtā yāthāvā aviparītā.
tathevā.example_2: saddhammapūjāpi nesaṃ tathevāti saddhammapūjā tathā tacchā bhūtā yāthāvā aviparītāti—

sakāyanānī.meaning_2: one's own course; one's own path; own way
sakāyanānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural in -āni at the end of a verse line. Can also be read as saka + āyana ('one's own arriving/welfare') or as sakā + yānāni ('own vehicles'), but the PEU split saka + ayana is taken here.

bhaveyyun.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd plural optative of bhavati, written bhaveyyuṃ (Sandhi with -ti). The sentence quotes 'sabbeva vādā tathiyā bhaveyyuṃ' (all doctrines would be true).
bhaveyyun.example_1: sabbeva vādā tathiyā bhaveyyunti sabbeva vādā tathā tacchā bhūtā yāthāvā aviparītā bhaveyyunti—
bhaveyyun.example_2: Sabbeva vādā tathiyā bhaveyyunti sabbeva vādā tathā tacchā bhūtā yāthāvā aviparītā bhaveyyunti – sabbeva vādā tathiyā bhaveyyuṃ.

paccattamevā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of paccattaṃ (adverb, 'individually') and eva (emphatic, 'just, only'). In the text -ti is appended, so the form is paccattamevā ti. The meaning is 'their purity is only individual/personal'.
paccattamevā.example_2: Sabbeva vādā tathiyā bhaveyyuṃ, suddhī hi nesaṃ paccattamevā ’’ ti.
paccattamevā.translation_2: If all doctrines were true, their purity would only be personal.”

dhammamaññan.meaning_2: one who knows another dhamma (as supreme)
dhammamaññan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, from the verse quoted in the Niddesa (na hi seṭṭhato passati dhammamaññan = he does not regard any other dhamma as supreme).
dhammamaññan.example_2: Tasmā vivādāni upātivatto, na hi seṭṭhato passati dhammamaññan ’’ ti.
dhammamaññan.translation_2: Therefore, he has transcended strife; for he does not see any other dhamma as supreme.”

jānāmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 1st person singular present of jānāti, used in the text in the phrase jānāmīti (= jānāmi + iti).
jānāmī.example_1: jānāmīti paracittañāṇena vā jānāmi, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇena vā jānāmi.

nāmarūpan.meaning_2: name-and-form; mind and body; mental and physical phenomena
nāmarūpan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the final -ṃ is changed to -n by sandhi before ti (nāmarūpan ti). Subject/accusative of dakkhati in the quotation. Also written nāmarūpaṃyeva in the prose.
nāmarūpan.example_1: passaṃ naro dakkhati nāmarūpanti passaṃ naro dakkhati paracittañāṇena vā passanto, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇena vā passanto, maṃsacakkhunā vā passanto, dibbena cakkhunā vā passanto nāmarūpaṃyeva dakkhati niccato sukhato attato, na tesaṃ dhammānaṃ samudayaṃ vā atthaṅgamaṃ vā assādaṃ vā ādīnavaṃ vā nissaraṇaṃ vā dakkhatīti—
nāmarūpan.example_2: Passaṃ naro dakkhati nāmarūpanti passaṃ naro dakkhati paracittañāṇena vā passanto, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇena vā passanto, maṃsacakkhunā vā passanto, dibbena cakkhunā vā passanto nāmarūpaṃyeva dakkhati niccato sukhato attato, na tesaṃ dhammānaṃ samudayaṃ vā atthaṅgamaṃ vā assādaṃ vā ādīnavaṃ vā nissaraṇaṃ vā dakkhatīti – passaṃ naro dakkhati nāmarūpaṃ.
nāmarūpan.translation_2: “The person seeing sees name-and-form” means the person seeing—whether seeing by the knowledge of others' minds, seeing by the knowledge of recollection of past lives, seeing with the fleshly eye, or seeing with the divine eye—sees only name-and-form as permanent, as pleasurable, and as self; he does not see the origination, the disappearance, the gratification, the danger, or the escape of those phenomena—that is the meaning of “The person seeing sees name-and-form.”

tānimevā.meaning_2: and just those things?; those very things
tānimevā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Quotation form in Niddesa glosses; alternative analysis tāni + ime + eva, 'those very things'. Final -vā may belong to the following word in the source.
tānimevā.translation_2: “Having seen, he knows only those things”:

akubban.meaning_2: not making; not doing; not creating
akubban.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Negative present participle (na + kubbanta) used adverbially with nave; commentarial gloss explains navā as the present five aggregates. The text form akubban is a sandhi/variant spelling.

asmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of asmi (I am) + iti. Used in the Niddesa as the formula 'asmī ti' representing the conceit 'I am'. In the second quotation it appears without the iti, as asmī ti (asmī + iti) too.
asmī.example_1: asmīti rūpe asmīti māno asmīti chando asmīti anusayo;
asmī.example_2: Tassa rūpaṃ samannesato yāvatā rūpassa gati, vedanaṃ … saññaṃ … saṅkhāre … viññāṇaṃ samannesato yāvatā viññāṇassa gati, yampissa taṃ hoti ‘ ahan ’ ti vā ‘ maman ’ ti vā,‘ asmī ’ ti vā, tampi tassa na hotī ’’ ti.
asmī.translation_2: For him, as he scrutinizes form as far as the destination of form extends, and scrutinizes feeling... perception... volitional formations... consciousness as far as the destination of consciousness extends, whatever occurs to him as ‘I am’ or ‘mine’ or ‘I am,’ that also does not exist for him.”

ajjhattan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the final -ṃ of ajjhattaṃ has been assimilated to a following t- (ajjhattan ti). An indeclinable used in the Niddesa commentarial style to gloss taṇhā.

kubbethā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Second person plural optative in the text (kubbethāti = kubbetha + iti); the -ā is the sandhi of -a + iti. See kubbati.

anekarūpehī.meaning_2: of many forms; having various appearances; manifold
anekarūpehī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental plural in the text (anekarūpehi). Bahubbīhi compound describing one who is touched (phuṭṭho) by many forms.

parissayavinayan.meaning_2: removal of dangers; dispelling of troubles; warding off of perils
parissayavinayan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is glossed by parissayavinayaṃ, parissayappahānaṃ, parissayavūpasamaṃ, and amataṃ nibbānaṃ. Accusative singular in the text; in the first sentence it agrees with sakkhidhammaṃ.

sakkhidhamman.meaning_2: as a witness; by personal experience; with one's own eyes
sakkhidhamman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text sakkhidhamman is a sandhi of sakkhi + dhammaṃ, accusative singular of sakkhidhamma. sakkhi is an indeclinable meaning 'as a witness; by direct experience', used adverbially before dhammaṃ. The phrase is glossed with sāmaṃ sayamabhiññātaṃ attapaccakkhaṃ dhammaṃ.
sakkhidhamman.example_1: sakkhidhammanti na itihitihaṃ, na itikirāya, na paramparāya, na piṭakasampadāya, na takkahetu, na nayahetu, na ākāraparivitakkena, na diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā sāmaṃ sayamabhiññātaṃ attapaccakkhaṃ dhammanti—
sakkhidhamman.example_2: sakkhidhammanti na itihitihaṃ na itikiriyāya na paramparāya na piṭakasampadāya na takkahetu na nayahetu na ākāraparivitakkena na diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā sāmaṃ sayamabhiññātaṃ attapaccakkhadhammaṃ addasi addakkhi apassi paṭivijjhīti—

samādhin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, in the phrase pātimokkhaṃ atha vāpi samādhiṃ; the -n is sandhi before ti.
samādhin.example_2: atha vāpi samādhinti yā cittassa ṭhiti saṇṭhiti avaṭṭhiti avisāhāro avikkhepo avisāhatamānasatā samatho samādhindriyaṃ samādhibalaṃ sammāsamādhīti—

pātimokkhan.meaning_2: Pātimokkha; monastic code of discipline; highest virtue
pātimokkhan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the -n is the sandhi form before ti (pātimokkhan ti = pātimokkhaṃ iti); alternative analysis pāti + mokkha. Explained as sīlaṃ patiṭṭhā ādi caraṇaṃ saṃyamo saṃvaro mukhaṃ.
pātimokkhan.example_1: pātimokkhanti sīlaṃ patiṭṭhā ādi caraṇaṃ saṃyamo saṃvaro mukhaṃ pamukhaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā.

sotan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (sotan = sotaṃ, ear), object of āvaraye; from √su 'hear', literally 'that by which one hears'.

vatthānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive plural vatthānaṃ, with sandhi -an before ti. In the Niddesa gloss it is glossed by cha cīvarāni, 'the six robes'.

annānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The reading annānan is doubtful; the commentary glosses it with a list of foods (odano kummāso sattu maccho maṃsaṃ). It could be a by-form of anna (food), with -nan a text corruption. The PEU entry annā (mother) may be unrelated.

pānānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is written pānānan, probably a variant or scribal form of pānāni, the nominative/accusative plural of pāna. The quotation introduces the list of the eight drinks.
pānānan.example_2: Pānānanti aṭṭha pānāni – ambapānaṃ, jambupānaṃ, cocapānaṃ, mocapānaṃ, madhupānaṃ, muddikapānaṃ, sālukapānaṃ, phārusakapānaṃ.
pānānan.translation_2: Drinks refer to the eight [allowable] drinks: mango-syrup, rose-apple syrup, coca-syrup, moca-syrup, madhuka-syrup, grape-syrup, lilyroot-syrup, [and] phārusaka-syrup.

khādanīyānan.meaning_2: hard food; chewable food; food that is to be chewed
khādanīyānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text khādanīyānan is a sandhi form of khādanīyānaṃ (genitive plural), resolved by ti: khādanīyānanti. It is paired with bhojanīya in the phrase bhojanīyaṃ khādanīyaṃ, and glossed here with a list of chewable foods.
khādanīyānan.example_1: khādanīyānanti piṭṭhakhajjakaṃ, pūvakhajjakaṃ, mūlakhajjakaṃ, tacakhajjakaṃ, pattakhajjakaṃ, pupphakhajjakaṃ, phalakhajjakaṃ.

nappamajjeyyā.meaning_2: would not be negligent; should not be heedless; let one not neglect
nappamajjeyyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + pamajjeyya; optative 3rd singular in -eyyā, used in the quoted phrase nappamajjeyyā ti and glossed by appamādo kusalesu dhammesu.
nappamajjeyyā.example_2: nappamajjeyyāti sakkaccakārī assa sātaccakārī aṭṭhitakārī anolīnavuttiko anikkhittacchando anikkhittadhuro appamādo kusalesu dhammesu.

bhajeyyā.meaning_2: should associate with; should engage in; should practice; should cultivate
bhajeyyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular of bhajati, glossed in the text by sambhajeyya, seveyya, niseveyya, saṃseveyya, paṭiseveyya. Here with jāgariyaṃ: 'should engage in vigilance'.
bhajeyyā.example_1: jāgariyaṃ bhajeyyāti jāgariyaṃ bhajeyya sambhajeyya seveyya niseveyya saṃseveyya paṭiseveyyāti—
bhajeyyā.example_2: Jāgariyaṃ bhajeyyāti jāgariyaṃ bhajeyya sambhajeyya seveyya niseveyya saṃseveyya paṭiseveyyāti – jāgariyaṃ bhajeyya.
bhajeyyā.translation_2: “Should engage in vigilance”: he should engage in, practice, serve, cultivate, attend to, and pursue vigilance—this is “should engage in vigilance.”

savibhūsan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears as savibhūsan due to sandhi before ti (savibhūsanaṃ or savibhūsana), accusative singular agreeing with methunaṃ.
savibhūsan.example_1: tandiṃ māyaṃ hassaṃ khiḍḍaṃ, methunaṃ vippajahe savibhūsanti.
savibhūsan.example_2: Tandiṃ māyaṃ hassaṃ khiḍḍaṃ, methunaṃ vippajahe savibhūsan ’’ ti.
savibhūsan.translation_2: One should abandon indolence, deceit, disputatiousness, and play, as well as sexual intercourse together with adornment.”

hassan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text hassan is the absolutive/general form hasan, i.e. 'laughing' (prp), quoted as a gloss (hasan ti). The form here is hasan, a present participle (-anta) used in the quotation, from √has. Here the object is the noun dantavidaṃsakaṃ. The lemma_1 hasati is the 3rd singular present.

nakkhattan.meaning_2: constellation; star; auspicious star; a nakkhatta (astrological observance)
nakkhattan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, in a list of superstitions that a monk should not practise. The PEU gives an alternative popular etymology (na khayati / na kharati).
nakkhattan.example_1: āthabbaṇaṃ supinaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ, no vidahe athopi nakkhattanti.

seveyyā.meaning_2: should serve; should practise; should associate with
seveyyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular with the -eyya ending, from the root √sev. In the text it is negated: na seveyyā, "one should not practise". The final -ā is a metrical lengthening before the quotation particle ti.
seveyyā.example_2: Virutañca gabbhakaraṇaṃ, tikicchaṃ māmako na seveyyā ’’ ti.
seveyyā.translation_2: A devotee should not serve (the study of) animal cries, establishing the womb, or medical treatment.”

nābhisajjeyyā.grammar: pr, 3rd sg, opt of na abhisajjati
nābhisajjeyyā.meaning_2: should not become attached; should not cling (to)
nābhisajjeyyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Negative optative of abhisajjati used in the phrase gāme ca nābhisajjeyyā. The form is na + abhisajjeyya (na + abhi + √saj + eyya), with -eyyā perhaps influenced by sandhi or metre. The commentary glosses it with na sajjeyya, na gaṇheyya, na bajjheyya, na palibajjheyya.
nābhisajjeyyā.example_2: gāme ca nābhisajjeyyāti gāme na sajjeyya na gaṇheyya na bajjheyya na palibajjheyya, agiddho assa agadhito amucchito anajjhosanno vītagedho vigatagedho cattagedho …pe…

niyyethā.meaning_2: should one proceed; should one go on; should one enter (into)
niyyethā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 2nd plural of niyyāti (ni + √yā), used impersonally in the quoted phrase mosavajje na niyyethā: 'one should not proceed into lying'. Alternative analysis: optative of neti/nayati with the ni- prefix, meaning 'should not be led (into)'. Commentarial gloss.

puthujanānan.meaning_2: ordinary person; commoner; worldly person; the unlearned multitude
puthujanānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of puthu (ordinary; separate; many) and jana (people). In the Niddesa it is glossed as a list of ordinary people (khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā, gahaṭṭhā, pabbajitā, devā, manussā). Genitive plural in the text (puthujanānaṃ).
puthujanānan.example_2: puthujanānanti khattiyā ca brāhmaṇā ca vessā ca suddā ca gahaṭṭhā ca pabbajitā ca devā ca manussā ca, te bahukāhi vācāhi aniṭṭhāhi akantāhi amanāpāhi akkoseyyuṃ paribhāseyyuṃ roseyyuṃ viroseyyuṃ hiṃseyyuṃ vihiṃseyyuṃ heṭheyyuṃ viheṭheyyuṃ ghāteyyuṃ upaghāteyyuṃ upaghātaṃ kareyyuṃ tesaṃ bahuṃ vācaṃ aniṭṭhaṃ akantaṃ amanāpaṃ sutvā suṇitvā uggahitvā upadhārayitvā upalakkhayitvāti—

samaṇānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive plural in the text (samaṇānaṃ, with the final consonant of the sandhi form). The commentarial gloss explains it as paribbājakas, wanderers.
samaṇānan.example_1: samaṇānanti ye keci ito bahiddhā paribbajūpagatā paribbajasamāpannā.

vicinan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Glossed in the text with pavicinanto, tulayanto, tīrayanto, vibhāvayanto, vibhūtaṃ karonto. The form vicinan is the 3rd plural present of vicinati (also analysable as the participle vicinanto, nominative singular masculine, agreeing with a subject).
vicinan.example_1: vicinanti vicinanto pavicinanto tulayanto tīrayanto vibhāvayanto vibhūtaṃ karonto.

sakkhidhammamanītihamaddasī.meaning_2: who saw the state of a witness, free from danger; seer of the truth of the witness, beyond calamity
sakkhidhammamanītihamaddasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in the text only as the quotation-word sakkhidhammamanītihamaddasīti; here taken as sandhi of sakkhi + dhamma + anītiha + addasī (cf. the stock epithet sakkhidhammo anītihadhammo). Analysis uncertain; alternatively a single compound adjective with the -ī ending.

namassan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has namassan, which is a quotation form of namassati with -ti dropped (or an absolutive-like form used in glosses). The gloss explains it with namassamāno, sakkurumāno, pūjayamāno, etc., so the entry is for the verb namassati.
namassan.example_1: namassanti kāyena vā namassamāno vācāya vā namassamāno cittena vā namassamāno anvatthapaṭipattiyā vā namassamāno dhammānudhammapaṭipattiyā vā namassamāno sakkurumāno garukurumāno mānayamāno pūjayamāno apacayamāno.
namassan.example_2: Namassanti kāyena vā namassamāno vācāya vā namassamāno cittena vā namassamāno anvatthapaṭipattiyā vā namassamāno dhammānudhammapaṭipattiyā vā namassamāno sakkurumāno garukurumāno [sakkāramāno garukāramāno (syā.)] mānayamāno pūjayamāno apacayamāno.
namassan.translation_2: ‘Showing reverence’ means showing reverence with the body, showing reverence with speech, showing reverence with the mind, showing reverence through practice in accordance with the meaning, showing reverence through practice in accordance with the Dhamma, acting with respect, acting with regard, honoring, worshipping, and paying homage.

jātan.meaning_2: born; arisen; produced; come into being
jātan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the quotation attadaṇḍā bhayaṃ jātaṃ, the form is jātaṃ (nom. sg. nt), written jātan before the quotative ti; jātaṃ agrees with bhayaṃ (fear).

medhagan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Pāḷi medha + ga (√gam, kvi), a quotation in the Niddesa; in janaṃ passatha medhagan, medhagan is sandhi for medhagaṃ, accusative singular.

kittayissāmī.meaning_2: will proclaim; will recount; will tell; will declare
kittayissāmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 1st person singular in the text (kittayissāmi); headword given as the 3rd singular future. Built on the causative stem of kitteti; the glosses pakittayissāmi etc. show it is used as a synonym of pakitteti.
kittayissāmī.example_2: kittayissāmīti pakittayissāmi ācikkhissāmi desessāmi paññapessāmi paṭṭhapessāmi vivarissāmi vibhajissāmi uttānīkarissāmi pakāsissāmīti—

anositan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, qualifying a place (bhavana). Negative compound of na + osita.
anositan.translation_2: Desiring shelter for myself, I did not see any place that was not inhabited.”

tvevā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tva (emphatic particle, 'truly, indeed') + eva ('thus, so'); glossed by the commentary as tveva. Quoted form in the phrase osāne tvevā ti.
tvevā.example_1: osāne tvevāti sabbaṃ yobbaññaṃ jarā osāpeti, sabbaṃ ārogyaṃ byādhi osāpeti, sabbaṃ jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ osāpeti, sabbaṃ lābhaṃ alābho osāpeti, sabbaṃ yasaṃ ayaso osāpeti, sabbaṃ pasaṃsaṃ nindā osāpeti, sabbaṃ sukhaṃ dukkhaṃ osāpetīti—
tvevā.example_2: Osāne tvevāti sabbaṃ yobbaññaṃ jarā osāpeti, sabbaṃ ārogyaṃ byādhi osāpeti, sabbaṃ jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ osāpeti, sabbaṃ lābhaṃ alābho osāpeti, sabbaṃ yasaṃ ayaso osāpeti, sabbaṃ pasaṃsaṃ nindā osāpeti, sabbaṃ sukhaṃ dukkhaṃ osāpetīti – osāne tveva.
tvevā.translation_2: “Truly in the ending” means old age brings to an end all youthfulness, disease brings to an end all health, death brings to an end all life, loss brings to an end all gain, disrepute brings to an end all status, blame brings to an end all praise, suffering brings to an end all pleasure—thus: “Truly in the ending.”

sallamaddakkhin.meaning_2: seeing the arrow; knowing the dart
sallamaddakkhin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sallaṃ + addakkhin (the nasal assimilated to the following vowel). Here a gloss on the word being explained. The related entry for addakkhin (ī-stem adjective) gives the pattern.

addakkhin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist first person singular; the text's addakkhin is a variant spelling. Glossed in the Niddesa with addasaṃ, adakkhiṃ, apassiṃ, paṭivijjhiṃ.
addakkhin.example_2: Addakkhinti addasaṃ adakkhiṃ apassiṃ paṭivijjhinti – athettha sallamaddakkhiṃ.
addakkhin.translation_2: “I saw” means I saw, I perceived, I looked upon, I penetrated—thus: “And then I saw the thorn.”

hadayassitan.meaning_2: dependent on the heart; resting on the heart; connected with the heart-mind
