hadayassitan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is part of a quoted gloss (duddasaṃ hadayassitan ti), where hadayaṃ is explained as cittaṃ. The reading hadayassitaṃ (with niggahīta) is likely; the nissita etc. that follow are synonyms.

duddasan.meaning_2: hard to see; difficult to perceive; hard to understand
duddasan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is duddasan ti, i.e. the adjective duddasa with the quotation particle ti and the accusative singular ending -aṃ assimilated to -an. The gloss explains it with duddasaṃ duddakkhaṃ duppassaṃ dubbujjhaṃ.
duddasan.example_1: duddasanti duddasaṃ duddakkhaṃ duppassaṃ dubbujjhaṃ duranubujjhaṃ duppaṭivijjhanti—
duddasan.example_2: Duddasanti duddasaṃ duddakkhaṃ duppassaṃ dubbujjhaṃ duranubujjhaṃ duppaṭivijjhanti – duddasaṃ.
duddasan.translation_2: “Hard to see” means it is hard to see, hard to perceive, hard to observe, hard to understand, hard to know, hard to penetrate—thus: “Hard to see.”

sīdatī.meaning_2: sinks; sinks down; founders; goes under
sīdatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text negated (na sīdatīti) and glossed by na saṃsīdati, na osīdati, na avasīdati with reference to the four floods (ogha). The form before -ti is sīdati with the final i lengthened before the quotation.
sīdatī.example_2: na sīdatīti kāmoghe na sīdati, bhavoghe na sīdati, diṭṭhoghe na sīdati, avijjoghe na sīdati, na saṃsīdati na osīdati na avasīdati na gacchati na avagacchatīti—

gadhitānī.meaning_2: which are clung to (by); that are attached (in the world)
gadhitānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text, gadhitānī is gadhitāni + iti (the sandhi form before the quotation ti). Probably neuter plural of gadhita, 'clung to; attached; desired'. The PEU entry suggests an alternative reading gadhitāse (gadhitā + se).

anugīyantī.meaning_2: is sung after; is recited; is chanted; is spoken of
anugīyantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text anugīyantī is a sandhi form of anugīyanti (nominative plural neuter of the present participle), followed by ti. The verbal gloss explains it with passive verbs meaning 'is sung; is recited; is spoken; is proclaimed'.
anugīyantī.example_1: anugīyantīti gīyanti niggīyanti kathīyanti bhaṇīyanti dīpīyanti voharīyanti.

thīnan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text thīnan is a sandhi form of thīnaṃ, accusative singular, glossed with thina and thiyanā as a synonym of cittassa līnatā. The PEU derives it from √thi with the suffix yu; the alternative analysis thā + kta = ta is also recorded there.
thīnan.example_2: thīnanti yā cittassa akalyatā akammaññatā olīyanā sallīyanā līnaṃ līyanā līyitattaṃ, thinaṃ thiyanā thiyitattaṃ cittassa.

tandin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Qualifies one who is full of sloth (tandī). In the text it is the head word explained in the gloss, nominative singular, quoted in the -ti construction.
tandin.example_1: tandinti yā tandī tandiyanā tandiyitattaṃ tandimanakatā ālasyaṃ ālasyāyanā ālasyāyitattaṃ.
tandin.example_2: Tandinti yā tandī [tandi (sī. syā. ka.)] tandiyanā tandiyitattaṃ tandimanakatā ālasyaṃ ālasyāyatā ālasyāyitattaṃ.
tandin.translation_2: “Sloth” (tandi) means any sloth, laziness, sluggishness, the state of being sluggish, or idleness.

mahoghotī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text mahogho hoti is sandhi for mahogho + iti, the quotation being an explanation of gedhaṃ. Here figuratively the great flood of craving.

jappanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text jappanaṃ is accusative singular of the quote ājavaṃ brūmi jappanaṃ, where jappana stands in apposition to ājava (craving). The word also means reciting mantras.
jappanan.example_2: ājavaṃ brūmi jappananti ājavaṃ “jappanā”ti brūmi ācikkhāmi …pe… uttānīkaromi pakāsemīti—

pakampanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the subject of a gloss, nominative singular; the final -n for -ṃ is possibly sandhi before ti. The sense is 'trembling, shaking' (of an object).

kassacī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Indefinite pronoun with the enclitic -ci, written kassacī before following ti (kassaci + iti). Genitive singular used with na to mean "not of anyone".

duraccayan.meaning_2: hard to overcome; hard to get past; difficult to give up
duraccayan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular modifying saṅgaṃ in the verse; from du + accaya ("going beyond, overcoming").

nājjhetī.meaning_2: does not yearn; does not crave; does not fret
nājjhetī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + ajjhati (√jhā, meditative yearning); glossed in the text with najjheti, nijjhāyati, pajjhāyati.
nājjhetī.example_2: nājjhetīti najjheti na ajjheti na upanijjhāyati na nijjhāyati na pajjhāyati.

mamāyitan.meaning_2: regarded as mine; cherished as one's own; held dear
mamāyitan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is written mamāyitan before ti (mamāyitaṃ). It occurs in a quotation and is glossed by mamattā. The PEU treats it as a derivative of mama with -āya and -ta, so the four root fields are left empty.

asaṃvindan.meaning_2: not obtaining; not getting; not finding
asaṃvindan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle used as a noun meaning 'one who does not obtain'. Accusative singular modifying 'mamattaṃ' in the text.

avikampinan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form avikampinan is accusative singular (niggahīta sandhi for avikampitaṃ); the -an spelling is unusual. The PEU relates it to na + vikampita.
avikampinan.translation_2: When asked about the unshakeable one, I declare these as his rewards.”

nādetī.meaning_2: does not grasp; does not cling to; does not take hold of; does not appropriate
nādetī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text nādetīti = na + ādeti + iti; glossed na ādiyati na upādiyati. Probably an irregular contraction of na ādiyati, not related to √nad 'roar' despite the PEU suggestion.
nādetī.example_1: nādetīti rūpaṃ nādiyati na upādiyati na gaṇhāti na parāmasati nābhinivisati,
nādetī.example_2: Nādetīti rūpaṃ nādiyati na upādiyati na gaṇhāti na parāmasati nābhinivisati, vedanaṃ … saññaṃ … saṅkhāre … viññāṇaṃ … gatiṃ … upapattiṃ … paṭisandhiṃ … bhavaṃ … saṃsāraṃ … vaṭṭaṃ nādiyati na upādiyati na gaṇhāti na parāmasati nābhinivisatīti – nādeti.
nādetī.translation_2: “He does not grasp” means: he does not grasp materiality, does not cling to it, does not take hold of it, does not touch it, does not become attached to it; he does not grasp feeling... perception... volitional formations... consciousness... path... rebirth... re-linking... existence... saṃsāra... the round — he does not cling to it, does not take hold of it, does not touch it, does not become attached to it — thus, “he does not grasp.”

ratin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text as ratin, accusative singular, m inserted before ti. Explained in the Niddesa as nekkhammaratiṃ vivekaratiṃ upasamaratiṃ sambodhiratiṃ. Feminine i-stem.
ratin.example_1: ratinti nekkhammaratiṃ vivekaratiṃ upasamaratiṃ sambodhiratiṃ ajjhagā samajjhagā adhigacchi phassesi sacchākāsīti—
ratin.example_2: Ratinti nekkhammaratiṃ vivekaratiṃ upasamaratiṃ sambodhiratiṃ ajjhagā samajjhagā adhigacchi phassesi sacchākāsīti – ekova ratimajjhagā.
ratin.translation_2: Delight: he attained, arrived at, obtained, contacted, and realized the delight of renunciation, the delight of seclusion, the delight of the stilling of defilements, and the delight of awakening—alone, he attained delight.

tādin.meaning_2: such; of that nature; stable; firm (epithet of the Buddha)
tādin.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Used as an adjective and as a noun for the Buddha. In the text tādin is nominative singular, and tādī is a variant form; the Niddesa explains it with five tādī qualities.

asitan.meaning_2: attached; clung to; dependent (on); relied upon
asitan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text asitan ti glosses a term split as na + sita by the commentator (two kinds of nissaya: taṇhā and diṭṭhi), i.e. 'dependent, attached'. Alternatively it could be an absolutive of āsati ('having sat near') or a past participle of asati (√as 3 / √as 4, 'eaten' — cf. asitabba). Accusative singular in the text.
asitan.example_2: Asitanti dve nissayā – taṇhānissayo ca diṭṭhinissayo ca.
asitan.translation_2: Unattached: There are two kinds of attachment—the attachment of craving and the attachment of views.

gaṇimāgatan.meaning_2: come to the group; arrived at the crowd; gone to the multitude
gaṇimāgatan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of gaṇi + āgata; accusative singular agreeing with the person described in the Niddesa gloss, not a proper name. Perhaps to be read as gaṇim āgataṃ with the accusative of gaṇi, 'come to the group'.

āgatan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is accusative singular, qualifying saṅkassanagaraṃ; the gloss is upagataṃ samupagataṃ samupapannaṃ.
āgatan.example_2: Āgatanti upagataṃ samupagataṃ samupapannaṃ [sampattaṃ (bahūsu)] saṅkassanagaranti – akuhaṃ gaṇimāgataṃ.
āgatan.translation_2: Having arrived: He has arrived at, approached, and attained the city of Saṅkassa—without deceit, having arrived among the community.

baddhānan.meaning_2: of the bound; of those bound
baddhānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi form of baddhānaṃ (genitive plural), occurring as baddhānan before ti. The Niddesa glosses baddhānaṃ with baddhacarānaṃ paricārakānaṃ sissānaṃ.

rittamāsanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of ritta (empty) and āsana (seat). Found in the Niddesa commentary in the phrase bhajato rittamāsanaṃ, referring to resorting to an empty seat. The text form rittamāsanan is a sandhi variant (often before a vowel or as an accusative ending -aṃ with -n). The lemma is given as the compound; pos and grammar follow the head word āsana (neuter).

yathānudhamman.meaning_2: in accordance with the teaching; according to the Dhamma; corresponding practice
yathānudhamman.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Adverbial compound in -a used as an indeclinable ('according to the Dhamma'). The text glosses it with bodhiyā anudhammā, taking it as 'the practices in conformity with enlightenment'. The spelling with single n is unusual; possibly yathānudhammaṃ.

pavakkhāmī.meaning_2: I will declare; I will explain; I will announce
pavakkhāmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 1st person singular future, quoted with -ti and glossed by a series of future verbs (ācikkhissāmi, desessāmi ...). The doubled kk is assimilation of the future sign -ssa- after the root vac.
pavakkhāmī.example_1: pavakkhāmīti pavakkhāmi ācikkhissāmi desessāmi paññapessāmi paṭṭhapessāmi vivarissāmi vibhajissāmi uttānīkarissāmi pakāsissāmi.
pavakkhāmī.example_2: Pavakkhāmīti pavakkhāmi ācikkhissāmi desessāmi paññapessāmi paṭhapessāmi vivarissāmi vibhajissāmi uttānīkarissāmi pakāsissāmi.
pavakkhāmī.translation_2: “I will declare” means I will declare, I will explain, I will teach, I will set forth, I will establish, I will open up, I will analyze, I will make plain, and I will reveal.

sarīsapānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form is genitive plural (sarīsapānaṃ), written sarīsapānan before ti. In the Niddesa gloss on ḍaṃsādhipātānaṃ.

catuppadānan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text, genitive plural modifying manussaphassānaṃ and explained as referring to lions, tigers, etc. Sometimes analysed as catuppadānaṃ (genitive plural of catuppada).
catuppadānan.example_2: catuppadānanti sīhā byagghā dīpī acchā taracchā kokā mahiṃsā hatthī.

bahubheravānī.meaning_2: many terrors; many fearful things; many dreadful objects
bahubheravānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of bahu + bheravāni, neuter nominative/accusative plural. The reading and split in the text is uncertain: bahubheravānīti = bahubheravāni + iti.

tehī.meaning_2: those; by those; with those (instrumental plural of ta)
tehī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental plural of the demonstrative pronoun ta, with the sandhi form -ī for -ehi. Refers back to ātaṅkaphassa, khudā, sīta and uṇha in the following gloss. Analysed in the text as tehi.
tehī.example_1: so tehīti ātaṅkaphassena ca khudāya ca sītena ca uṇhena ca phuṭṭho pareto samohito samannāgato assāti—
tehī.example_2: So tehīti ātaṅkaphassena ca khudāya ca sītena ca uṇhena ca phuṭṭho pareto samohito samannāgato assāti – so tehi phuṭṭho.
tehī.translation_2: “Touched by those” means he is touched, overcome, combined, and possessed by the touch of illness, hunger, cold, and heat—this is “touched by those.”

bhaṇeyyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular of bhaṇati, here negated: na musā bhaṇeyyā, 'one should not speak falsely'. The -ā is a variant of the usual -a ending.
bhaṇeyyā.example_2: na musā bhaṇeyyāti idha bhikkhu musāvādaṃ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato assa saccavādī saccasandho theto paccayiko avisaṃvādako lokassāti—

tasathāvarānī.meaning_2: moving and unmoving; animate and inanimate; the fearful and the firm
tasathāvarānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of tasa (moving, animate) and thāvara (unmoving, inanimate). Accusative plural in the text, depending on phasse.

abhisambhaveyyā.meaning_2: should overcome; should master; should prevail over
abhisambhaveyyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular of abhisambhavati; in the text it refers to overcoming the dear and the un-dear.
abhisambhaveyyā.example_1: athappiyaṃ vā pana appiyaṃ vā, addhā bhavanto abhisambhaveyyāti.
abhisambhaveyyā.example_2: Athappiyaṃ vā pana appiyaṃ vā, addhā bhavanto abhisambhaveyyā ’’ ti.
abhisambhaveyyā.translation_2: Now, whether it be dear or un-dear, one should indeed overcome it, O venerable one.”

taccariko.meaning_2: devoted to that; practising that; intent on that
taccariko.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it describes one whose conduct is bent on that (paññā). bahubbīhi formed with a pronoun (tad).
taccariko.example_1: paññaṃ purakkhatvāti idhekacco paññaṃ purato katvā carati paññādhajo paññāketu paññādhipateyyo vicayabahulo pavicayabahulo pekkhāyanabahulo sampekkhāyanabahulo vibhūtavihārī taccariko tabbahulo taggaruko tanninno tappoṇo tappabbhāro tadadhimutto tadadhipateyyoti.

asissan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Future 1st singular asissaṃ in the text, with the ending -issaṃ rather than -issāmi; the Niddesa glosses it with bhuñjissāmi. The PEU cross-reference to asata is uncertain.
asissan.example_2: kuva vā asissanti kattha bhuñjissāmi khattiyakule vā brāhmaṇakule vā vessakule vā suddakule vāti—

sessan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse 'dukkhaṃ vata settha kuvajja sessan' the reading 'sessan' looks like a sandhi or quotation form (possibly seyyaṃ or sessāmi), and the gloss explains it with 'sayittha', 2nd person plural aorist of sayati = you slept. The lemma here is sayati, present 3rd singular, and the form is an aorist-like finite form.
sessan.example_1: dukkhaṃ vata settha kuvajja sessanti imaṃ rattiṃ dukkhaṃ sayittha phalake vā taṭṭikāya vā cammakhaṇḍe vā tiṇasanthāre vā paṇṇasanthāre vā palālasanthāre vā.

annan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text annan is a sandhi form of annaṃ before ti. The Niddesa gloss lists foods such as odano, kummāso, sattu, maccho, maṃsaṃ. Sometimes spelled aṇṇa.

vasanan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Here vasana means clothing, explained by cha cīvarāni. The form vasanan is the sandhi of vasanaṃ before ti.
vasanan.example_2: Vasananti cha cīvarāni – khomaṃ, kappāsikaṃ, koseyyaṃ, kambalaṃ, sāṇaṃ, bhaṅgaṃ.
vasanan.translation_2: “Clothing” means: the six types of robes—linen, cotton, silk, wool, hemp, and hemp-cloth.

tosanatthan.meaning_2: for the purpose of satisfaction; for the sake of contentment; benefit of satisfaction
tosanatthan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of tosana (satisfaction) + attha (benefit, purpose). In the text it appears as tosanatthan, with the accusative singular ending -aṃ assimilated to -an before ti.

nātivelan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Contains the negative particle na and ativelan. In the quoted sentence vācaṃ pamuñce kusalaṃ nātivelan, the term qualifies the manner of speech: one should utter a wholesome word, not excessively.

rajānī.meaning_2: dusts; defilements (in the phrase 'five dusts': forms, sounds, smells, tastes, touches)
rajānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text 'pañca rajānīti' stands for pañca rajāni (nominative plural of rajas, nt). Probably to be read as rajas + āni, not as the masculine plural rajāni, which would not fit the number pañca; also it is glossed by rūparajo etc., all neuter.
rajānī.example_1: pañca rajānīti rūparajo, saddarajo, gandharajo, rasarajo, phoṭṭhabbarajo.

rāgan.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (sahetha rāgaṃ). The niggahīta is written as 'n' before the quotation ti.
rāgan.example_1: rūpesu saddesu atho rasesu, gandhesu phassesu sahetha rāganti.
rāgan.example_2: Rūpesu saddesu atho rasesu, gandhesu phassesu sahetha rāgan ’’ ti.
rāgan.translation_2: one should overcome passion among forms, sounds, and also flavors, odors, and contacts.”

kālenā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text, with -nā (kālena) before the quotation ti; glossed uddhate citte samathassa kālo. Not related to the verb kāleti.
kālenā.example_1: kālenāti uddhate citte samathassa kālo, samāhite citte vipassanāya kālo.
kālenā.example_2: Kālenāti uddhate citte samathassa [samādhissa (sī.)] kālo, samāhite citte vipassanāya kālo.
kālenā.translation_2: “At the proper time” means when the mind is restless, it is the time for serenity; when the mind is concentrated, it is the time for insight.
